# File: candidate-brand-context.md

# Candidate A — "brand-context"

Core model for the ownership/reference/effect redesign. Built against
`VERDICT-D0.md` §2 (R1–R15, M1–M11), §4 (C1–C18), §5 (premises), §7 (owner
decisions, interim positions taken as settled), `MECHANISM-MAP.md` §3 (the
hazard ladder), `PROGRAMS.md` (P1–P19) and `OPTIONS.md` D1–D4.

Nothing here is compared to another candidate. Every claim about a program is
shown as pseudocode with per-line accept/reject comments naming the fact used.

---

## 1. The tuple

| Point | Family (OPTIONS.md name) | Members drawn on |
|---|---|---|
| **D1** | **Allocation-scoped location name in the type** | AI-D1-01 (per-allocation type parameter `'a`), THE-D1-01 (abstract location in store typing), THE-D1-04 (nominal atom with freshness `a # b`), HIS-D1-04 (`ptr<'a,T>` plus per-identity state), HIS-D1-05 (identity parameters distinct by default) |
| D1, stated combination for sub-identity | **Path / resolved place** + **Element identity by index** + **Range, tile, partition** | AI-D1-02 (`'a.x`), HIS-D1-03 (resolved place: root plus ordered steps); AI-D1-03 (`'v[i]` with index proof), HIS-D1-23 (symbolic slot on a captured index); AI-D1-04 (proved range `'v[lo..hi]`), SYS-D1-13 (half-open extent) |
| D1, stated combination for results | **Result-origin provenance sets** | HIS-D1-14 (finite static origin set per returned view) |
| **D2** | **Implicit checker context** | AI-D2-01 (checker context facts only), THE-D2-01 (implicit checker context, ENT-5 today), HIS-D2-02 (the resource context is compiler state) |
| **D3** | **Three-state minimum**, refined by **State as a term over captured conditions** | AI-D3-01 / SYS-D3-01 / THE-D3-01 / HIS-D3-05 (`Init`/`Uninit`/`Gone` per identity); AI-D3-07, SYS-D3-14 (`ite(c, Init, Uninit)`), THE-D3-12, HIS-D3-07 (term over branch condition) |
| D3, stated combination for occupancy-as-data | **State as ordinary data or typed outcome** | HIS-D3-04 (vacancy as an `Option`-shaped value) — the admitted route for P11 |
| **D4** | **Unrestricted aliasing, safety from per-storage state** | AI-D4-01, THE-D4-02, SYS-D4-01, RAD-D4-02, THE-D4-23 (facts degrade monotonically, never reject), HIS-D4-02 |
| D4, stated combination for fact quality | **Overlap judged by resolved paths and proved extents** + **Read-only as a type flag, not a loan** | HIS-D4-12 (overlap by complete resolved paths), HIS-D4-13 (proved half-open view extents), SYS-D4-10; AI-D4-05, SYS-D4-04, HIS-D4-03 (C10) |

**Refused inside the chosen families, and why.** `'a` is an *allocation-scoped*
name, not the **Scope-introduced brand** family (AI-D1-06, THE-D1-05,
RAD-D1-08): a rank-2 scope brand cannot appear in an ordinary signature, and
P4's `Cursor<'v>` and P9's `reserve` need the name in a stored field and in an
`ensures`. Inside D2, RAD-D2-03 (Datalog EDB) and RAD-D2-04 (BDD over
condition atoms) are refused as the internal representation: both are
deterministic, but a BDD's size is data-dependent, which puts M10's measure
outside the syntax (§4, M10). Inside D3, RAD-D3-06 (BDD joins) is refused for
the same reason, and AI-D3-02 (`PartiallyInit(range)`) is unnecessary because
partial initialization is the product of the *field and element path* states
that D1 already supplies.

### Why these four cohere

The four are not independently selectable; each one is the only choice that
keeps the others' cost at zero.

| If we changed… | …the others break |
|---|---|
| D1 → no identity / runtime address (SYS-D1-19) | D3's per-storage state has nothing to attach to; D4's "safety from state alone" becomes safety from address comparison, a runtime check (M2(ii) violated) |
| D1 → scope brand only (THE-D1-05) | D4's aliased pointers cannot be *stored* (P4's cursor field, P3's link fields), and R7 cannot state an exit state for a storage the caller names |
| D2 → linear ghost tokens (AI-D2-02, SYS-D2-03, THE-D2-02) | D4 dies immediately: a token is a linear value, so copying a pointer must split or duplicate authority. P7's `p` and `q` both writable is unrepresentable |
| D2 → permission in the reference type (AI-D2-04, HIS-D2-01) | D4 dies: the reference carries permission, so two writable references to one slot is the very thing rejected. This is today's OWN-5 |
| D3 → plain lattice join (AI-D3-08, HIS-D3-08) | P8's `if c { free(a) } else { free(b) }` joins to `Top` and the only repair is a runtime drop flag — M2(ii) violated |
| D3 → typestate automata per nominal (AI-D3-05, THE-D3-06) | the vocabulary stops being fixed, so M1's "specification-fixed families" and M8's card budget both move to the writer |
| D4 → shared-xor-mutable (AI-D4-02, HIS-D4-01) | D1's identity is then redundant with the reference's exclusivity, D2's context is redundant with the reference's mode, and R9's negative test (P3's four link writes) fails |

The positive direction, stated once: **D1 makes a name that survives copying;
D2 keeps facts under that name rather than under a reference, so copying is
free; D3 makes the fact under that name path-sensitive enough to replace a
runtime flag; D4 then has nothing left to forbid, because every hazard R1–R3
owns is decided by the name's state and not by how many names exist.** That is
exactly the ladder's finding (`MECHANISM-MAP.md` §3, last table row: "borrowing
is not the mechanism that refuses any hazard once storage state and identity
exist").

## 2. The model

### 2.1 What a pointer's type says

```text
'a                      a location name. Minted fresh at an allocating operation
                        (existential unpack), or a parameter of a declaration or
                        of a nominal type. Erased. Never a runtime value.
'a.f  'a[i]  'a[lo..hi] sub-identity paths: field, element at a (possibly symbolic)
                        index, half-open range. Equality is path equality under a
                        fixed normalizer (HIS-D1-03).
'x | 'y                 a finite static origin set for a returned view (HIS-D1-14).

ptr<'a, T>              copyable, unrestricted, no duration, no mode, no region.
ptr<'a, T> read         the read-only interface flag (C10). A type flag, never a loan.
own<'a, T>              an affine binding carrying 'a's release obligation.
slice<'a[lo..hi], T>    a range sub-identity view.
```

A pointer's type says **which storage it names and nothing else**. It does not
say who else names it, for how long, or what may be done through it. Modes,
loans, regions, suspension windows and view-origin recovery are all deleted.

### 2.2 What the checker holds per storage

Nothing is written in source; the checker holds, per identity path, at every
program point:

```text
st('a.π)     ::= Init | Uninit | Gone | ite(c, st, st)
own('a)      ::= held-by b | discharged | ite(c, own, own)
layout('a)   ::= the current variant/representation term
backing('v)  ::= 'b                       (an ordinary replaceable fact)
facts        ::= a set of propositions, each keyed by its support paths (R6)
distinct     ::= a relation over paths, derived from freshness, containment,
                 path form, and proved index/extent arithmetic — never from
                 inequality of identity *names* (C3, P2's negative test)
```

`c` ranges over **captured condition atoms**: the guard expression of a
conditional, or a proposition written in a `requires` / `ensures` /
`invariant` / `use`. An atom is captured at its site with its support (the
bindings it reads); a write to that support kills the atom, and a term over a
dead atom collapses to the lattice join, whose `Top` is not a state but a
rejection at the next access naming the atom that died (M7 payload).

Each leaf of a state term carries the **source site of the transition that set
it**. This is the whole answer to D2's known repair problem: an implicit
context is invisible only if it cannot say where a value came from.

### 2.3 How state changes

| Operation | Precondition | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `alloc` | the allocator's own contract | fresh `'a` by existential unpack; `st('a) := Uninit`; `own('a) := held`; `distinct('a, x)` for every `x` live at the site that is not an ancestor of `'a` |
| `read(p: ptr<'a.π>)` | `st('a.π) = Init`, `layout('a)` current | none |
| `write(p, v)` | `st('a.π) ≠ Gone` | `st('a.π) := Init`; kill every fact whose support may-overlap `'a.π` |
| `take(p)` | `st('a.π) = Init` | `st('a.π) := Uninit`; the value leaves with its obligations (R3) |
| `put(p, move v)` | `st('a.π) = Uninit` | `st('a.π) := Init` |
| `replace(p, new)` | `st('a.π) = Init` | `st` unchanged; old returned with its obligations |
| `free(own<'a>)` | `own('a) = held`, `st('a) ≠ Gone` | `st('a.π) := Gone` for `'a` and **every** path under it, permanently; `own('a) := discharged`; kill every fact supported by any path under `'a` |
| `move own<'a>` (rebinding) | source holds | source binding consumed; `st('a)` **unchanged** — the owner moved, the storage did not (ladder Step 1) |
| relocating move of storage | — | `st('a) := Gone`; fresh `'b` with the moved contents; **no** rule revives `'a` at the same address |
| `push` / `reserve` | the container's contract | `len` fact updated; `backing('v)` either unchanged or `st(old) := Gone` and `backing('v) := fresh`, selected by a **term over the captured `cap` condition**, not by a runtime flag |

### 2.4 Join and loop head

**Join.** For each identity, if the incoming arms agree, keep the value. If
they differ, the result is `ite(c, s_then, s_else)` where `c` is the captured
guard of *this* construct. Definiteness of `own` is checked the same way: R2's
join rule is one rule, reused by R3.

**Loop head.** At a loop head, and at every function exit, each identity's
state must be a **constant** or a **term over atoms named in a written
`invariant` / `ensures`**. A term over a body-local atom is refused at the head,
naming the identity and the back edge. This rule is what bounds term growth
(§4, M10) and it is the candidate's only mandatory writer cost beyond
signatures.

Consequence for P8's loop: nothing is written, because `st = Init` at the head
is a constant.

### 2.5 What a signature states

```text
fn drain<'x>(p: ptr<'x, T>)
    requires st('x) = Init
    ensures  st('x) = Uninit
    writes   'x

fn reserve<'v, 'b>(v: ptr<'v, Vec<'b>>, m: u64)
    requires st('v) = Init and backing('v) = 'b
    ensures  exists 'b2. backing('v) = 'b2
             and (cap0 >= m ==> 'b2 = 'b)
             and (cap0 <  m ==> st('b) = Gone and st('b2) = Init and len('v) = len0)
    writes   'v, 'b

fn pick<'x, 'y>(c: bool, x: ptr<'x,T>, y: ptr<'y,T>) -> ptr<'x|'y, T>
    // a finite static origin set; reading through the result demands
    // st('x) = Init AND st('y) = Init; writing through it writes both.

fn helper<'s, 'in>(sl: slice<'s, u8>, input: ptr<'in, In> read)
    writes 's   reads 'in
```

The vocabulary is closed: identity parameters; `requires` / `ensures` over
`st`, `own`, `layout`, `backing`, `len` and `distinct`; `reads` / `writes`
footprints over paths; `exists 'b` for a fresh or replaced identity; an origin
set for a returned view. Distinct-by-default (HIS-D1-05) is a **call-site
obligation**, discharged at each call for every pair including sub-identities,
never an axiom of the checker (C3).

### 2.6 What the writer writes, and where

| Site | What is written | When it may be omitted |
|---|---|---|
| Signature | one identity parameter per distinctly named storage the interface mentions; entry/exit `st` clauses for each identity the call transitions; `reads` / `writes`; `exists` for fresh or replaced identities | a parameter that appears in exactly one argument position and nowhere in the clauses is elidable (D12) |
| Nominal type | one identity parameter per pointer-carrying field (`Cursor<'v>`, `Cols<'a..'h>`, a closure's captured roots) | same elision |
| Loop head | `invariant` only where an identity's state at the head is non-constant, or where a contents fact must survive the body | P5, P6, P8's loop need none |
| Join | **nothing** | always — the term is formed from the construct's own guard |
| Statement | **nothing**, except a `use` step where an R11 domain, an index disjointness, or a range disjointness is outside the automatic families | P2, P3, P5, P6, P7, P8 need none; P1 needs two |

### 2.7 What is erased

Every identity name, every `st`, `own`, `layout`, `backing` fact, every
captured atom, every term, every `use` step, every `requires` / `ensures` /
`invariant`, and the whole distinctness relation. Lowering receives machine
pointers plus the R4 channel: proved-distinct pairs, per-span write
footprints, and termination witnesses for removable calls. Nothing in the
lowered program branches on anything the source did not branch on (M2(ii),
M6(iii)).

## 3. Derivations

Notation follows the ladder. `//` comments give the verdict and the fact used.

### P1 Container split with a runtime index

```text
v: Vec<'b> in 'v, backing('v) = 'b, len('v) = n
qi = take(v, i)                 // accept: st('b[i]) = Init -> Uninit. R3 transfer.
                                //   qi : own<'qi,Elem>, 'qi fresh (frame slot)
qj = take(v, j)                 // accept: st('b[j]) = Init -> Uninit
                                //   distinct('qi,'qj): freshness at two allocating sites

write(qi.f, x)                  // accept: st('qi.f) != Gone
write(qj.f, y)                  // accept
                                // PAR overlap of the two writes:
                                //   footprints {'qi.f} and {'qj.f}; distinct by freshness.
                                //   overlap PERMITTED. no index proof needed here, because
                                //   the parts left the container. (R5 ground (i))

read(v[k])                      // REJECT.
                                //   st('b[k]) = ite(k = i, Uninit,
                                //                ite(k = j, Uninit, Init))
                                //   the term's Uninit leaves carry the two take() sites.
                                //   diagnostic (M7): "R1(i): 'b[k] holds no value when
                                //     k = i (site L2) or k = j (site L3).
                                //     missing fact: k != i and k != j"
use k != i                      // the writer's explicit finite step, or...
use k != j
read(v[k])                      // accept: both index atoms discharge the term to Init
                                //   (alternatively the writer writes
                                //    `if k != i && k != j { read(v[k]) } else { ... }`
                                //    and the branch guard is the captured atom — the branch
                                //    is the writer's, never the compiler's. M2 met.)

put(v, i, move qi)              // accept: st('b[i]) := Init
put(v, j, move qj)              // accept: st('b[j]) := Init
push(v, x)                      // accept: Vec's contract requires
                                //   forall e in 0..len. st('b[e]) = Init
                                //   which the two puts restored.
                                // (written before either put: REJECT, naming 'b[i] Uninit
                                //  and the take site. this is P1's "only after both are back".)
```

**Verdict: accepted as required.** No runtime check; the only branch at
`v[k]` is one the writer wrote; the diagnostic names the missing fact.

### P2 Arena with independently released blocks

```text
arena A in 'A, with sub-paths 'A.meta and 'A.bytes

b1 = alloc(A, 64)               // accept. ensures: exists 'b1.
                                //   st('b1)=Uninit, own held, 'b1 <= 'A.bytes (containment),
                                //   distinct('b1, every live block)
                                //   writes 'A.meta        <- NOT 'A.bytes, NOT 'A
b2 = alloc(A, 64)               // accept; distinct('b1,'b2) from the contract, not from
                                //   name inequality
b3 = alloc(A, 64)               // accept

fill(b1) || fill(b2) || fill(b3)
                                // accept: footprints {'b1},{'b2},{'b3}, pairwise distinct.
                                // nobody holds 'A: each fill's row names its own block only,
                                // and alloc's writes clause named 'A.meta, which no fill reads.
                                // overlap PERMITTED (R5 ground (i)).

free(A, b2)                     // accept: own('b2) discharged.
                                //   st('b2.π) := Gone for every π, permanently.
                                //   writes 'A.meta, 'b2.
                                //   R14(iii): the allocator may write inside 'b2 afterwards;
                                //   the model admits it, the program cannot observe it.
b4 = alloc(A, 32)               // accept: fresh 'b4, distinct from 'b1,'b3.
                                //   'b4 and 'b2 are related by NO rule. address reuse is
                                //   not a relation the checker has.

old: ptr<'b2, u8>               // holding the value is legal; copying it is legal (D4)
read(old)                       // REJECT: R1(ii), st('b2) = Gone (site: free(A,b2)).
                                //   'b4's reuse of the bytes cannot revive 'b2.

read(b1)                        // accept
free(A,b1); free(A,b3); free(A,b4)
                                // accept: four frees, four owns, no double. R2 met.

// R4 NEGATIVE test: distinct('A.bytes, 'b1) is NOT derivable —
//   'b1 <= 'A.bytes is a containment edge, and the distinctness relation is
//   over the containment structure, so an ancestor never becomes distinct from
//   a descendant. (R4(b), C3)
```

**Verdict: accepted as required.** Cost: the allocator's signature carries one
existential, one containment clause and one freshness clause; it is written
once per allocator.

### P3 Graph with back edges in a pool

```text
pool P in 'P of Node{ next, prev, data }
// the pool is ONE named identity; slots are sub-identities 'P[s].
// a stored link has type   exists s. ptr<'P[s], Node>
// representation invariant, written once on the pool type:
//   inv_links: forall s. st('P[s]) = Init ==>
//                st('P[ idx(P[s].next) ]) = Init and st('P[ idx(P[s].prev) ]) = Init

write(a.next, n)                // accept: st('P[a]) = Init, path 'P[a].next writable.
                                //   D4: a, b, n may alias each other; no rejection.
                                //   kills: facts whose support names 'P[a].next only.
                                //   R6: len, data facts and all other slots' facts survive.
write(n.prev, a)                // accept
write(n.next, b)                // accept
write(b.prev, n)                // accept
use inv_links                   // one finite step re-establishing the invariant from the
                                //   four writes; the invariant is STATED ONCE and reused
                                //   across all four (R6's (e) test).

// R9 negative test: a design that rejected these four writes fails R9.
//   this candidate accepts them with no window, no suspension, no mode.

remove(m)                       // accept: st('P[m].π) := Gone for every π.
                                //   kills every fact supported under 'P[m].
q : ptr<'P[m], Node>            // a back edge, a traversal cursor, any path to m
read(q)                         // REJECT: st('P[m]) = Gone. ONE fact refuses EVERY path
                                //   to m, because the fact is on the storage, not the pointer.
m2 = insert(P, ...)             // accept: the pool's contract returns a FRESH slot identity
                                //   'P[m2] even where the physical slot is m's.
                                //   no generation counter, no runtime compare (M2(ii)).

// traversal
p = unpack(a.next)              // accept: unpack gives a fresh index variable s with
                                //   st('P[s]) = Init from inv_links. ONE fixed unpack,
                                //   the writer writes nothing.
read(p.data)                    // accept

// parallel map
for s in slots(P) { write(P[s].data, f(P[s].data)) }
                                // accept: footprint per iteration {'P[s].data};
                                //   distinct('P[s], 'P[s']) for s != s' from the pool's
                                //   containment structure (slots are pairwise disjoint,
                                //   a premise of the pool type, discharged once).
                                //   PAR-2 overlap PERMITTED.
```

**Verdict: accepted with a stated cost.** The cost is at the back edges: a
stored link's identity is `exists s. 'P[s]`, so two unpacked links are not
provably distinct without a written step. Every *access* is accepted — that is
D4 — but the *facts* weaken exactly where the writer stored an unresolved
link. That is the candidate's declared trade, not a defect of the program.

### P4 Cursor over a growing vector

```text
struct Cursor<'v> { at: ptr<'v, Vec<'b>>, i: u64 }    // one identity parameter (C8)
c = Cursor{ at: &v, i: 0 }      // accept
a = c.read()                    // accept: requires st('v)=Init, i < len('v),
                                //   st(backing('v)[i]) = Init

push(v, 5)                      // accept. ensures:
                                //   len' = len0+1 and
                                //   (len0 < cap0  ==> backing('v) = 'b) and
                                //   (len0 >= cap0 ==> st('b) = Gone and
                                //                     backing('v) = fresh 'b2)
                                // NOTE: no borrow of v is outstanding, so nothing blocks push.
                                //   this is R8a/R1's (e) test and the candidate's answer to it.

b = c.read()                    // REJECT.
                                //   st('b) = ite(len0 < cap0, Init, Gone)
                                //   diagnostic (M7): "R1(ii): 'b has ended when len0 >= cap0
                                //     (site: push, ensures clause 3).
                                //     missing fact: len0 < cap0"
reserve(v, len0+1)              // ...written BEFORE the push: ensures cap0 >= len0+1
push(v, 5)
b = c.read()                    // accept: the atom len0 < cap0 discharges, term = Init

free(v)                         // accept: st('v) := Gone, st('b) := Gone
c.read()                        // REJECT: R1(ii), Gone. a compile-time rejection,
                                //   not a trap and not a generation compare (M2(i),(ii)).
```

**Verdict: accepted as required.** Validity is carried across `push` by the
term, decided by state and proof, never by a borrow that blocks `push`.

### P5 Struct-of-arrays kernel

```text
struct Cols<'a,'b,'c,'d,'e,'f,'g,'h> {
  a: buf<'a,u64>, b: buf<'b,u64>, ... h: buf<'h,u64>
}                               // 8 identity parameters, distinct by default (HIS-D1-05)
                                // the 28 pairwise obligations are discharged at each
                                // CONSTRUCTION site, not assumed by the checker (C3)

for i in 0..n {
  a[i] = f(a[i], c[i], d[i])    // accept. reads {'a[i],'c[i],'d[i]}, writes {'a[i]}
                                //   f's overflow behavior selected at this site (R11)
  b[i] = g(b[i], e[i], f[i], g[i], h[i])
                                // accept. reads {'b[i],'e[i],'f[i],'g[i],'h[i]}, writes {'b[i]}
}
// PAR-2 iteration overlap, iterations i and j, i != j:
//   written(i) = {'a[i],'b[i]},  written(j) = {'a[j],'b[j]}
//   distinct('a[i],'a[j]) from index arithmetic (i != j, same base path)
//   written(i) disjoint from read(j) likewise.
//   overlap PERMITTED. accept.
// R4 per-load facts the SOURCE carries to lowering:
//   distinct('a,'b), distinct('a,'c), ... all 28 pairs, from the construction-site
//   discharge. no `restrict`, no loop-level annotation, no restructuring.
// the obvious shape IS the checked shape: the loop above is written exactly as a
//   C programmer would write it, and is accepted with no hint. (M9's obvious-shape half.)
```

**Verdict: accepted as required.** Stated cost: 8 identity parameters on
`Cols` and 28 pairwise discharges per construction site. This is where M8 and
R15 are charged; see §6.

### P6 Range partition helper

```text
out: buf<'o, u8> of n bytes; k workers; s = n / k

fn helper<'s,'in>(sl: slice<'s,u8>, input: ptr<'in,In> read)
     writes 's  reads 'in       // the caller judges from THIS LINE ALONE (R7's (e) test)

for w in 0..k {
  sw = subrange(out, w*s, (w+1)*s)
                                // accept: yields slice<'o[w*s .. (w+1)*s]>.
                                //   a RANGE SUB-IDENTITY of 'o, not a fresh identity;
                                //   no split token is consumed and nothing is returned.
  helper(sw, input)             // accept: instantiates 's := 'o[w*s..(w+1)*s]
}
// PAR-2 iteration overlap, w != w':
//   written(w)  = {'o[w*s  .. w*s+s]}
//   written(w') = {'o[w'*s .. w'*s+s]}
//   distinct: half-open affine interval disjointness. both bounds normalize to
//     alpha*w + beta with alpha = s >= 0; for w != w' the intervals do not meet.
//   FIXED AUTOMATIC FAMILY (§4): normalize, compare sign of alpha, O(1). terminating,
//     order-independent, budget-free.
//   read(w) = {'in} for every w: read-read never interferes.
//   overlap PERMITTED. accept.
// no worker count appears in the source beyond k. accept.
```

**Verdict: accepted as required.** The overlap comes from the arithmetic of
the ranges and the helper's signature alone, with nothing written per
iteration.

### P7 Take, put, replace through aliases

```text
p : ptr<'A, T>
q = p                           // accept: copying a pointer is free. no token split,
                                //   no fraction, no loan, no mode. (D2 + D4)

v = take(p)                     // accept: st('A) := Uninit
read(q)                         // REJECT: R1(i), st('A) = Uninit (site: take through p).
                                //   the hole is on 'A, visible through EVERY name of 'A.
                                //   this is the row's "property of the storage" test.

put(q, move v)                  // accept: st('A) := Init. a DIFFERENT alias fills the hole.
read(p)                         // accept: st('A) = Init

old = replace(p, new)           // accept: st('A) stays Init; `old` leaves with its obligations
read(q)                         // accept: reads `new`. the contents fact written by replace
                                //   is keyed on 'A, so the read through q sees it —
                                //   no re-derivation, no must-alias analysis. (R6)

free('A)                        // accept: st('A.π) := Gone for every π
read(p)                         // REJECT forever: R1(ii). address reuse never revives 'A.
```

**Verdict: accepted as required.** This program is the candidate's home
ground; R1's whole acceptance test is satisfied by construction.

### P8 Conditional release and loop exits

```text
if c { free(a) } else { free(b) }
// join:
//   st('a)  = ite(c, Gone, Init)      own('a) = ite(c, discharged, held)
//   st('b)  = ite(c, Init, Gone)      own('b) = ite(c, held, discharged)
//   atom c captured with its support = the bindings c reads.
//   NO drop flag, NO bit, NO runtime state: the term is checker state, erased.

use_survivor_wrong:
  use(a); free(a)               // REJECT: R2. "own('a) is discharged when c holds
                                //   (site: then-arm free). the path through the then-arm
                                //   differs from the else-arm at 'a.
                                //   missing: a branch on c, or a proof that c is false."
                                //   <- P8's "rejection names the path whose state differs"

use_survivor_right:
  if c { use(b); free(b) }      // accept: inside the arm the atom c is TRUE, so
                                //   st('b) evaluates to Init and own('b) to held.
  else  { use(a); free(a) }     // accept: c FALSE, st('a) = Init, own('a) = held
  // at the join, own('a) and own('b) are BOTH discharged on both paths. R2 met.
  // the selecting branch is the writer's `if c`, already in the source. M2(ii) met.

loop {
  if stop { break }             // exit edge: st('A) = Init here (before the take)
  v = take(p)                   // st('A) := Uninit
  ...
  put(p, move v)                // st('A) := Init
}                               // latch edge: st('A) = Init
// loop head join of entry edge (Init) and latch edge (Init) = Init, a CONSTANT.
// no invariant is written. accept.
free(p)                         // accept: st('A) = Init, own held on every exit edge

// contrast, to show the rule bites:
loop { v = take(p); if stop { break }; put(p, move v) }
                                // REJECT at the loop head: the break edge carries
                                //   st('A) = Uninit and the latch carries Init; the join
                                //   is a term over `stop`, an atom not live at the head.
                                //   "R1: 'A's state at the loop head is not constant.
                                //    write `invariant st('A) = ...` or restore before break."
```

**Verdict: accepted as required.** No runtime drop flag; the writer's own
branches carry the state; the rejection names the differing path.

### P9 A callee that changes storage state

```text
fn drain<'x>(p: ptr<'x,T>) requires st('x)=Init ensures st('x)=Uninit writes 'x
fn reserve<'v,'b>(...)   // as §2.5
fn pick<'x,'y>(c, x, y) -> ptr<'x|'y, T>

caller:
  drain(q)                      // accept: st('Q) = Init satisfies requires.
                                //   after: st('Q) = Uninit, from the ensures ALONE.
                                //   the body is never opened (R7, FN-1).
  read(q)                       // REJECT: R1(i). "'Q holds no value; set by drain's
                                //   `ensures st('x) = Uninit` at the call on line N."
  put(q, move w)                // accept

  r = pick(c, x, y)             // accept: r : ptr<'X|'Y, T>
  read(r)                       // accept iff st('X)=Init AND st('Y)=Init
  write(r, 5)                   // accept. writes footprint = {'X,'Y} (a may-write).
                                //   kills contents facts on BOTH.
                                //   R6 cost, and it is NAMED by the stated footprint,
                                //   so R6's letter is met: nothing died that the
                                //   footprint did not name.

  reserve(v, 100)               // accept: the `exists 'b2` is unpacked to a fresh name
  read(old_elem)                // REJECT unless cap0 >= 100 discharged; the diagnostic
                                //   quotes reserve's third ensures clause.

// callee side, checked ONCE:
//   drain's body must exhibit exactly `writes 'x` and leave st('x)=Uninit at every exit.
//   reserve's body must satisfy both arms of its ensures on the paths that produce them.
```

**Verdict: accepted as required.** Each effect is in the signature; the caller
judges by the signature alone; the body is checked once. Stated cost: `pick`'s
origin-set result degrades R6 precision at exactly the site where the writer
asked the callee to choose — a cost that is visible in `pick`'s own return
type.

### P11 Write-once-then-frozen cache

Two shapes. The candidate admits one and refuses the other, and the refusal is
the interesting half.

```text
// SHAPE 1 (REFUSED): occupancy as a checker state, tested at run time
cache: array<'c, V>, st('c[k]) = Uninit initially
get(k):
  if is_filled('c[k]) { read(cache[k]) } else { ... }
                                // REJECT at `is_filled`: there is no such operation.
                                //   `st` is checker state, erased; nothing at run time
                                //   can read it. Supplying a runtime occupancy test would
                                //   be a bookkeeping bit the source did not bind and a
                                //   branch selecting between source-visible behaviors on
                                //   a predicate the checker did not discharge: M2(ii).
                                //   The candidate does NOT add a `Frozen` state
                                //   (AI-D3-03, SYS-D3-09) for exactly this reason.

// SHAPE 2 (ACCEPTED): occupancy as ordinary data (HIS-D3-04)
cache: array<'c, Option<V>>     // st('c[k]) = Init for every k from construction.
                                //   there is no hole anywhere in this program.
get(k):
  match cache[k] {              // accept: an ordinary data match the WRITER wrote
    Some(v) => read(v)          // accept
    None    => { w = compute(k);
                 cache[k] = Some(w);
                                // accept: write to 'c[k]. kills facts supported by 'c[k].
                 read(cache[k]) }   // accept: st('c[k]) = Init
  }

// "may a reader hold ptr<'c[j]> across another slot's fill?"
pj : ptr<'c[j], Option<V>>
fill(cache, k)                  // writes 'c[k]
read(pj)                        // accept ALWAYS: a write can never make a live storage
                                //   Gone, so st('c[j]) = Init survives unconditionally.
                                //   the POINTER stays valid with no proof at all.
                                //   only CONTENTS facts about 'c[j] need distinct('c[j],'c[k]),
                                //   i.e. j != k; without it the value fact dies and the
                                //   read reloads. loss of speed, never of safety (R4(a)).
```

**Verdict: accepted with a stated cost, and the pass/fail under R1 alone is
recorded.** Under R1 alone, Shape 2 passes: every slot is `Init` from
construction and no sub-property of R1 is ever at risk. The cost is one
discriminant word per slot — which is precisely why-whitefoot §5's stance that
the absence of such cells is a *performance* argument. Admitting the
zero-overhead Shape 1 is therefore a capability question the candidate answers
"no" on M2(ii) grounds; reversing that answer needs D3's access-mode family
plus a D2 carrier that is data, and both contradict this tuple.

### P13 Relocation by a compacting third party

```text
pool 'P, compacting. h : Handle (an index), p = pointer_of(h) : ptr<'P[h], Node>

pool.compact()                  // its contract MUST state the relocation as a
                                //   storage-ending event (R8a):
                                //     ensures forall s. st('P[s]) = Gone
                                //             and exists 'P2. st('P2) = Init
                                //             and len('P2) = len('P)
                                //     writes 'P
read(p)                         // REJECT: R1(ii), st('P[h]) = Gone
                                //   (site: compact's first ensures clause).
read(pool[h])                   // accept: the HANDLE is an index, not a pointer.
                                //   `index(pool, h)` re-derives the element identity by
                                //   unpack against 'P2, requiring only h < len('P2),
                                //   which compact's ensures preserved.

// Why there is no fixup form here:
//   'a is a static, erased name with NO runtime representation. There is nothing in the
//   lowered program to rewrite, so a fixup channel cannot be built inside this tuple.
//   R8a's price is therefore paid in full: "the compiler relocates no storage while an
//   interior pointer names it ... unless the fixup form is used", and this candidate
//   uses none.
```

**Verdict: accepted as required — as a refusal.** R8a's stated requirement is
that interior pointers and third-party relocation are mutually exclusive
without a contract-visible fixup form, and the candidate refuses exactly there
and lets the handle survive. **Needs a mechanism from D8** ("Relocation with a
fixup channel": RAD-D8-11, SYS-D8-06, SYS-D8-12) if the owner wants `p` to
survive compaction; nothing in this tuple supplies or forbids adding one.

### P16 Abstraction over identities

```text
fn map_nodes<'P, T>(g: Pool<'P, Node<T>>, f: fn(&T) -> T)
     reads  forall s. 'P[s].data
     writes forall s. 'P[s].data
// accept. ONE identity parameter for a callee touching |slots| storages, because the
// pool is one containment structure and the element domain is quantified.
// R15 metric: parameters per interface = 1 for a callee touching n storages. SUBLINEAR.

fn kernel<'a,'b,'c,'d,'e,'f,'g,'h, E>(cols: Cols<'a..'h, E>)
// accept. 8 identity parameters for 8 distinctly named storages.
// R15 metric: LINEAR in storages touched, and at the bound. This is the candidate's
// worst abstraction case and it is the honest number.
// Mitigation available inside D1+D12: the parameters are declared once on the NOMINAL
// `Cols`, elided at every mention, distinct by default, and printed on demand. The
// writer types `Cols<E>`; the checker holds eight names.

let h = |slice| helper(slice, input)
// the closure captures `input : ptr<'in, In>`, so the closure's own type carries it:
//   closure<['in], fn(slice<'s,u8>) -> ()>  writes 's  reads 'in       (C8)
// accept. P6 with h: the overlap judgment reads the closure's row exactly as it read
// helper's, because a captured identity is a parameter, not a hidden root.

fn pick<'x,'y, N: Nominal>(c: bool, x: N<'x>, y: N<'y>) -> N<'x|'y>
// accept: the finite origin set crosses the nominal unchanged; instantiation substitutes
// names and is decidable by the fixed substitution rule (no search, HIS-REQ-07's cycle
// check unchanged).
```

**Verdict: accepted with a stated cost.** Identity, state and effect facts all
cross the boundary; generic definitions are checked once and instantiation is
substitution. The cost is parameter count on nominals whose fields are
separately-named storages, and it is the row where this candidate is most
exposed. **Needs D12's elision family** (THE-D12-06, THE-D12-07, HIS-D12-07)
to keep the written form small; without it the candidate is accepted-with-cost,
not rejected.

### P17 Partial operations

```text
q = a / d                       // REJECT: R11. "division requires d != 0.
                                //   missing fact: d != 0"
use d != 0                      // accept ...or...
if d != 0 { q = a / d } else { outcome DivByZero }
                                // accept: the outcome arm is R12's, the branch is the writer's

b: u8 = narrow(x)               // REJECT: R11. "narrow to u8 requires x < 256"
if x < 256 { b = narrow(x) } else { outcome TooWide }
                                // accept

y = v[i]                        // TWO facts, TWO diagnostics, never conflated:
                                //   (1) R11 domain:  i < len('v)
                                //   (2) R1(i) state: st(backing('v)[i]) = Init
                                // REJECT (1) first: "index requires i < len(v)"
use i < len(v)
y = v[i]                        // accept, since st('b[i]) = Init holds from Vec's
                                //   representation invariant for i < len.
                                // (in P1's shape, where a take left a hole, (2) fails
                                //  INSTEAD and the diagnostic is R1's, not R11's —
                                //  which is R1's (e) requirement that the diagnostic
                                //  name which sub-property failed.)
```

**Verdict: accepted as required.** The candidate contributes only the index
case, and its contribution is the *separation* of the bounds fact from the
state fact so each gets its own repairable diagnostic.

## 4. Requirements

### 4.1 The 27 rows

| Row | Verdict | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| **R1** Sequential memory safety | **met** | (i) hole = `Uninit`, (ii) ended = `Gone` (permanent, unrevivable by reuse — P2, P7), (iii) stale layout = the `layout('a)` fact; all three are per-identity-path facts checked at every access, and the diagnostic names which sub-property failed (P17) |
| **R2** Resource lifecycle accounting | **met** | `own('a)` is definite at every join because a differing join is a term over the construct's own guard (P8); no release depends on runtime state the source did not branch on; the join rule is stated once and reused by R3 |
| **R3** Value classes and transfer | **met** | take/put/replace/move are the four transitions of §2.3; the multiplicity lemma is over transfers, separate from R1's state lemma; "used twice" (a second `take` on `Uninit`) and "never released" (`own` held at exit) are distinct diagnostics |
| **R4** Licensed facts for the backend | **met** | distinctness is a relation over a containment structure — freshness at allocation, path form, index and half-open extent arithmetic — and *never* name inequality; P2's negative test (`'A.bytes` vs `'b1`) holds because containment blocks distinctness; a missing fact costs speed only |
| **R5** Data-race freedom and permitted overlap | **partial** | ground (i) is met and is the candidate's whole overlap story (P1, P3, P5, P6); grounds (ii) (checked accumulator laws) and (iii) (named weaker levels) are R14(ii)/D5 choices this tuple neither supplies nor forecloses |
| **R6** Frame: proof-fact retention | **met** | kills are keyed by may-overlap of support paths against the *stated* footprint, so a write to `'v[i]` cannot kill a `len('v)` fact, and a call's kills are exactly its `writes` row; the widest kill in the corpus (`pick`'s origin set, P9) is named by its own footprint |
| **R7** Compositional call judgement | **met** | the interface vocabulary of §2.5 states entry/exit states, returned interior pointers with origin sets, fresh allocations by `exists`, and read/write/end footprints; P9's three callees are judged from signatures alone and P6's helper's one line tells the caller what it writes |
| **R8a** Storage-ending and relocation events | **met** | the set is `free`, relocating move, reallocating `push`/`reserve`, arena reset, scope exit, container insertion, return, and R14(iii) actors; each is a `Gone` transition and an interface clause; no fixup form is supplied, so interior pointers and third-party relocation are mutually exclusive, which is what the row requires (P13) |
| **R8b** Placement and physical demands | **partial** | not supplied by this tuple; `'a` is the natural attachment point for an alignment/layout demand and nothing here forecloses one, but no demand vocabulary is defined |
| **R9** Shared mutation among several holders | **met** | this is D4 stated as a row: several long-lived writable pointers to one storage are accepted with no judgment (P3's four link writes, P7's `p` and `q`); the row's negative test is passed; the cost the row demands be named is named — lost distinctness and widened kills exactly where identities coincide |
| **R10** External resources as ordinary objects | **partial** | a descriptor, mapping or socket is an ordinary identity with `st` and contracts, and P14's three identities (close-obligation wrapper, description with cursor, foreign contents) are directly expressible as three names; the foreign-contents half needs R14(iv)'s access class, which this tuple does not define |
| **R11** Partial operations and overflow | **met** | orthogonal to D1–D4; discharged by the same `use`-step and diagnostic machinery, and the candidate's contribution is keeping the domain fact and the state fact separate (P17) |
| **R12** Failure paths and typed outcomes | **partial** | each outcome arm is an ordinary branch whose guard is a captured atom, so R2 discharges per arm and the join is checked (P8's machinery, unchanged); the outcome *type* vocabulary and the no-allocate context are D7/D11 choices this tuple does not make |
| **R13** Resource bounds where demanded | **partial** | no cost semantics or bound derivation is supplied; the arena identity `'A` carries a measure term naturally and nothing forecloses R13, but a program declaring a byte budget cannot be accepted by this tuple alone |
| **R14** Stated execution model and external conditions | **partial** | (iii) is actively used and required — P2's derivation depends on the allocator's right to write inside freed `'b2` — and the per-storage interference qualifier attaches to `'a`; (i), (ii), (iv), (v), (vi) are untouched |
| **R15** Abstraction | **met (with cost)** | identity, state and effect facts cross every boundary as ordinary parameters; generics are checked once and instantiation is substitution; the metric is sublinear where a containment structure names a family (P16 `map_nodes`: 1 parameter for n storages) and linear at its bound where it does not (`Cols`: 8) |
| **M1** Specified deterministic acceptance | **met** | exactly four automatic families, each specification-fixed, order-independent and terminating: path normalization and equality; containment/overlap over paths; half-open affine interval disjointness (O(1) sign test); state-term evaluation and join (finite, over a syntactically determined atom set). No search, no solver, no portfolio, no budget, no cap |
| **M2** No unstated failure edge, no unchosen cost | **met** | (i) every failure is a compile-time rejection; nothing traps. (ii) no drop flag (P8), no generation or epoch compare (P3's slot reuse mints a fresh static identity), no occupancy bit (P11 refuses the checker-state-tested shape by rule), no permission counter anywhere — because D4 has no permission to count |
| **M3** Enumerated, writer-closed trusted base | **met** | no escape form exists; the allocator's and pool's freshness/containment clauses are contracts checked against their bodies under PROG-1, not axioms; the base is the R14 entries and the backend |
| **M4** Writer regularity | **met** | one spelling per construct: the identity parameter, `requires`/`ensures`, `reads`/`writes`, `invariant`, `use`, and the `read` type flag. Modes, loans, regions, `region { }` blocks, suspension windows and view-origin recovery are deleted rather than refined (C13) |
| **M5** Acceptance independent of permission | **met, structurally** | the candidate has no permission judgment at all, so no acceptance verdict can depend on one. The dependency-graph test is passed by construction, not by wiring |
| **M6** Soundness evidence | **partial** | (i) a bounded small-model check is directly runnable: the state space per identity is three values plus a term over a finite atom set, which is the access-state experiment's form; (ii) frame soundness holds by may-overlap over-approximation; (iii) erasure is total (§2.7). The operational semantics and adequacy theorem are the stated later obligation (owner decision 9(b)); (iv)'s facts-withheld differential is straightforward — withhold distinctness pairs, rebuild, diff |
| **M7** Repairable rejection | **met** | every rejection names one rule, one identity path, the term leaf that failed **and the source site of the transition that set it** (§2.2), plus the missing atom. Routes are taught for each: `use` a fact, branch on the condition, write an `invariant` at the head, restore before the break. This is the direct answer to implicit context's known repair problem |
| **M8** Teaching and retrieval budget | **partial** | the taught surface this tuple adds is small — names and paths; three states plus `ite`; the transition table; footprints; four families — and it *removes* modes, borrow durations, regions, suspension windows, loan strengths and origin recovery. The row is red project-wide against K = 48k regardless, and the candidate's own exposure is signature width on nominals (P5, P16), not rule count |
| **M9** Measured performance floor | **partial** | unmeasurable until an alias channel exists (the emitter emits no alias facts today). The obvious shape of P5 and P6 is the accepted shape with no hint, and distinct-by-default keeps the default fact strong. The residue is real: a writer who coarsens identities is accepted and silently slower, and no rule catches it (§6) |
| **M10** Checking cost, scaling and edit stability | **violated (stated, with the amendment)** | the state-term family is exponential in the nesting depth of conditionals whose innermost arms differ on one identity: `if c1 { if c2 { take(p) } else {} } else { if c3 {} else { take(p) } }` yields a term of size 2^d. M10's ceiling is cubic and its text says "never exponential". Declared, not hidden. Mitigations, all budget-free: terms collapse to a constant or a written-invariant term at every loop head, call boundary and function exit (§2.4), and an atom dies with its support, so accumulation is bounded by simultaneously-live guards over one identity. Edit stability is met: FN-1's interface is the reach boundary; a body edit changes one declaration's verdict |
| **M11** Evolution with stated loss | **met** | the verdict diff over the retained corpus is computable, the candidate is a whole replacement whose losses are listable (every `region { }` block and every mode annotation in the corpus disappears), and `use` steps survive any revision that does not change their rule |

**Counts: 17 met, 9 partial, 1 violated (M10).**

### 4.2 The price this candidate charges the compiler

| Price | Ground |
|---|---|
| May not relocate storage while an interior pointer names it (no moving collector, no address-changing copy), because no fixup form exists | R8a's price, paid in full (P13) |
| May not insert any check, trap, flag, tag, generation or counter; no lowered branch may select between source-visible behaviors on a path the source does not name | M2(ii) |
| Must carry, per identity path per program point: a state term with per-leaf provenance, an `own` term, a layout term, and a support-keyed fact set. Memory is O(identities × points) with terms up to 2^(conditional nesting depth over one identity) | D3's refinement; the M10 amendment |
| Must implement exactly four automatic families and no fifth; anything harder is a written `use` step the checker verifies without rediscovering | M1, the constitution |
| Must discharge distinct-by-default at *every* call and construction site for every pair including sub-identities, never assume it | C3, P2's negative test |
| Must erase every name, state, atom and proof before lowering, and must not require re-derivation to reach a stated fact | M6(iii), R4's price |
| May not use whole-program points-to as an acceptance input | M1, FN-1 |
| Gains: no borrow checker, no region inference, no loan lattice, no suspension-window machinery, no view-origin recovery | C13 |

### 4.3 Writer cost

| Per… | Cost |
|---|---|
| **signature** | one identity parameter per distinctly named storage the interface mentions (sublinear where a pool/container names a family, linear where it does not); one `requires`/`ensures` clause per identity the call transitions; one `reads`/`writes` row; one `exists` per fresh or replaced identity |
| **nominal type** | one identity parameter per pointer-carrying field (`Cursor<'v>`, `Cols<'a..'h>`, closure captures) — the single largest writer cost and the one D12 elision must absorb |
| **loop** | an `invariant` only where an identity's state at the head is non-constant or a contents fact must survive the body. P5, P6, P8's loop, P3's map: **zero** |
| **join** | **zero**, always |
| **statement** | **zero**, except a `use` step where an R11 domain, an index disjointness or a range disjointness falls outside the four families. P1: two. P2, P3's writes, P5, P6, P7, P8: zero |

## 5. Consequences at D5–D13

| Point | Forced | Foreclosed |
|---|---|---|
| **D5** interference source | **Effect footprints over identities** (AI-D5-01, SYS-D5-01, THE-D5-01, HIS-D5-07) — the footprint is over `'a` paths and is the same object R4 and R6 read (C2). **Optimizer-facing alias fact channel** (HIS-D5-23/24/25) becomes mandatory, since D4 makes fact quality the only performance lever | **Loans on references beside footprints** (AI-D5-04, SYS-D5-02, HIS-D5-01/04/05): there are no references to loan. **Fractional or counting permissions** (AI-D5-05, THE-D5-03): D4 has no permission to divide. **Runtime dependence tracking** (RAD-D5-06, SYS-D5-05): M2(ii) |
| **D6** distinctness default | **Distinct by default, call-site proof** (AI-D6-01, SYS-D6-01, THE-D6-01, HIS-D6-02), with **Apartness as a judgment** (THE-D6-06/07) and **Index-arithmetic distinctness** (RAD-D6-04, THE-D6-16) as its discharge routes | **May-alias by default, callee copes** (AI-D6-02, HIS-D6-01): would put P5's obvious shape off M9's floor. **Distinct names are distinct storage** as a checker *axiom* (AI-D6-06): refused by C3 and P2. **Dynamic distinctness check** (RAD-D6-06, SYS-D6-11): M2 |
| **D7** contract vocabulary | **Requires/ensures over identity states** (AI-D7-01, SYS-D7-01, THE-D7-01, HIS-D7-14) + **Footprint and frame clauses** (AI-D7-02, THE-D7-02) + **Existential result identities** (AI-D7-05, SYS-D7-09, THE-D7-15) + **Ownership and identity transfer as the summary** (SYS-D7-11). **Closed catalog and size budget** (AI-D7-11/12) is needed for M8 | **No contracts: whole-program inference** (AI-D7-08, RAD-D7-01, HIS-D7-24): R7 + FN-1. **Prophecies and backward functions** (THE-D7-16): not forbidden, but there is no mutable borrow to prophesy, so the family becomes dead weight |
| **D8** relocation | **Explicit relocating move as the storage-ending event** (AI-D8-03, SYS-D8-02, HIS-D8-01); **Reallocation as a contract-visible name change** (AI-D8-05, SYS-D8-05, THE-D8-01, HIS-D8-13) — P4 depends on it; **Aggregates travel as handles** (AI-D8-01, HIS-D8-14) per C4; **Pools with stable index handles** (AI-D8-08, SYS-D8-07, HIS-D8-17) for P3 and P13 | **Compiler-inferred placement** (RAD-D8-02, THE-D8-06) wherever it would move storage under a live interior pointer. **Relocation with a fixup channel** (RAD-D8-11, SYS-D8-06, SYS-D8-12) is *not* foreclosed but is left unchosen, and until it is chosen a compacting pool must end every element identity (P13) |
| **D9** containers | **Path identity `'v[i]`** (AI-D9-01, SYS-D9-01, THE-D9-01, HIS-D9-03); **Existential backing per formation** (AI-D9-02, SYS-D9-02, THE-D9-02, HIS-D9-04) — P4's `backing('v)`; **Quantified element permission** (THE-D9-04, HIS-D9-08/09) — P3's map; **Bounded views and proved subrange subdivision** (HIS-D9-13..16) — P6 | **Generations and epochs** (AI-D9-05, SYS-D9-04, RAD-D9-06) as a *safety* mechanism: M2(ii). **Per-element ghost tokens** (AI-D9-04, SYS-D9-03, HIS-D9-05/06): contradicts D2. **Split-and-join range tokens** (AI-D9-08, SYS-D9-07) as the *only* route: P6's ranges are sub-identities, not consumed tokens |
| **D10** concurrency | **Lock as custodian of identity state** (AI-D10-01, SYS-D10-01, THE-D10-01, HIS-D10-06) is the natural fit and C11 already names it: the lock holds `st` while no thread does, and the cost lands on the write. **Structured fork/join with linear task handles** (AI-D10-09, HIS-D10-03/04) fits R5's non-erasable-construct rejection | **Typed reference capabilities and sendability** (THE-D10-14/15/16, RAD-D10-06): there are no reference capabilities to send. **Transactions** (RAD-D10-03, SYS-D10-17): M2(ii). Global writable storage as a holder stays the owner's (decision 10, interim: the ban stands) |
| **D11** external resources | **Foreign identity: retain no contents fact** (AI-D11-01, SYS-D11-01, THE-D11-01) as an *interference qualifier on the identity* — the cleanest fit in the catalog, because the qualifier sits exactly where `st` and the fact table already key. **Three identities per descriptor** (THE-D11-15, HIS-D11-14): P14 becomes three ordinary names. **States as ordinary enums or identities with declared states** (AI-D11-05, HIS-D11-13) | **Ambient and forgeable host access** (SYS-D11-13, HIS-D11-03/27). **Second host-authority category** (HIS-D11-25/26/28): R10 forbids a compiler-special path |
| **D12** surface form | **Modes as sugar over pointer plus state** (AI-D12-01, SYS-D12-01, THE-D12-01, HIS-D12-10): `&`/`&uniq` survive only as abbreviations, if at all. **Elision and implicit identity parameters** (THE-D12-06, THE-D12-07, HIS-D12-07) stops being optional and becomes load-bearing — it is the only thing standing between P5/P16's parameter counts and M8. **Region sigil fate** (AI-D12-15, HIS-D12-08/09) must be decided | **Region block and borrow-endpoint spelling** (HIS-D12-11..14): there are no borrows to spell and no endpoints to place. **Annotation layer beside the declaration** (SYS-D12-03, HIS-D12-16): identity parameters are types, not annotations |
| **D13** validation | **Bounded exhaustive enumeration** (AI-D13-01, SYS-D13-01, THE-D13-01, HIS-D13-01/02/03) as M6(i)'s runnable form: the per-identity state space is three values plus a term over a finite atom set, which is *small enough to enumerate*, and that is a genuine advantage of the three-state choice. **Fact-channel review and runtime attribute checks** (HIS-D13-05/06, SYS-D13-06) because D4 makes fact quality the measured object. **Dual acceptance and acceptance-set diffs** (SYS-D13-14, THE-D13-09, HIS-D13-15/16) for M11 | **Executable semantics with a dynamic shadow-state oracle** (RAD-D13-04, SYS-D13-05) as the *primary* evidence: a shadow state at run time is the thing M2(ii) forbids in the product, so it is a test harness only, never a build mode (M6(iv)) |

---

## 6. Weaknesses and the strongest objection

### 6.1 The strongest objection

> **D4 moves the entire aliasing burden out of acceptance and into fact
> quality. The compiler's optimization power becomes a function of how
> carefully the writer named identities — and nothing in acceptance tells the
> writer when they lost it. A program that names one identity where two would
> do is accepted, silently slower, with no diagnostic and no rule to catch it.
> M9 is a measurement, not a gate, so the floor is defended by hope.**

This is the catalog's own tension on the D4 family ("the obvious shape stops
being the fast shape and R4 quality becomes a writer-effort question") and it
is the objection I cannot fully answer. Three partial answers and the residue:

1. **Distinct-by-default inverts the default.** Losing a fact requires a
   deliberate act — passing one identity into two parameters, or storing an
   unresolved link. Both are visible at the call or construction site, not
   diffuse. The failure mode is not "the writer forgot to write `restrict`";
   it is "the writer wrote the same name twice".
2. **The loss is reportable without touching acceptance.** A fact-loss report
   (AI-D4-09) printed beside the build names the pair of coinciding identities
   and the facts that died. It is a diagnostic channel, so it cannot influence
   any verdict: M1 and M5 are untouched. What it cannot do is *force* a fix.
3. **P5 and P6 need no annotation at all.** The two programs the floor is
   measured on are accepted in their obvious shape with zero hints and full
   distinctness, so the default shape is not the degraded shape.

**Residue I concede:** there is no rule that refuses a coarsened identity, and
there cannot be one without reintroducing a permission judgment, which is the
thing D4 exists to delete. The candidate's honest position is that this trade
is the price of R9 and P3, and that M9 must therefore be wired as a real
measurement before this candidate is selected, not after.

### 6.2 The other weaknesses, stated

| Weakness | Where it bites | Best answer available |
|---|---|---|
| **M10 is violated**: term size 2^(conditional nesting depth) per identity | a deeply nested conditional whose innermost arms differ on one storage | collapse at loop heads, calls and function exits (§2.4); atoms die with their support; the writer can always buy the bound back with one `invariant`. It is still exponential in the worst case and is declared as an M10 amendment, not argued away |
| **Signature width on nominals** — the D1 family's own named weak spot, "forgetting a parameter on a nominal" | `Cols<'a..'h>` (P5, P16), and every struct that stores a pointer | D12 elision with distinct-by-default and a printed form. But elision is outside this tuple, so the candidate depends on a decision it does not make. Forgetting a parameter is not unsound — it *merges* two identities, which loses facts and never gains permission |
| **Stored links are existential**, so back-edge facts weaken | P3's traversal, any graph or intrusive list | this is D4 working as designed: accesses stay legal, facts weaken. The writer buys a fact back with a `use` step where it matters, and nowhere else |
| **Implicit context is invisible** (the D2 family's named tension) | every rejection, and every "why is this slow" question | per-leaf transition provenance in the state term (§2.2) turns "a fact died" into "this operation on line N set this identity to this state". It does not make the *surviving* state readable in the source; a reader must ask the compiler. This candidate accepts that and refuses AI-D2-08's transcription, which would make the context a source artifact and reopen D2 |
| **No fixup channel**, so compacting allocators and moving pools are out | P13, and any future GC-shaped experiment | R8a's price, paid deliberately. Handles survive; interior pointers do not. Reversing it is a D8 decision, not a change to this tuple |
| **P11's zero-overhead shape is refused** | lazy caches, memo tables | occupancy becomes an `Option` discriminant, one word per slot. The refusal is on M2(ii) and it is a capability answer, not an oversight: admitting it needs a `Frozen` state plus a data carrier, and both contradict D3 and D2 |
| **R13, R14(i)(ii)(iv)(v), R8b are unsupplied** | budgets, threads, foreign writes, layout demands | none is foreclosed, and `'a` is the attachment point each of them would use. But a candidate scored only on the sequential fragment is exactly what R15's admission note warns about, so these must be derived before selection, not after |

### 6.3 One objection I think fails

> "Unrestricted aliasing means a write through a stale pointer with no
> warning."

It does not. A stale pointer is a pointer to `Gone` storage, and every access
through it is refused at compile time by the same single fact that refuses
every other path to that storage (P2's `old`, P3's `q`, P4's post-`free`
read, P7's final read). What unrestricted aliasing loses is *facts about
contents*, never *state*. The catalog's phrasing describes C, where there is no
per-storage state; it does not describe this tuple, where the state is the
whole mechanism.


# File: candidate-brand-tokens.md

# Candidate core model: `brand-tokens`

Research date: 2026-09-16. One coherent choice for D1, D2, D3 and D4 of
[OPTIONS.md](../../whitefoot-access-effects-research/research/investigations/access-effects/OPTIONS.md),
derived against the requirement list of VERDICT-D0 §2, the couplings of §4, the
hazard ladder of MECHANISM-MAP §3 and the discriminating programs P1–P19.
Nothing here is selected; this file builds the strongest form of one tuple.

---

## 1. The tuple

| Point | Family (OPTIONS.md name) | Members drawn on | What this candidate takes from them |
|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | **Allocation-scoped location name in the type** | THE-D1-02 (copyable name, linear capability) as the flagship; AI-D1-01 (`'a` per allocation) for spelling; THE-D1-04 (nominal atom with freshness `a # b`) for minting and retirement; THE-D1-01 (abstract location in a store typing); HIS-D1-04, HIS-D1-05 (WF's own `ptr<'a,T>` float); HIS-D1-14 (finite static origin set) for returned pointers | A pointer's type names one location. The name is a **term**, not only an atom: `ℓ ::= a | slot(ℓ, i, g) | backing(ℓ)`. Atoms are minted fresh at allocation and **retired** at ending; they are never reused. |
| D2 | **Explicit ghost linear tokens and guards**, combined with **Tokens with implicit flow or elided sugar** for the common case | SYS-D2-03, THE-D2-02, AI-D2-02 (explicit erased linear ghost tokens); RAD-D2-15 (split: pointer plus ghost token); HIS-D2-05 (Verus `Tracked<PointsTo>`); HIS-D2-07 (FocusKey linear closing key) for `Deed`; SYS-D2-07 (guard restores on drop) for the `share` construct. Hybrid: AI-D2-03 (sugar eliding the thread), AI-D2-07 (facts by default, tokens opt-in) | All permission and all state live in an erased linear ghost value keyed by a location and an extent. The pointer carries nothing. The token argument is **elided** wherever exactly one token of the required type is in scope; the desugaring is printable and deterministic. |
| D3 | **Quantitative state: fractions, counts, grades**, combined with **Three-state minimum** and the extent axis of **Partial initialization at field, range or byte granularity** | THE-D3-15 (counting permissions) as the share axis, in its structured subset; THE-D3-14 (fractional) refused as the free-arithmetic form; AI-D3-01, THE-D3-01, SYS-D3-01, HIS-D3-05 (Init/Uninit/Gone); AI-D3-02 (`PartiallyInit(range)`), THE-D3-02 (Cogent take/put slot state) for the extent; AI-D3-04 / SYS-D3-13 (occupant generation) **as a ghost term only** | The token carries `⟨extent, share, init⟩`. `Gone` is not a state: it is the **absence of any token** plus a retired atom. |
| D4 | **Permission accounting** | THE-D4-15 (counting permissions) in the structured share-tree form; THE-D4-14 (fractional) refused; HIS-D4-12/HIS-D4-13 (overlap by resolved paths, proved half-open extents) absorbed as the extent algebra's disjointness judgment | Any number of copyable pointers to one storage is legal. A write needs the whole (`W`) token for the extent written; a read needs any share. Holding `W` **is** the exclusivity fact, because the algebra cannot produce two overlapping `W` tokens. |

### Why the four cohere

| Coupling | How the tuple closes it |
|---|---|
| C12 (per-storage state is primary) | The token is keyed by `ℓ▷e`, never by a pointer. D2's carrier and D3's vocabulary are the same object. |
| C1 (identity granularity: allocation, field, element, range) | D1 gives the *name*; D3's extent gives the *refinement below the name*. One vocabulary serves state, distinctness, footprints and kills, because all four read the same token. |
| C2 (one distinctness relation, two exactness directions) | R4 and R5 read the **same** token multiset. R4 tolerates a missing token (fewer facts, slower); R5's erasable constructs fall back to sequential, its non-erasable ones reject. Nothing is stated twice. |
| C5 (sequential aliased writes allowed) | D4's policy is not a rule about references; it is arithmetic on tokens, so aliased pointers cost nothing and aliased *permission* is unrepresentable. |
| C7 (the storage-ending set) | Every ending event is one rule: consume the token, consume the carve receipt, retire the atom. The set is complete because there is exactly one way to end storage. |
| C6 (state as a term over captured conditions) | **Not needed.** Linearity replaces path sensitivity: a join matches token multisets up to existential packing, with no condition atoms and no lattice. This is the single largest simplification the tuple buys. |

---

## 2. The model

### 2.1 Vocabulary

```text
ℓ  ::= a                     -- fresh atom, minted at allocation, retired at ending
     | backing(ℓ)            -- a container's element storage
     | slot(ℓ, i, g)         -- pool slot i, ghost generation g

e  ::= ·                     -- the whole location
     | e.f | e[n] | e[lo..hi) | e ⊖ e
                             -- closed extent grammar, fixed normalizer,
                             -- decidable disjointness and coverage over a
                             -- linear index fragment

q  ::= W | R                 -- whole (read+write) share | read share
s  ::= U | I                 -- uninitialized | initialized

ptr<ℓ, T>                    -- copy class; a machine pointer; carries no permission
Pt<ℓ▷e, q, s>                -- ghost, LINEAR; the permission and the state
Deed<ℓ▷e ⇒ ℓ'>               -- ghost, LINEAR; the carve receipt (release obligation)
In(ℓ' ⊑ ℓ▷e)                 -- ghost, COPY; a containment fact
Gone(ℓ)                      -- ghost, COPY; retirement, for diagnostics only
```

### 2.2 What a pointer's type says

`ptr<ℓ,T>` says **which storage** and **what shape**. It says nothing about
validity, initialization, exclusivity, duration, or who else points there. It
is freely copyable, storable in a struct, and returnable. It is the only part
that survives lowering.

### 2.3 What the checker holds per storage

A **multiset of tokens**. Nothing else. There is no per-identity state table,
no lattice, no flow-sensitive map. The judgment at a program point is
"does the context contain a token of the required type".

### 2.4 The rules

```text
T-READ    p:ptr<ℓ,T>, Pt<ℓ▷e,q,I>   ⊢  read(p) : T   ⊗ Pt<ℓ▷e,q,I>   -- token RETURNED UNCHANGED
T-WRITE   p:ptr<ℓ,T>, Pt<ℓ▷e,W,_>   ⊢  write(p,v)    ⊗ Pt<ℓ▷e,W,I>
T-TAKE    Pt<ℓ▷e,W,I>               ⊢  take(p) : T   ⊗ Pt<ℓ▷e,W,U>
T-PUT     Pt<ℓ▷e,W,U> ⊗ v           ⊢  put(p,v)      ⊗ Pt<ℓ▷e,W,I>
T-REPL    Pt<ℓ▷e,W,I> ⊗ v           ⊢  replace(p,v):T ⊗ Pt<ℓ▷e,W,I>

R-REFINE  Pt<ℓ▷e,q,s>  ⟺  Pt<ℓ▷e1,q,s1> ⊗ Pt<ℓ▷e2,q,s2>
                                    side condition: e = e1 ⊎ e2, disjoint and covering
R-CARVE   Pt<ℓ▷e,W,_>  ⟺  Pt<ℓ'▷·,W,U> ⊗ Deed<ℓ▷e ⇒ ℓ'> ⊗ In(ℓ' ⊑ ℓ▷e)    ℓ' fresh
R-RETIRE  Pt<ℓ'▷·,W,_> ⊗ Deed<ℓ▷e ⇒ ℓ'>  ⊢  Pt<ℓ▷e,W,U> ⊗ Gone(ℓ')
                                    ℓ' is retired: no rule ever produces a token for it again
```

`R-SHARE` is **not a free rule** — free counting needs arithmetic the checker
would have to search for. It is one structured construct whose arity is
syntactic:

```text
share t { arm1 | ... | armk }     -- consumes Pt<ℓ▷e,q,I>; binds Pt<ℓ▷e,R,I> in each arm;
                                  -- restores the original token at the construct's end;
                                  -- no arm may write, take from, carve or end ℓ▷e
share t over i in lo..hi { ... }  -- one share per iteration; restored at loop exit
```

### 2.5 The read objection, answered

> "A single linear token makes every read serialize."

Three facts, in order of force:

1. **A read is not a flow edge.** `T-READ` returns the token it was given,
   syntactically unchanged. The context before the read and after it are the
   same multiset, so the checker records no dependency and the writer is never
   forced to rebind. Serialization would come from the token *changing*; it
   does not.
2. **Sequential reads need no share at all.** One token — `W` or `R` — serves
   every read on every path. The `share` construct exists only where two
   *contexts* need the token simultaneously: parallel arms, a call wanting two
   read tokens for one extent, a closure capture.
3. **At a parallel construct the split is derived, never written.** The
   checker refines `W` tokens by the arms' written footprints (`R-REFINE`) and
   opens `share` for the read-only intersection, in one pass over the arms.
   A failed derivation leaves the construct sequential (M5), it never rejects.

The cost lands where the hazard is: on **writes**, which must serialize
because two simultaneous writes to one extent is the hazard R1 and R5 exist to
refuse.

### 2.6 State changes

| Event | Rule | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `take(p)` | T-TAKE | `I → U`; the hole is on the storage, visible through every pointer to `ℓ` |
| `put(p,v)` | T-PUT | `U → I`; any alias may fill the hole |
| `replace(p,v)` | T-REPL | `I → I`, old value returned |
| `move` of the storage | R-RETIRE then R-CARVE at the destination | old `ℓ` retired; fresh `ℓ'` |
| `free(ℓ')` | R-RETIRE against the allocator's deed | `ℓ'` retired forever; the parent extent returns `U` |
| `realloc` / reallocating `push` | R-RETIRE ⊗ R-CARVE in one contract | `backing(ℓv)` retired, fresh `backing(ℓv)` minted |
| pool slot recycle | R-RETIRE on `slot(ℓP,i,g)`, R-CARVE as `slot(ℓP,i,g+1)` | ghost generation bumped; **no runtime compare** |
| scope exit | the context must be empty of tokens whose deeds are unreturned | a leaked `Deed` is R2's diagnostic |

### 2.7 Joins and loop heads

```text
JOIN      Γ1 ▷ join ◁ Γ2   accept iff  Γ1 ≡ Γ2  as multisets, up to
                           existential packing:  ∃ℓ. (ptr<ℓ,T> ⊗ Pt<ℓ▷·,q,s>)
LOOP      the token multiset at the head must equal the multiset on every back
          edge, up to existential packing. This is an EQUALITY CHECK against a
          multiset derived from the entry context — one pass, no fixpoint, no
          lattice height, no widening.
```

There are **no condition terms** (`ite(c, Init, Uninit)`), no drop flags, no
Top. Where two arms genuinely end different storage, the writer packs an
existential; that is the one join the writer writes.

### 2.8 What a signature states

A signature is a **store-typing rewrite**: the token multiset in, the token
multiset out.

```text
fn drain<ℓx>(x: ptr<ℓx,T>, t: Pt<ℓx▷·,W,I>) -> (T, Pt<ℓx▷·,W,U>)
fn reserve<ℓv>(v: ptr<ℓv,Vec>, tv: Pt<ℓv▷·,W,I>, tb: Pt<backing(ℓv)▷·,W,I>, m: u64)
    -> (Pt<ℓv▷·,W,I>, ∃ℓ'. Pt<ℓ'▷·,W,I> ⊗ Eq(backing(ℓv), ℓ'))     -- old backing retired
fn helper<ℓ>(p: ptr<ℓ,u8>, t: Pt<ℓ▷[0..s),W,U>, inp: ptr<ℓi,Buf>, ti: Pt<ℓi▷·,R,I>)
    -> (Pt<ℓ▷[0..s),W,I>, Pt<ℓi▷·,R,I>)                            -- writes its slice only
```

Entry states, exit states, ended storage, replaced backings, fresh
allocations, read and write footprints, and returned interior pointers are all
**one vocabulary**: the token type. R7's list needs no second notation.

### 2.9 What the writer writes, and where

| Site | What is written | Typical count |
|---|---|---|
| signature | one location parameter per storage named; one token clause in, one out | 2 lines per touched storage |
| loop head | the loop's token multiset, **only when the body changes it** | 0 for P5, P6, every read-only loop |
| join | an existential pack, **only when the arms end different storage** | 0 where the arms agree |
| per statement — read | **nothing** (token unchanged; argument elided) | 0 |
| per statement — write through a held token | **nothing** | 0 |
| per statement — splitting a storage | one `refine` or `carve` line plus its disjointness proof | 1 per split |
| per statement — symbolic element access | the index fact (`i < len`, `k ≠ i ∧ k ≠ j`) | 1, shared with R11 |

### 2.10 What is erased

Everything except `ptr<ℓ,T>` reduced to a machine pointer and ordinary data:
all tokens, deeds, containment and retirement facts, extents, shares, location
terms, ghost generations, packs, unpacks, `share` constructs and written `use`
steps. Lowering sees pointers and data. M6(iii) holds by construction: no rule
of the operational semantics mentions a token.

---

## 3. Derivations

Notation: `Γ` is the token multiset. Comments name the fact used.

### P1 Container split with a runtime index

```text
v: vec<u64>, len n;  ℓb = backing(ℓv)
Γ = { Pt<ℓb▷[0..n),W,I> }
(part_i, part_j) = split(v, i, j)
  // R-REFINE twice; side conditions i<n, j<n, i≠j
  // accept: Γ = { Pt<ℓb▷[i],W,I>, Pt<ℓb▷[j],W,I>, Pt<ℓb▷[0..n)⊖[i]⊖[j],W,I> }
write(part_i, x)                 // accept: T-WRITE with Pt<ℓb▷[i],W,_>
write(part_j, y)                 // accept: T-WRITE with Pt<ℓb▷[j],W,_>
par { write(part_i,x) | write(part_j,y) }
                                 // accept (R5 i): footprints {ℓb▷[i]} and {ℓb▷[j]};
                                 //   disjoint by the extent judgment; no runtime check
read(v[k]), k runtime
  // needs Pt<ℓb▷[k],R,I>; the only candidate source is Pt<ℓb▷[0..n)⊖[i]⊖[j]>
  // R-REFINE side condition: [k] ⊑ [0..n)⊖[i]⊖[j]  ==  k<n ∧ k≠i ∧ k≠j
  // reject unless proved.  Diagnostic payload: "missing k ≠ i ∧ k ≠ j"
if k != i && k != j { read(v[k]) } // accept: the writer's own branch (M2 ii);
                                   //   the fact is discharged in the then-arm
put_back(part_i, part_j)         // accept: R-REFINE inverse; Γ = { Pt<ℓb▷[0..n),W,I> }
push(v, x)                       // accept ONLY here: needs Pt<ℓb▷·,W,I> whole
push(v, x)  // before put_back    // reject: no whole-extent token; names the two
                                  //   outstanding element tokens and their binders
```
**Verdict: accepted as required.** The diagnostic's missing fact is literally
the side condition of `R-REFINE`; no mechanism outside D1–D4 is used.

### P2 Arena with independently released blocks

```text
arena A: metadata at ℓM, byte storage at ℓS      // two locations, per P2's own text
Γ = { Pt<ℓM▷·,W,I>, Pt<ℓS▷·,W,U> }
b1 = alloc(A, 64)
  // contract: consumes Pt<ℓM▷·,W,I> ⊗ Pt<ℓS▷[o..o+64),W,U>
  //           returns  Pt<ℓM▷·,W,I> ⊗ ∃ℓ1. (ptr<ℓ1,[u8;64]> ⊗ Pt<ℓ1▷·,W,U>
  //                                          ⊗ Deed<ℓS▷[o..o+64) ⇒ ℓ1>)
  // accept: R-CARVE; ℓ1 fresh.  Metadata written at alloc only (R2 e)
b2 = alloc(A, 64); b3 = alloc(A, 64)             // accept: ℓ2, ℓ3 fresh; extents bump-disjoint
par { fill(b1) | fill(b2) | fill(b3) }
  // accept (R5 i): footprints {ℓ1▷·}, {ℓ2▷·}, {ℓ3▷·}; disjoint because
  //   In(ℓ1 ⊑ ℓS▷[o1..]), In(ℓ2 ⊑ ℓS▷[o2..]) with the extents proved disjoint.
  //   NOT by inequality of the names ℓ1, ℓ2  (R4 b)
  // nobody holds A exclusively: Pt<ℓM> is idle and ℓM ∦ ℓ1..ℓ3
distinct(ℓS, b1)?                // REJECT the claim: In(ℓ1 ⊑ ℓS▷[o1..o1+64)) is a
                                 //   containment, so no distinctness is derivable.
                                 //   P2's negative test passes (R4 e)
free(A, b2)
  // accept: R-RETIRE consumes Pt<ℓ2▷·,W,_> ⊗ Deed<ℓS▷[o2..] ⇒ ℓ2>;
  //         ℓ2 RETIRED; Pt<ℓS▷[o2..o2+64),W,U> returns to the arena
b4 = alloc(A, 32)                // accept: R-CARVE mints ℓ4 (fresh) over [o2..o2+32)
read(p_into_b2)                  // reject: p_into_b2 : ptr<ℓ2,_>; no rule produces
                                 //   Pt<ℓ2▷_,_,_>; Gone(ℓ2) names the free at its line.
                                 //   Address reuse by ℓ4 is irrelevant: ℓ4 ≠ ℓ2 as TYPES
read(b1); free(A,b1); free(A,b3); free(A,b4)
                                 // accept: four R-RETIREs, four deeds, no double free;
                                 //   scope exit finds Γ = { Pt<ℓM>, Pt<ℓS▷·,W,U> }
```
**Verdict: accepted as required.** The address-reuse case is refused at the
type level, before any state is consulted.

### P3 Graph with back edges in a pool

```text
pool P at ℓP;  node i lives at slot(ℓP, i, g_i)   // g_i is a GHOST generation term
struct Node { next: (k: idx, g: ghost nat), prev: (k: idx, g: ghost nat), data: u64 }
invariant Live(P): ∀ stored link (k,g) in P . g = gen(P,k) ∧ occupied(P,k)
                   // stated ONCE on the pool (R6 e)

insert n between a and b:
  write((node a).next, (n, gen(P,n)))   // accept: Pt<slot(ℓP,a,ga)▷.next,W,I>
  write((node n).prev, (a, gen(P,a)))   // accept: distinct extent of a distinct slot
  write((node n).next, (b, gen(P,b)))   // accept
  write((node b).prev, (n, gen(P,n)))   // accept: several PATHS to node n are fine —
                                        //   pointers are copy class; only the token
                                        //   for the written extent is required (R9 e)
remove m:
  // accept: R-RETIRE on slot(ℓP,m,g_m); the slot extent returns to the pool
  // Live(P) is now FALSE at any link still naming (m, g_m)
  // the writer must relink first, or re-establish Live(P) with a written `use` step
read((node a).next) then deref
  // needs Pt<slot(ℓP,k,g)▷.data,R,I> for the STORED (k,g).
  // accept iff Live(P) gives g = gen(P,k); after a removal, one `use` step per
  //   traversal re-establishes it from the relink
  // reject after `remove m` with no relink: names "stored generation g_m ≠ gen(P,m)"
par map over all nodes { write((node i).data, f(i)) }
  // accept (R5 i): footprints slot(ℓP,i,g_i)▷.data for distinct i;
```
