```text
  //   disjoint by index disjointness of the slot extents
reuse of m's storage for a later insert
  // accept: R-CARVE mints slot(ℓP,m,g_m+1); every path to the old occupant names
  //   g_m and is refused by Live(P)  (R1 ii)
```
**Verdict: accepted with a stated cost.** The cost is one written pool
invariant plus one `use` step per traversal step across a removal; the
alternative — a per-node location atom stored in a homogeneous `next` field —
needs an existential whose unpacked name cannot be matched against a held
token, which is why the location *term* `slot(ℓP,i,g)` is in D1.

### P4 Cursor over a growing vector

```text
c = Cursor { at: ptr<ℓv,Vec>, i: 0 }   // a POINTER in a struct; no token stored
a = c.read()
  // needs Pt<ℓv▷·,R,I> (len, backing ptr) and Pt<backing(ℓv)▷[0],R,I>
  // accept: both supplied by the caller's context; i=0 < len
push(v, 5)        // the reallocating operation
  // contract: consumes Pt<backing(ℓv)▷·,W,I>; RETIRES it; returns a fresh backing
b = c.read()      // reject: c.at is fine, but the extent needed is
                  //   backing(ℓv)▷[0] under the NEW backing atom while the proof
                  //   the writer holds names the old one. Diagnostic: R1(ii),
                  //   naming push's `ensures` clause as the ending event
if len(v) < cap(v) { push_within(v, 5) } else { reserve(v, 2*cap); push_within(v,5) }
  // push_within: requires len < cap; ensures backing(ℓv) UNCHANGED
b = c.read()      // accept in the then-arm: the backing atom never changed; the
                  //   element token survives; the writer's own branch carried it
free(v); c.read() // reject forever: ℓv and backing(ℓv) retired; no token obtainable
```
**Verdict: accepted with a stated cost.** The cost is that a *conditional*
reallocation contract is not expressible (the join rule admits no condition
terms), so the one operation splits into two — `push` (ends the backing) and
`push_within` (requires headroom) — and the writer writes the branch. This
matches R8a's recorded red status for conditional reallocation contracts, and
it keeps M2(ii): the branch is the writer's, not the lowering's.

### P5 Struct-of-arrays kernel

```text
struct Cols<ℓa..ℓh> { a: ptr<ℓa,buf>, ..., h: ptr<ℓh,buf> }
fn kernel<ℓa..ℓh>(c: Cols<ℓa..ℓh>,
                  ta: Pt<ℓa▷[0..n),W,I>, tb: Pt<ℓb▷[0..n),W,I>,
                  tc..th: Pt<ℓ_▷[0..n),R,I>) -> (same)
for i in 0..n {
  a[i] = f(a[i], c[i], d[i])
    // accept: write needs Pt<ℓa▷[i],W,_>, derived from ta by R-REFINE at [i];
    //         reads need R shares of ℓc▷[i], ℓd▷[i]
  b[i] = g(b[i], e[i], f[i], g[i], h[i])
    // accept: write Pt<ℓb▷[i],W,_>; reads on ℓe..ℓh
}
// PAR-2 overlap of iterations i ≠ j:
//   write footprints {ℓa▷[i], ℓb▷[i]} vs {ℓa▷[j], ℓb▷[j]} — disjoint by i≠j
//   read footprints share ℓc..ℓh — read/read never interferes
//   accept: the per-iteration refine and the `share ... over i` are DERIVED from
//           the written signature footprints; the writer wrote no split
// R4 per-load fact: every load carries its token's extent ℓx▷[i]; the eight
//   columns are pairwise non-containing atoms, so a per-load distinctness fact
//   exists for every pair — the strongest per-load channel any D1 family offers
```
**Verdict: accepted as required.** The obvious shape is the accepted shape:
the loop body is unannotated and the signature costs one clause per column,
which is R15's metric (parameters ≤ storages touched).

### P6 Range partition helper

```text
out: ptr<ℓo,[u8;n]>, t: Pt<ℓo▷[0..n),W,U>;  k workers, s = n/k
fn helper<ℓ>(p: ptr<ℓ,u8>, t: Pt<ℓ▷[0..s),W,U>,
             inp: ptr<ℓi,Buf>, ti: Pt<ℓi▷·,R,I>) -> (Pt<ℓ▷[0..s),W,I>, Pt<ℓi▷·,R,I>)
  // the signature ALONE says: writes exactly [0..s) of ℓ; reads ℓi; ends nothing
share ti over w in 0..k {
  for w in 0..k { helper(slice_of(out, w*s..(w+1)*s), refine(t, [w*s..(w+1)*s)), input, ti_w) }
    // accept: R-REFINE k ways; side condition is pairwise disjointness of
    //   [w*s..(w+1)*s) for w ≠ w', which is  w<w' ⟹ (w+1)*s ≤ w'*s  —
    //   inside the linear index fragment, discharged by the fixed normalizer
    // accept overlap (R5 i): write footprints pairwise disjoint; the read on
    //   `input` is a share, and read/read does not interfere
}
// the `share` over w and the k-way refine are DERIVED at the PAR-2 loop from the
// written footprints; the writer wrote k and the range arithmetic and nothing else
```
**Verdict: accepted as required.** No worker count beyond `k`; the caller
judges from the helper's signature alone (R7 e).

### P7 Take, put, replace through aliases

```text
p, q : ptr<ℓA, T>          // both copy class, both legal, no judgment at the copy
Γ = { Pt<ℓA▷·,W,I> }
v = take(p)                // accept: T-TAKE.  Γ = { Pt<ℓA▷·,W,U> }
read(q)                    // reject: T-READ needs s = I; the token says U.
                           //   The hole is on ℓA, so it is visible through q.
                           //   Diagnostic: R1(i), naming take(p)'s line
put(q, move v)             // accept: T-PUT through the OTHER alias; Γ = { Pt<ℓA▷·,W,I> }
read(p)                    // accept: T-READ; the fill through q restored p's read
old = replace(p, new)      // accept: T-REPL, I → I, returns the old value
read(q)                    // accept: reads `new` — one storage, one token, one state
free ℓA                    // accept: R-RETIRE; ℓA retired
read(p)                    // reject forever: no rule produces Pt<ℓA▷_,_,_>
```
**Verdict: accepted as required.** P7 is the row R1 uses to test "state is a
property of the storage, never of the pointer"; under this tuple the property
is structural — the token's index is `ℓ`, and no pointer appears in it.

### P8 Conditional release and loop exits

```text
Γ = { Pt<ℓa▷·,W,I> ⊗ Deed_a, Pt<ℓb▷·,W,I> ⊗ Deed_b }
let s = if c { free(a); pack(b, tb) } else { free(b); pack(a, ta) }
  // then-arm:  Γ1 = { ∃ℓ.(ptr<ℓ,T> ⊗ Pt<ℓ▷·,W,I> ⊗ Deed) }, Gone(ℓa)
  // else-arm:  Γ2 = { ∃ℓ.(ptr<ℓ,T> ⊗ Pt<ℓ▷·,W,I> ⊗ Deed) }, Gone(ℓb)
  // accept at the join: Γ1 ≡ Γ2 as multisets up to the existential.
  //   Gone facts are COPY and diagnostic-only; dropping them is sound because
  //   no rule ever CONSUMES a Gone fact to produce a token.
  //   NO drop flag, NO condition term, NO lattice Top  (M2 ii)
use(s)                     // accept: unpack gives a fresh opaque ℓ and its token
free(s)                    // accept: R-RETIRE on the unpacked ℓ; obligation discharged
let s = if c { free(a); b } else { free(b); a }   // without the pack
  // reject: Γ1 = { Pt<ℓb..> } ≢ Γ2 = { Pt<ℓa..> }.
  //   Diagnostic is a MULTISET DIFF naming the path and the differing token type:
  //   "on the `else` path this binding carries Pt<ℓa▷·,W,I>, on `then` Pt<ℓb▷·,W,I>;
  //    pack an existential at the join"  (M7: local, non-empty, names the path)

loop { if stop { break }; take(p); ...; put(p) }
  // head requires Pt<ℓp▷·,W,I>; body: I → U → I; back edge carries I: accept
  // loop-head check is an EQUALITY against the entry multiset: one pass, no fixpoint
free(p)                    // accept: the break edge carries Pt<ℓp▷·,W,I>
loop { if stop { break }; take(p); if bad { break }; put(p) }
  // reject: the second break edge carries U, the head requires I.
  //   Diagnostic names THAT break edge — "the path whose state differs"
```
**Verdict: accepted as required.** No runtime drop flag exists because nothing
in the lowering reads a token.

### P9 A callee that changes storage state

```text
fn drain<ℓx>(x: ptr<ℓx,T>, t: Pt<ℓx▷·,W,I>) -> (T, Pt<ℓx▷·,W,U>)
  // the hole is IN THE SIGNATURE; caller judges from it alone; body checked once
fn reserve<ℓv>(v: ptr<ℓv,Vec>, tv: Pt<ℓv▷·,W,I>, tb: Pt<backing(ℓv)▷·,W,I>, m: u64)
     -> (Pt<ℓv▷·,W,I>, ∃ℓ'. Pt<ℓ'▷·,W,I> ⊗ Eq(backing(ℓv), ℓ'))
  // the backing REPLACEMENT is in the signature; the old atom is retired
fn pick<ℓx,ℓy>(c: bool, x: ptr<ℓx,T>, y: ptr<ℓy,T>) -> ∃ℓ ∈ {ℓx, ℓy}. ptr<ℓ,T>
  // a FINITE origin set computed from the signature alone (HIS-D1-14)
caller:
  let r = pick(c, x, y)
  match origin(r) {                      // a GHOST match, two arms, erased
    ℓx => write(r, 1) with tx            // accept: T-WRITE with Pt<ℓx▷·,W,_>
    ℓy => write(r, 1) with ty            // accept: T-WRITE with Pt<ℓy▷·,W,_>
  }
  write(r, 1) without the match
  // reject: no token is typed at the existential ℓ.
  //   Diagnostic: "the result's origin is {ℓx, ℓy}; match on it to select a token"
```
**Verdict: accepted with a stated cost.** The cost is a two-arm erased ghost
match at the caller when a call returns a pointer with a non-singleton origin
set. R7's three clauses (`drain`, `reserve`, `pick`) are all in one vocabulary.

### P11 Write-once-then-frozen cache

```text
cache at ℓc, slot per key; occupancy as ORDINARY DATA (Option), not checker state
get(k):
  if is_none(cache[k]) { cache[k] = compute(k) }   // needs Pt<ℓc▷[k],W,I>
  return read(cache[k])                            // needs Pt<ℓc▷[k],R,I>
// SEQUENTIAL, one holder:
//   accept: one Pt<ℓc▷·,W,I>; the refine to [k] needs k < cap; the branch is the
//   writer's and reads the Option, not a compiler state  (M2 ii)
// A READER HOLDING A POINTER ACROSS ANOTHER SLOT'S FILL:
//   reader holds Pt<ℓc▷[k1],R,I>; fill of [k2] needs Pt<ℓc▷[k2],W,_>
//   accept: R-REFINE separates them; the reader's fact SURVIVES the fill exactly,
//   because the fill's footprint does not name [k1]  (R6 metric: 0 facts killed)
// MANY READERS, ONE LAZY WRITER PER SLOT:
//   reject: a reader holding R on [k] cannot upgrade to W; `share` forbids its
//   arms to write the shared extent. There is no rule from n readers to one writer.
```
**Verdict: rejected for the many-readers-one-lazy-writer shape; accepted
sequentially. The requirement is not at fault and the candidate is not wrong —
the shape needs a mechanism from D10** ("Protocol-governed shared regions and
ghost state", or "Single-writer publish protocols as constructs"). Under R1
alone the write-once transition is expressible and costs nothing; the
admission question is a capability question, exactly as why-whitefoot §5 frames
it.

### P13 Relocation by a compacting third party

```text
h = handle(i);  p = pointer_of(h) : ptr<slot(ℓP,i,g), Node>
pool.compact()
  // contract: requires Pt<ℓP▷·,W,I> WHOLE — i.e. every carved slot token and deed
  //           has been returned; ensures ∀j. gen(P,j) = old gen +1, with a ghost
  //           relocation map Fixup : {old slot ↦ new slot}
  // accept: the whole-extent requirement is exactly R8a's price — the compiler may
  //   not relocate while an interior token is outstanding, and the CHECKER enforces
  //   it, so no analysis is needed
read(p)
  // reject: p : ptr<slot(ℓP,i,g),_>; the current generation is g+1; no token of
  //   that type exists. Diagnostic: R1(ii)/R8a, naming compact() as the event
read(pool[h])
  // accept: the handle is ORDINARY DATA; pool[h] re-derives
  //   ptr<slot(ℓP, Fixup(h), g+1), Node> together with its token from Pt<ℓP▷·>
p2 = fixup(Fixup, p)
  // accept: the CONTRACT-VISIBLE fixup form — a ghost function on location terms,
  //   erased; no runtime compare, no generational check  (M2 ii)
```
**Verdict: accepted as required.** The mutual exclusion R8a demands
(interior pointers vs third-party relocation) is enforced by the token algebra
rather than by a separate rule, and the fixup form is contract-visible.

### P16 Abstraction over identities

```text
fn map_nodes<ℓP, T>(g: ptr<ℓP,Pool<T>>, t: Pt<ℓP▷·,W,I>, f: fn(&T)->T) -> Pt<ℓP▷·,W,I>
  // accept: ONE location parameter and ONE token for the whole pool; the parallel
  //   map's per-slot refine is derived inside the body. Parameters: 2, storages: 1

fn kernel<ℓa..ℓh, E>(c: Cols<ℓa..ℓh, E>, ta..th: Pt<ℓ_▷[0..n),_,I>) -> (same)
  // accept: 8 location parameters + 8 token clauses for 8 storages.
  //   R15 metric (parameters ≤ f(storages touched)) met at 2 per storage
  // if the columns are INLINE in the struct, one token and eight field extents: 2 total

let h = |slice, t| helper(slice, t, input, ti)
  // h : ∀ℓ. (ptr<ℓ,u8>, Pt<ℓ▷[0..s),W,U>) -> Pt<ℓ▷[0..s),W,I>
  //     capturing Pt<ℓi▷·,R,I>
  // accept: the closure is LOCATION-POLYMORPHIC; the captured read share is
  //   reproduced per call by the enclosing `share ... over w`
  // cost: closure types carry location quantifiers and a capture clause

fn pick<N: Nominal>(c: bool, x: N, y: N) -> N
  // accept only when N's location parameters are exposed: N = Ref<ℓ>; the result
  //   carries the origin set {ℓx, ℓy} and the caller writes the ghost match (P9)
  // reject if N is opaque in its locations: "the nominal hides the location
  //   parameter the result's origin set needs"
```
**Verdict: accepted with a stated cost.** The cost is location and permission
polymorphism on signatures and closure types, and the requirement that a
nominal expose the location parameters of any storage its values name. This is
the known price of D1's chosen family, and it is the candidate's largest open
risk (see §6).

### P17 Partial operations

```text
q = a / d                  // reject: domain d ≠ 0 undischarged.
                           //   Diagnostic names "d ≠ 0"  (R11, M7)
invariant { use d_nonzero } ; q = a / d       // accept: written finite step
match checked_div(a,d) { Ok(q) => .. | DivZero => .. }   // accept: written outcome (R12)

b: u8 = narrow(x)          // reject: "x < 256"
if x < 256 { b = narrow(x) }                  // accept: the writer's branch

y = v[i]
  // TWO obligations collapse into ONE: R-REFINE needs [i] ⊑ [0..len) to produce
  //   Pt<backing(ℓv)▷[i],R,I>, which is exactly R11's index domain i < len.
  // reject without the fact: "i < len(v)" named once
if i < len(v) { y = v[i] }                    // accept
```
**Verdict: accepted as required.** The tuple contributes a real economy: the
index proof the token refine already demands discharges R11's domain, so the
element access pays once.

---

## 4. Requirements

### 4.1 Row by row

| Row | Verdict | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| R1 | **met** | (i) hole = token state `U`; (ii) ended = no producible token plus a retired atom, so address reuse cannot revive an identity (P2); (iii) stale layout = a layout change carves a fresh atom. The diagnostic names which sub-property failed because the three have different failure sites (state field, absent token, wrong atom). |
| R2 | **met** | Every allocation yields a linear `Deed` that only `R-RETIRE` consumes; joins match multisets on every path including outcome arms; scope exit rejects a leaked deed. Release decisions are static because no lowered value is read to select one. |
| R3 | **met** | Pointers are copy; tokens and deeds are linear; values are affine or linear as today. `take`/`put`/`replace` are exactly `T-TAKE`/`T-PUT`/`T-REPL` on the storage's token, so "used twice" (a consumed token reused) and "never released" (a deed at scope exit) are two different diagnostics. |
| R4 | **met** | The token multiset *is* the fact set: holding `Pt<ℓ▷e,W,_>` licenses "no other access to `ℓ▷e` exists at this point", per load, per span. Distinctness is proved over the containment structure (`In` facts and extent disjointness), never by name inequality — P2's `S` vs `b1` is correctly non-distinct. A missing token costs speed only. Status stays unmeasurable until a channel exists (MAP §8 Q15). |
| R5 | **partial** | Ground (i) is met exactly and cheaply (P1, P2, P3, P5, P6). Ground (iii) is met (a level names the construct, not the tokens). Ground (ii) — a recombinable accumulator under a checked law — has no rule in the algebra: it needs an accumulator share `Acc<ℓ▷e,⊕>` whose recombination is licensed by a law, which is a **D5** mechanism ("Declared reductions and deterministic merge"), not a token rule. |
| R6 | **met** — the candidate's strongest row | The frame is exact **by construction**: a call can falsify only facts about extents whose tokens it received. No kill rule exists, so there is nothing to under- or over-kill. The measured ENT-5 tax (34 of 41 `len()` rebinds caused by whole-parameter footprints) disappears: a call that receives `Pt<backing(ℓv)▷[i],W,_>` cannot touch `ℓv`'s length. |
| R7 | **met** | The signature is a store-typing rewrite; entry/exit states, ended storage, replaced backings, fresh allocations, footprints, returned interior pointers and origin sets are one vocabulary. A declaration whose entry context is unsatisfiable (two `W` tokens over overlapping extents) is rejected at the declaration. |
| R8a | **met** | Every ending event is one rule (`R-RETIRE`), so the set is complete by construction and contract-visible by the signature. The price R8a names — no relocation while an interior pointer's token is outstanding — is enforced, not assumed (P13). The fixup form is the generation term plus handle re-derivation. |
| R8b | **partial** | The candidate neither supplies nor obstructs a placement-demand vocabulary; layout *currency* is R1(iii), which the carve rule covers, but alignment, field order, address spaces and the marked erasing store are orthogonal additions. |
| R9 | **partial** | Sequentially met, and the negative test passes: P3's four link writes through several paths are accepted, and unlike an exclusivity rule no fact is lost, because coinciding permission is unrepresentable rather than tolerated. The concurrent half waits on the thread trigger. The honest cost: the *permission* must be routed to whichever holder writes, which is structural (through signatures) but real. |
| R10 | **met** | An external resource is a location with a token; a descriptor is three identities — the close-obligation wrapper (a `Deed`), the open-file description (a location with a cursor extent), and the contents (a foreign-class location whose token carries no contents fact). No acceptance rule mentions host crossing. Provisional until P14 is derived. |
| R11 | **met** | Orthogonal to the tuple, and the tuple pays part of it: the index fact a symbolic element access needs for `R-REFINE` is the same fact R11's index domain needs (P17). |
| R12 | **met** | Every outcome arm must present the same token multiset up to existential packing, so R2's obligations discharge per arm by the same rule joins use. Arm count multiplies the contexts to match; charged to M10 per C15. |
| R13 | **partial** | Opt-in budgets are orthogonal, but the tuple offers an accounting hook: the arena's outstanding byte budget is the sum of live deed extents, checkable in the extent fragment. Depth counts and termination measures are not token facts. |
| R14 | **partial** | (iii) and (iv) fall out: a non-program actor's rights are stated as "the program does not hold the token over this interval", and a DMA loan is a token transferred to a declared ghost agent and returned by the program-observed completion event (R2's loan clause, exactly). (i), (ii), (v), (vi) are not this tuple's business. |
| R15 | **partial** | Identity, state and effect facts cross boundaries as location and permission parameters, and the metric is met at ~2 parameters per storage touched. Partial because higher-order and nominal code needs location-polymorphic closure types and requires a nominal to expose the location parameters of storage its values name; P16's `pick<N>` is rejected over an opaque `N`. |
| M1 | **met** | Every rule is syntax-directed. The only derivations are: extent disjointness and coverage in a fixed linear index fragment with a fixed normalizer; multiset matching at joins with a fixed unification order for existentials; the one-pass share/refine derivation at parallel constructs. No fixpoint (the loop-head rule is an equality check, not an iteration), no budget, no solver, no order dependence. |
| M2 | **met** | (i) No failure edge is added: tokens do not exist at run time. (ii) No bookkeeping state the source did not bind (no drop flag, no refcount, no generational or epoch compare — generations are ghost terms in location names), and no lowered branch selects between source behaviors. Every branch in P1, P4, P11 and P17 is the writer's. |
| M3 | **met** | The token algebra is closed: `Pt`, `Deed`, `In` and `Gone` are produced only by the listed rules. There is no writer-reachable form that manufactures a token, so there is no `unsafe` analogue. A foreign entry obtains its initial tokens from an enumerated adapter declaration carrying the boundary obligation. |
| M4 | **partial** | One production per construct holds for the core, but the **elision** of the token argument is an optional element of the `read`/`write` productions. It is a deterministic argument-recovery rule with a printable desugaring, not a second construct — but a strict reading of "one spelling to the byte" refuses it. Dropping the elision costs one token mention per access, which is the measurable alternative. |
| M5 | **met** | The permission judgment is only the share/refine derivation at erasable constructs; a failed derivation leaves the construct sequential. Acceptance depends on the *token* judgment, which is safety (R1), not permission. The corpus stays accepted with the parallel derivation disabled. |
| M6 | **partial** | (ii) frame soundness and (iii) erasure hold structurally — no operational rule mentions a token, and a fact survives an operation exactly when the operation did not receive its token. (i) the bounded small-model check over the token algebra has **not been run**, and it is the obligation that must precede selection. |
| M7 | **partial** | Strong where the tuple is strong: an absent token names the rule, the location, the extent and the line that consumed it; P1's payload is literally `k ≠ i ∧ k ≠ j`; P8's join payload is a multiset diff naming the path. Partial because P16's higher-order wall ("the nominal hides the location parameter") has no taught repair route yet, which M7's last clause forbids. |
| M8 | **violated** | The taught surface adds a genuine second sub-language: the extent grammar with its normalizer and disjointness judgment, the share/refine/carve/retire rules, existential pack and unpack, deeds and retirement, location terms with ghost generations, location and permission polymorphism. It displaces the whole borrow apparatus (OWN-2, OWN-3, OWN-4, OWN-5, OWN-6, OWN-10, OWN-11, OWN-13, OWN-14, PAR-1's loan clause), which is the repair path, but the net against a K already failed at ~130k is unmeasured and the extent algebra is the largest single new item in the list. Declared violated rather than argued down. |
| M9 | **partial (unmeasurable)** | The obvious shape of P5 and P6 is the accepted shape with no hints, which is the floor's precondition, and the per-load fact channel is the richest of any D1 family (every load carries its token's extent). Unmeasurable until an alias channel exists (SYS-REQ-13, MAP §8 Q15). |
| M10 | **met** | Extent disjointness: O(k²) atom comparisons per location, k = live extents of that location (P1's worst shape has k = 3). Join and loop-head matching: multiset equality, O(n log n) in live tokens, no fixpoint. Parallel split derivation: one pass over arms. No family above quadratic. Edit stability: a one-token signature edit reaches exactly that declaration's callers, bounded by FN-1's interface. |
| M11 | **met** | The verdict diff is computable over the retained corpus; migration is stated (`&` and `&uniq` become sugar for a token clause in and out of a signature; region syntax retires); written `use` steps survive a revision that does not change their rule. |

### 4.2 Counts

| | Count | Rows |
|---|---|---|
| met | 16 | R1, R2, R3, R4, R6, R7, R8a, R10, R11, R12, M1, M2, M3, M5, M10, M11 |
| partial | 10 | R5, R8b, R9, R13, R14, R15, M4, M6, M7, M9 |
| violated | 1 | M8 |

### 4.3 The price this candidate charges the compiler

| Price | Ground |
|---|---|
| No storage may be relocated while any token naming it is outstanding — no moving collector, no address-changing copy | R8a; enforced by the checker, so the backend needs no analysis to respect it |
| No release inserted, moved or removed except where a token-derived fact makes the move unobservable | R2 |
| The token multiset at a program point is the complete alias fact set the lowering may use without a guard; the emitter may not invent one | R4 soundness clause |
| No re-derivation may be *required* to reach a stated fact: the extent is already exact | R4 price |
| The checker must implement: an extent normalizer; a decidable disjointness and coverage judgment over a linear index fragment; multiset context matching with a fixed existential unification order; the one-pass split derivation at parallel constructs | M1, M10 |
| Nothing is constrained about scheduling, tiling, worker counts, versioning, remainder loops or fence choice | M2(ii), R5 price |

### 4.4 Writer cost

| Unit | Cost | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| per signature | one location parameter and one token clause (in and out) per storage the callee names; an existential for a fresh or replaced storage; an origin set for a returned pointer | P6, P9; ≈2 parameters per storage, R15's metric |
| per loop | the loop's token multiset, **only if the body changes it** | 0 for P5, P6, P11's read loop; 1 line for P8's take/put loop |
| per join | an existential pack, **only if the arms end different storage** | 0 for P1, P5, P6, P17; 1 line for P8 |
| per statement — read | 0 (token unchanged; argument elided) | §2.5 |
| per statement — write with the token in hand | 0 | P5's loop body |
| per statement — split, carve or end a storage | 1 line plus its disjointness or index fact | P1, P2, P6 |
| per statement — symbolic element access | 1 index fact, shared with R11 | P17 |
| per traversal of a recycling pool | 1 `use` step re-establishing the stated invariant after a removal | P3 |

---

## 5. Consequences at D5–D13

| Point | Forced | Foreclosed | Left open |
|---|---|---|---|
| **D5** interference source | *Effect footprints over identities* — the footprint IS the consumed/returned token multiset, so R4 and R5 read one relation (C2) with no second artifact; *Fractional or counting permissions* (already chosen, in the structured form) | *Derived footprints, not writer-owned* as the primary source; *Loans on references beside footprints* (there are no loans); *Runtime dependence tracking*; *Transactions and speculation* | *Declared reductions and deterministic merge* is **required** to close R5 ground (ii); *Optimizer-facing alias fact channel* must still be built |
| **D6** distinctness default | The question largely **dissolves**: two `W` tokens in one context cannot overlap, so distinctness is a theorem of the algebra, not a default. *Apartness as a judgment*, *Permission splitting at the call*, *Index-arithmetic distinctness* | *Distinct by default, call-site proof* (unnecessary and unsound-shaped here); *May-alias by default, callee copes*; *Per-function switch*; *Dynamic distinctness check*; *Distinct names are distinct storage* (P2 refutes it) | Whether the caller's refine obligation at a call is written or derived |
| **D7** contract vocabulary | *Typestate and permission pre/post per parameter*; *Store-typing rewrite signatures* (the signature literally is one); *Existential result identities*; *Ownership and identity transfer as the summary*; *Outcome-routed states and result obligations* for R12 | *No contracts: whole-program inference*; *Derived contracts, writer-confirmed* as the authority; *Prophecies and backward functions*; *Predicate-transformer and Hoare-type indices* (the rewrite is first-order) | *Closed catalog and size budget* is where M8's repair must be argued |
| **D8** relocation | *Explicit relocating move as the storage-ending event*; *Aggregates travel as handles, storage fixed* (C4); *Reallocation as a contract-visible name change*; *Relocation with a fixup channel*; *Pinning* is free — a held token **is** a pin | *Moves as byte copies the compiler elides* silently; *Compiler-inferred placement* as a fact source; any implicit relocation | *Arenas and regions with whole-region release* fit as a whole-extent retire; *destination-passing* is compatible |
| **D9** containers | *Per-element ghost tokens*; *Quantified element permission* (a range token is quantified permission); *Split-and-join range tokens*; *Bounds in the type* / *index-only access with bounds proofs*; *Relocation-stable ghost identity*; *Pools, free lists and slot recycling* with a **ghost** generation | *Generations and epochs* in their runtime-compare form (M2); *Snapshot plus delta log*; *Probe-sequence identity* without an extent | *Ring buffers and two-span views* need the extent grammar to carry two spans; *Structural decomposition: chunks, columns, lanes* is the natural P5 shape |
| **D10** concurrency | *Structured fork/join and linear task handles* (the token split at spawn, returned at join — Chalice's `fork tk`/`join tk` shape); *Lock as custodian of identity state* (the lock owns a token and hands it out at acquire, so cost lands on the write, C11) | *Shared storage keeps no facts* as the default; *Transactions*; *Convergent or monotone shared state* without a protocol | **P11's shape and R9's concurrent half need a mechanism this tuple does not supply**: *Protocol-governed shared regions and ghost state* or *Single-writer publish protocols as constructs*. The unjoined-child obligation leak (MAP §8 Q13) is unanswered |
| **D11** external resources | *Device handoff and escrow* (a DMA loan is a token transferred to a declared ghost agent, returned by the observed completion event); *Three identities per descriptor*; *Foreign identity: retain no contents fact* (a foreign-class token licenses access but carries no contents fact, R14(iv)); *Host values as ordinary declarations, one domain* | *Ambient and forgeable host access*; *World token, monadic sequencing*; *Second host-authority category* | *Typed failure and partial outcomes* is R12's, unchanged |
| **D12** surface form | *Modes as sugar over pointer plus state* (`&`/`&uniq` desugar to token clauses); *Elision and implicit identity parameters*; *Annotation site placement* at signatures; the region sigil retires | *Conventions instead of pointer types*; *Flat three-address source* is unnecessary; *Non-textual source of record* | **Direct tension with *Explicit-only core, one spelling per construct*** — this is M4's partial verdict and where the elision must be defended or dropped |
| **D13** validation | *Bounded exhaustive enumeration* over the token algebra is the M6(i) obligation and is directly runnable (the algebra is finite per program); *Certificate-producing acceptance* is natural — the token derivation **is** a certificate; *Dual acceptance and acceptance-set diffs* for migration; *Fact-channel review* for the R4 channel | *Executable semantics with a dynamic shadow-state oracle* as the primary channel (there is no runtime state to shadow); *Random generation* as the primary evidence | *Writer-trial and repair-loop benchmarks* remain evidence only (owner decision 12) |

---

## 6. Weaknesses, and the strongest objection

### 6.1 Honest weaknesses

| # | Weakness | How far it can be answered |
|---|---|---|
| W1 | **The extent algebra is a second language.** `e ⊖ e`, coverage, and symbolic index disjointness are real vocabulary, and P1's `[0..n) ⊖ [i] ⊖ [j]` is the shape a writer must read in a diagnostic. | Not answered away. It is charged to M8 as violated. Its defence is that the same algebra pays for R1's holes, R4's distinctness, R5's footprints, R6's frame and R11's index domains — five rows, one vocabulary (C1). |
| W2 | **No conditional contracts.** The join rule admits no condition terms, so `push` splits into `push` and `push_within` (P4) and every conditionally-reallocating API doubles. | Partly answered: the split moves the branch into the source where M2(ii) wants it, and R8a already records conditional reallocation contracts as red. The corpus cost is unmeasured. |
| W3 | **Existentials in containers.** A homogeneous field cannot hold pointers with per-object location atoms; the fix is the location *term* `slot(ℓP,i,g)` plus a written pool invariant (P3). | Answered for pools and arrays. Not answered for a heterogeneous graph whose nodes come from unrelated allocations: those need per-node existentials and lose name equality. |
| W4 | **Higher-order and nominal code.** Closures need location-polymorphic types with capture clauses, and a nominal must expose the location parameters of any storage its values name; `pick<N>` over an opaque `N` is rejected with no taught route (M7 partial, R15 partial). | Partly answered: the rejection is local and names the hidden parameter. The route — a location-parameter bound on the nominal — is a D7/D12 design not written here. |
| W5 | **Elision or verbosity, pick one.** With the elision, M4's one-spelling rule bends; without it, every access names a token. | Not answered. The measurement that decides it (token mentions per program, with and without) does not exist. |
| W6 | **R5 ground (ii) is missing.** Recombinable accumulators have no token rule; P15 is unanswerable without a D5 mechanism. | Named, not answered. |
| W7 | **M6(i) has not been run.** The bounded small-model check over the token algebra is the obligation that must precede selection, and it is the check most likely to find a hole in `R-CARVE`/`R-RETIRE` interaction with existential packing. | Not answered; declared. |

### 6.2 The objection I expect

> The read objection is answered, but it is replaced by the **write**
> objection. One linear `W` token per extent means every state-changing
> operation is a flow edge, and routing that single token through a program
> whose structure is not a tree — P3's graph with back edges, P9's `pick`, any
> code where the storage that must be written is chosen at run time — costs an
> existential, a written invariant, and a ghost match per site. So the
> candidate buys R4 and R6 exactness with an M8 budget it already fails and an
> M7 wall at exactly the abstraction boundary R15 was added to protect.

Answer, in four parts.

1. **Writes should serialize.** Two simultaneous writes to one extent is the
   hazard R1 and R5 exist to refuse. The objection is not that the token
   serializes writes; it is that the token must be *routed*. Those are
   different complaints and only the second is a cost.

2. **The routing is structural, not textual.** The token travels through
   signatures, which the writer writes once per function, and the checker
   threads it everywhere else. The writer names a token only at four sites:
   a signature clause, a join where arms end different storage, a split of one
   storage into parts, and a ghost match on a non-singleton origin set. §4.4
   counts them: zero per read, zero per ordinary write, one per split. The
   per-statement tax the objection imagines does not exist.

3. **The cost is bounded by R3's own line.** Token mentions scale with
   *state-changing* operations, which R3 already prices at "one keyword per
   transfer" and accepts. The candidate does not add a new axis of cost; it
   makes the existing transfer keyword carry the permission too.

4. **What it buys back is measured.** R6's tax is not hypothetical: 34 of 41
   `len()` rebinds in the blind-writer corpus exist only because ENT-5 kills at
   a whole-parameter footprint. Under this tuple that kill rule does not exist
   — a call cannot falsify a fact about an extent whose token it never
   received — so those 34 rebinds go to zero, and so does the OWN-6
   non-local-borrow wall, because there are no borrows to be non-local about.
   The honest trade is: the writer pays location parameters and split lines,
   and stops paying rebinds, region blocks and suspension windows.

What the answer does **not** cover, and is conceded: W4's higher-order wall and
W7's unrun soundness check. Those are the two findings that should decide
whether this candidate survives, not the write-routing cost.


# File: candidate-columns-first.md

# Candidate core model: **columns-first**

Research date: 2026-09-16. A candidate for D1–D4 of
[OPTIONS.md](../../whitefoot-access-effects-research/research/investigations/access-effects/OPTIONS.md),
derived against the settled requirement list (VERDICT-D0 §2, owner interim
positions of §7 taken as settled), the couplings C1–C18 (§4), the hazard ladder
(MECHANISM-MAP §3) and the discriminating programs P1–P19.

Prior art the candidate draws on: Futhark and Dex (index sets as types, uniqueness
on arrays), Halide and Exo (extents and tiles as first-class named things), ECS
archetypes (Unity DOTS chunks, Bevy conflict detection over declared component
sets), Apache Arrow (record batches, validity bitmaps as ordinary data), ISPC
`soa<N>`, and Whitefoot's own SoA doctrine (why-whitefoot §5 `Cols`,
`research/experiments/scoped-alias-channel/RESULTS.md`).

---

## 1. The tuple

| Point | Family chosen (name exactly as in OPTIONS.md) | Members drawn on |
|---|---|---|
| **D1** | **Column / plane within one backing**, refined by **Element identity by index** and by **Range, tile, partition** | SYS-D1-12, HIS-D1-09; AI-D1-03, HIS-D1-07, HIS-D1-23; AI-D1-04, SYS-D1-13, SYS-D1-14. Two ghost refinements: AI-D1-12 (statically tracked generation, as a *ghost* epoch only) and THE-D1-04 (nominal atom with freshness `a # b`) for pool occupants. Result identities use HIS-D1-14 (finite static origin set). |
| **D2** | **Declared access sets and schedules**, carried by **Permission as an effect on the statement or arrow**; the intra-body residue is **Implicit checker context** | SYS-D2-10, SYS-D2-11 (declared access set per launch / per job); AI-D2-11, THE-D2-14 (effect on the statement, row on the arrow); AI-D2-01, THE-D2-01 (checker context inside a body). RAD-D2-06 (runtime scheduler) and RAD-D2-16 (separate schedule artifact) are **refused** inside this candidate: the first is bookkeeping the source did not bind (M2(ii)), the second is a second artifact to check (M4, M10). |
| **D3** | **Sequence initialized-window states**, with **Occupancy as separate data** admitted *as data and never as language state*; joins by **State as a term over captured conditions** | HIS-D3-11, HIS-D3-15, HIS-D3-18 (window typestate, the three run families, measure terms with descriptor support); SYS-D3-18 (validity as parallel array) restricted as below; HIS-D3-04 (vacancy as Option-shaped value); AI-D3-07, SYS-D3-14, THE-D3-12, HIS-D3-07 (term over captured branch conditions). HIS-D3-12, HIS-D3-16, HIS-D3-17 stay **refused**: no per-slot tag, occupancy bitmap or runtime discriminant is *language state*. |
| **D4** | **Column-level distinctness (the SoA rule)** as the default and the boundary rule, refined inside a plane by **Overlap judged by resolved paths and proved extents**; **Value semantics, purity, and copy-on-write** for storage that is not a plane | RAD-D4-14, SYS-D4-08; HIS-D4-12, HIS-D4-13, SYS-D4-10; RAD-D4-01, RAD-D4-06, RAD-D4-09. HIS-D4-01 (OWN-5 reference exclusivity) is **retired**; HIS-D4-09 (suspension windows on references) is replaced by extent splitting, which is not reference-borne. |

### Why the four cohere

One relation answers all four. A **backing** is carved into **planes**; a plane is
carved into **extents**; an extent is indexed into **elements**. That containment
tree is:

| Consumer | What it reads from the tree | Row |
|---|---|---|
| Sequential safety | the state of the named plane or element | R1 |
| Optimizer distinctness | "no common leaf", proved by the carving, not by name inequality | R4(b) |
| Parallel permission | footprints as sets of tree nodes | R5(b) |
| Frame kills | a write kills facts supported by that node and its descendants only | R6(b) |
| Layout demands | the plane map *is* stride, offset and alignment | R8b |
| Byte budgets | the sum of issued extents is bounded by the parent extent, by construction | R13 |

- **D1 → D4.** Because planes are a *partition* of a backing, "columns never
  alias" is a theorem of the carving, not a policy the writer declares and not a
  property of a reference. D4's default costs nothing to check.
- **D4 → D2.** Once distinctness is a fact about identities rather than about
  references, the only thing a boundary must state is *which identities are
  touched and how* — a declared access set. There is nothing else for a
  parameter mode to carry, so modes retire (C13).
- **D1 → D3.** A plane is homogeneous and contiguous, so its initialization is a
  *window* (a measure over its own descriptor), not a per-slot fact. Length lives
  in a sibling plane, so an element write cannot kill a length (HIS-D3-18).
- **D3 → D4.** Because the state lives on the plane and never on a reference,
  several writable descriptors to one plane are ordinary (R9, P7), and the only
  thing aliasing costs is a *fact*, exactly where the identities coincide (C5).
- **D2 → D1.** A declared access set is only as precise as the identity
  vocabulary; extents and indices are what make `helper(out[w*s .. (w+1)*s))`
  say something stronger than "writes `out`" (P6).

---

## 2. The model

### 2.1 Identity grammar (erased)

```text
ident ::= 'B                  // backing: one allocation, one arena, one frame slot, one mapping
        | 'B.c                // plane: a carved, strided extent of 'B with element type T
        | 'B.c@e              // plane under ghost occupancy epoch e (only planes declared `permutable`)
        | 'B.c[lo..hi)        // extent: half-open, endpoints are captured measure terms
        | 'B.c[i]             // element: i a captured index term
        | 'B.c#n              // occupant: n a ghost atom, resolved to a slot through the plane's ghost map
```

The **plane map** of a backing is fixed at its formation and is part of its type:

```text
backing Cols { a,b,c,d,e,f,g,h : plane<u64, len n, align 64> }   // 8 planes, disjoint by the map
backing Arena { meta : plane<Hdr>, bytes : plane<u8, len N> }    // 2 planes
```

Struct fields are planes of a one-element backing; an ordinary local scalar is a
one-plane backing. There is no separate "field path" mechanism: `'a.x` of the
ladder's Step 1 *is* `'B.c` with `len 1`.

**Disjointness** is a single judgment over the tree:

```text
disj(u, v)  iff  neither is a descendant of the other, and
                 - different planes of one backing            (plane map)          , or
                 - different backings                          (formation)          , or
                 - extents proved disjoint by half-open arithmetic in the linear
                   index fragment                              (split algebra)      , or
                 - elements with a proved i != j               (index fragment)
```

`disj` is never "the names differ". P2's arena `S` and a live block `b1` are
ancestor/descendant, so `disj` is false — the negative test R4(e) demands.

### 2.2 What a reference's type says

Three forms, all copyable, all carrying identity and **no permission and no
duration**:

```text
plane<'B.c, T>          // runtime: base, len       -- a descriptor
view<'B.c[lo..hi), T>   // runtime: base, len       -- endpoints captured as terms
elem<'B.c[i], T>        // runtime: address         -- index captured as a term
handle<'B.c#n, T>       // runtime: slot index      -- resolved through the ghost map
```

Permission is not here. Permission is the access set in force: the enclosing
function's declared row, or the row of the construct (`par`, `split`) the
statement is under.

### 2.3 What the checker holds per storage

```text
state('B)    ::= Live | Gone
state('B.c)  ::= ( run , punct , epoch )
   run   ::= Full | [lo,hi) | Ring(head,count) | Empty        // HIS-D3-15's three families
   punct ::= a finite set of index terms, |punct| <= the number of textual
             `take` sites in scope                             // bounded syntactically
   epoch ::= a ghost natural, bumped only by an operation whose contract says `permutes`
```

`Init('B.c[i])` iff `i ∈ run ∧ i ∉ punct`. `Gone('B.c)` iff `state('B) = Gone`.
Contents facts are keyed by tree node; a write to `u` kills facts whose support
is `u` or a descendant of `u`, and nothing else (R6).

Nothing above is ever materialized. `run`, `punct` and `epoch` are erased; the
*measures* a run is written over (`len`, `head`, `cap`) are ordinary data in a
sibling plane, which is why they can be named in contracts and branched on.

### 2.4 Occupancy as data, stated as a rule

> A validity plane, a per-slot tag, an occupancy bitmap or an `Option`-shaped
> element is **ordinary data**. Reading it is ordinary control flow the writer
> wrote. It may never discharge an R1 obligation: the payload plane it describes
> must be `Full` independently, so that a read of any slot is memory-safe
> whatever the bit says.

This is what keeps Arrow's shape and M2(ii) in the same candidate. The bitmap
carries *semantic* presence; the language state carries *memory* presence; the
first never stands in for the second, so no runtime comparison satisfies a rule of
acceptance. HIS-D3-12/16/17 stay refused as *language state*; SYS-D3-18 is
admitted as *data*.

### 2.5 How state changes

| Operation | Precondition | Post-state | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `read elem<'B.c[i]>` | `Live('B)`, `i ∈ run \ punct`, epoch current | — | R1(i)(ii)(iii) in one check |
| `write elem<'B.c[i]>` | same | kills facts supported by `'B.c[i]` | R6 |
| `take elem<'B.c[i]>` | `i ∈ run \ punct` | `punct ∪= {i}` | value is affine, moves out (R3) |
| `put elem<'B.c[i]>, v` | `i ∈ punct`, or `i` adjacent to a run end | `punct \= {i}`, or run extends | fills the hole any alias left |
| `replace elem, v` | `i ∈ run \ punct` | unchanged | returns old; no hole ever exists |
| `split(view, at)` | `at` in the view's extent | parent's access is partitioned into the two children plus the **residue** (the complement); restored at the split construct's join | the access-set algebra, not a borrow |
| `alloc(A, n)` | `A.bytes` residue has `n` free | yields `∃o. view<'A.bytes[o..o+n)>`, epoch of `A.meta` unchanged | existential extent, unpacked at the call |
| `free(A, b)` | `b` is a live issued extent, its own obligations discharged | `b`'s identity is `Gone`; its bytes return to the residue | address reuse mints a *fresh* identity |
| `free('B)` | every plane `Empty` of affine elements, `punct = ∅` | `state('B) = Gone` | every plane and element under it is Gone |
| `move` of a backing | — | source `Gone`, fresh backing begins | the ladder's Step 1 distinction |
| `push`/`reserve` | — | `ite(len0 < cap0, 'B unchanged, 'B Gone ∧ fresh 'B')` | contract-visible (R8a), ladder Step 3 |
| `compact`/`permutes` | plane declared `permutable` | `epoch += 1`; every captured `[i]` identity is ill-typed after | handles `#n` survive: they resolve through the map |

### 2.6 Joins and loop heads

**Join.** Each plane's state is a term over captured condition atoms:
`state = ite(c, s1, s2)` where `c` is a pure boolean the writer bound. A later
access under a branch on the same `c` resolves the term. The atom set of one term
is bounded by a fixed specification constant `k` (nesting of writer-written,
captured conditions); beyond `k` the join takes the meet and the diagnostic says
which atom it dropped. The rule is syntactic, so acceptance is a function of the
source (M1); the bound is a stated precision rule with an M7 payload.

**Loop head.** The writer states, once:

```text
for i in 0..n
  invariant run(v.data) = [0, n)          // what the body preserves
  writes  v.data[i]                       // the per-iteration access set
  reads   v.other[i]
```

The `writes`/`reads` row over the *iteration index* is the PAR-2 permission
ground: iteration `i` and `j` are non-interfering because `disj('v.data[i],
'v.data[j])` follows from `i ≠ j` (R5(a)(i)). If the writer omits the row, the
loop is sequential and still accepted (M5's chosen degradation).

### 2.7 What a signature states

```text
fn helper<'B.c>(s: view<'B.c[lo..hi), u8>, input: plane<'I.d, u8>)
  reads  'I.d
  writes 's                                  // the extent, not the plane
  entry  run('B.c) ⊇ [lo,hi)
  exit   run unchanged
```

Per identity: entry state, exit state, read/write/end footprints, freshness or
existential results, outcomes (R12), resource effects (R13). Nothing else; there
is no mode, no region parameter and no loan.

### 2.8 What the writer writes, and where

| Site | What must be written | Typical size |
|---|---|---|
| Type definition | the plane map (one line per plane, with any layout demand) | 1 line / plane |
| Signature | one identity parameter per plane or extent touched; one access-row clause; entry/exit state only where it changes | 1 + (1 per touched identity) |
| Loop head | the per-iteration access row; the run invariant if the loop changes a run | 1–2 lines |
| Join | nothing, unless the state term exceeds `k` atoms or the writer wants a coarser joined state | 0–1 line |
| Statement | nothing, except a `use` step for an index-fragment goal the automatic family does not close | 0 |
| Split | `split`/`join` of an extent where two writers must overlap | 1 line per split |

### 2.9 What is erased

Identities, plane maps as facts (not as layout), runs, punctures, epochs, atoms,
access rows, origin sets, every proof step. What remains is base pointers,
lengths, indices, and any occupancy data the writer *wrote as data*. No epoch,
atom or bit is consulted at run time for safety (M2, M6(iii)).

---

## 3. Derivations

Notation follows the ladder: pseudocode lines with `// accept:` or `// reject:`
and the fact used.

### P1 Container split with a runtime index

```text
v : backing V { data: plane<u64, len n>, len: plane<usize, len 1> }

pi = split_one(v.data, i)          // view<'V.data[i..i+1)>   accept: extent carve
pj = split_one(v.data, j)          // accept iff  i != j       fact: disj by index fragment
                                   // reject otherwise: "needs i != j"       M7 payload
par { write(pi, x) ; write(pj, y) } // accept: disj('V.data[i..i+1), 'V.data[j..j+1))
                                   //         R5(a)(i), footprints are the two extents
k = f(...)                          // runtime index
read(v.data[k])                     // reject: 'V.data's access is split; the residue is
                                    //   [0,n) \ ([i,i+1) ∪ [j,j+1)).
                                    //   needs: k != i && k != j            <- the diagnostic
if k != i && k != j { read(v.data[k]) }   // accept: residue covers k        writer's own branch
join pi, pj                          // accept: access returns to 'V.data
push(v, x)                           // accept: parent access whole, punct = ∅
                                     // (before `join`: reject, "'V.data is split at [i,i+1)")
```
No runtime check is emitted: the only branch is the one the writer wrote (M2(i)).
**Verdict: accepted as required.**

### P2 Arena with independently released blocks

```text
backing A { meta: plane<Hdr>, bytes: plane<u8, len N, permutable=false> }

b1 = alloc(A, 64)?   // ∃o1. view<'A.bytes[o1..o1+64)>   accept: contract yields a fresh
b2 = alloc(A, 64)?   //   existential extent; arena invariant: issued extents pairwise disjoint
b3 = alloc(A, 64)?   //   and contained in 'A.bytes                        (written invariant)
                     // row of alloc: reads+writes 'A.meta, carves 'A.bytes residue

par { fill(b1); fill(b2); fill(b3) }
      // accept: footprints are three extents, pairwise disj by the arena invariant;
      //         none names 'A.meta, so no interference on metadata        R5(a)(i)
      // note: nobody holds 'A; the three extents are siblings under the residue

free(A, b2)          // accept: 'A.bytes[o2..o2+64) -> Gone; bytes return to the residue
                     //         writes 'A.meta only
b4 = alloc(A, 32)    // accept: mints a FRESH existential identity o4, even where o4 = o2
read(b2[0])          // reject: R1(ii), the identity is Gone. Address reuse never revives it.
read(b1[0])          // accept: b1 still live
free(A,b1); free(A,b3); free(A,b4)   // accept: each issued extent released once  R2
```
Cost: the disjointness of a *recycled* extent from the live ones is not split
arithmetic — it is the arena's own invariant over its free list, stated once in
the arena's contract and proved in its body with written `use` steps (measured
guess: one invariant, ~6 steps). The plane algebra gives containment and split
disjointness for free; recycling needs the invariant.
**Verdict: accepted with a stated cost** (one written arena invariant; the
recycling half wants **D9 "Pools, free lists and slot recycling"** and **D8 "Slot
reuse in pools"** to supply the standard form so each arena does not re-prove it).

### P3 Graph with back edges in a pool

```text
backing Pool { next: plane<handle>, prev: plane<handle>, data: plane<u64>,
               live: plane<bool> }             // `live` is DATA, not language state
invariant  forall s in occupied(Pool): atom(next[s]) in atoms(Pool)
                                    && atom(prev[s]) in atoms(Pool)   // stated ONCE   R6(e)

// insert n between a and b  -- four link writes
next[a] = n    // accept: write to 'Pool.next[a]; aliasing inside a plane is free (D4)
prev[n] = a    // accept: 'Pool.prev is a different plane from 'Pool.next  (plane map)
next[n] = b    // accept: same plane as line 1, different element; no distinctness needed
prev[b] = n    // accept.   proof obligation: the invariant is re-established -> 1 `use` step
               // R9's negative test passes: several writable paths to one node, sequentially

// remove m; the slot is reused later
unlink(m)      // accept; proof: no occupied s has atom(next[s]) = m        (written)
retire(m)      // accept: the atom #m is retired
p = stale handle<'Pool#m>
read(data[p])  // reject: R1(ii), atom #m retired.  Identity, not address, is what ended.
insert_reusing_slot_of_m(...)   // accept: a FRESH atom #m' occupies the same slot

// traverse
cur = head; while live(cur) { x = data[cur]; cur = next[cur] }
               // accept: `live` is data, the branch is the writer's; data[cur] is safe
               // because 'Pool.data is Full (total init), not because the bit said so

par map over occupied slots { data[s] = f(data[s]) }
               // accept: footprint is 'Pool.data[s], distinct per s by index      R5(a)(i)
               // and disjoint from 'Pool.next / .prev by the plane map
```
The link fields hold `handle<'Pool#n>` (slot index at run time, ghost atom in the
type), not addresses. Without the atom refinement, a stale index is an in-bounds
read of a recycled slot — a silent wrong value that R1 does not forbid, and the
program's stated requirement "removal invalidates every path to `m`" would be
violated.
**Verdict: accepted with a stated cost** — one ghost atom per occupant, an
existential atom in the plane's element type, one plane-level invariant. The
mechanism is **D9 "Relocation-stable ghost identity"**; the apartness judgment it
needs is **D6 "Apartness as a judgment"**. The residual honest loss: an
*intrusive* list embedded in an object and reached by address (`container_of`) is
not expressible; the structure must live in a pool.

### P4 Cursor over a growing vector

```text
struct Cursor<'B.c> { at: plane<'B.c, u64>, i: usize }   // the identity is a type parameter
v : V { data: plane<u64>, len: plane<usize,1>, cap: plane<usize,1> }
c  = Cursor { at: v.data, i: 0 }

a = c.read()        // accept: run('V.data) = [0,len) and i < len    R1(i)
push(v, 5)          // contract: exit  ite(len0 < cap0, 'V unchanged, 'V Gone ∧ fresh 'V')
b = c.read()        // reject unless len0 < cap0 is provable: "'V may be Gone; needs len<cap"
if len(v) < cap(v) { push(v,5); b = c.read() }   // accept: the term resolves on the writer's
                                                 //   own atom; no borrow blocked the push
else { push(v,5); c = Cursor { at: v.data, i: c.i } }  // accept: rebind to the fresh identity
free(v)
c.read()            // reject forever: R1(ii), 'V Gone
```
**Verdict: accepted with a stated cost** — the struct carries the backing
identity as a parameter (R15 cost: 1 parameter), and the conditional
reallocation contract must be expressible as a state term over `len<cap`
(R8a status: red today). No loan blocks `push`, which is what P4 asks for.

### P5 Struct-of-arrays kernel

```text
backing Cols { a,b,c,d,e,f,g,h : plane<u64, len n, align 64> }

for i in 0..n
  writes Cols.a[i], Cols.b[i]
  reads  Cols.c[i], Cols.d[i], Cols.e[i], Cols.f[i], Cols.g[i], Cols.h[i]
{
  a[i] = f(a[i], c[i], d[i])     // accept: 8 planes pairwise disj by the PLANE MAP, no proof
  b[i] = g(b[i], e[i], f[i], g[i], h[i])   // accept: same
}
// PAR-2 overlap: accept. footprint of iteration i is {a[i],b[i]} write / {c..h}[i] read;
//   disj across i != j by the index fragment.                               R5(a)(i)
// Backend: one !alias.scope per plane on every loaded data pointer; zero runtime guards.
//   EVIDENCE D1 (retired `democ`): 8 vector ops / 0 guards / 121 asm lines
//   vs Rust obvious shape 65 / 29 guards / 2132 lines; 16-column addendum 29 -> 111 guards.
```
The obvious shape *is* the declared shape: the writer wrote the plane map because
that is how the data is laid out, and it is the whole distinctness proof.
**Verdict: accepted as required.** This is the candidate's home case and the one
place where the source form and the backend fact are the same artifact (R4(e),
M9's P5 half).

### P6 Range partition helper

```text
out : O { bytes: plane<u8, len n> }
s = n / k

par for w in 0..k
  writes out.bytes[w*s .. (w+1)*s)
{
  helper(split(out.bytes, w*s, (w+1)*s), input)
}
// helper's signature:  fn helper<'X>(s: view<'X[lo..hi), u8>, inp: plane<'I,u8>)
//                        reads 'I  writes 's
// accept: the caller judges from the signature alone — helper writes its extent and
//   nothing else.                                                            R7(e)
// accept overlap: disj( [w*s,(w+1)*s), [w'*s,(w'+1)*s) ) for w != w' is half-open
//   arithmetic in the linear index fragment.                                 R5(a)(i)
// k appears once, as the loop bound; no worker count anywhere else.
```
**Verdict: accepted as required.**

### P7 Take, put, replace through aliases

```text
A : backing A { v: plane<T,1> }        // T affine
p = elem<'A.v[0]>   ;   q = elem<'A.v[0]>      // two descriptors, ONE identity term

x = take(p)     // accept: 0 ∈ run.  post: punct = {0}
read(q)         // reject: R1(i), 0 ∈ punct — the hole p made is visible through q,
                //   because state is on 'A.v, never on p or q.
put(q, move x)  // accept: 0 ∈ punct.  post: punct = ∅
read(p)         // accept: 0 ∈ run \ punct
old = replace(p, new)   // accept: replace needs Init and leaves Init; no hole exists
read(q)         // accept: reads `new` — one storage, one state
free(A)         // accept: punct = ∅, the affine occupant was consumed by `replace`'s result
read(p)         // reject forever: R1(ii), 'A Gone
```
**Verdict: accepted as required.** No mechanism beyond D1+D3 is used; this is
the test that decides "state is a property of the storage" and columns-first
passes it by construction.

### P8 Conditional release and loop exits

```text
if c { free(a) } else { free(b) }
   // post:  state('a) = ite(c, Gone, Live) ,  state('b) = ite(c, Live, Gone)
   //        no drop flag: the atom `c` is the writer's own binding             M2(ii)

use(b); free(b)     // reject: "state('b) is Gone on the path where c is false;
                    //          the differing path is the `else` arm"           M7 payload
if c { use(b); free(b) } else { use(a); free(a) }   // accept: the terms resolve on `c`

loop {
  invariant punct('p) = ∅                  // one line, at the loop head
  if stop { break }                        // break edge carries punct = ∅
  x = take(p) ; ... ; put(p, x)            // accept: take then put restores the invariant
}
free(p)     // accept: punct = ∅ on the break edge and on the fallthrough      R2
```
**Verdict: accepted as required.**

### P9 A callee that changes storage state

```text
fn drain<'X>(x: plane<'X,T>)  writes 'X  entry run('X) = [0,len)  exit run('X) = Empty
fn reserve<'V>(v: &V, m: usize)
      exit  ite(cap0 >= m, 'V.data unchanged, 'V.data Gone ∧ fresh ∃'V'.data)
fn pick<'X,'Y>(c: bool, x: elem<'X>, y: elem<'Y>) -> elem<{'X,'Y}>
      // result identity is the FINITE ORIGIN SET {'X,'Y}                    HIS-D1-14

d = drain(v.data)          // accept: caller now knows run = Empty; no body was opened
reserve(v, 100)            // accept: caller's state for 'V.data becomes a term over cap0>=100
r = pick(c, px, py)
write(r)                   // accept only for facts true of BOTH origins; a fact private to
                           //   'X is not available.  reject with "the origin set is {'X,'Y};
                           //   branch on c or state the fact for both"
if c { write(px) } else { write(py) }   // accept: full precision, writer's own branch
```
**Verdict: accepted with a stated cost** — the origin-set meet loses precision at
`pick`, repaired by one writer branch. Each effect is in the signature; the body
is checked once against it (R7(e)).

### P11 Write-once-then-frozen cache

```text
backing Cache { val: plane<u64, len K>, filled: plane<bool, len K> }   // `filled` is DATA
// language state:  run('Cache.val) = Full   from construction (total init: u64 has a total
//                  constructor).  It never changes.                         <- R1 pass

fn get(c: &Cache, k: usize) -> u64 {
  if !filled[k] { val[k] = compute(k); filled[k] = true }  // accept: ordinary writes to
                                                           //  'Cache.val[k], 'Cache.filled[k]
  val[k]        // accept: R1(i) discharged by run = Full, NOT by the bit.
}               //   The bit's read is semantics, not a safety check.        M2(ii) intact

pr = elem<'Cache.val[r]>
get(c, j)       // writes 'Cache.val[j]; kills contents facts at 'Cache.val[j] only
read(pr)        // accept: r's Init fact comes from run = Full and no write kills it;
                //   a contents fact about r survives iff j != r is proved.       R6
```
Pass/fail under R1 alone, as the row demands: **pass**, because the plane is
`Full` and the per-slot occupancy is never language state. A reader *may* hold a
pointer to a slot across another slot's fill, unconditionally for the Init fact
and conditionally (`j != r`) for a contents fact.
**Verdict: accepted with a stated cost.** The cost is exactly why-whitefoot §5's
performance argument made concrete: the payload must be *totally
initializable*. A cache of affine, non-default-constructible values is **not**
expressible in this shape — it would need a per-slot `Uninit→Init` language
transition, which the run vocabulary does not have, and which the punctured form
cannot supply because `punct` is bounded by textual take sites, not by data.
That residue wants **D9 "Affine elements, vacancy and occupancy"** to rule on
whether a fourth run family (`sparse`) is admitted; this candidate refuses it.

### P13 Relocation by a compacting third party

```text
backing Pool { data: plane<Obj, len K, permutable> , map: ghost slot-of : atom -> index }
h = handle<'Pool#n>                  // runtime: a slot index, resolved through the map
p = elem<'Pool.data@e[ slot_of(n) ]> // pointer_of(h) captures the CURRENT epoch e

pool.compact()    // contract:  permutes 'Pool.data    =>  epoch e -> e+1
                  //            run unchanged, contents permuted, map updated
read(p)           // reject: the identity names 'Pool.data@e and the current epoch is e+1.
                  //   R1(iii): access under a stale layout. No runtime compare was emitted;
                  //   the epoch is a ghost term, so this is a typing failure.   M2 intact
read(pool[h])     // accept: the handle is resolved through the CURRENT map at each use —
                  //   this is the contract-visible fixup form R8a demands.
```
**Verdict: accepted with a stated cost.** The cost is the `permutable` plane
attribute plus the ghost epoch (one spelling more in D1) and the rule that an
`elem` identity is invalidated wholesale by a permutation — coarse, and it kills
every interior pointer into the plane, not only the ones that moved. Interior
pointers and third-party relocation remain mutually exclusive, exactly as R8a
says, and the handle is the named fixup channel. Relatedly this forecloses
**D8 "Relocation with a fixup channel"**'s runtime-rewriting variants: nothing
rewrites a stored pointer, because stored pointers into permutable planes do not
exist.

### P16 Abstraction over identities

```text
fn kernel<E, 'C : planes(Cols<E>)>(c: Cols<E>)
      reads/writes rows over 'C                 // one identity parameter per plane touched
// accept: R15's metric — parameters per interface = the number of planes the callee
//   touches, not the number of fields of the type.                           R15(e)

let h = |s: view<'X[lo..hi)>| helper(s, input)
// the closure's type carries a capture row naming 'I (input's plane)
// accept: P6 through a closure, provided the capture row is part of the closure type

fn pick<N: Nominal>(c: bool, x: N, y: N) -> N
// accept: through the finite origin set, as in P9

fn map_nodes<T>(g: Pool<Node<T>>, f: fn(&T) -> T)
// PROBLEM: the plane map of Pool<Node<T>> depends on T's own decomposition, so the
//   identity parameter is a *row of planes of unknown length*.
// reject under the first-order vocabulary: "'Pool.? cannot be named"
```
**Verdict: needs a mechanism from D7** — **"Effect rows as the contract"** with
row polymorphism over a plane list (a row variable ranging over the plane map of
a type parameter). The `Cols<E>` and closure cases are accepted with a stated
cost; the generic-pool case is the one that does not type without it. This is
exactly the "signature explosion" risk R15 was admitted to catch, and it lands on
columns-first harder than on candidates whose identity is per-allocation, because
the number of identities scales with the *decomposition* of the element type.

### P17 Partial operations

```text
q = a / d          // reject: "needs d != 0"     R11; not a D1..D4 matter
                   // accept with: if d != 0 { a / d } else { ...outcome arm... }
b: u8 = narrow(x)  // reject: "needs x < 256"    R11; same
y = v.data[i]      // inside `for i in 0..len(v)`:
                   // accept: i ∈ run('V.data) = [0, len) is closed by the automatic index
                   //   family from the loop bound and the run state. ZERO writer cost.
y = v.data[k]      // k a runtime value: reject, "needs k < len(v.data)";
                   //   repaired by the writer's own bound test or by a `use` step.
```
**Verdict: accepted as required** for the index arm, which is the arm this
candidate touches: the bound is a measure of the plane's own descriptor, so the
obvious loop shape needs no proof at all. The divisor and narrowing arms are
R11's existing OP rules and are orthogonal to D1–D4.

## 4. Requirements

### 4.1 Row-by-row

| Row | Verdict | Reason (one sentence) |
|---|---|---|
| R1 Sequential memory safety | **met** | (i) is `i ∈ run \ punct`, (ii) is `Gone` on the backing plus atom retirement, (iii) is the ghost epoch; the diagnostic names which sub-property failed. |
| R2 Resource lifecycle | **met** | Obligations sit on backings and on affine occupants; `free` requires every plane emptied and `punct = ∅` on every path, with joins by condition term and no drop flag (P8, P2). |
| R3 Value classes and transfer | **met** | Unchanged from today; `take`/`put`/`replace` are the run-and-puncture transitions and the multiplicity lemma is independent of identity granularity. |
| R4 Licensed facts | **met** | `disj` is literally "a proved disjointness relation over a containment structure of identities, never inequality of identity names", and P2's `S` vs `b1` is false by ancestry. |
| R5 Race freedom and overlap | **partial** | Ground (i) is supplied exactly and cheaply (P1, P3, P5, P6); grounds (ii) and (iii) need a law table and R14(ii)'s level set, which this candidate does not decide. |
| R6 Frame precision | **met** | A kill is keyed by tree node, and because a length lives in a sibling plane, an element write cannot kill it — the measured 34/41 `len()` rebinds have no cause left. |
| R7 Compositional call judgement | **met** | Entry/exit states, footprints, existential results and origin sets are all terms over the same tree; P9 and P6 are judged from signatures alone. |
| R8a Storage-ending and relocation | **met** | `free`, `move`, reallocating `push`, arena reset, permutation (epoch) and non-program relocation are the complete, contract-visible set; the handle-through-map is the fixup form (P13). |
| R8b Placement and physical demands | **met** | The plane map *is* the layout vocabulary: stride, offset, alignment, SoA/AoS and foreign representation are declared where the identity is declared, so an `align(64)` demand is not a second mechanism. |
| R9 Shared mutation, sequentially | **met** | Aliasing inside a plane is unrestricted and safety is the plane's state, so P3's four link writes and P7's two descriptors are accepted; facts weaken only where identities coincide. |
| R10 External resources | **partial** | A mapping or descriptor is a backing with planes (contents plane carrying R14(iv)'s foreign class, cursor plane, obligation on the wrapper), which fits P14's three identities, but P14 is not derived here. |
| R11 Partial operations | **met** | The index arm is discharged from the plane's own run measure at zero writer cost; the other arms are unchanged (P17). |
| R12 Typed outcomes | **partial** | Outcome arms are ordinary control flow and the state term over the outcome discriminant is the same machinery as a branch condition; allocation failure follows owner decision 5 and is outside the model, so the row's red clause stays red. |
| R13 Resource bounds | **partial** | A byte budget is proved by construction — the sum of issued extents is bounded by the parent extent, so P18's budget half needs no cost semantics — but declared depth and termination are untouched by D1–D4. |
| R14 Execution model | **partial** | The candidate supplies (iv) naturally (a foreign plane is a plane whose contents facts never survive) and (iii) for allocator writes into the residue, but (i), (ii), (v) and (vi) are R14's to state. |
| R15 Abstraction | **partial** | `Cols<E>` and closures cross the boundary with parameters linear in planes touched, but a generic pool of a generic element type needs row polymorphism over plane lists (P16). |
| M1 Deterministic acceptance | **met** | Every family is syntactic and terminating: plane-map lookup, half-open arithmetic in a fixed linear index fragment, term normalization with a fixed atom bound; no search, no budget, no solver. |
| M2 No unstated edge, no unchosen cost | **met** | Epochs, atoms, runs and punctures are ghost; the occupancy-as-data rule forbids a bit from discharging an R1 obligation, so no runtime comparison satisfies a rule of acceptance; every branch in P1, P4, P8 and P11 is one the writer wrote. |
| M3 Trusted base | **met** | The only new base entries are a foreign backing's plane map and an allocator's declared invariant, both ordinary enumerated declarations with boundary obligations; no writer-reachable escape is added. |
| M4 Writer regularity | **violated** | Two spellings name one construct: an element is `[i]` or `#n`, and absence is a `punct` entry, an `Empty` run *or* an occupancy plane; the collapse (atoms only) is available but costs P5's arithmetic, so the duplication is chosen, not accidental — recorded as a violation rather than argued away. |
| M5 Acceptance independent of permission | **met** | Omitting a loop's access row leaves the loop sequential and still accepted; no acceptance verdict reads a permission judgment. |
| M6 Soundness evidence | **partial** | The bounded small-model check is unusually cheap here — per plane the state space is (4 run shapes x bounded punctures x epoch) — but the adequacy theorem is the stated later obligation (owner decision 9). |
| M7 Repairable rejection | **met** | Every rejection is an unsatisfied arithmetic goal over a named tree node (`k != i && k != j`, `k < len`, `len0 < cap0`, "the `else` arm"), which is a non-empty payload naming a location. |
| M8 Teaching and retrieval budget | **partial** | It deletes modes, regions, loans, region blocks and the borrow rules; it adds the plane map, split algebra, run families, punctures, epochs and atoms — provisionally a wash against the ~18.5k subsystem share, with the global K test red for reasons no candidate fixes. |
| M9 Measured performance floor | **partial** | The strongest available evidence points here (per-plane `!alias.scope`: 8 vector ops / 0 guards / 121 asm lines vs 65 / 29 / 2132) but it is retired-prototype evidence and unmeasurable on the current compiler until a fact channel exists. |
| M10 Checking cost and edit stability | **partial** | Plane lookup is O(1) and extent arithmetic is linear in the fragment, but the join term is bounded by `2^k` for a fixed spec constant `k`, which is a large constant to defend, and edit reach stops at the interface. |
| M11 Evolution with stated loss | **met** | The verdict diff is computable over the retained corpus; the named loss is the intrusive, address-identified structure (§6). |

**Counts: met 17, partial 9, violated 1 (M4).**

### 4.2 The price this candidate charges the compiler

| Forbidden to the compiler | Ground |
|---|---|
| Emitting a distinctness fact for two planes whose carving does not prove it (e.g. a recycled extent, absent the arena invariant) | R4 soundness |
| Relocating a plane that any live `elem` identity names, unless the plane is declared `permutable` and the epoch is bumped | R8a |
| Reordering or coalescing planes of a backing, once the plane map states offsets or alignment | R8b |
| Inserting a bounds, occupancy, generation or epoch comparison; all four are ghost | M2(ii) |
| Choosing a tile, worker count or schedule that changes which programs are accepted | M5 |
| Deriving a run or a puncture set from anything but the syntactic state transitions | M1 |

Freedoms retained: any schedule for a permitted overlap, stack coloring and reuse
of ended storage, loop versioning and remainder loops, and every transformation
whose facts are licensed by the tree.

### 4.3 Writer cost

| Unit | Cost |
|---|---|
| Per type | one line per plane (which is the layout declaration the writer wanted anyway) |
| Per signature | one identity parameter per touched plane or extent + one access-row clause + entry/exit states only where they change; measured against R15's metric: linear in **planes touched**, not fields declared |
| Per loop | 1 line (the per-iteration access row), plus 1 more if the loop changes a run |
| Per join | 0, unless the state term exceeds `k` atoms (then 1 `invariant` line) |
| Per statement | 0; a `use` step only where the index fragment does not close a goal |
| Per pool | one ghost atom per occupant type + one plane-level invariant, stated once (P3) |
| Per arena | one written free-list invariant + ~6 `use` steps, once per arena implementation (P2) |
