## 5. Consequences at D5–D13

| Point | Forced | Foreclosed |
|---|---|---|
| **D5** interference source | **Effect footprints over identities** (AI-D5-01, SYS-D5-01) keyed to the tree, refined by **Affine or polyhedral dependence** restricted to the linear index fragment; the optimizer channel is per-instruction `!alias.scope` per plane and `llvm.experimental.noalias.scope.decl` per tile (EVIDENCE D1, D2) | **Runtime dependence tracking with static summaries** and **Transactions and speculation** (M2(ii)); **Loans on references beside footprints** — there are no reference-borne facts left to judge, so PAR-1's loan clause retires |
| **D6** distinctness at boundaries | **Split and partition tokens**, **Index-arithmetic distinctness**, **Apartness as a judgment** (for pool atoms), and **Distinct names are distinct storage** *only via the plane map*, never via name inequality | **Distinct by default, call-site proof** as a primitive (C3's unsound-by-name form): distinctness is derived from the carving, so two identity parameters that are planes of one backing are distinct without a call-site obligation, and two extents of one plane are never distinct without arithmetic; **Dynamic distinctness check** |
| **D7** contract vocabulary | **Requires/ensures over identity states** + **Footprint and frame clauses** + **Existential result identities** + **Effect rows as the contract** with row polymorphism over plane lists (P16 needs it) | **No contracts: whole-program inference**; **Capabilities instead of contracts**; **Prophecies and backward functions** (nothing is a borrow, so there is no final value to prophesy) |
| **D8** placement and relocation | **Allocation that never relocates by construction** as the default; **Reallocation as a contract-visible name change**; **Pools with stable index handles**; **Arenas and regions with whole-region release**; **Writer-declared placement per binding** (the plane map is the declaration) | **Moves as byte copies the compiler elides** for any plane with live element identities; **Relocation with a fixup channel** in its runtime-rewriting form (nothing rewrites stored pointers; the handle-through-map is the only fixup); a moving collector |
| **D9** containers and elements | Largely pre-decided: **Structural decomposition: chunks, columns, lanes** + **Path identity `'v[i]`** + **Bounded views and proved subrange subdivision** + **Ring buffers and two-span views** (the third run family) + **Affine elements, vacancy and occupancy** resolved as *vacancy is data* | **Per-element ghost tokens** (one token per slot is unaffordable beside a run); **Generations and epochs** in their runtime-compare form; **Index-only access with bounds proofs** as the *only* form (element descriptors exist); a `sparse` run family (the P11 residue) |
| **D10** concurrency | **Deterministic parallelism only** and **Determinism by model: barrier launches**; **Per-core ownership: shards and context discipline** (a shard is a plane partition); a lock, when it arrives, is custodian of a **plane set**, not of an object graph | **Message passing only: nothing shared** (planes are shared and partitioned, not sent); **Convergent or monotone shared state** as the primary story; fine-grained pointer-shared mutation across threads |
| **D11** external resources | **Foreign identity: retain no contents fact** as a *plane attribute* (`foreign` planes, R14(iv)); **Backing as a file or mapping**; **Three identities per descriptor** fits the tree (wrapper value, description backing with a cursor plane, foreign contents plane) | **Ambient and forgeable host access**; **Trusted adapters outside the language** as an exception (they are ordinary M3 entries under owner decision 15) |
| **D12** surface form | **Annotation site placement** = type definitions, signatures and loop heads only; **Qualifier-prefixed types** for plane declarations; **Region sigil fate** = the sigil becomes a plane/extent identity and loses every region meaning | **Modes as sugar over pointer plus state** (`&`/`&uniq` do not desugar into anything here — there is no permission on a reference to sugar); **Region block and borrow-endpoint spelling**; **Algorithm and schedule split** (the access row is in the signature, not in a second artifact) |
| **D13** validation | **Bounded exhaustive enumeration** (the per-plane state space is finite and tiny, so M6(i)'s small-model check is unusually cheap); **Fixed discriminating program set**; **Fact-channel review and runtime attribute checks** for the per-plane alias facts before they ship; **Real programs as discriminator** using the SoA corpus (compute-bench, zlib-core-kernels) | **Dual acceptance and acceptance-set diffs** as a migration path (the reference forms change shape, so the acceptance sets are not comparable program-by-program); **Gradual aliasing policy per module** |

---

## 6. Honest weaknesses

1. **Pointer-shaped structures pay an indirection and a ghost layer.** P3 costs
   one ghost atom per occupant, an existential in the element type and a
   plane-level invariant; P4 costs an identity parameter on the struct. An
   *intrusive* structure — a list node embedded in an object, reached by address
   and recovered with `container_of` — is **not expressible**. It must become a
   pool with index links. This is a real capability loss and it is stated, not
   argued away.
2. **M4 is violated deliberately.** Two element spellings (`[i]`, `#n`), two
   plane refinements (`@e`, `#n`) and three carriers of absence (`punct`, an
   `Empty` run, an occupancy plane). The collapse to atoms alone is available and
   costs P5's arithmetic; the collapse to indices alone loses P3 and P13.
3. **Punctures are a second state axis.** `run x punct` multiplies cases, and the
   bound on `|punct|` (textual take sites in scope) is a syntactic device that a
   reader must learn before writing a loop that takes.
4. **The join term's `k`.** A fixed specification constant bounding the condition
   atoms in one state term is deterministic but arbitrary, and `2^k` is a large
   constant to defend under M10.
5. **Arenas are not automatic.** The plane algebra proves containment and split
   disjointness; recycling needs a written invariant per arena. P2 passes with
   writer work that P5 and P6 do not need.
6. **P11's residue.** A cache of affine, non-default-constructible values is not
   expressible: it needs a sparse per-slot init state the run vocabulary refuses.
7. **Generics over plane lists is unbuilt.** P16's generic pool does not type
   without row polymorphism over the plane map of a type parameter, and the
   identity count scales with the *decomposition* of the element type, which is
   precisely where signature explosion would show up.
8. **The split window looks like a borrow.** It is scoped, it suspends the
   parent's access, and its children may not be stored.

### The strongest objection, and the answer

> **Objection.** This is a data-parallel array language wearing a systems
> language's clothes. It wins P5 and P6 — which were never the hard cases — and
> pays for it in P3 and P4, the pointer-shaped programs that are the entire
> reason ownership systems exist. Worse, the win it advertises (per-column
> `!alias.scope`) is available to *any* candidate that gives struct fields
> identities; the plane algebra, the split tokens, the epochs and the atoms are
> all being bought for a fact that field identity alone already delivers. And the
> split window is a borrow with better marketing: it suspends the parent, it is
> scoped, and its children may not escape — so the OWN-6 wall has been renamed,
> not removed.

**Answer, in four parts.**

(a) *P3 and P4 are not refused; they are re-shaped, and the re-shape is the one
the evidence already uses.* P4 is accepted with one type parameter and the
ladder's Step-3 proof — and, unlike a borrow-based design, `push` is **never
blocked** by the cursor's existence, which is P4's actual requirement. P3's link
updates through several paths are accepted *sequentially with no proof at all*
(R9's negative test), which the reference-exclusivity family fails. What P3 costs
is a ghost atom — and every candidate that answers "removal invalidates every
path to `m`" pays that cost somewhere: as a generation compared at run time
(M2-refused), as a provenance token threaded by hand, or as a borrow that forbids
the back edge outright.

(b) *Field identity alone does not deliver the win.* Fields give a static,
finite set of names. The measured programs need three more things from the same
relation: a **dynamic** carve (P2's `alloc`, P6's `split`), an **element**
refinement (P1's `i != j`, P17's `i < len`) and a **range** refinement (P6's
worker slices, PAR-2's tiles). A field-identity candidate needs a second
mechanism for each, and C2 warns that two mechanisms for one relation silently
retune R4, R5 and R6 against each other. Columns-first is the claim that *one*
containment tree answers all four consumers — that is what is being bought, and
P1, P2, P5 and P6 are four different withdrawals from the same account.

(c) *The split window is not a borrow, in the one way that matters.* A borrow is
a property of a reference with a duration: the reference's liveness decides
legality, and the parent is dead for the whole duration. A split is arithmetic on
an access set: the parent keeps the **residue** and can read and write it
throughout (P1's `k != i && k != j` read is *accepted*, and no borrow-based
design accepts it), the descriptors that name the children are ordinary copyable
values with no lifetime, and the window is the construct the writer wrote rather
than a region inferred from last use. The OWN-6 wall was non-local
reborrow reasoning about references; here every rejection is a local arithmetic
goal over an extent, with the missing fact in the payload (M7).

(d) *The part of the objection that lands.* The escape restriction is real: a
child view may not be stored into long-lived storage, so a design that wants
stored sub-views of a live parent is not served. Columns-first accepts that as
its stated boundary — stored interior access goes through a `handle` and its
plane, which survives everything except retirement — and the price is one
indirection on exactly the shapes (graphs, cursors, intrusive lists) where the
candidate is honest about being second-best.


# File: candidate-generational-handles.md

# Candidate core model: generational handles into named pools

Research date: 2026-09-16. Candidate generator "generational-handles". This
file builds one candidate for D1–D4 of
[OPTIONS.md](../../whitefoot-access-effects-research/research/investigations/access-effects/OPTIONS.md)
against the settled requirement list (VERDICT-D0 §2), the couplings (§4), the
premises (§5), the hazard ladder (MECHANISM-MAP §3) and the discriminating
programs (PROGRAMS.md). It makes no comparison to other candidates. Every
program claim is shown as pseudocode with per-line accept/reject comments and
the fact used. Supersede in place.

**Headline honesty statement, stated before the argument so nothing below
reads as a hedge:** the candidate has two tiers. Tier A carries the
generation as a ghost term and emits no check at all; all fourteen derived
programs are decided in Tier A. Tier B materialises the generation and turns
staleness into a written `Stale` arm; Tier B is an **M2(ii) violation by the
verdict list's own enumeration** ("generational or epoch checks that safety
depends on, and a Vale-style check wrapped as a library outcome are refused by
(ii)"). §6 states the case for Tier B and concedes the refusal. The candidate
stands or falls on Tier A.

---

## 1. The tuple

| Point | Family chosen (name exactly as in OPTIONS.md) | Members drawn on |
|---|---|---|
| **D1** | **Generation-stamped handle**, combined with **Index into a named pool / row key** | AI-D1-12 (statically tracked generation counter) is the load-bearing member; SYS-D1-03 ((index, generation) copyable handle) is the surface shape; HIS-D1-10 FLOATED (per-slot generation distinguishes reuse) is the slot rule; SYS-D1-02 ((cache, slot) in a type-stable pool) and SYS-D1-04 (index only, append-only pool) give the root; RAD-D1-06 (generation compare yields typed outcome) is admitted **only** as Tier B. Step vocabulary borrowed and named: HIS-D1-03 ADOPTED (resolved place: root plus ordered steps), AI-D1-04 (proved range `'v[lo..hi]`), AI-D1-05 / SYS-D1-17 (existential identity per formation) for the slot a runtime `alloc` returns. Refused inside the family: HIS-D1-11 (generation alone as store safety), HIS-D1-12 (Vale runtime-validated refs with a trap), HIS-D1-13 (runtime owner IDs in the checker relation), HIS-D1-25 (bare `u64` index into a pool). |
| **D2** | **Runtime-carried state with proofs deleting the check** | AI-D2-10 (runtime tags, proofs eliminate checks), THE-D2-23 (runtime tag with proofs deleting the check), RAD-D2-10 (generation/epoch field in the value) — taken in the one form in which the family's own tension line ("violates M2 unless every check is provably removed") is discharged: **every check is removed in Tier A, and the residual carrier is materialised only where a written `open` consumes it**. HIS-D2-08 (runtime proof table / occupancy bitmap / extra scan) and HIS-D2-09 (runtime drop flags) stay refused: nothing the *compiler* maintains exists at run time. Adjacent members kept: HIS-D2-12 ADOPTED (capability as an ordinary value, no ambient resource) — a handle is an ordinary value, not an authority. |
| **D3** | **Occupancy as separate data or runtime discriminant**, over a **Three-state minimum** ghost vocabulary, joined by **State as a term over captured conditions** | SYS-D3-18 (validity as a parallel array) and HIS-D3-04 ADOPTED (vacancy as an Option-shaped value) are the primary: for a pool slot, "partially initialised" is not a language state but the slot's own occupant data, read by the writer's own `match`. AI-D3-01 / THE-D3-01 (Init/Uninit/Gone per identity) remain the ghost vocabulary for every non-pool storage. AI-D3-07 / SYS-D3-14 / THE-D3-12 / HIS-D3-07 (term over captured conditions) is the join rule (C6). HIS-D3-12, HIS-D3-16, HIS-D3-17 stay refused *as stated*: no per-slot tag, bitmap or discriminant is **language state**; here the discriminant is program data and the compiler never consults it. |
| **D4** | **Dynamic exclusivity where static proof fails**, layered on **Unrestricted aliasing, safety from per-storage state** as the base stance | THE-D4-02 / AI-D4-01 / SYS-D4-01 (several writable names, safety from state, loss localised to coinciding storages) is the default: exclusivity is never a safety rule, only a fact. SYS-D4-10 (proved-disjoint byte ranges) and HIS-D4-13 ADOPTED (proved half-open view extents) buy the fact statically. RAD-D4-04 (typed-outcome dynamic exclusivity check) and SYS-D4-09 (Swift checked exclusivity, flag per dynamic site) supply the fallback, reshaped so that the branch is **pure index arithmetic the writer wrote** and its path condition *is* the disjointness fact. AI-D4-05 / HIS-D4-03 (read-only as a type flag, never a loan) is kept (C10). HIS-D4-01 (OWN-5 unconditional exclusivity) is dropped. |

### Why these four cohere

One thesis runs through all four:

> **Every fact the checker uses is either proved statically from written
> premises, or is the path condition of a branch the writer wrote on data the
> writer bound. Nothing is established by state the compiler maintains.**

- D1 makes identity a **value** (`(pool, slot, generation)`) rather than a
  scope or a duration. A value can be stored in a struct (P4's cursor), read
  back out of data (P3's back edges), compared, passed through a signature,
  and survive third-party relocation (P13) — the four places where a
  duration-shaped identity breaks.
- D2 follows immediately: if identity is a value, its state cannot live on
  the pointer (C12), so state lives per storage and the carrier question
  becomes "ghost or materialised". The family's answer — materialised, with
  proof deleting the check — is exactly "ghost wherever the proof reaches".
- D3 follows from D1's reuse: a pool that reuses slots needs *occupancy*,
  and a reusable identity makes occupancy a property of the pool's data, not
  a state of a name. Dissolving occupancy into data removes R1(i)'s hole-read
  hazard for pools entirely: there is nothing to read without matching.
- D4 follows from D2: because safety is per storage, several writable handles
  into one pool are already safe, so exclusivity is downgraded from a rule to
  a fact, and a fact may be bought by arithmetic or left unbought (R4
  tolerates a missing "distinct"; R9 is then satisfied by construction).

The coupling table confirms the fit: C1 (one refinement vocabulary), C5
(sequential aliased writes allowed, loss localised), C9 (backing identity for
containers), C12 (per-storage state primary; pointers carry no permission) are
all this tuple's direct consequences. C4 (`own` aggregates as handles) is
generalised: *every* long-lived aggregate travels as a handle.

---

## 2. The model

### 2.1 Notation

```text
pool P : Pool<Node>            // a storage root with a brand; declared, written in WF
h : H<P>                       // copyable handle VALUE.  runtime {idx}  + ghost {σ, γ}
ptr<π, T>                      // pointer to a place;  π ::= root | π.f | π[σ] | π[lo..hi)
                               // `ro ptr<π,T>` is the read-only flag (C10), never a loan

state(π) ∈ {Init, Uninit, Gone}          // ghost, three-state minimum; non-pool storages
gen(P[σ]) : Gen                          // ghost monotone counter term per slot
Live(P)  : set of σ                      // ghost set of allocated slots
Live(h)  ≜ σ(h) ∈ Live(P) ∧ gen(P[σ(h)]) = γ(h)
backing('v) = 'b                         // container backing identity (C9)
```

A **place** is a root plus ordered steps (HIS-D1-03). Steps are field names,
ghost slot names, and proved half-open ranges. Steps are *not* parameters:
`Cols` with eight columns is one identity with eight places (R15's metric).

### 2.2 What a pointer's type says

`ptr<π, T>` says exactly three things: the place `π` it names, whether it is
read-only, and `T`. It says nothing about duration, exclusivity, permission,
or who else points there. A dereference of `ptr<π,T>` is accepted iff the
checker holds, at that point: `state(π) = Init`, `layout(root(π))` unchanged
since formation, and no storage-ending event on `root(π)` since formation.

`H<P>` says: the pool it indexes. Applying a handle to the wrong pool is a
type error (this is the candidate's answer to the HIS-D1-11 refusal, "a
generation alone does not prevent a handle being applied to the wrong store").

### 2.3 What the checker holds per storage

| Kept per | Fact |
|---|---|
| every root | `layout`, `backing` (containers), written `invariant`s keyed to the root |
| every place | `state ∈ {Init, Uninit, Gone}` as a **term**: a list of (path-condition literal conjunction, state) pairs, collapsed when equal |
| every pool | `Live(P)` (ghost set), `gen(P[σ])` per named slot, the pool's declared invariant |
| every handle binding | `σ(h)`, `γ(h)` (ghost); `Live(h)` is derived, never stored |
| every statement | read / write / end footprints over places (D5 consequence) |
| every pair of places | the R4 disjointness relation over the containment structure — never name inequality (P2: `S` contains `b1`) |

### 2.4 State transitions

| Operation | Ghost effect | Runtime |
|---|---|---|
| `h = alloc(P)` | fresh ghost `σ ∉ Live(P)`; `Live(P) ∪= {σ}`; `state(P[σ]) := Uninit`; `γ(h) := gen(P[σ])` | the pool's own written free-list pop |
| `put(P[σ], v)` / `init` | `state := Init` | store |
| `v = take(P[σ])` | `state := Uninit`; contents facts on `P[σ]` killed | load (+ discriminant store if occupancy is data) |
| `old = replace(P[σ], v)` | `state` stays `Init`; contents facts killed | load+store |
| `free(P, h)` | requires `Live(h)`; `state(P[σ(h)]) := Gone`; `gen(P[σ(h)]) := succ(γ)`; `Live(P) \= {σ(h)}`; **every fact `gen(P[σ(h)]) = γ_old` is killed**, so every other handle with that generation is dead | free-list push |
| `move x` (relocating) | `state(place(x)) := Gone` permanently; place never revived | byte copy or nothing |
| `compact(P)` | ends every place `P[σ].f` (layout version bumps; interior pointers refused); **`Live(P)` and every `gen` survive** — the footprint names `backing(P)` and `slotmap(P)`, not `Live(P)` | slot map rewrite |
| `grow(P)` / `push(v,x)` | `backing` := existential fresh `'b2` when `cap0 < need`, else unchanged; **handles unaffected** (the handle names the root, not the backing) | realloc |

Two rules carry the weight:

1. **`free` bumps the generation and kills by generation, not by handle.** A
   hole or an end is a property of the storage, so it is visible through every
   alias at once (P7), and reuse of the bytes cannot revive the old identity
   (P2, R1(a)(ii)).
2. **`Gen` is a symbolic successor term in Tier A** — unbounded, so no
   wraparound and no retirement. Only Tier B, where `Gen` is a machine word,
   needs `free` to carry a `Retired` outcome (see §6); this answers the HIS
   refusal "a finite generation must retire/refuse on exhaustion or justify
   safe reuse, not wrap".

### 2.5 Joins and loop heads

**Join.** Per place, the incoming states are combined into a term
`[(c₁, s₁), (c₂, s₂), …]` where each `cᵢ` is the conjunction of literals that
labels its edge. A use of the place requires the state to be uniform under the
*current* path condition, decided by entailment of a conjunction of literals
by a conjunction of literals — linear, total, deterministic (M1, M10). No
drop flag, no bookkeeping: the writer's own branches carry the state (P8).
When no atom discriminates, the place goes to `⊤` and the diagnostic names the
two paths and their differing states (M7).

Handle liveness joins the same way: `Live(h)` is a conjunction of a set
membership and a generation equality, each a fact carried per edge.

**Loop head.** The checker requires a written `invariant` clause **only** for:

- a place whose state the body leaves different from the state it found, and
- each pool the body frees into, for every handle-liveness fact the loop body
  uses after the free.

Everything else is framed in automatically (R6). A loop that takes and puts
back (P8's `loop { take(p); …; put(p) }`) writes nothing.

### 2.6 What a signature states

```text
fn f<'P, 'v>(h: H<'P>, v: &Vector<'v>, i: u64) -> R
  reads    'P[σ(h)].data, 'v.meta
  writes   'v.backing['v.len .. 'v.len+1)
  ends     -                                   // storage-ending events, R8a
  requires Live(h),  state('v) = Init,  i < len('v)
  ensures  Live(h),  backing('v) = if cap0 >= len0+1 { 'b0 } else { fresh 'b2 }
  outcomes Ok(R)                               // R12; arms listed, each with its ensures
```

The vocabulary is exactly R7(a)'s list: per-identity entry/exit states,
returned interior pointers, fresh allocations, read/write/end footprints,
outcomes, resource effects. Existential results (`fresh 'b2`, `∃σ`) are the
mechanism for `reserve` and `alloc`.

### 2.7 What the writer writes, and where

| Where | What | Typical count |
|---|---|---|
| signature | one identity parameter per **root** touched (not per place); one footprint row; one `requires`/`ensures` pair per storage whose state changes; one existential clause per replaced backing | P5 `kernel(c: Cols)`: 1 parameter, 1 row. P9 `reserve`: 1 parameter, 1 row, 1 existential |
| pool type, once | the pool's invariant (`disjoint extents`, `next/prev point into Live`) and its proof: 3–8 `use` steps | once per pool type, reused everywhere (P3's requirement, R6's test) |
| loop head | one clause per storage the body leaves changed; one per pool the body frees into | P5, P6, P8's loop: 0 |
| join | nothing | 0 |
| statement | one proof or one written outcome arm per partial operation (R11); one `use` step where the fixed arithmetic family does not reach | P1: 1 (`k ≠ i ∧ k ≠ j`); P5, P6: 0 |

### 2.8 What is erased

All of: ghost slot names `σ`, generation terms `γ`, `Live(P)`, `state`, every
invariant and `use` step, every footprint, every distinctness fact
(M6(iii)). What survives into the lowered program:

| Runtime datum | Present iff |
|---|---|
| `h.idx` | always (it is the program's index) |
| `h.gen` | **iff some Tier-B `open` in the program consumes it** — a checkable erasure property |
| slot map indirection | iff the pool is declared compacting |
| occupancy discriminant / validity array | iff the writer declared the slot occupant as `Option`-shaped or declared a parallel validity array; dense pools carry neither |

---

## 3. Derivations

Notation for comments: `// accept: fact` or `// reject: missing fact`.

### P1 Container split with a runtime index

```text
v: Vector<u64> in 'v, backing 'b, len n
(part_i, part_j) = take2(v, i, j)
  // requires i < n, j < n, i != j            -- written proof or a written try_split2 arm
  // accept: i<n, j<n from the writer's premises; i!=j from the writer's premise
  // effect: state('b[i]) := Uninit ; state('b[j]) := Uninit ; two exclusive element views
write(part_i, x)            // accept: part_i is an exclusive view of 'b[i]; footprint {'b[i]}
write(part_j, y)            // accept: footprint {'b[j]};  distinct('b[i],'b[j]) from i!=j
  // PAR: the two footprints are proved non-interfering -> R5(i) overlap permitted
read(v[k])                  // reject: state('b[k]) is Uninit under the term
                            //   [(k=i, Uninit), (k=j, Uninit), (k!=i & k!=j, Init)]
                            //   missing fact: k != i AND k != j        (M7 payload)
if k != i && k != j { read(v[k]) }   // accept: path condition entails the Init arm.
                                     //   the ONLY branch here is the writer's (M2(e))
put2(part_i, part_j)        // accept: states return to Init
push(v, x)                  // accept: requires state('b[i]) = Init for all i<n -- both back
```

No runtime check is emitted; the generation machinery is not used (a vector is
not a pool). **Verdict: accepted as required.**

### P2 Arena with independently released blocks

```text
arena A : Pool<Block> with metadata M(A), byte storage S(A)
  invariant IA: forall p,q in Live(A). p != q => extent(p) disjoint extent(q)   // written once
b1 = alloc(A,64)   // accept: fresh ghost σ1 ∉ Live(A); Live(A) ∪= {σ1}; γ1 = gen(A[σ1])
b2 = alloc(A,64)   // accept: fresh σ2; σ2 != σ1 by freshness (NOT by name inequality)
b3 = alloc(A,64)   // accept: fresh σ3
  // footprint of alloc = {M(A), Live(A), gen(A)} ; NOT S(A)[σ] for any live σ
fill(b1) || fill(b2) || fill(b3)
  // footprints {S(A)[σ1]}, {S(A)[σ2]}, {S(A)[σ3]}
  // accept overlap: pairwise disjoint by IA instantiated at (σ1,σ2),(σ1,σ3),(σ2,σ3)
  // accept: no exclusive hold on A is needed -- the writes name sub-places of S(A),
  //         and M(A) is disjoint from S(A) by the containment structure
free(A, b2)        // accept: Live(b2); state(A[σ2]) := Gone; gen(A[σ2]) := succ(γ2);
                   //   Live(A) \= {σ2}.  Kills every fact `gen(A[σ2]) = γ2`.
b4 = alloc(A,32)   // accept: fresh σ4; its extent may reuse b2's BYTES
p2 = old pointer into b2 ; read(p2)
                   // reject: state(A[σ2]) = Gone.  fact used: the ending event at free.
                   //   address reuse by σ4 is irrelevant: σ4 is a different identity
                   //   (R1(a)(ii)); no distinctness between S(A) and any live block is
                   //   claimed or needed (R4(b) negative test)
                   // allocator metadata written inside b2's bytes: admitted, R14(iii)
read(b1); free(A,b1); free(A,b3); free(A,b4)
                   // accept: each requires Live(·), each true exactly once
end of A           // requires Live(A) = {} -- discharged: 4 allocs, 4 frees (R2)
```

Cost: `IA` is a written invariant with a proof (3–8 `use` steps) once per pool
type; without it the three `fill`s do not overlap (they stay sequential under
M5, not rejected). **Verdict: accepted with a stated cost** (one written pool
invariant; the parallel arm degrades to sequential if it is absent).

### P3 Graph with back edges in a pool

```text
pool G : Pool<Node{ next: H<G>, prev: H<G>, data: u64 }>
  invariant IG: forall σ in Live(G). Live(G[σ].next) && Live(G[σ].prev)   // written once
                                                                          // R6's "stated once and reused"
// insert n between a and b: four link writes
G[σn].next := b        // accept: Live(n) ; footprint {G[σn].next}
G[σn].prev := a        // accept: footprint {G[σn].prev}
G[σa].next := n        // accept: Live(a) ; footprint {G[σa].next}
                       //   several writable paths to one node: permitted, safety is per
                       //   storage (D4 base stance) -> R9's negative test passes
G[σb].prev := n        // accept: Live(b)
use IG_restore(n,a,b)  // accept: the four writes re-establish IG; a written finite step,
                       //   verified, not rediscovered (M1)
// remove m
unlink(m); free(G, m)  // accept: gen(G[σm]) := succ; Live(G) \= {σm}
                       //   every handle value equal to m, wherever stored, is now dead:
                       //   the killed fact is `gen(G[σm]) = γm`, not "the binding m"
use IG_restore_after_remove(m)   // accept: the unlink re-established IG before the free
h = G[σx].next ; read(G[h].data)
  // accept: Live(h) from IG instantiated at σx.  NO generation comparison is emitted.
  //   this is the whole point: the invariant, not a runtime compare, discharges liveness
p = stale handle to m ; read(G[p].data)
  // reject: Live(p) requires gen(G[σm]) = γm, killed at the free.  fact named by M7.
parallel map over Live(G): G[σ].data := f(G[σ].data)
  // accept: per-iteration footprint {G[σ].data}; σ ranges injectively over Live(G)
  //   -> pairwise distinct by injectivity of the slot->place map.  R5(i).
parallel map over a TRAVERSAL (h := h.next): G[h].data := ...
  // reject: two data-derived handles have opaque slot names; IG gives liveness, not
  //   injectivity.  missing fact: distinct(σ(h1), σ(h2)).  Repair: iterate the pool,
  //   or write an acyclicity/injectivity invariant.  (Honest limit, §6.)
```

**Verdict: accepted with a stated cost** (one pool invariant plus two `use`
steps at insert/remove; the traversal-order parallel map is refused and the
repair is named).

### P4 Cursor over a growing vector

```text
c = Cursor { at: H<'v>, i: 0 }        // a HANDLE to the vector, not a pointer to its backing
a = c.read()
  // accept: requires Live(c.at) && state('v) = Init && c.i < len('v)
  //   c.i = 0 < n from the writer's premise n > 0
push(v, 5)
  // effect: backing('v) = if cap0 >= n+1 { 'b0 } else { fresh 'b2 } ; len('v) := n+1
  //   footprint {'v.meta, 'v.backing}.  Live(c.at) is a fact about 'v, NOT about
  //   backing('v): the push footprint does not name it, so R6 frames it in.
b = c.read()
  // accept: Live(c.at) survived; c.i = 0 < n+1.
  //   NO PROOF OF len0 < cap0 IS NEEDED -- this is what the handle indirection buys.
  //   cost: c.read() is two loads (backing pointer, then element), stated under M9.
q = pointer_of(v[0]) ; push(v, 6) ; read(q)
  // reject: q names place 'b0[0]; push may end 'b0.  missing fact: len0 < cap0.
  //   the pointer form still pays the proof; the handle form does not.
free(v); c.read()
  // reject: state('v) = Gone.  permanent; no later operation revives it (R1(a)(ii))
```

**Verdict: accepted as required**, and strictly: validity is decided by state
and proof, and `push` is never blocked.

### P5 Struct-of-arrays kernel

```text
struct Cols { a,b,c,d,e,f,g,h : buffer<u64> }     // one root 'c, eight places 'c.a .. 'c.h
for i in 0..n {
  a[i] = f(a[i], c[i], d[i])
    // accept: state('c.a[i]) = Init (whole-buffer Init; no occupancy, no discriminant)
    // accept: distinct('c.a[i], 'c.c[i]) etc. by the containment structure: distinct
    //   FIELD PATHS of one root are disjoint by construction, not by name inequality
    // licensed to lowering: per-load disjointness for every pair of the eight (R4)
  b[i] = g(b[i], e[i], f[i], g[i], h[i])          // same
}
  // PAR-2: iteration i footprint = { 'c.a[i], 'c.b[i] } write, { 'c.c[i].. } read
  //        iteration j: disjoint by i != j from the loop index -> overlap permitted (R5(i))
  // overflow behaviour of f and g selected per site (R11); no arm needed if proved
```

No handle, no generation, no occupancy: the candidate charges this program
nothing. Writer cost: one identity parameter for `Cols` (steps are free), zero
loop clauses. **Verdict: accepted as required.** The obvious shape is the fast
shape here.

### P6 Range partition helper

```text
out: buffer<u8> of n in 'o ; k workers ; s = n / k          // s proved: k > 0 written
for w in 0..k {
  helper(view(out, w*s .. (w+1)*s), input)
    // view's place is 'o[w*s .. (w+1)*s), a proved half-open extent (HIS-D4-13)
    // helper's signature: `writes 'slice[0..len)` -- the caller judges from it alone (R7)
    // accept: w*s <= (w+1)*s from s >= 0 ; (w+1)*s <= n from w < k and s = n/k
}
  // PAR-2 overlap: for w1 != w2, [w1*s,(w1+1)*s) disjoint [w2*s,(w2+1)*s)
  //   decided by the fixed affine-arithmetic family: normalise both extents to
  //   (base + coeff*w, length) and compare; deterministic, terminating, no search (M1)
  // accept: k appears once, as the loop bound; no worker count elsewhere
```

**Verdict: accepted as required.**

### P7 Take, put, replace through aliases

```text
A : slot holding an affine value ; p, q : H<A-pool> with sigma(p) = sigma(q), gamma equal
v = take(p)      // accept: Live(p), state(A) = Init -> state(A) := Uninit
read(q)          // reject: state(A) = Uninit.  fact used: state is a property of the
                 //   STORAGE; both handles name sigma, so the hole is visible through q
put(q, move v)   // accept: state(A) := Init ; the OTHER alias fills the hole
read(p)          // accept: state(A) = Init
old = replace(p, new)
                 // accept: state stays Init; contents facts on A killed
read(q)          // accept: reads new.  fact used: the kill at replace removed the old
                 //   contents fact; the new one is keyed to the same place
free A           // accept: gen(A[sigma]) := succ ; Live \= {sigma}
read(p)          // reject: Live(p) false.  permanent.
read(q)          // reject: same fact, same message -- one kill, both aliases
```

**Verdict: accepted as required.**

### P8 Conditional release and loop exits

```text
if c { free(a) } else { free(b) }
  // state(a) = [(c, Gone), (!c, Init)] ; state(b) = [(c, Init), (!c, Gone)]
  // NO drop flag: nothing is stored; the term is ghost and erased (M2(ii))
use(b)          // reject under no path condition: state(b) is not uniform.
                // diagnostic: "state differs on the two paths of the `if` at L1:
                //   Init under `c`, Gone under `!c`" -- names the path (P8's requirement)
if c { use(b); free(b) } else { use(a); free(a) }
  // accept: under `c`, entailment c |= c gives state(b) = Init ; free(b) discharges
  // accept: under `!c`, symmetric.  R2: exactly one free per resource per path
loop { if stop { break }; v = take(p); …; put(p, v) }
  // loop head: state(p) = Init on entry and on the back edge -> NO invariant clause written
  // accept: break edge carries state(p) = Init (the take/put pair closed before it)
free(p)         // accept: state(p) = Init on every incoming edge of the loop exit
```

**Verdict: accepted as required.** Cost: the state term's entailment is
restricted to conjunctions of literals, so the join is linear in the number of
incoming edges and the check is linear in captured atoms (M10); a condition
the writer did not branch on is not an atom, so no path-sensitive search
exists.

### P9 A callee that changes storage state

```text
fn drain<'s>(x: &Slot<'s,T>) -> T
  requires state('s) = Init
  ensures  state('s) = Uninit
  writes   's
fn reserve<'v>(v: &Vector<'v>, m: u64)
  writes   'v.meta, backing('v)
  ends     backing('v) when cap0 < m
  ensures  backing('v) = if cap0 >= m { 'b0 } else { fresh 'b2 }
         && len('v) = len0                       // R6: len facts survive a backing change
fn pick<'x,'y>(c: bool, x: ptr<'x,T>, y: ptr<'y,T>) -> ptr<ite(c,'x,'y), T>
  // the result identity is a TERM over the captured condition -- the same mechanism
  // as D3's join rule, reused at the interface (one vocabulary, C1)

// caller:
t = drain(s)        // accept from the signature alone: state('s) := Uninit here
read(s)             // reject: state('s) = Uninit.  body never opened (R7)
reserve(v, 100)     // accept; any ptr into 'b0 is refused after unless cap0 >= 100 proved
len_fact_after = len(v)   // accept: len fact framed in -- reserve's footprint does not
                          //   name it.  (R6's measured tax: 0 rebinds needed here)
z = pick(c, px, py) ; write(z, 1)
  // accept: footprint { ite(c,'x,'y) } ; under path condition c it is 'x
  // a later read of 'y is accepted under `c` and killed under `!c` -- precision follows
  //   the same entailment used at joins
```

**Verdict: accepted as required.**

### P11 Write-once-then-frozen cache

```text
cache : Array<Option<V>, N> in 'k      // occupancy is DATA (D3 seed), not language state
                                        // state('k[j]) = Init for every j, always
get(k):
  match cache[k] {                     // the writer's own match; exhaustive; not a check
    Some(v) => read v                  // accept: state('k[k]) = Init throughout
    None    => { cache[k] := Some(compute(k)) ; read cache[k] }
                                       // accept: a write of ordinary data; no state
                                       //   transition at all -> R1 is satisfied trivially
  }
// R1 verdict stated alone, as §3 of the requirement list demands:
//   PASS.  A slot goes Uninit->Init never: it is Init from construction, holding None.
//   The "uninitialised" hazard is dissolved into the Option's discriminant.
p = pointer_of(cache[j]) ; get(k) ; read(p)
  // accept if j != k provable: the write's footprint is {'k[k]}; R6 frames 'k[j]'s
  //   contents fact.  The POINTER stays valid either way (no relocation, fixed array).
  // if j != k is not provable: the pointer is still valid, only the CONTENTS fact dies.
  //   reject only a read that depended on the killed contents fact; the deref itself
  //   is accepted.  This is the precision/safety split R1 vs R6.
```

Admission is therefore not a capability question for this candidate: it needs
no new mechanism. Cost: one discriminant word per slot and one branch per
first access — the D3 seed's price, paid only where the writer declared an
`Option`-shaped occupant. **Verdict: accepted as required.**

### P13 Relocation by a compacting third party

```text
pool C : Pool<Obj> declared compacting        // declaration -> a slot map exists at runtime
h = alloc(C) ; …
p = pointer_of(C[h])
  // accept: forms ptr<C[sigma].*>, requires Live(h) ; layout version v0 recorded
C.compact()
  // footprint: writes backing(C), slotmap(C) ; ends every place C[sigma].f
  // does NOT name Live(C) or gen(C[.]) -> those facts are framed in (R6)
  // layout version v0 -> v1
read(p)
  // reject: place C[sigma].* ended by the compaction (R8a storage-ending event; also
  //   R1(a)(iii) stale layout).  missing fact: no relocation since formation.
  //   M7 payload: "re-derive the pointer from the handle: p = pointer_of(C[h])"
read(C[h])
  // accept: Live(h) survived the compaction.  The handle IS the fixup form R8a demands:
  //   identity is (pool, ghost slot), the slot map is the pool's own data, and the
  //   lookup is an operation the SOURCE WROTE -- not a compiler-inserted fixup.
  // cost: one extra load per access, stated under M9.
open_window(C) { p2 = pointer_of(C[h]) ; loop { read(p2) } }
  // accept: the window's contract says `no relocation of C`; inside it the pointer is
  //   re-obtained once and the indirection is hoisted.  compact() inside the window is
  //   refused by the window's own ensures, not by a runtime flag.
```

This is the candidate's flagship: R8a's "interior pointers and third-party
relocation are mutually exclusive without a contract-visible fixup form" is
satisfied with the fixup form being the ordinary access path.
**Verdict: accepted as required.**

### P16 Abstraction over identities

```text
fn map_nodes<'G, T>(g: &Pool<'G, Node<T>>, f: fn(&T) -> T)
  where invariant IG<'G>                      // the pool invariant travels as a bound
  writes 'G[*].data
  // parameters per interface: 1 identity ('G) + 1 invariant bound + 1 footprint row
  // R15 metric: 1 per ROOT touched, 0 per place -> meets "a function of the storages
  //   the callee touches", not linear in fields

fn kernel<'c, E>(c: &Cols<'c, E>)
  writes 'c.a[0..n), 'c.b[0..n)
  reads  'c.c[0..n), …
  // 8 columns, ONE identity parameter: steps are not parameters (the D1 step vocabulary
  // is what makes this work; a per-column-identity scheme would charge 8)

let h = |slice: View<'s,u8>| helper(slice, input)
  // closure type carries a footprint row: `reads 'input ; writes 's[0..len)`
  // accept at P6's call: the captured identity 'input is read-only in every instance,
  //   so the k instantiations remain pairwise non-interfering
  // cost: the capture set is part of the closure's type -- a real signature charge

fn pick<N: Nominal>(c: Bool, x: N, y: N) -> N
  // accept: N is a nominal over VALUES; identity facts cross only where N is a handle
  //   type H<'P>, in which case 'P is an extra parameter.  A nominal over handles into
  //   TWO pools needs two parameters; the generic body is checked once (PROG-1 spent).
```

Cost, stated: the pool invariant must be *generic over the element type*, so
invariants are parameterised and instantiated per monomorphisation. That is
the candidate's largest unmeasured M10 item. **Verdict: accepted with a stated
cost.**

### P17 Partial operations

```text
q = a / d
  // reject: missing fact d != 0.  M7 payload names `d != 0` and the tree location
if d != 0 { q = a / d }            // accept: path condition entails the domain
match checked_div(a, d) { Ok(q) => …, DivZero => … }
                                   // accept: a written typed outcome (R12), both arms
                                   //   discharge every R2 obligation

b: u8 = narrow(x)
  // reject: missing fact x < 256
if x < 256 { b = narrow(x) }       // accept
y = v[i]
  // reject: missing fact i < len(v)
if i < len(v) { y = v[i] }         // accept: the only branch is the writer's

// and the fourth, which this candidate adds and which is NOT of the same kind:
match C.open(h) { Live(p) => read(p), Stale => … }

```

**Verdict for the three required cases: accepted as required.** The fourth is

## 4. Requirements

### 4.1 Row by row

| Row | Verdict | Reason (one sentence) |
|---|---|---|
| R1 | **met** | (i) hole reads are refused by per-place `state` and, for pool slots, dissolved into the occupant's discriminant; (ii) `free` bumps the generation so no later handle or pointer reaches the ended identity and byte reuse never revives it; (iii) a layout-version bump at `compact`/`grow` refuses stale-layout access. |
| R2 | **met** | Copyable handles hold no obligation; the **pool's `Live` set is the ledger**, `free` requires `Live(h)` (so a double free is refused by the killed fact) and a pool's end requires `Live(P) = ∅` (so a leak is refused), on every path including outcome arms. |
| R3 | **met** | Values move/take/put/replace with the states in §2.4; handles are copy values carrying no obligation, so the multiplicity lemma quantifies over value transfers only and the "used twice" and "never released" diagnostics stay distinct. |
| R4 | **met** | Disjointness is proved over the containment structure — field paths, proved extents, freshness of allocated slots, injectivity of the slot map — and never from name inequality; `S(A)` and `b1` correctly have no distinctness (P2). |
| R5 | **partial** | Ground (i) is supplied in full (P1, P3, P5, P6 derived above); grounds (ii) (checked accumulator law) and (iii) (named weaker level) are R14's vocabulary and this tuple neither supplies nor obstructs them. |
| R6 | **partial** | Kills are keyed by written footprints over places and the flagship cases frame correctly (P4's `Live` across `push`, P13's `Live` across `compact`, P9's `len` across `reserve`); but `free(P, h)` with an opaque `σ(h)` must kill every generation fact of that pool, an over-kill the stated footprint permits but precision does not want. |
| R7 | **met** | §2.6's vocabulary covers every R7(a) item; `pick`'s `ite` identity and `reserve`'s existential backing are stated, and the caller in P9 is judged from the signature alone. |
| R8a | **met** | The storage-ending set is enumerated (§2.4) and contract-visible, and the fixup form R8a demands for third-party relocation is the handle lookup itself (P13). |
| R8b | **met** | Placement demands are orthogonal and the occupancy carrier is itself a placement choice — inline `Option`, a parallel validity array (SYS-D3-18), or nothing for dense pools — so a demanded layout and an occupancy discriminant do not collide. |
| R9 | **met** | Several long-lived writable handles to one storage is the default shape, not an exception; P3's four link writes and P7's two aliases are accepted sequentially, and the cost is exactly the localized loss of distinctness for the coinciding places (C5). |
| R10 | **met** | A descriptor is a handle into a descriptor pool, so fd-number reuse after `close` is refused by the same generation kill that refuses P2's `b2` — no rule mentions the host boundary. |
| R11 | **met** | Every partial operation takes a proof or a written arm (P17); in Tier A `Gen` is a symbolic successor with no wraparound, so the candidate introduces no new silent-overflow site. |
| R12 | **met** | Outcome arms are ordinary control flow; `try_split2` and (in Tier B) `open`/`free`'s `Retired` are stated as outcomes with per-arm `ensures`, and R2 discharges on each arm. |
| R13 | **met** | A pool makes a byte or slot budget a counting fact over `Live(P)` plus the extent invariant, so `\|Live(P)\| ≤ N` and `Σ extent ≤ B` are proved where promised and cost nothing where not. |
| R14 | **partial** | The candidate *needs* R14(iii) (the allocator may write freed bytes; P2) and would need (i)/(ii) for a concurrent pool, and it supplies neither — it consumes the model rather than stating it. |
| R15 | **partial** | Identity, state and effect facts cross boundaries with one parameter per root and zero per place (P16), but pool invariants must be parameterised over the element type and instantiated per monomorphisation, which is unmeasured. |
| M1 | **met** | Four fixed families, each total and terminating with no search: literal-conjunction entailment for state terms, affine normalisation for extents and indices, lattice-height fixpoint for states, and syntactic instantiation of written invariants (`use` steps are verified, never rediscovered). |
| M2 | **violated (declared, Tier B only)** | (i) holds everywhere: every failure edge is a written arm. (ii) holds in Tier A — nothing runtime is consulted and every ghost datum is bound by an operation the source wrote — but Tier B's `open` is a generational check that safety depends on, which the verdict list refuses **by name**; §6 states the case and concedes the refusal. |
| M3 | **met** | The pool, arena and free list are ordinary WF code with written invariants, so the candidate adds **no** trusted-base entry; no `unsafe`, no bare assume, no compiler-primitive pool. |
| M4 | **met** | Added constructs each have one spelling: `pool`, `handle`/`H<P>`, `invariant`, `use`, `open`, `view`; handle access and pointer access are different constructs with different meanings, not two spellings of one. |
| M5 | **met** | No permission judgement feeds acceptance: a missing distinctness at PAR-1/PAR-2 (P2's three `fill`s without `IA`, P3's traversal map) leaves the program sequential, never rejected. |
| M6 | **partial** | The state model is finite and small (`state × gen × Live` over a bounded pool), so M6(i)'s bounded check and M6(iv)'s differential oracle are unusually cheap (§5, D13); frame soundness under generation kills is the obligation the candidate must discharge and has not. |
| M7 | **met** | Every rejection above names one missing fact of a closed list — `k ≠ i`, `state(π) = Init`, `Live(h)`, `no relocation since formation`, `distinct(σ₁,σ₂)` — and a local repair (a written premise, a `use` step, a re-derivation from the handle, an outcome arm). |
| M8 | **partial** | The tuple adds pools, ghost slots, generations, `Live` sets, invariants with `use`, footprints over places, and state terms: provisionally ~8–10k tokens against an ownership share of ~18.5k of a K already measured at 130k, so it fits the subsystem share and worsens the global red. |
| M9 | **partial** | P5 and P6 pay nothing and keep the obvious shape fastest, but every pool access costs one indirection and every occupancy read one discriminant load, so pointer-chasing shapes (P3's traverse) are two loads per hop unless hoisted into a no-relocation window. |
| M10 | **partial** | Entailment is linear, extent arithmetic is affine-normal-form comparison, and the reach of an edit stops at the declaration plus the pool's invariant users; invariant instantiation per monomorphisation (P16) is the unbounded item and is unmeasured. |
| M11 | **met** | The verdict diff of admitting Tier B is exactly the set of programs containing an `open`, and dropping Tier B is a loss statable as a program list, not a migration. |

**Counts: 18 met, 8 partial, 1 violated (M2, Tier B only).**

### 4.2 The price this candidate charges the compiler

| # | Price |
|---|---|
| 1 | It may not relocate a pool's slots except through the pool's own written slot-map update; no moving collector, no address-changing copy while a place is named. |
| 2 | It may not synthesise a generation comparison, a liveness test, an occupancy read or a drop flag the source did not write — in Tier A it emits none at all. |
| 3 | The erasure rule is fixed and checkable: a handle's `gen` field exists in the layout **iff** some `open` consumes it; the compiler may neither materialise it otherwise nor erase it when consumed. |
| 4 | It must carry per-place disjointness (field paths, proved extents, fresh slots) to lowering as the R4 channel; it may not require re-derivation to reach a fact the source proved. |
| 5 | It may not reorder a `free` past a use of the same pool's `Live` facts at the source level; after erasure it is free, because the facts are ghost. |
| 6 | A pool's slot-index width and occupancy carrier are declared layout (R8b) and may not be chosen by the compiler. |

### 4.3 Writer cost

| Site | Cost |
|---|---|
| per signature | 1 identity parameter per root touched; 1 footprint row; 1 `requires`/`ensures` pair per storage whose state changes; 1 existential clause per replaced backing. P5: 1+1+0+0. P9 `reserve`: 1+1+1+1. |
| per pool type, once | the pool invariant and its proof, 3–8 `use` steps, reused at every site (P2's `IA`, P3's `IG`). |
| per loop | 0 clauses when the body preserves state and frees nothing (P1, P5, P6, P8's loop); 1 clause per storage the body leaves changed; 1 clause per pool the body frees into. |
| per join | 0. The state term is automatic; the writer's branches are the only branches. |
| per statement | 0, except 1 proof or 1 written arm per partial operation (R11), and 1 `use` step where the affine family does not reach (P3's insert/remove). |

## 5. Consequences at D5–D13

| Point | Forced | Foreclosed |
|---|---|---|
| **D5** interference source | **Effect footprints over identities** (footprints over places are already the kill vocabulary, C2); **Disjointness by index arithmetic**; **Structure- and shape-derived independence** for pools (slot-map injectivity). | **Runtime dependence tracking with static summaries**, **Transactions and speculation**, **Per-task access declarations checked at schedule build** (a schedule artifact would re-introduce facts the source did not write); **Loans on references beside footprints** (pointers carry no permission, C10/C12). |
| **D6** distinctness default | **Distinct by default, call-site proof** (C3) with **Index-arithmetic distinctness** and **Split and partition tokens** (`take2`, `view`) as the discharge forms; **Apartness as a judgment** for fresh slots. | **Distinct names are distinct storage** (refused outright: `S(A)` contains `b1`, and two slot names in one pool are distinct places but not distinct bytes without `IA`); **Whole-program inference** (FN-1); **Dynamic distinctness check** except in D4's written-arithmetic form. |
| **D7** contract vocabulary | **Requires/ensures over identity states** + **Footprint and frame clauses** + **Existential result identities** + **Outcome-routed states and result obligations**; the `ite` identity term makes **Predicate-based contracts** partly necessary (states are terms, not constants). | **No contracts: whole-program inference**; **Capabilities instead of contracts** (a handle is a value, not an authority — HIS-D2-12); **Prophecies and backward functions** (unneeded: the handle already survives the call). |
| **D8** relocation | **Pools with stable index handles**; **Slot reuse in pools: generations and free lists**; **Relocation with a fixup channel**; **Aggregates travel as handles** (C4 generalised); **Reallocation as a contract-visible name change**. | **Allocation that never relocates by construction** as the *only* story; **Compiler-inferred placement**; **Pinning and immobility** as the default answer to P13 (pinning remains available as a demand, not as the mechanism). |
| **D9** containers | **Pools, free lists and slot recycling**; **Generations and epochs**; **Relocation-stable ghost identity**; **Existential backing per formation**; **Affine elements, vacancy and occupancy**; **Path identity `'v[i]`**. | **Per-element ghost tokens** as the primary (one token per element is an M8 and M10 charge the slot/generation pair already covers); **Index-only access with bounds proofs** alone (bare indices are HIS-D1-25, refused); **Probe-sequence identity** stays open. |
| **D10** concurrency | A shared pool's `Live`/free list is itself mutable shared state, so the concurrent story must pick **Lock as custodian of identity state** or **Phase / epoch discipline** or **Per-core ownership: shards** for the *allocator*, while element access stays free; **Structured fork/join and linear task handles** fits the handle model directly. | Lock-free slot reuse (the `SLAB_TYPESAFE_BY_RCU` shape) without R14(iv)'s declared access class; **Shared storage keeps no facts** (the pool must keep `Live`). |
| **D11** external resources | **Three identities per descriptor** fits exactly (wrapper handle with the close obligation, description as the pool slot, foreign contents under **Foreign identity: retain no contents fact**); **Typed failure and partial outcomes**; **Capacity and exhaustion accounting** via `\|Live\|`. | **Ambient and forgeable host access**; **Second host-authority category** (a descriptor pool is an ordinary pool, so R10's no-host-premise theorem survives). |
| **D12** surface form | **Explicit-only core, one spelling per construct** plus **Elision and implicit identity parameters** (without elision the handle and identity noise breaks M8); **Diagnostics as a specified surface** (M7's closed missing-fact list). | **Modes as sugar over pointer plus state** (there are no modes to sugar — C13); **Conventions instead of pointer types**; **Non-textual source of record** is untouched. |
| **D13** validation | **Bounded exhaustive enumeration** (the model is finite: a 3-slot pool, 2-generation domain, 3 states covers P2/P3/P7 exhaustively) and, uniquely, **Executable semantics and dynamic shadow-state oracle**: because the ghost state has a *direct runtime shadow*, a build that materialises `gen`, `Live` and `state` and asserts that every erased check would have passed is a ready-made M6(iv) channel **outside** the accepted program. **Certificate-producing acceptance** for `use` steps. | **Verified or bounded-verified checker implementation** is not forced; **Differential testing against other compilers** buys little here. |

---

## 6. Weaknesses, and the objections

### 6.1 The M2 question, stated without a hedge

Tier B is `match P.open(h) { Live(p) => …, Stale => … }`. Its case:

1. The compared values are **ordinary program data the source bound**: `h.gen`
   is a field of a value the writer holds, `P.gen[i]` is a column of a pool the
   writer declared and whose `free` the writer wrote.
2. The implication "`Live` arm ⟹ `state(P[σ]) = Init` and the occupant is
   `h`'s" is **machine-checked**, not assumed: it is the pool's written
   invariant, proved once in WF, exactly as `IA` and `IG` are.
3. Generation exhaustion is **not** wrapped: `free` carries a `Retired`
   outcome and a retired slot never re-enters allocation, which answers the
   recorded refusal "a finite generation must retire/refuse on exhaustion or
   justify safe reuse, not wrap".
4. Cross-pool misapplication is a **type** error, which answers "a generation
   alone does not prevent a handle being applied to the wrong store".
5. The shape is then identical to `if d != 0 { a / d }`, which M2(e) blesses
   as "the writer's own branch".

The concession, which I do not argue around: M2(ii) draws its line not at
*who bound the value* but at *whether the branch condition is a safety
predicate the checker discharged*, and it names generational checks and
"a Vale-style check wrapped as a library outcome" explicitly. In `d != 0` the
path condition **is** the domain fact. In `open` the path condition is a
proxy for it, and the bridge is an invariant about the allocator's discipline.
By the list as written, **Tier B violates M2(ii)**. Admitting it requires
owner decision 4 to move off interim (a); nothing in this document should be
read as claiming otherwise.

What the concession costs: the capability Tier B adds is exactly (a) handles
whose provenance the checker cannot relate to a pool — deserialised, foreign,
or from a table the writer did not prove injective — and (b) an ECS-shaped
"is this entity still alive" query. **None of P1–P19 needs it.** All fourteen
programs above are decided in Tier A.

### 6.2 Other weaknesses, unhedged

| # | Weakness | What it costs; any mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Indirection on every pool access.** `C[h]` is a slot-map load plus an element load where a pointer is one load. | M9. Mitigated by the no-relocation window (`open_window`) which hoists the pointer once, and absent entirely for non-pool storages (P5, P6). Not mitigated for P3's traversal: two loads per hop. |
| 2 | **Occupancy costs a branch and a word.** The D3 seed's price. | M9 and R8b. Mitigated by making the carrier a writer choice (inline `Option`, parallel validity array, or nothing); dense pools pay zero. |
| 3 | **`free` with an opaque slot over-kills.** Every `gen` fact of that pool dies. | R6 precision (marked partial). Mitigated by the pool invariant when it gives injectivity; unmitigated in a loop that frees a runtime-selected slot, where the writer must restate liveness at the loop head. |
| 4 | **Data-derived handles are not provably distinct.** P3's parallel map over a traversal is refused. | R4/R5 precision. The repair is named (iterate the pool, or write an injectivity invariant), so M7 holds, but it is a genuine capability gap. |
| 5 | **The pool invariant is a real proof burden.** `IA` and `IG` must be written and proved, and parameterised for generics (P16). | M8 and M10, both marked partial. Refusing to pay it by making the pool a compiler primitive is refused on M3 grounds. |
| 6 | **The candidate consumes R14 without supplying it.** Allocator writes into freed bytes (R14(iii)) are assumed; a concurrent pool needs R14(i). | Marked partial at R14; the tuple obstructs nothing, but it does not discharge it either. |

### 6.3 The strongest objection I expect, answered

> **"At full strength this is not a generational candidate at all. Every
> program you derived is decided in Tier A, where the generation is a ghost
> monotone counter — that is, a fresh static identity name. So the runtime
> machinery buys nothing that an existential-name candidate does not already
> have, while charging an indirection on every access and a discriminant on
> every occupancy read; and the one thing it uniquely buys, Tier B, you have
> just conceded is refused by name."**

The objection is correct that Tier A is where the candidate lives, and I do
not dispute the costs. It is wrong that the counter is only a fresh name, on
three counts that the derivations show:

1. **A generation is a *reusable* name with decidable equality; a fresh
   existential name is not.** P4's cursor and P3's back edges store the
   identity *in data*. An existential name must be unpacked at each use and
   cannot be compared to another unpacking, so a handle read out of
   `G[σ].next` has no relation to the pool's live set. The generation makes
   `Live(h)` a proposition over two ghost terms, which an invariant can
   quantify over (`IG`) — that is what discharges P3's traversal and P4's
   read-after-push with no proof of `len0 < cap0`.
2. **Reuse is the point of the counter, and reuse is what a fresh name
   forbids.** P2's `b4` reuses `b2`'s bytes; P3's removal frees a slot for a
   later insert. Under fresh-names-only, the pool's slot count grows without
   bound or the allocator is a trusted primitive. The generation is what lets
   a *finite* store carry an *unbounded* identity supply while keeping R1's
   "address reuse never revives an ended identity".
3. **The indirection is what buys P13, and P13 is a stated requirement, not a
   bonus.** R8a demands a contract-visible fixup form for third-party
   relocation. The handle *is* that form, and it is written by the source, so
   the cost is chosen rather than inserted (M2(ii) satisfied in the direction
   that matters).

The residual force of the objection stands and I record it as the candidate's
real shape: **this is a static-identity candidate whose identity happens to be
a reusable pair, whose runtime residue is zero unless the writer asks for
Tier B, and whose price is one indirection wherever reuse and relocation are
wanted.** If the owner's answer to P13 and P4 is "refuse the shape", the
candidate's distinguishing machinery is unearned and the tuple should lose to
a pure place-identity design. If the answer is "accept the shape", the
indirection is the only honest way to pay for it, and the generation is the
only honest way to keep R1 under reuse.

### 6.4 Second objection: the join rule is smuggled path sensitivity

> "State as a term over captured conditions is a path-sensitive analysis in
> disguise, and M10's degree ceiling will not survive it."

Answered by construction, not by assertion: the atoms are exactly the literals
of branches the writer wrote in the enclosing declaration; the term is a list
with one entry per incoming edge, collapsed on equality; the entailment
question is "does a conjunction of literals entail a conjunction of literals",
which is linear. No disjunctive normal form is built, no BDD is constructed
(RAD-D3-06 is *not* the member taken), and when no atom discriminates the
place goes to `⊤` with a diagnostic rather than to a larger term. P8 is
decided by one entailment per use.

# Candidate core model: ownership topology

Research date: 2026-09-16. Generator: `ownership-topology`. This file builds
the strongest case for one tuple over D1–D4 of
[OPTIONS.md](../../whitefoot-access-effects-research/research/investigations/access-effects/OPTIONS.md),
derived against the discriminating programs and the settled requirement list of
[VERDICT-D0.md](../../whitefoot-access-effects-research/research/investigations/access-effects/VERDICT-D0.md)
§2, the couplings C1–C18 of its §4, the premises of its §5, the owner interim
positions of its §7, and the hazard ladder of
[MECHANISM-MAP.md](../../whitefoot-access-effects-research/research/investigations/access-effects/MECHANISM-MAP.md)
§3. No other candidate is referred to or compared against. Supersede in place.

Prior art the seed names: ownership types (Clarke–Potter–Noble OOPSLA 1998),
ownership domains (Aldrich–Chambers ECOOP 2004), Verona regions, Cyclone
regions (USENIX 2002), DPJ region path lists (Bocchino et al. OOPSLA 2009).
Additional load-bearing prior art: Clarke–Wrigstad external uniqueness (ECOOP
2003), Legion partitions (SC 2012), Tofte–Talpin regions (1997), LLVM
`!alias.scope`/`!noalias` domains and `!tbaa` parent chains (both tree-shaped).

---

## 1. The tuple

| Decision | Family chosen (exact OPTIONS.md family name) | Members drawn on | Members of the same family explicitly refused |
|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | **Ownership tree / relative owner** combined with **Region as the identity unit** | RAD-D1-12 (position in ownership tree), THE-D1-15 (owner-as-name), THE-D1-16 (declared ownership domain), THE-D1-13 (region is the identity unit), THE-D1-14 (linear region value), HIS-D1-01 ADOPTED (region names a store, PROV-1), HIS-D1-21 ADOPTED (region axis of nominal identity, erased) | THE-D1-17 (`rep`/`peer`/`any` universe modifier): a relative *modifier* has no absolute distinctness, which R4(b) needs; RAD-D1-15 (whole heap one linear world): zero distinctness, zero parallelism |
| D1 (stated borrow) | from **Range, tile, partition**: index-parameterized and extent-parameterized tree children | AI-D1-04 (proved range `'v[lo..hi]`), SYS-D1-13 (half-open `[lo,hi)` extent), SYS-D1-08 (region-tree node + partition color) | SYS-D1-14 (tile named by a schedule): a schedule is not a source artifact (M5) |
| D1 (stated borrow) | from **Result-origin provenance sets**: the tree's least common ancestor *is* the finite origin set | HIS-D1-14 ADOPTED (finite static origin set per slice) | HIS-D1-15, HIS-D1-16 (body-derived / annotated origins) stay refused |
| D2 | **Permission as an effect on the statement or arrow** | AI-D2-11 (effect on the statement, EFF-1/EFF-2), THE-D2-14 (effect row on the arrow) | HIS-D2-16 REFUSED (effects grant write authority) stays refused — see §1.2 |

| D2 (internal representation only) | from **Implicit checker context**: the per-path fact store inside a body | THE-D2-01 (implicit checker context) | RAD-D2-03 (Datalog EDB), RAD-D2-04 (BDD): acceptance would depend on an analysis engine, not on written rows |
| D3 | **Pin, residency and backing states** | SYS-D3-04 (Reserved/Committed/Decommitted) as the core ladder, SYS-D3-03 (Pinned, no relocation) as the second axis, SYS-D3-05 (Pinned-in-pool/Evictable) and SYS-D3-08 (Dirty/Clean) admitted only as declared foreign-region states under R10 | SYS-D3-20 (states indexed by storage tier) refused as core vocabulary |
| D3 (stated borrow) | from **State as a term over captured conditions**: the join rule | AI-D3-07, SYS-D3-14 (`ite(c, Init, Uninit)`), THE-D3-12, HIS-D3-07 FLOATED | RAD-D3-06 (BDD over condition atoms): data-dependent blowup is an M10 risk with no stated degree |
| D3 (stated borrow) | from **State as ordinary data or typed outcome**: occupancy of a *cache cell* is data, not state | HIS-D3-04 ADOPTED (vacancy as Option-shaped value) | HIS-D3-12, HIS-D3-16, HIS-D3-17 (runtime tags, bitmaps, slot enums as language state) stay refused |
| D4 | **Aliasing bounded by ownership topology** | THE-D4-05 (ownership domains with declared links), THE-D4-07 (external uniqueness, aliased interior), THE-D4-22 (region isolation with viewpoint adaptation), THE-D4-08 (islands/confined) for the isolation boundary only | **THE-D4-04 (owners-as-dominators) refused**: it forbids the back edges P3 requires and the interior pointers R8a requires; THE-D4-06 (owner-as-modifier, universes) refused with THE-D1-17 |
| D4 (stated borrow) | from **Unrestricted aliasing, safety from per-storage state**, scoped to the inside of a region | AI-D4-01, THE-D4-02, THE-D4-23 (facts degrade monotonically, never reject), HIS-D4-02 FLOATED | HIS-D4-01 ADOPTED (OWN-5 unconditional exclusivity) is *retired* by this candidate; see §5 and §6 |
| D4 (stated borrow) | from **Overlap judged by resolved paths and proved extents** | HIS-D4-12 ADOPTED (overlap by complete resolved paths), HIS-D4-13 ADOPTED (proved half-open view extents) | HIS-D4-14 (literal-only ranges) stays refused |

### 1.1 The one sentence

**The tree owns; paths name; effects permit; state decides.**

- **The tree owns** (D1, D4): every storage sits at one position in one
  ownership tree. Its parent is the only holder of its release obligation
  (external uniqueness). Children of a node are pairwise disjoint sub-extents
  of the node.
- **Paths name** (D1): a storage's identity *is* its path from a binding in
  scope — `v.elems[i]`, `A.bytes.b2`, `c.a`. Distinctness is path disjointness
  over the tree, never inequality of names (R4(b), C3).
- **Effects permit** (D2): a pointer type carries a path and nothing else — no
  mode, no duration, no permission, no region-live scope. What may be read,
  written, initialized, ended or rebased is an effect row on the statement and
  on the arrow, over relative paths.
- **State decides** (D3): every path carries a backing state
  (`Res`/`Com`/`Dec`) and a pin state (`Mov`/`Pin`), as a term over captured
  branch conditions. Every hole read, use-after-end and stale-layout access is
  refused by the state, never by an aliasing rule.

### 1.2 Why these four cohere

| Pair | The shared object | What would break if one were swapped |
|---|---|---|
| D1 × D4 | The tree that *names* identities is the tree that *bounds* facts. A path is disjoint from another exactly when the topology says the two subtrees do not meet. | With a flat identity set (D1 elsewhere), D4's "bounded by topology" has no lattice to bound with, and disjointness degenerates to name inequality — the P2 negative case (`S` vs `b1`) that R4(b) forbids. |
| D1 × D2 | An effect row's clauses are *paths*, and a path is relative to a binding, so `writes c.a` needs no identity parameter. Relative naming (THE-D1-15) is what keeps D2's row short. | With absolute location variables, every first-order signature grows one `'a` per storage (R15's signature-explosion failure, the metric in R15(e)). |
| D2 × D3 | The row states the *state transition* per path (`ends`, `inits`, `rebases`), so R7's entry/exit-state vocabulary and R8a's storage-ending set are the same syntax. The set of ending events is exactly the set of rows containing `ends` — complete and contract-visible by construction (C7). | With permission in the reference type, ending events are implicit in borrow expiry and are not statable in a signature (R7(a), R8a(a)). |
| D3 × D1 | One state vocabulary applies at *every* node of the tree: `take` on a place is `Com→Res` at a leaf path; `free` on a region is `Com→Dec` at an interior node, propagated down. C1's "one refinement vocabulary serves state, distinctness, footprints and kills" is literally one vocabulary. | With whole-storage-only states, P1's per-element hole and P5's per-column footprints need a second mechanism. |
| D4 × D3 | Because aliasing inside a region is unrestricted, *all* sequential safety falls to D3's state — which is what the ladder's Step 0 finding already says ("borrowing is not the mechanism that refuses any hazard once storage state and identity exist", MECHANISM-MAP §3). D4 therefore never rejects a sequential access; it only supplies or withholds facts. | With shared-xor-mutable on references, D3's states become redundant for holes and R9's shape (P3, P7) becomes unrepresentable. |
| D2 × D4 | Overlap permission (R5) reads the same rows as the optimizer (R4): the footprint is a set of subtrees, non-interference is subtree disjointness. C2's "one relation, two exactness directions" is one predicate `disjoint(p, q)` read with `⊨` at a `spawn` and with `may` at lowering. | Two relations would silently retune (C2's stated hazard). |

**Answer to HIS-D2-16** (REFUSED: effects grant write authority — "they neither
manufacture an owned resource nor prove that storage exists"). In this
candidate effects do not grant. The row is a *declaration of footprint*
checked against the body and against the caller's state map; authority to
touch `x.f` comes from (i) `x` being a binding in scope, (ii) the path being
inside a subtree the caller's own row already covers, and (iii) `state(x.f)`
admitting the operation. An effect row that names a path the caller cannot
reach is rejected at the call; an effect row naming a path in state `Dec` is
rejected at the call. The refused member's objection is preserved exactly:
the row proves nothing, it *states* what will be touched.

---

## 2. The model

### 2.1 What a pointer's type says

```text
ptr<π, T>        // π is a path term; T is the referent type. Nothing else.
                 // No mode, no region-lifetime, no duration, no permission,
                 // no generation, no bounds. Copyable, erased to a machine word.

π ::= b                    // root: a binding in scope (parameter, local, region value)
    | π . name             // declared child: a struct field, a container's `meta`/`elems`,
                           //   a nominal's declared domain
    | π . ⟨site⟩           // minted child: named by the binding occurrence that formed it
                           //   (`b2 = alloc(A, 64)` mints child `b2` under `A.bytes`)
    | π [ e ]              // index child, e a value term in the D5 index fragment
    | π [ lo .. hi )       // extent child, half-open, from a `partition`/`split` operation
    | π . *                // wildcard: some descendant; supplies containment, no distinctness
```

A pointer stored in a struct field forces the struct type to carry one region
parameter naming the root of that path (`Cursor<'v>`); this is the only place
identity parameters appear in source (C8).

### 2.2 What the checker holds per storage

| Held per path | Values | Set by | Read by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `back(π)` backing state | `Res` (storage exists, no value) · `Com` (value present) · `Dec` (identity ended) | `inits`, `take`/`put`, `ends`, region end, `rebases` | R1(i)(ii), R2, R3 |
| `pin(π)` pin state | `Mov` · `Pin` | forming an interior pointer pins the ancestor chain up to the nearest region root; releasing the last one unpins | R8a, R14(iii), P13 |
| `layout(π)` | a layout token, changed only by `rebases` | `rebases` | R1(iii) |
| `msr(π)` measure terms | `len`, `cap`, extent bounds (HIS-D3-18 MSR-2) | container ops | R11 index proofs, extent disjointness |
| contents facts, keyed by path | writer facts and `invariant` clauses | writes, calls | R6 |
| foreign qualifier | `resident`/`evicted`, `dirty`/`clean`, `device-owned`, per R10 declaration | foreign contracts | R10, R14(iv) |

Every one of these is a *term over captured branch conditions*, canonicalized
as a decision list over atoms in source order:

```text
back(π) ::= Res | Com | Dec | ite(c, back, back)     // c a Boolean binding in scope
```

### 2.3 State transitions

| Operation | Effect row clause | Transition | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `let x = ...` in region `r` | `inits r.⟨x⟩` | `Res → Com` at the minted child | the child name is the binding occurrence; two occurrences are distinct by construction |
| `take(p)` | `takes π` | `Com → Res` at `π` | the value leaves; the storage does not (R3, ladder Step 0) |
| `put(p, v)` | `puts π` | `Res → Com` | any alias to `π` sees it (P7) |
| `replace(p, v)` | `writes π` | `Com → Com` | contents facts on `π` and descendants killed |
| `free(r)` / scope end | `ends π` | `Com|Res → Dec` at `π` **and every descendant** | no operation maps `Dec` anywhere; identity never revives (R1(a)(ii)) |
| `move x` (relocating) | `ends π_src`, `inits π_dst` | `π_src → Dec` | ladder Step 1: a relocating move is the storage ending |
| container growth (`push`, `reserve`) | `ends v.elems unless len < cap ; inits fresh v.elems` | `back(v.elems) := ite(len₀ < cap₀, Com, Dec)`; on the `Dec` arm a fresh minted child replaces it | the two-armed row is the whole of R8a's "conditional reallocation contract" |
| `compact` / third-party relocation | `rebases π.*` | `layout(π.*) := fresh`; `back` unchanged; **requires `pin(π) = Mov`** | paths and handles survive; raw interior pointers named the pre-event layout and are refused (R8a, P13) |
| `partition(π, k)` / `split(π, i, j)` | `partitions π` | children `π[..]` minted, each `Com` or `Res` as the parent was | the tiling obligation is discharged **once**, here |
| foreign loan (`map_for_device`) | `lends π to A` | `back(π)` unchanged, foreign qualifier `device-owned`; contents facts killed | R2's obligation discharged by the observed completion (R14(iv)) |

**Downward propagation** is the single soundness rule that makes the tree pay:
`ends π` sets `Dec` on the whole subtree; `back(π) = Res` forbids reads of any
descendant; `pin(π)` pins every ancestor. **Upward propagation** is its dual:
`inits π.c` leaves `back(π)` at `Com` only when every declared child is `Com`
(partial aggregate initialization is exactly "some child is `Res`").

### 2.4 Join and loop head

```text
JOIN(c, M₁, M₂):  for each path π mentioned in either map:
                    if M₁(π) = M₂(π)  then M(π) := M₁(π)          // no writer cost
                    else              M(π) := ite(c, M₁(π), M₂(π)) // no writer cost
                  atoms are ordered by source position; equal terms are syntactically equal

LOOP HEAD:        M_head := JOIN over entry and every back edge, then
                    every atom bound *inside* the loop is not nameable at the head:
                    a path whose arms disagree on such an atom collapses to ⊤ and
                    the writer must write one `invariant` clause naming its state,
                    or the first access under ⊤ is rejected naming the path.
```

No widening, no iteration cap, no lattice climb: the atom set of a function is
the finite set of its Boolean bindings, terms are decision lists over a fixed
order, and the loop rule is one collapse step. Termination is by the syntactic
atom count (M1).

### 2.5 What a signature states

```text
fn name(params) -> result
    reads  P…        // paths, relative to params; `x.*` covers a subtree
    writes Q…
    inits  I…        // Res → Com
    ends   E…        // → Dec, subtree
    rebases R…       // layout change, requires Mov at the call
    takes/puts …     // Com → Res / Res → Com
    requires  state and measure preconditions per path
    ensures   exit state per path, and the result's path expression
```

A result path is an **expression over the parameter bindings**, not a fresh
name: `-> ptr<x ⊔ y>` denotes the least common ancestor of the two argument
paths with a wildcard tail. This is HIS-D1-14's "finite static origin set
computed from signatures alone", and the tree makes the set a single path.

A declaration is rejected at the declaration when its `requires` is
unsatisfiable (`ends x` together with `reads x` after it) or when its result
path names a root no caller can name (HIS-REQ-06's provenance case) — R7(a).

### 2.6 What the writer writes, and where

| Where | What | Typical count |
|---|---|---|
| struct/nominal declaration | nothing new — the fields *are* the children | 0 |
| container type | its declared children (`meta`, `elems`) come from the library type | 0 |
| allocation site | `let b = alloc(A, 64)` — the parent region is the receiver | 0 extra tokens |
