| region root creation | `region r = arena(...)` — one binding | 1 per arena/pool |
| first-order signature | one effect row over paths rooted at parameters | 1 row, ~1 clause per touched subtree |
| struct holding a pointer | one region parameter on the type (`Cursor<'v>`) | 1 per stored pointer root |
| loop head | nothing, unless an arm inside the loop leaves a path in a different state | 0 in P1–P9 except P8's take/put loop, which is also 0 |
| join | nothing — the `ite` term is automatic | 0 |
| statement | nothing, except the existing R3 transfer keywords and `partition`/`split` at a splitting site | 0 |
| where two footprints share a container | one index or extent disjointness proof, discharged **once at the partition**, not per pair | 1 per partition |
| where a subtree's invariant survives a mutation | one `use` step inside a local `invariant` | 1 per mutation site of a linked structure (P3) |

### 2.7 What is erased

| Erased entirely before lowering | Survives lowering |
|---|---|
| paths, the ownership tree, region *identities* | region *values* that are real arenas or pools (ordinary data with an extent) |
| `back`, `pin`, `layout`, measure terms, `ite` condition terms | the writer's own branches that those terms were built from |
| effect rows, `requires`/`ensures`, `invariant`/`use` | — |
| every distinctness judgment, after emission as an R4 fact | `!alias.scope`/`!noalias` metadata derived from paths; `readonly` from a `reads`-only row |

M6(iii) holds by construction: no lowered operation consults a path, a state or
a row. The lowering reads them only through R4's licensed facts.

### 2.8 The backend channel the tree gives for free

LLVM's `!alias.scope`/`!noalias` domains and `!tbaa` parent chains are trees.
A path maps to a scope chain: `c.a[i]` emits scope `c.a` inside domain `c`;
`disjoint(c.a, c.b)` becomes two sibling scopes with each in the other's
`!noalias` list. A wildcard path emits the parent scope only. R4's relation and
the metadata form are the same shape, so no translation layer decides
granularity (MAP §8 Q15's channel is a direct map, though still unmeasured —
M9).

---

## 3. Derivations

Notation for the comment column follows the ladder: `// accept:` or
`// reject:` then the fact used. `⊨` means the checker discharged it.

### P1 Container split with a runtime index

```text
v : Vec<u64> at path `v`; declared children `v.meta`, `v.elems`; `v.elems[·]` index children
                                       // tree: v ▸ {meta, elems ▸ [0..n)}

(pi, pj) = split_out(v, i, j)          // accept: split_out requires i != j (⊨ from the caller's
                                       //   guard or a literal); row: takes v.elems[i], v.elems[j]
                                       //   back(v.elems[i]) := Res ; back(v.elems[j]) := Res
                                       //   result paths: ptr<v.elems[i]>, ptr<v.elems[j]>
write(pi, x)                           // accept: back(v.elems[i]) = Res, this is a `puts`-shaped
                                       //   write into a hole → Res → Com. fact: state on the path
write(pj, y)                           // accept: same at v.elems[j]
par { write(pi, x) ; write(pj, y) }    // accept: R5(i). footprints {v.elems[i]}, {v.elems[j]};
                                       //   disjoint by index children with i != j already ⊨ at split
read(v[k])                             // reject: back(v.elems[k]) = ite(k=i ∨ k=j, Res, Com);
                                       //   proving Com needs k != i ∧ k != j. R1(a)(i) hole read.
                                       //   diagnostic: "read of v.elems[k] requires k != i and
                                       //   k != j; both holes were opened at split_out (line L)"
if k != i && k != j { read(v[k]) }     // accept: the writer's own branch binds the atoms;
                                       //   inside the arm back(v.elems[k]) = Com. M2(ii): the only
                                       //   branch is the one the writer wrote
put(pi); put(pj)                       // accept: Res → Com at both
push(v, 5)                             // accept: push requires com(v.elems[*]) (no holes);
                                       //   before the two puts this fails naming the open hole
```

**Fact used**: index children of one parent are disjoint iff their index terms
are provably distinct; taking a value out is a state change on the path, never
on the pointer.

**Verdict: accepted with a stated cost** — the `k != i ∧ k != j` discharge is
delegated to D5's index fragment; this candidate fixes the *shape* of the
obligation (a disequality between two index terms of one parent) but not the
fragment. The diagnostic names exactly the fact R1/M7 demand.

### P2 Arena with independently released blocks

```text
region A = arena(cap)                  // tree: A ▸ {meta, bytes}
                                       //   invariant of the tree: children of `A.bytes` are
                                       //   pairwise disjoint sub-extents of `A.bytes`
                                       //   (for the language's own arena, proved from the extent
                                       //    arithmetic in `alloc`; for a foreign allocator it is
                                       //    one enumerated M3 base entry, marked as such)

b1 = alloc(A, 64)                      // accept: row = reads A.meta, writes A.meta,
                                       //   inits A.bytes.⟨b1⟩ ; mints child ⟨b1⟩ at this binding
b2 = alloc(A, 64)                      // accept: mints ⟨b2⟩, a distinct binding occurrence
b3 = alloc(A, 64)                      // accept: mints ⟨b3⟩

fill(b1) ∥ fill(b2) ∥ fill(b3)         // accept: R5(i). footprints {A.bytes.⟨b1⟩}, {⟨b2⟩}, {⟨b3⟩};
                                       //   pairwise disjoint as distinct minted siblings.
                                       //   fill's row is `writes x.*` only — it does not name
                                       //   A.meta, so no write-write conflict on the metadata
alloc(A,_) ∥ alloc(A,_)                // reject: both rows write A.meta. correct and wanted
                                       //   (nobody may overlap two allocations)

free(A, b2)                            // accept: row = writes A.meta, ends A.bytes.⟨b2⟩
                                       //   back(A.bytes.⟨b2⟩) := Dec, propagated to descendants
read(p) where p : ptr<A.bytes.⟨b2⟩.f>  // reject: back = Dec (ancestor propagation). R1(a)(ii)
b4 = alloc(A, 32)                      // accept: mints ⟨b4⟩. ⟨b4⟩ ≠ ⟨b2⟩ as binding occurrences,
                                       //   whatever addresses the allocator reuses.
                                       //   R1: "address reuse never revives an ended identity"
read(p) after b4                       // reject: still Dec. the reuse did not touch ⟨b2⟩'s state
read(b1); free(A,b1); free(A,b3); free(A,b4)
                                       // accept: each `ends` on a distinct minted child; each
                                       //   exactly once — a second `free(A,b1)` rejects on Dec
distinct(A.bytes, A.bytes.⟨b1⟩)?       // NO: ancestor/descendant are never disjoint.
                                       //   R4(e)'s negative test passes: no distinctness is
                                       //   emitted between the arena's byte storage and a block
drop A                                 // accept: ends A → Dec on the whole subtree; R2's
                                       //   "exactly once" is one event for the subtree
```

**Fact used**: sibling minted children are disjoint by the tree invariant;
ancestor/descendant never are; identity is a tree position, not an address.

**Verdict: accepted as required.** This is the candidate's best program: the
arena's metadata/bytes split, the per-block identity, the reuse-without-revival
property and the "nobody holds A exclusively" property all fall out of the tree
with no extra mechanism.

### P3 Graph with back edges in a pool

```text
region P = pool<Node>(n)               // tree: P ▸ {slots ▸ [0..n)}; an occupant of a slot is a
                                       //   minted child of the slot: P.slots[j].⟨o⟩
                                       //   invariant LIVE: every occupant reachable from P's roots
                                       //   is Com  (written once, at the pool's declaration)

a, b : ptr<P.slots[*].*>               // accept: wildcard paths. containment only, no distinctness
n = insert(P, data)                    // accept: mints ⟨n⟩ under some slot; result path is the
                                       //   concrete P.slots[j].⟨n⟩ where j is the returned index

// four link writes through several paths to one node — D4's interior rule
a.next = n                             // accept: aliasing inside P is unrestricted; the write's
                                       //   footprint P.slots[*].next kills LIVE's support
n.prev = a                             // accept
n.next = b                             // accept
b.prev = n                             // accept
use LIVE by link_insert(a, n, b)       // accept: one written `use` step re-establishes LIVE from
                                       //   the four writes. R6: the kill was licensed because the
                                       //   footprint named the support; the writer pays one step

traverse: p = p.next; read(p.data)     // accept: p : ptr<P.slots[*].*>; the read is licensed by
                                       //   LIVE (back = Com for every reachable occupant),
                                       //   not by a per-occupant state lookup

// removal
m : ptr<P.slots[j].⟨m⟩>                // a concrete minted path held since insert
remove(P, m)                           // accept: row = writes P.slots[*].{next,prev},
                                       //   ends P.slots[j].⟨m⟩, leaves back(P.slots[j]) = Res
                                       //   use LIVE: m is unlinked before it ends
read(m)                                // reject: back(P.slots[j].⟨m⟩) = Dec. R1(a)(ii)
m2 = insert(P, other)                  // accept: reuses slot j, mints ⟨m2⟩ ≠ ⟨m⟩
read(m)                                // reject: still Dec — the slot was reused, the occupant
                                       //   identity was not revived. "removal invalidates every
                                       //   path to m" holds for every *concrete* path to m

par for j in 0..n { P.slots[j].data = f(...) }
                                       // accept: R5(i). footprints P.slots[j].data vs
                                       //   P.slots[j'].data, disjoint from j != j' over index
                                       //   children. the link fields are not in the footprint,
                                       //   so LIVE survives the parallel map untouched
```

**Fact used**: two reading disciplines coexist — a *concrete* minted path,
whose state is exact and whose removal is permanent, and a *wildcard* path,
licensed by one region-level invariant stated once and re-established at each
mutation.

**Verdict: accepted with a stated cost** — (i) one written `use` step per
mutation site of the linked structure (the price of R6 precision under a
wildcard footprint); (ii) the parallel map's `j != j'` again lands in D5's
index fragment.

### P4 Cursor over a growing vector

```text
struct Cursor<'v> { at: ptr<'v.elems[·]>, i: u64 }
                                       // the one place an identity parameter is written:
                                       //   a pointer stored in a struct (C8)

c = Cursor { at: ptr_of(v.elems[0]), i: 0 }
                                       // accept: back(v.elems[0]) = Com; forming an interior
                                       //   pointer sets pin(v.elems) := Pin (proof-only, erased,
                                       //   no counter — M2(ii))
a = c.read()                           // accept: requires com(v.elems[c.i]) ∧ c.i < len(v);
                                       //   ⊨ from msr(v).len and the initialization of elems

push(v, 5)                             // accept — the pin does NOT block the push.
                                       //   row: writes v.meta ; ends v.elems unless len₀ < cap₀ ;
                                       //        inits fresh v.elems
                                       //   back(v.elems) := ite(len₀ < cap₀, Com, Dec)
                                       //   (a pin blocks only a *foreign* relocation: see P13)

b = c.read()                           // reject unless len₀ < cap₀ is ⊨ here.
                                       //   diagnostic: "read through c.at requires
                                       //   back(v.elems) = Com; it is Dec on the arm
                                       //   len(v) >= cap(v) introduced by push at line L.
                                       //   missing fact: len(v) < cap(v)"
reserve(v, n+1); push(v, 5); b = c.read()
                                       // accept: reserve's row ensures cap >= n+1, so push's
                                       //   ending arm is unreachable and the ite collapses to Com

free(v); c.read()                      // reject: back(v.elems) = Dec unconditionally, forever
```

**Fact used**: validity is decided by the path's state term and a proof about
capacity — not by a borrow, and not by a pin that forbids the push. P4's
required property ("validity decided by state and proof, not by a borrow that
blocks push") is met literally.

**Verdict: accepted as required.** Cost: one region parameter on `Cursor`.

### P5 Struct-of-arrays kernel

```text
struct Cols { a,b,c,d,e,f,g,h : buffer<u64> }
                                       // tree, from the declaration alone:
                                       //   x ▸ {a ▸ [0..n), b ▸ [0..n), …, h ▸ [0..n)}
                                       // the writer writes NO region annotation anywhere

fn kernel(x: &Cols, n: u64)
    writes x.a, x.b
    reads  x.c, x.d, x.e, x.f, x.g, x.h        // one row; eight clauses; no identity parameters
{
  for i in 0..n {
    x.a[i] = f(x.a[i], x.c[i], x.d[i])         // accept: paths x.a[i], x.c[i], x.d[i].
                                               //   disjoint(x.a, x.c) — distinct declared children
                                               //   of one node. per-load fact emitted: scope x.a
                                               //   in domain x, noalias {x.b…x.h}
    x.b[i] = g(x.b[i], x.e[i], x.f[i], x.g[i], x.h[i])
                                               // accept: same, eight sibling scopes, no guards
  }
}
par-2 over i                                   // accept: R5(i). iteration i's footprint
                                               //   {x.a[i], x.b[i]} vs i' primed; disjoint from
                                               //   i != i' over index children of the same parent
                                               //   (the affine loop-index case of D5's fragment)
```

**Fact used**: distinct declared children of one node are disjoint by the tree
invariant, with no arithmetic and no annotation; the data declaration *is* the
distinctness proof.

**Verdict: accepted as required.** The obvious shape is the annotated shape is
the fast shape (M9's obvious-shape clause, still unmeasured). The only
arithmetic is the loop index's `i != i'`, the fragment's easiest case.

### P6 Range partition helper

```text
out : buffer<u8> at path `out`, extent [0, n)

parts = partition(out, k, s)           // accept: one obligation, discharged once here:
                                       //   ⋃ w∈[0,k) [w*s, (w+1)*s) ⊆ [0,n) and pairwise disjoint.
                                       //   mints extent children out[w*s .. (w+1)*s) for w ∈ [0,k)

fn helper(dst: &mut buffer<u8>, input: &Input)
    writes dst.*                       // relative: the helper names its OWN parameter.
    reads  input.*                     //   the caller instantiates dst := out[w*s..(w+1)*s)
{ … }

for w in 0..k { helper(parts[w], input) }
                                       // accept sequentially: each call's footprint is
                                       //   out[w*s..(w+1)*s), inside `out`, state Com
par for w in 0..k { helper(parts[w], input) }
                                       // accept: R5(i). footprints are distinct extent children
                                       //   of `out`, disjoint BY CONSTRUCTION of the partition —
                                       //   no per-pair arithmetic at the loop at all.
                                       //   `input` is in every footprint but read-only:
                                       //   read/read never conflicts
                                       // the caller judged this from helper's row alone (R7(e))
```

**Fact used**: a partition converts one arithmetic obligation at the split site
into structural disjointness for every later pair — the Legion/DPJ property.
No worker count appears in the source beyond `k`.

**Verdict: accepted as required.** This is the second-best program for the
candidate: the helper's signature alone tells the caller what it writes, and
the overlap follows from topology rather than from re-proving range arithmetic
at each of the k² pairs.

### P7 Take, put, replace through aliases

```text
A : region; slot at path A.slot; v : affine
p = ptr_of(A.slot); q = ptr_of(A.slot) // accept: two writable pointers to one path.
                                       //   D4: aliasing inside a region is unrestricted,
                                       //   and these are the SAME path, so no fact is claimed
w = take(p)                            // accept: back(A.slot) := Res
read(q)                                // reject: back(A.slot) = Res — a hole. R1(a)(i).
                                       //   the state is a property of the storage: q sees it
put(q, move w)                         // accept: Res → Com. another alias filled the hole
read(p)                                // accept: back(A.slot) = Com
old = replace(p, new)                  // accept: Com → Com; contents facts on A.slot killed;
                                       //   reads `new` through q (one storage, one state)
read(q)                                // accept: reads `new`
free A                                 // accept: ends A → Dec on A and every descendant
read(p)                                // reject: Dec. no transition leaves Dec — permanent
read(q)                                // reject: Dec
```

**Fact used**: the state lives on the path; every alias to that path reads the
same state; `Dec` is absorbing.

**Verdict: accepted as required.** P7 is the program that the map's §6
decomposition was built from, and this candidate keeps it exactly.

### P8 Conditional release and loop exits

```text
a, b : owned regions, both Com

if c { free(a) } else { free(b) }
                                       // accept both arms.
                                       // JOIN: back(a) := ite(c, Dec, Com)
                                       //       back(b) := ite(c, Com, Dec)
                                       // nothing written by the writer; no drop flag exists
use(a)                                 // reject: back(a) = ite(c, Dec, Com); the Dec arm is
                                       //   reachable. diagnostic names the path: "a is Dec on
                                       //   the arm c = true (freed at line L1); it is Com on
                                       //   c = false". M7: the rejection names the path whose
                                       //   state differs
if c { use(b); free(b) } else { use(a); free(a) }
                                       // accept: inside each arm the atom c is bound, the ite
                                       //   collapses, both paths are Com where used and each is
                                       //   ended exactly once on each path (R2)
                                       // at the join: back(a) = ite(c, Dec, Dec) = Dec,
                                       //             back(b) = Dec. definiteness ⊨, no leak

loop {
  if stop { break }                    // accept
  x = take(p)                          // back(p) := Res
  …
  put(p, x)                            // back(p) := Com
}                                      // LOOP HEAD: entry Com, back edge Com → agree → Com.
                                       //   nothing written. the `break` edge carries Com
free(p)                                // accept: Com → Dec, once, on every exit edge
// counter-example the rule catches:
loop { if stop { break }; take(p); … } // reject at the loop head: back edge gives Res, entry Com;
                                       //   the disagreeing atom (`stop`) is bound inside the loop
                                       //   → collapse to ⊤ → the next access rejects naming
                                       //   "p is Res on the back edge (taken at line L, never put)"
```

**Fact used**: the `ite` term over writer-bound atoms replaces the drop flag;
the loop-head collapse rule replaces a fixpoint over an unbounded term.

**Verdict: accepted as required.** No bookkeeping state exists that the source
did not bind (M2(ii)).

### P9 A callee that changes storage state

```text
fn drain(x: &mut Buf)
    takes x.slot                       // exit state: back(x.slot) = Res
    writes x.meta
{ … }

fn reserve(v: &mut Vec, m: u64)
    writes v.meta
    ends   v.elems unless cap(v) >= m
    inits  fresh v.elems
    ensures cap(v) >= m
{ … }

fn pick(c: bool, x: ptr<T>, y: ptr<T>) -> ptr<T> @ (x ⊔ y)
    reads  x, y                        // the result's path is the least common ancestor of the
{ if c { x } else { y } }              //   two argument paths, with a wildcard tail.
                                       //   computed from the signature alone (HIS-D1-14)

// caller
drain(&mut buf); read(buf.slot)        // reject: back(buf.slot) = Res after the call, from the
                                       //   row alone. the body was never opened (R7)
reserve(&mut v, 100); read(pe)         // reject if pe : ptr<v.elems[i]> was formed before:
                                       //   back(v.elems) = ite(cap₀ >= 100, Com, Dec)
r = pick(c, &v.a[3], &v.b[7])          // accept: result path = v.* (lca of v.a[3], v.b[7])
write(r, 1)                            // accept; but the footprint is v.*, so contents facts
                                       //   about v.a, v.b, v.c … are all killed (R6 cost)
r2 = pick(c, &v.a[3], &v.a[7])         // accept: result path = v.a[*]; only v.a's facts die
```

**Fact used**: every state change is a row clause; the caller reads the row and
nothing else; the tree supplies a canonical join for a two-origin result.

**Verdict: accepted with a stated cost** — `pick`'s result is coarsened to the
least common ancestor, so a write through it kills the whole subtree's contents
facts. When the two arguments are near each other in the tree the loss is
small; when they are in different regions the loss is the whole of both. This
is the candidate's R6 tax, and it is visible to the writer in the printed
result path.

### P11 Write-once-then-frozen cache

```text
cache : region K ▸ { slots ▸ [0..m) }, each slot of type Option<V>
                                       // D3 choice: the *cell's* occupancy is ordinary data
                                       //   (HIS-D3-04), not a language state. back(K.slots[j])
                                       //   is Com from construction and never changes

fn get(k: Key) -> V
    reads K.slots[*], writes K.slots[*]
{
  match K.slots[h(k)] {
    None => { K.slots[h(k)] = Some(compute(k)) }   // accept: ordinary write to a Com path;
                                                   //   the branch is the writer's own (M2(ii))
    Some(_) => {}
  }
  match K.slots[h(k)] { Some(v) => v, None => unreachable-arm }
                                       // reject if written naively: the checker does not know
                                       //   the second match cannot see None.
                                       // accept as written by the pattern:
                                       //   let s = &mut K.slots[h(k)];
                                       //   if s.is_none() { *s = Some(compute(k)) }
                                       //   match s { Some(v) => v }     // one match, one arm ⊨
                                       //   from the assignment in the same block
}

// a reader holding a pointer across another slot's fill
p = ptr_of(K.slots[3])                 // accept: back = Com
get(other_key)                         // row writes K.slots[*]
read(p)                                // accept: back(K.slots[3]) = Com — the row's `writes`
                                       //   does not change any path's state, only contents.
                                       //   R1 passes.
                                       // but: contents facts about K.slots[3] are killed,
                                       //   because K.slots[*] names 3's support (R6, licensed)
read(p) with h(other_key) != 3 ⊨       // accept and the contents fact SURVIVES: the row is
                                       //   instantiated at the concrete path K.slots[h(other)]
                                       //   and disjointness with [3] is provable
```

**Pass/fail under R1 alone**: **pass**. A slot goes `Uninit → Init` once in the
*data* sense, while the storage's backing state is `Com` throughout; R1 never
sees a hole, because the vacancy is an `Option` discriminant the writer
branches on, not a checker state. The admission question is therefore not R1's:
it is whether the language wants a cell whose occupancy is data (one branch per
read, which why-whitefoot §5 counts as the performance argument against such
cells). This candidate records that the cost is one writer-written branch per
read and no checker vocabulary at all.

**Verdict: accepted with a stated cost** — one written branch per read; a
pointer held across another slot's fill stays valid, and keeps its contents
fact exactly when the other slot's index is provably different.

### P13 Relocation by a compacting third party

```text
region Pool = compacting_pool<T>       // tree: Pool ▸ { slots ▸ [0..n) }
h : handle = index into Pool.slots     // a handle IS a path component, not an address
p = pointer_of(h)                      // accept: forms an interior pointer at Pool.slots[h];
                                       //   pin(Pool.slots[h]) := Pin, and Pin propagates to
                                       //   every ancestor, so pin(Pool) := Pin

Pool.compact()                         // reject: row = rebases Pool.slots.* and
                                       //   requires mov(Pool). pin(Pool) = Pin from p.
                                       //   diagnostic: "compact rebases Pool.slots.*, which
                                       //   requires Pool to be Mov; it is Pin because of the
                                       //   interior pointer p formed at line L. missing step:
                                       //   end p's live range, or use the fixup form"

drop p; Pool.compact()                 // accept: pin(Pool) = Mov; layout(Pool.slots.*) := fresh;
                                       //   back unchanged; contents facts keyed by path SURVIVE
read(p)                                // reject: p is out of scope. and had it survived:
                                       //   layout(Pool.slots[h]) changed after p was formed →
                                       //   R1(a)(iii) stale layout
read(Pool[h])                          // accept: the handle names the path Pool.slots[h]; the
                                       //   rebase preserved path→value, so back = Com and the
                                       //   layout token is the current one
// the fixup form, when the writer wants a pointer across a compaction:
with_fixup(p) { Pool.compact() }       // accept: `with_fixup` is a contract-visible form whose
                                       //   row states `rebases Pool.slots.*` and
                                       //   `ensures relayout(p)`; the backend re-forms p from
                                       //   the handle after the rebase. one written form,
                                       //   no runtime check, no generation compare
```

**Fact used**: identity is a tree position, so a relocation that preserves
positions preserves handles and every fact keyed by a path; only the *layout*
token, which raw interior pointers depend on, changes. R8a's "interior pointers
and third-party relocation are mutually exclusive without a contract-visible
fixup form" is met with the fixup form supplied.

**Verdict: accepted as required.**

### P16 Abstraction over identities

```text
fn map_nodes<T>(g: &mut Pool<Node<T>>, f: fn(&T) -> T)
    reads  g.slots.*
    writes g.slots.*.data              // ONE parameter-rooted row; no identity parameters:
{ … }                                  //   the paths are relative to `g`

fn kernel<E>(x: &mut Cols<E>, n: u64)
    writes x.a, x.b
    reads  x.c … x.h                   // identical to P5's monomorphic row; E does not appear
{ … }                                  //   in any path. R15: identity facts crossed the boundary

let h = |slice: &mut buffer<u8>| helper(slice, input)
                                       // closure: its captured environment is a subtree of the
                                       //   closure value's own path. the closure type carries
                                       //   one capture clause: `captures reads input.*`
P6 with h                              // accept: instantiating h at out[w*s..] gives the same
                                       //   footprints as P6; overlap still from the partition

fn pick<N: Nominal>(c: bool, x: &N, y: &N) -> &N @ (x ⊔ y)
    reads x, y                         // nominal-parameterized: the path expression is over the
{ … }                                  //   argument bindings, so N's identity structure is
                                       //   irrelevant to the result's origin set

// R15's metric: parameters per interface vs storages touched
| interface        | storages touched | identity parameters written |
| map_nodes        | n slots + data   | 0                           |
| kernel (P5)      | 8 columns        | 0                           |
| helper (P6)      | 1 extent         | 0                           |
| Cursor (P4)      | 1                | 1 (stored pointer)          |
| pick             | 2                | 0 (path expression)         |
```

**Fact used**: paths root at bindings, so a signature that touches a subtree
names the parameter, not a fresh identity variable. Identity parameters are
written only where a pointer is *stored* in a type, i.e. once per stored
pointer root.

**Verdict: accepted with a stated cost** — the cost is (i) one region parameter
per stored-pointer field, and (ii) a capture clause per closure that captures a
reference. R15's stated metric (parameters ≤ a function of the storages
touched) is met as "parameters = number of stored-pointer roots, independent of
the number of storages touched", which is stronger than the metric asks.

### P17 Partial operations

```text
q = a / d                              // reject without a fact: `/` requires d != 0.
                                       //   nothing in D1–D4 touches this. diagnostic names
                                       //   "missing fact: d != 0" (R11, M7)
if d != 0 { q = a / d } else { … }     // accept: the writer's own arm binds the atom
b : u8 = narrow(x)                     // reject without ⊨ x < 256; accept with the proof or a
                                       //   written outcome arm. untouched by this candidate
y = v[i]                               // accept iff (1) i < msr(v).len — a measure term this
                                       //   candidate does carry per path (HIS-D3-18), and
                                       //   (2) back(v.elems[i]) = Com — the state.
                                       //   TWO facts, and the diagnostic names which failed:
                                       //   "index out of the initialized extent" vs
                                       //   "read of a hole at v.elems[i] opened at line L"
```

**Fact used**: the only contribution of D1–D4 is that the bound check's length
is a measure term on the container's path, and that the initialization half of
`v[i]` is a separate, separately named failure.

**Verdict: accepted as required.** The candidate is neutral on division and
narrowing and strictly helps the index case by splitting its two failure modes
into two named facts (R1's sub-property naming, M7).

### Derivation summary

| Program | Verdict | Load-bearing fact | Residual need |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | accepted with a stated cost | index children disjoint from `i != j`; take is a state change on the path | D5 index fragment for `k != i ∧ k != j` |
| P2 | accepted as required | minted siblings disjoint; ancestor/descendant never; identity is a position | — |
| P3 | accepted with a stated cost | concrete minted occupant vs wildcard path licensed by one invariant | one `use` per mutation; D5 for the parallel map |
| P4 | accepted as required | two-armed `ends` row; pin does not block a program-visible end | — |
| P5 | accepted as required | distinct declared children of one node, from the struct declaration | D5's trivial `i != i'` |
| P6 | accepted as required | partition discharges the tiling obligation once; relative footprint in the helper's row | — |
| P7 | accepted as required | state on the path, seen by every alias; `Dec` absorbing | — |
| P8 | accepted as required | `ite` over writer-bound atoms; loop-head collapse | — |
| P9 | accepted with a stated cost | rows state entry/exit state; result path = least common ancestor | R6 loss at the LCA |
| P11 | accepted with a stated cost | cell occupancy is data, backing state constant | one branch per read |
| P13 | accepted as required | path ≠ address; `rebases` + `Pin`; fixup form | — |
| P16 | accepted with a stated cost | paths root at bindings, so first-order rows carry no identity parameters | 1 parameter per stored pointer; capture clause per closure |
| P17 | accepted as required | measure term on the path; two named failure modes for `v[i]` | — |

**Rejected: none.** **Needing a D5..D13 mechanism by name: P1, P3, P5** (D5's
fixed linear index-disequality fragment), **P3 and P11** (D9's container and
pool element vocabulary, which this candidate fixes as index children).

---

## 4. Requirements

### 4.1 Row by row

| Row | Verdict | Reason (one sentence) |
|---|---|---|
| R1 Sequential memory safety | **met** | (i) hole reads are refused by `back = Res` at the accessed path (P7, P1), (ii) ended storage by `back = Dec` with downward propagation and identity-as-position so address reuse never revives (P2, P3), (iii) stale layout by the `layout` token that only `rebases` changes (P13); the diagnostic names which sub-property failed. |
| R2 Resource lifecycle accounting | **met** | The release obligation is held by exactly one tree parent (external uniqueness), `ends` is a row clause, the `ite` join makes definiteness decidable on every path and arm without a drop flag (P8, P2), and a foreign loan is a state on the path discharged by the observed completion. |
| R3 Value classes and transfer | **met** | Unchanged and orthogonal: `take`/`put`/`replace`/`move` are the state transitions of §2.3, and the "used twice" (R3) and "never released" (R2) diagnostics are different clauses of different rows. |
| R4 Licensed facts for the backend | **met** | Distinctness is a proved *relation over a containment structure* — path disjointness over the tree — never name inequality, and the P2 negative case (`S` vs `b1`) falls out as ancestor/descendant; facts map onto scope trees without a granularity decision. |
| R5 Data-race freedom and permitted overlap | **partial** | Ground (i) is supplied structurally and strongly (P1, P2, P3, P5, P6); grounds (ii) recombinable accumulators and (iii) named weaker levels are owned by D5 and D10 and this candidate neither supplies nor obstructs them. |
| R6 Frame: proof-fact retention | **partial** | Facts are keyed by path and a write kills exactly the subtrees its footprint names, so the letter is met; the metric is not, because a wildcard footprint (`g.slots.*`, `pick`'s LCA) names supports it does not touch and kills them — the measured residue this candidate must report. |
| R7 Compositional call judgement | **met** | The row states entry and exit state per path, returned interior pointers as path expressions, fresh allocations as minted children, read/write/end footprints, and a declaration with an unsatisfiable `requires` or an unnameable result root is rejected at the declaration (P9, P6). |
| R8a Storage-ending and relocation events | **met** | The ending set is exactly the set of rows containing `ends`, `moves` or `rebases` — complete and contract-visible by construction — and the fixup form for third-party relocation is supplied (P13, P4, P2, P3). |
| R8b Placement and physical demands | **partial** | A region root is the natural carrier of alignment, layout and address-space demands (`region r : arena align 64`) and nothing here obstructs them, but no P1–P19 program demands one, so the row stays provisional (owner decision 7 interim (b)). |
| R9 Shared mutation among several holders | **partial** | Sequentially met in full — several writable pointers to one path are legal and safety is the state's alone (P7, P3's four link writes) — with the stated fact cost where holders coincide; the concurrent half waits on D10 and R14(i)'s trigger, and the global-state ban stands (owner decision 10 interim (a)). |
| R10 External resources as ordinary objects | **met** | A resource is a region with declared foreign states (`dirty`/`clean`, `device-owned`, `resident`) and a per-region interference qualifier; no acceptance rule mentions the host boundary, and the adapter is an ordinary M3 entry (owner decision 15 interim (a)). |
| R11 Partial operations and overflow | **met** | Neutral, and improved at the index case: the length is a measure term on the path and the two failure modes of `v[i]` are separately named (P17). |
| R12 Failure paths and typed outcomes | **met** | An outcome arm is an ordinary branch whose condition becomes an `ite` atom, so every arm's exit state is checked and R2 discharges per arm; the cost is that arms multiply the terms, charged to M10 (C15). |
| R13 Resource bounds where demanded | **partial** | A region carries an extent, so a declared byte budget per arena is the natural form and `alloc` rows can carry it, but the bound derivation is not designed here and no program in this set demands one. |
| R14 Stated execution model | **partial** | This candidate supplies (iii)'s vocabulary (a non-program actor's rights are declared per region: which paths it may write, whether it may `rebases`) and (iv)'s per-identity access class, but the memory model, the level set and the excluded exhaustion set are D10's and the specification's. |
| R15 Abstraction | **met** | Paths root at bindings, so generic and nominal-parameterized rows are the monomorphic rows unchanged; identity parameters appear only per stored-pointer root, which beats the row's stated metric (P16). |
| M1 Specified deterministic acceptance | **met** | Path disjointness is structural plus a delegated fixed index fragment; joins are canonical decision lists over a syntactically finite atom set; the loop head collapses in one step; there is no fixpoint iteration, no widening, no search, no budget. |
| M2 No unstated failure edge, no unchosen cost | **met** | Every state, term, pin and row is erased; there is no generation, no pin counter, no drop flag, no occupancy bitmap, and the only branches are the writer's; `Pinned-in-pool`/`Dirty` are admitted **only** as declared states of a foreign region whose transitions the writer writes as ordinary calls. |
| M3 Enumerated, writer-closed trusted base | **met** | Exactly one new base entry kind: a foreign allocator's claim that its returned blocks are disjoint sub-extents of its region (the language's own arena proves this from extent arithmetic), enumerable and marked apart from checker facts. |
| M4 Writer regularity | **met** | One production for a path (`root ('.' step)*`), one production for an effect row, one state vocabulary reused at every tree node; no construct has a second spelling and no rule has a cross-rule exception. |
| M5 Acceptance independent of permission | **met** | Acceptance consults `back`, `layout`, measures and row conformance; the disjointness relation is consulted for *overlap* only, and a missing disjointness fact at an erasable construct leaves the loop sequential. |
| M6 Soundness evidence | **partial** | The bounded small-model check is not run here; the two obligations it must discharge are named: downward propagation of `Dec`/`Res` and the tree invariant (siblings disjoint) — frame soundness reduces to path-support containment, which is decidable. |
| M7 Repairable rejection | **partial** | Every rejection above names a path, a state and the statement that set it, and the repair is local (a branch, a proof, a `use` step); the residue is a signature whose region parameter or footprint is too coarse, whose fix is named but touches callers. |
| M8 Teaching and retrieval budget | **partial** | The taught surface is one path grammar, one five-value state vocabulary, one row grammar and one join rule — small and rule-addressable — but every signature now carries a row, and the per-program token delta is unmeasured against K. |
| M9 Measured performance floor | **partial** | Unmeasurable today for the same reason every candidate is (no fact channel exists); the candidate's specific claim, to be measured, is that P5's obvious shape emits eight sibling scopes with zero guards and zero annotations. |
| M10 Checking cost, scaling and edit stability | **met** | Path disjointness is linear in path length; the per-function state map is O(paths × ending sites) with decision-list terms; the loop head is one collapse; edit reach stops at the declaration and its direct callers, because a path is relative to a binding. |
| M11 Evolution with stated loss | **met** | Neutral; the verdict diff of adopting this tuple is stated as a corpus rewrite from modes to regions, and written `use` steps survive revisions that do not change their rule. |

**Met: 17. Partial: 10. Violated: 0.**

Declared violations of the two constraint rows: **none**. M1 holds under the
condition that D5's index fragment is a fixed, terminating, specification-named
family; M2 holds under the conditions that (a) `Pin` is a proof-only state with
no counter, (b) occupancy of a cache cell is ordinary data with a written
branch, and (c) the residency and dirty axes of D3's family are admitted only
as declared foreign states. If any of those three is relaxed, the candidate
violates M2 and must be rejected.

### 4.2 The price this candidate charges the compiler

| Forbidden to the compiler | Ground |
|---|---|
| Relocating any storage while an interior pointer names it, unless the operation's row says `rebases` and the source used the fixup form | R8a Price, P13 |
| Emitting a distinctness fact between an ancestor and a descendant path, however the addresses fall | R4(b), P2 |
| Emitting any alias fact the source's paths did not license, or requiring a re-derivation to reach a stated fact | R4 Price |
| Inserting a pin counter, a generation, a drop flag, an occupancy bitmap, or any branch selecting between source-visible behaviors | M2(ii) |
| Choosing the alias-metadata granularity independently: the scope tree is the path tree | this candidate's channel claim (a `design/compiler` decision under owner decision 3 interim (c)) |
| Reordering a region's `ends` across any access to its subtree | R1 |
| Deciding acceptance from the disjointness relation at an erasable construct | M5 |

What is **not** forbidden: any schedule, tiling, worker count, vectorization
width, loop versioning, remainder loop or fence set; stack coloring and spill
reuse of ended storage; and adding backend-derived facts on top of the stated
ones, if owner decision 3 admits them (they belong to the backend's M3 entry).

### 4.3 The writer's cost

| Unit | What must be written | P1–P9 count |
|---|---|---|
| per signature | one effect row; clauses are parameter-relative paths | 1 row, 1–8 clauses; **0 identity parameters** in every first-order program above |
| per type holding a pointer | one region parameter | 1, only in P4's `Cursor` |
| per closure capturing a reference | one capture clause | 1, only in P16 |
| per loop | 0, unless an arm inside the loop leaves a path in a different state, then 1 `invariant` clause | 0 across P1–P9 |
| per join | 0 — the `ite` term is built by the checker | 0 |
| per statement | 0 beyond R3's existing transfer keywords | 0 |
| per allocation | the parent region is the receiver of `alloc`; no extra token | 0 |
| per region root | one binding (`region A = arena(...)`) | 1 per arena/pool (P2, P3) |
| per split of a container | one `partition`/`split` with its (once-discharged) arithmetic | 1 in P1, 1 in P6 |
| per mutation of a linked structure under an invariant | one `use` step | 1 per site in P3 |
| per pair of footprints sharing a container | one index disequality, **or zero if a partition already separated them** | 1 in P1, 1 in P5's loop, 0 in P6 |

The headline writer property: **in P5, P6, P7, P8 and P9 the writer writes no
identity name at all.** The tree comes from the declarations and the allocation
sites the writer already wrote.

---

## 5. Consequences at D5–D13

| Decision | Forced | Foreclosed |
|---|---|---|
| **D5** interference source | A structural source: disjointness is derived from the path tree, plus one fixed linear fragment for index and extent children (disequality and half-open non-overlap over affine terms). The fragment is the *only* arithmetic the checker runs. | Whole-program points-to as the source of facts; runtime schedulers deriving a dependence graph; any solver-backed fragment (M1); emitter-manufactured scopes from static paths (HIS-D2-18 stays refused, since a path is now in the source). |
| **D6** distinctness default at boundaries | Distinct-by-**position**, not by declaration: two parameter paths are distinct iff structurally disjoint, and a caller that passes overlapping subtrees gets the least-common-ancestor coarsening automatically rather than a rejection. C3's "every call site discharges distinctness for every pair" becomes a structural check, not a per-pair obligation. | Per-pair `alias 'a 'b` declarations as the *default* (AI-D4-03 survives only as an escape hatch for two roots the writer wants treated as one); distinct-by-default identity parameters needing call-site discharge (HIS-D1-05's shape is replaced). |
| **D7** contract vocabulary | Effect rows over parameter-relative paths, with the state ladder as the clause vocabulary (`inits`/`takes`/`puts`/`writes`/`ends`/`rebases`/`lends`) and two-armed rows for conditional reallocation. | Per-statement contracts (M10's cost); inferred-and-unprinted interfaces (R7 needs the printed row, though *infer-and-pin* stays open since R7 binds the interface, not its authorship); a separate footprint sub-language beside the effect row. |
| **D8** relocation and moves | Path-preserving relocation as the default; `Pin` as the only guard, demanded automatically by forming an interior pointer; `rebases` plus a written fixup form as the only way to relocate under a pointer. | A moving collector without a fixup form; an address-changing copy that does not appear in a row; identity based on address or on a generation compare (D1's generation family stays refused for the runtime form). |
| **D9** containers and backings | A container is a region node with declared children `meta` and `elems`; the backing is a child, so replacing it is `ends v.elems ; inits fresh v.elems` — C9's "existential backing a contract may replace" is a tree edge. Elements are index children; slices are extent children; pool occupants are minted children of slots. | An opaque backing identity requiring a separate existential mechanism; a bare `u64` index as the identity (HIS-D1-25 stays refused); per-slot runtime tags. |
| **D10** concurrency | Region isolation (Verona's shape): a thread receives a region by moving its owning tree edge, so cross-thread races are impossible by topology and need no footprint proof; within a region, a lock owns the region's state facts across acquire/release (C11). The level set and the memory model still have to be written (R14(i)(ii)). | Ambient shared-memory concurrency with per-object atomics as the default; fine-grained cross-region interior sharing without a declared foreign access class (C17). |
| **D11** external resources | A resource is a region with a foreign-declared state vocabulary and a per-region interference qualifier; P12's escrow is `lends buf to Device` with a completion event, P14's three identities are three tree nodes (wrapper ▸ description ▸ contents) with the close obligation on the wrapper edge. | A compiler-special path for I/O values (R10 Price); modelling a descriptor as one identity. |
| **D12** surface form | Regions declared at allocation sites and struct declarations; rows on arrows; **no modes on references** — C13's "modes retired instead of refined" is taken literally, which retires OWN-2's `own`/`&`/`&uniq` and OWN-5's exclusivity as *source* constructs. Read-only reaches the backend from a `reads`-only row, so C10's pointer flag is not needed either. | A two-axis mode vocabulary (HIS-D4-04/05 stay deferred and become unnecessary); `cell<T>` as a gated interior-mutability type (unnecessary: aliased writes are legal); borrow-scope syntax of any kind. |
| **D13** validation | The bounded small-model check has two obligations to discharge (downward propagation, sibling disjointness) and a natural differential: withhold path-derived facts and compare. Migration from today's modes is mechanical in one direction only (a mode-checked program has a legal tree; the reverse is not true). | A facts-on/facts-off pair of builds (HIS-D0-17 stays superseded); a debug-only shadow state (two semantics). |

---

## 6. Weaknesses, and the strongest objection

### 6.1 The strongest objection I expect

> *You have re-invented the borrow checker's non-locality as a tree-shape tax.
> The writer must choose the ownership topology before writing the code, every
> wrong choice is a non-local rewrite, and that is exactly blind-writer's OWN-6
> wall moved from references to regions. Ownership types have been tried for
> thirty years and the reason none shipped in a systems language is that the
> topology never matches the program.*

Answered as far as I can:

1. **The topology never rejects an aliased access.** OWN-6's wall was a
   *rejection*: the writer wrote two writable references and the checker said
   no. Here two writable pointers to one path are always legal (P7), four link
   writes through several paths to one node are always legal (P3), and a
   sequential program is never rejected because of aliasing. The only
   rejections are state rejections — hole, ended, stale layout — and each names
   one path and the statement that set it. A wrong topology costs *facts*, and
   under M5 a missing fact leaves the loop sequential rather than rejected.
   This is the precise sense in which owners-as-dominators (THE-D4-04) is
   refused and external uniqueness (THE-D4-07) is kept: **ownership is unique,
   reference is free.**
2. **The writer mostly does not choose the topology; the declarations do.** A
   struct's fields are its children. A container's `elems` is its child. An
   arena's blocks are minted at the `let` that allocates them. In P5, P6, P7,
   P8 and P9 the writer writes no identity name. The genuine choices are: which
   arena or pool an allocation goes into (one token at the allocation site),
   and where a container is partitioned (one statement, once).
3. **The residue is real and I will not hide it.** When a *signature's*
   footprint is too coarse — `pick`'s least common ancestor, `map_nodes`'s
   `g.slots.*` — the fix is to refine the row, which touches the declaration
   and its direct callers. That is non-local in M10's sense (reach = 1 call
   layer) though named in M7's sense. And when two objects that must be treated
   as one distinct storage were allocated into different regions, the repair is
   to move one allocation, which is one token at one site but requires the
   writer to see *why*, from a diagnostic that prints both paths and their
   least common ancestor. I claim the diagnostic makes it mechanical; I have
   not measured it, and M7 stays partial for exactly this.

### 6.2 Honest weaknesses

| # | Weakness | How bad | What it costs, stated |
|---|---|---|---|
| W1 | **Wildcard footprints over-kill.** `writes g.slots.*` names the support of every per-node fact, so R6's letter licenses the kill while the writer loses facts they had proved. P3 pays one `use` step per mutation site for this. | Moderate; it is the candidate's R6 tax and the reason R6 is partial. | One `use` step per mutation site of a wildcard-addressed structure; measured as retained-fact count on P3. |
| W2 | **The least-common-ancestor join is coarse across regions.** `pick(c, &a, &b)` with `a` and `b` in different arenas returns a path at the root, and a write through it kills both arenas' contents facts. | Moderate. The tree gives a *canonical* origin set, but a canonical coarse one. | Stated in P9; the writer can avoid it by not writing such a `pick`, which is a capability loss, not a rejection. |
| W3 | **Minted names multiply in loops.** A pool insert inside a loop mints one occupant name per iteration, which cannot be a static name; the loop head collapses them to a wildcard. | Moderate; it is why P3 needs two reading disciplines (concrete path, wildcard-plus-invariant). | The writer holds either a precise, removal-invalidated path or a wildcard licensed by an invariant, and cannot have both in one binding. |
| W4 | **Foreign sibling disjointness is an axiom.** For a foreign allocator, "two returned blocks are disjoint" is an M3 base entry, not a proof. | Small but real; it is the only new base-entry kind. | One enumerated entry per foreign allocator, marked apart from checker facts in M6(iv). |
| W5 | **D3's residency and dirty axes do not survive M2 as language state.** Pinned-in-pool, Evictable, Dirty/Clean are runtime mechanisms in every prior art that uses them. | The seeded family is therefore admitted in a narrowed form: backing and pin only, with residency and dirtiness as declared foreign-region states. | The narrowing is a declared deviation from the seed's family, taken because the unnarrowed form violates M2(ii). |
| W6 | **The state-term atom set is bounded but not small.** `ite` terms over branch conditions grow with outcome arms (C15) and with nested `if`s that end storage. | The stated bound is O(paths × ending sites) per function with decision-list terms; M10's ceiling is not exceeded, but the constant is untested. | Measured on the pinned bundle; M10 met on the degree, unmeasured on the constant. |
| W7 | **Retiring modes is a corpus-wide rewrite.** OWN-2 and OWN-5 are load-bearing in today's specification and corpus; adopting this tuple means the verdict diff is large. | Large but bounded and one-directional. | M11's stated loss; every mode-checked program has a legal tree, so the migration is mechanical in the direction that matters. |
| W8 | **P11's cell costs a branch per read.** Modelling cache occupancy as data rather than state is what keeps M2, and why-whitefoot §5 counts that branch as the performance argument against such cells. | Small, and it is an owner-visible capability question rather than a defect. | One branch per read, recorded so the admission question is decided on the measured cost. |

### 6.3 Two objections I can answer completely

> *"Region identity is coarse — same region does not mean same object, so R4 is
> weak"* (the catalog's own line on the region family).

That objection is against the whole-heap and one-name-per-region forms
(RAD-D1-15, THE-D1-13 read alone), both of which are refused here. In this
candidate the tree descends through declared fields, minted allocations, index
children and extent children to individual places; region *roots* are only the
top of the tree. P5's eight columns are eight distinct paths under one region,
and the fact emitted is per column, not per region. Coarseness appears exactly
at wildcards, which are the writer's declared uncertainty.

> *"Effect rows are over-declared; the failure mode of the effect family is
> over-declaring"* (the catalog's line on D2's effect family).

Over-declaring costs facts, never acceptance: a row that says `writes x.*` when
it writes `x.a` is accepted, and loses distinctness inside `x`. That is the
same monotone degradation as everywhere else in this candidate, so
over-declaration is a performance bug with a printed cause, not a rejection.
The row cannot be *under*-declared: the body check rejects a write outside the
row, naming the path.

---

## 7. What this candidate would need next

| # | Need | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | The index and extent fragment: a fixed, terminating disequality and non-overlap decision procedure over affine terms | D5 |
| 2 | The bounded small-model check over downward propagation and the sibling-disjointness invariant | M6(i), D13 |
| 3 | A measurement of row tokens per signature over the corpus against K | M8, owner decision 16 |
| 4 | A measurement of the repair rate for topology diagnostics (two paths plus their least common ancestor) | M7, owner decision 12 (evidence only) |
| 5 | The scope-tree emission experiment on P5: eight sibling scopes, zero guards | M9, MAP §8 Q15 |


# File: candidate-reference-refined.md

# Candidate core model: reference-refined

Key: `reference-refined`. Research date: 2026-09-16. This is one candidate core
model for D1–D4 of [OPTIONS.md](../../whitefoot-access-effects-research/research/investigations/access-effects/OPTIONS.md),
derived against the settled requirement list (VERDICT-D0 §2), the couplings
(§4), the hazard ladder (MECHANISM-MAP §3) and the discriminating programs
P1–P19. It builds the best version of the family the language has today and
fixes its recorded defects; it does not compare itself to other candidates.

---

## 1. The tuple

| Point | Family chosen (name exactly as in OPTIONS.md) | Members drawn on |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | **Path / resolved place**, combined with **Existential / witness identity per formation** for allocator and container results | AI-D1-02, THE-D1-09, HIS-D1-03 (ADOPTED: root plus ordered steps); plus THE-D1-16-class existential formation for `alloc` results, and **Two-level granularity** for pools (`'P` root, `'P[i]` steps) |
| D2 | **Permission in the reference type** | AI-D2-04, SYS-D2-04, THE-D2-03, HIS-D2-01 (ADOPTED: OWN-2 modes), **HIS-D2-03 (FLOATED: `Ref<'a,P,T>` validity obligation) adopted in a split form** — see §2.3; HIS-D2-17 stays refused |
| D3 | **Access-mode states on the identity** (the LEX-1 two-axis vocabulary) + **Per-place vacancy (holes)** + **State as a term over captured conditions**, over the **Three-state minimum** | AI-D3-03 (`Frozen`/`ExclusivelyLoaned`/`Suspended`), SYS-D3-09, HIS-D3-06 (fourth "suspended" state), HIS-D3-02 (typed holes — **un-refused**, §2.4), HIS-D3-04-class condition terms (CASES.md join refinement, coupling C6); occupancy-as-data (D3 "Occupancy as separate data or runtime discriminant") only where the writer binds it (P3) |
| D4 | **Shared-xor-mutable on references** + **Exclusivity rule refinements through a borrow**, with three refinements drawn from **Per-scope exclusivity windows** and **Scoped projections and non-escaping references** | AI-D4-02, SYS-D4-02, THE-D4-01, HIS-D4-01 (ADOPTED: OWN-5); HIS-D4-17 (SET-2 replace), HIS-D4-18 (BLK-4 reversal); refinements: last-use endpoints (THE-D4-16 access-span exclusivity, HIS-D4-09 suspension windows), **partial suspension / view splitting** (THE-D4-17), bounded reborrows (HIS-D4-09); HIS-D4-06/07/08 (interior mutability as mode, `cell`, runtime flags) stay refused |

### Why the four cohere

| Pair | The single fact that joins them |
|---|---|
| D1 × D2 | A reference's type names the **path** it resolves to. `!alias.scope` needs "a disjointness proof indexed by some static identity carried alongside the pointer value" (EVIDENCE §B.2); the retired `democ` prototype manufactured exactly that scope *from the resolved place of a field reached through a `&uniq`*. D1 makes that identity first-class in the type instead of re-derived at emission. |
| D2 × D4 | Shared-xor-mutable is a rule **about references**; it is only statable if the reference carries the permission. This is also why the candidate keeps PAR-1's loan channel for free: a loan is "a per-actual exclusivity claim, independent of the callee's row" (EVIDENCE §E), which footprints cannot express and a permission-carrying reference expresses by existing. |
| D3 × D1 | Every state (`Init`, `Hole`, `Ended`, `Frozen`, `Suspended`) is keyed by a **path**, not by a reference and not by a whole parameter. That is what makes R6's measured tax (34 of 41 `len()` rebinds) removable: a write to `'v.data[i]` does not kill a fact supported by `'v.len`. |
| D3 × D4 | The two axes of LEX-1 (exclusivity × write permission) are the *mode* half; `Frozen` and `Hole` are the *state* half. Exclusivity decides who may create a hole or a freeze; the state decides what any path may then do. Modes never duplicate states, and states never duplicate modes — the split that keeps M4 at one spelling per construct. |
| D4 × D1 | Partial suspension (P1) is only expressible when suspension can be **subtracted along paths**: `'v` minus `{'v[i], 'v[j]}`. Whole-holder suspension (today) is the degenerate case where the path algebra has no steps. |

The seam this tuple deliberately cuts: **permission lives on the reference;
validity and occupancy live on the path.** Today they are the same thing
(a borrow is live ⇒ its referent is valid), which is precisely why `push`
cannot be written while a cursor exists (P4) and why a graph with back edges
is unwritable (P3). Cutting the seam is the whole of this candidate's
refinement work.

---

## 2. The model

### 2.1 What a pointer's type says

```text
ref<M, 'p, T>            M = X·W ,  X ∈ {excl, shared} ,  W ∈ {mut, const}
own T                    an affine/linear binding; not a reference; carries the release obligation
'p                       a resolved place: a root (binding, existential brand, or path parameter)
                         plus ordered steps (.field, [literal], [proved index], [proved range])
{'p | 'q}                a written finite origin set (a result may resolve to either)
```

Four modes, two axes, no fifth mode. `excl·mut` is today's `&uniq`;
`shared·const` is today's `&`; the two new combinations are LEX-1's deferred
forms: `excl·const` (exclusive-read) and `shared·mut` (**bounded shared-write**,
the R9 shape). "Bounded" means its claim extent is an endpoint, not a program
lifetime. `Frozen` is *not* a fifth mode; it is a place state (§2.2) that
strengthens what `shared·const` may assume.

| Mode | May read | May write | Other usable paths may exist | Contents facts survive a write elsewhere | Backend fact |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `excl·mut` | yes | yes | no | yes (nobody else can write) | param `noalias`; per-load `!alias.scope` per derived path |
| `excl·const` | yes | no | no | yes | param `noalias readonly`; span-invariance fact |
| `shared·const` | yes | no | yes, readers only | yes, for the claim's extent | param `readonly` |
| `shared·const` on a `Frozen` path | yes | no | yes | yes, program-wide | `!invariant.load` |
| `shared·mut` | yes | yes | yes, writers included | **no** — killed by any may-overlapping write | **none** (the fact loss is localized here, C5) |

### 2.2 What the checker holds per storage

Per **path** `'p`, three orthogonal facts, all erased before lowering:

```text
occupancy('p)  ::= Init | Hole(T) | Ended                    -- R1(i),(ii); R3 transfers
backing('p)    ::= Current | Replaced('q) | Ended            -- R8a; containers name their backing
claims('p)     ::= set of live claims { (mode, endpoint, holder) }   -- R4/R5/R9; D4's judgment
freeze('p)     ::= Open | Frozen                             -- one-way; write-once cells, CONST-2 storage
```

Each fact may be a **term over captured immutable conditions** rather than a
lattice value: `occupancy('a) = if c then Ended else Init` (coupling C6). The
condition is a source-bound value, so nothing here becomes a drop flag (M2(ii)).

`Suspended` is not a separate state: a parent is suspended on exactly the
sub-paths its live children claim; `claims('p)` carries that, and "usable"
is derived (`claims` has no overlapping stronger claim).

### 2.3 How state changes

| Event | Effect on the facts |
|---|---|
| `take(p)` (p: `*·mut`) | `occupancy(resolved(p)) := Hole(T)`; the value leaves with its obligations (R3) |
| `put(p, move v)` | requires `Hole(T)`; `:= Init` |
| `replace p = e` (SET-2) | requires `Init`; stays `Init` at every program point; old value returned |
| `free`/`dispose`/scope exit of the owner | `occupancy := Ended`, `backing := Ended`, permanently; **live claims are not a bar** — the refusal falls on the next use of any path rooted there |
| relocating `move s` | `occupancy('s) := Ended`; a fresh root receives `Init`. `own` aggregates travel as handles, so a box's *content* path is unaffected (ladder Step 1) |
| `push`/`reserve` | the contract's conditional exit clause: `cap0 ≥ need ⇒ backing unchanged`, else `backing('v.buf) := Ended; backing('v) := fresh 'b` |
| `alloc(A, n)` | returns `own Block<'β>` with `'β` a **fresh existential brand**, disjoint from every live brand of `'A.S` by formation — never by name inequality (R4(b), P2's `S` vs `b1`) |
| `freeze(p)` | `freeze := Frozen`, one-way; requires an `excl` claim to perform |
| split / view formation | mints child claims on sub-paths; the parent's claim is **suspended on those sub-paths only** |

### 2.4 Joins and loop heads

- **Join.** For each path live on either edge, the merged fact is the
  condition term `if c then f₁ else f₂` when the branch condition `c` is a
  captured immutable value, and otherwise the meet (`Hole ⊓ Init = ⊥`, a
  rejection naming the differing path). Claims do not survive a join unless
  both edges carry the same claim on the same path with the same mode.
- **Loop head.** The writer writes the head state only where the backedge
  disagrees with entry (`invariant occupancy('p) = Init`). Agreement is the
  common case and costs nothing (today's OWN-11 rule, kept). No claim may be
  loop-carried unless its endpoint is inside the body; the diagnostic names
  the claim and the iteration boundary it crosses.
- **Endpoints.** A claim's extent ends at its holder's **last use**, computed
  by one backward liveness pass over the CFG — a fixpoint bounded by lattice
  height, printable in a diagnostic and pinnable in source. Lexical region
  blocks, the `outlives` lattice and named-region liveness (OWN-3, OWN-4,
  OWN-10, OWN-11's region role) are **retired**: the path parameter is the
  only name kind, and the only ordering question left is set inclusion of
  origin sets.

### 2.5 What a signature states

```text
fn reserve<'v>(v: ref<excl mut,'v,Vec<T>>, m: u64)
    writes('v.len, 'v.cap, 'v.buf)
    ensures cap('v) >= m
        and (cap0 >= m => backing('v.buf) = Current)
        and (cap0 <  m => occupancy('v.buf0) = Ended and backing('v) = fresh)

fn drain<'x>(x: ref<excl mut,'x,T>) ensures occupancy('x) = Hole(T)

fn pick<'x,'y>(c: bool, x: ref<excl mut,'x,T>, y: ref<excl mut,'y,T>)
    -> ref<excl mut,{'x|'y},T>
```

The vocabulary is exactly R7(a)'s list: entry and exit occupancy per named
path, ended and replaced backings, a returned interior reference with its
origin set and mode, fresh existential results, read/write/end footprints,
outcome-routed states (R12), and resource effects (R13). Two shared params
may alias unless a written `distinct 'x 'y` clause says otherwise; two
`excl` params are distinct **by the exclusivity rule itself** — no clause
needed, which is the family's structural gift at D6.

### 2.6 What the writer writes, and where

| Site | What is written | Elided when |
|---|---|---|
| Signature | mode per reference parameter; one path parameter per storage the callee names; footprint rows; entry/exit state clauses for state-changing effects only | a `pure`/read-only callee writes no state clause; path params elide when there is one per parameter |
| Loop head | a state `invariant` line | entry and backedge agree |
| Join | nothing | always — the condition term is derived from the source's own branch condition |
| Statement | `move`, `take`, `put`, `replace`, `split`, `freeze`; a `use` step to discharge an index or range disjointness the fixed family does not reach | proofs already in the ProofContext |
| Never | a lifetime/region block, an `outlives` bound, a drop flag, a generation, a lock or fence the source did not write | — |

### 2.7 What is erased

Modes, paths, occupancy, backing, claims, freeze, condition terms and all
`use` steps are erased before lowering. What survives is R4's licensed facts:
per-parameter `noalias`/`readonly`, per-load `!alias.scope`/`!noalias` derived
from resolved paths, `!invariant.load` on `Frozen` paths, `initializes` from a
`writes` row without a `reads` row, `memory(argmem: …)` from the row, and
`align`/`dereferenceable` from the reference's validity. No branch, no check,
no bookkeeping word is added.

---

## 3. Derivations

Notation as the ladder: pseudocode lines, each with accept/reject and the fact
used.

### P1 Container split with a runtime index

```text
v: own Vec<u64> in 'v, len n
(pi, pj) = split_mut(v, i, j)        // accept: use i != j (fixed index family)
                                     //   mints ref<excl mut,'v.buf[i]>, ref<excl mut,'v.buf[j]>
                                     //   claims('v) := suspended on {'v.buf[i], 'v.buf[j]} ONLY
write(pi, 1)                         // accept: excl.mut claim on 'v.buf[i]; occupancy Init
write(pj, 2)                         // accept: path 'v.buf[j], disjoint from 'v.buf[i] by i!=j
par { write(pi,1); write(pj,2) }     // accept: PAR-1 footprints {'v.buf[i]} vs {'v.buf[j]} disjoint
                                     //   no runtime check: the proof is the writer's i!=j
x = v[k]                             // reject: residual footprint is 'v.buf \ {i,j};
                                     //   missing fact "k != i and k != j"  (M7 payload names both)
use k != i; use k != j; x = v[k]     // accept: residual footprint covers 'v.buf[k]
(endpoint(pi), endpoint(pj)) = above // claims('v) resumes in full at the last use of both children
push(v, x)                           // accept: whole-'v excl.mut claim available
--- counterfactual ---
push(v, x)  with pi still used later // reject: whole-'v claim conflicts with the live child claim
                                     //   on 'v.buf[i]; diagnostic names the child and its endpoint
```

Verdict: **accepted as required.** Requires partial suspension, a refinement
this candidate carries; today's whole-holder suspension would reject the
`v[k]` read even with the proof.

### P2 Arena with independently released blocks

```text
A: own Arena in 'A  { M: 'A.M , S: 'A.S }
b1 = alloc(&excl mut 'A.M, 64)       // accept: claim on 'A.M for the call's extent only
                                     //   result own Block<'B1>, 'B1 fresh brand, disjoint from live brands of 'A.S
b2 = alloc(...) ; b3 = alloc(...)    // accept: 'B2,'B3 fresh; distinctness by formation, not by name inequality
                                     //   nobody holds a claim on 'A between the calls  (R2(e) requirement met)
par { fill(b1); fill(b2); fill(b3) } // accept: footprints 'B1,'B2,'B3 pairwise disjoint by formation
                                     //   metadata 'A.M is in no footprint here
p2 = &shared 'B2[0]                  // accept: occupancy('B2) = Init
free(&excl mut 'A.M, move b2)        // accept: consumes the affine owner exactly once (R2);
                                     //   occupancy('B2) := Ended, backing('B2) := Ended
read(p2)                             // reject: occupancy('B2) = Ended  (R1(ii)); the claim being live is irrelevant
b4 = alloc(&excl mut 'A.M, 32)       // accept: 'B4 fresh; 'B4 != 'B2 although the bytes coincide
read(p2)                             // reject: still Ended -- address reuse never revives an identity
read(b1); free(b1); free(b3); free(b4)  // accept: four frees, each consuming a distinct affine owner
free(b1)                             // reject: b1 already consumed (R3 multiplicity, not R1)
distinct('A.S, 'B1)?                 // no such fact: 'B1 is a sub-brand of 'A.S; containment, not inequality
```

Verdict: **accepted as required.**

### P3 Graph with back edges in a pool

```text
pool: own Pool<Node> in 'P ; Slot = Empty | Live(Node)   // occupancy as writer-bound DATA (M2(ii): the source binds it)
links are handles (u32), never stored references         // forced: see the cost line below
insert(n, a, b):
  match at(pool, a) { Empty => outcome arm ,
                      Live(na) => set na.next = h_n }    // accept: write through ref<excl mut,'P[a].next>;
                                                         //   requires a < cap (R11 proof); path step [a] proved
  ... three more link writes through 'P[b].prev, 'P[n].next, 'P[n].prev
                                                         // accept: several paths reach one node sequentially;
                                                         //   each claim's endpoint is its statement (bounded reborrow)
invariant links_live(pool)                               // written once
                                                         // each link write kills it: its support IS the links
use links_live_after_insert(n,a,b)                       // 1 written step per insert re-establishes it   [COST]
remove(m):
  let node = take(at(pool,m)) ; set at(pool,m) = Empty    // accept: typed hole then writer-written Empty tag
q = &shared 'P[m].data   (formed before remove)          // reject at its next read: occupancy('P[m]) = Hole/Ended
traverse: h = start
  loop { match at(pool,h) { Empty => break ,
                            Live(nd) => { read nd.data ; h = nd.next } } }
                                                         // accept: the branch is the writer's; no compiler check
par_map: for i in 0..cap { write 'P[i].data }            // accept: PAR-2 injective element map; 'P[i] distinct in i
--- what fails ---
store next: ref<shared mut,'P[?],Node> inside a node     // reject at formation: the step [?] is not a proved index,
                                                         //   so the path root degrades to 'P and every removal
                                                         //   would kill every stored link (reject-when-unsure)
```

Verdict: **accepted with a stated cost** — links must be handles, the writer
binds the occupancy tag and writes one match per traversal step and one `use`
step per insert. The stored-interior-pointer graph is refused. No candidate
satisfying M2(ii) can invalidate a stored pointer into a reused slot without
either a proved static slot index or writer-bound occupancy data, so the cost
is charged at D9 (containers), not at D1–D4.

### P4 Cursor over a growing vector

```text
c = Cursor<'v.buf> { at: ref<shared,'v.buf,[u64]> , i: 0 }
                                     // accept: a reference is storable; the struct carries the path parameter.
                                     //   (Today STOR-5 refuses this: region-bearing content in stored position.)
a = c.read()                         // accept: occupancy('v.buf)=Init, backing Current, i < len fact live
push(&excl mut 'v, 5)                // accept: the cursor holds mode `shared`, i.e. NO exclusivity claim,
                                     //   so it does not bar the writer.  (Today this is the rejection point.)
                                     //   contract: cap0 >= len0+1 => backing('v.buf) Current
                                     //             else occupancy('v.buf) := Ended, backing('v) := fresh
b = c.read()                         // reject: backing('v.buf) = (cap0 > len0 ? Current : Ended)
                                     //   missing fact "len(v) < cap(v)" -- M7 payload names it and the contract clause
use len(v) < cap(v) ; push(v,5) ; b = c.read()
                                     // accept: the conditional exit clause keeps 'v.buf Current; validity carried across push
free(v) ; c.read()                   // reject: occupancy('v.buf) = Ended, permanently
```

Verdict: **accepted with a stated cost** — the writer proves `len < cap` (or
writes the reallocation outcome arm). The requirement "validity decided by
state and proof, not by a borrow that blocks push" is met exactly: the
rejection moved from `push` to the read, and it names a discharge-able fact.

### P5 Struct-of-arrays kernel

```text
fn kernel<'s>(s: ref<excl mut,'s,Cols>) writes('s.a,'s.b) reads('s.c,'s.d,'s.e,'s.f,'s.g,'s.h)
  for i in 0..n {
     s.a[i] = f(s.a[i], s.c[i], s.d[i])
                                     // accept: loads tagged with scope('s.a[i]); noalias against 's.b..'s.h
                                     //   distinctness by FIELD STEP of one resolved path -- no proof obligation,
                                     //   no runtime guard, and the fact names a value LOADED from memory
     s.b[i] = g(s.b[i], s.e[i], s.f[i], s.g[i], s.h[i])
                                     // accept: same, scope('s.b[i])
  }                                  // PAR-2: iteration i vs j disjoint by the injective element map i |-> [i]
obvious shape = fast shape           // accept: eight distinct facts emitted with zero writer annotation beyond the row
```

Verdict: **accepted as required.** This is the shape whose channel was actually
measured (8 vector adds / 0 guards / 121 asm lines against 65 / 29 / 2132), and
the identity it needs is the resolved place of the field reached through the
exclusive reference — the two halves of this candidate's D1×D2 pair.

### P6 Range partition helper

```text
fn helper<'d,'i>(dst: ref<excl mut,'d,[u8]>, src: ref<shared,'i,[u8]>) writes('d) reads('i)
for w in 0..k {
   helper(slice_mut(out, w*s, (w+1)*s), input)
}                                    // accept: 'out[w*s .. (w+1)*s) vs 'out[w'*s .. ) disjoint by the
                                     //   fixed four-ordering family (s >= 0 => s*w + s <= s*w')
                                     // accept: every iteration reads 'input under `shared`; reads never conflict
                                     // accept: the CALLER needs only the row writes('d) -- signature-only (R7)
                                     // no worker count appears beyond k
```

Verdict: **accepted as required.**

### P7 Take, put, replace through aliases

```text
p = &shared mut 'A ; q = &shared mut 'A
```
