```text
                                     // accept: bounded shared-write; two live writable references to one place.
                                     //   COST, charged here: no distinctness fact between p and q, and no contents
                                     //   fact on 'A survives a write through either (C5: the loss is exactly local)
v = take(p)                          // accept: occupancy('A) := Hole(T)  -- the hole is on the PATH
read(q)                              // reject: occupancy('A) = Hole  (R1(i)); q's mode is irrelevant
put(q, move v)                       // accept: requires Hole; := Init
read(p)                              // accept: occupancy('A) = Init -- state is a property of the storage
old = replace(p, new)                // accept: SET-2; at no program point does 'A lack exactly one valid owner
read(q)                              // accept: reads new
free 'A                              // accept: consumes the owner; occupancy := Ended
read(p)                              // reject: Ended, forever
```

Verdict: **accepted with a stated cost.** Under unrefined shared-xor-mutable
this program is inexpressible (two live writable references). It is admitted
by the `shared·mut` mode, and the price is the R4 fact loss on `'A` and on
nothing else. Typed holes (HIS-D3-02, refused historically) are un-refused:
the objection "needs a meaning for `&uniq` over a vacant referent" is answered
— a claim of any mode over a `Hole` path permits only `put`/`replace`, and
R7's vocabulary must carry `Hole` at boundaries anyway.

### P8 Conditional release and loop exits

```text
if c { free(a) } else { free(b) }    // accept: each arm consumes one affine owner exactly once
                                     // join: occupancy('a) = if c then Ended else Init
                                     //       occupancy('b) = if c then Init  else Ended   (terms, not flags)
use(a)                               // reject: on the path c = true, 'a is Ended.
                                     //   M7 payload: "the path where c is true"  (P8's required diagnostic)
if c { use(b) } else { use(a) }      // accept: each arm's term discharges against the arm's own condition
if c { free(b) } else { free(a) }    // accept: both owners consumed on every path; no drop flag exists,
                                     //   because c is a source-bound value the writer branched on (M2(ii))
loop { if stop { break } ;
       v = take(p) ; ... ; put(p, v) }
                                     // accept: loop head invariant occupancy('P)=Init; backedge agrees;
                                     //   the break edge carries Init
free(p)                              // accept: Init on every exit edge
--- counterfactual ---
loop { take(p) ; if stop { break } ; put(p,v) }
                                     // reject: backedge Init, break edge Hole -- diagnostic names the break edge
```

Verdict: **accepted as required.**

### P9 A callee that changes storage state

```text
fn drain<'x>(x: ref<excl mut,'x,T>) ensures occupancy('x) = Hole(T)
fn reserve<'v>(v: ref<excl mut,'v,Vec<T>>, m: u64)
     ensures (cap0 >= m => backing('v.buf) = Current)
         and (cap0 <  m => occupancy('v.buf0) = Ended and backing('v) = fresh)
fn pick<'x,'y>(c: bool, x: ref<excl mut,'x,T>, y: ref<excl mut,'y,T>) -> ref<excl mut,{'x|'y},T>

caller:
  drain(&excl mut px) ; read(px)     // reject: occupancy = Hole(T) from the callee's exit clause alone
  put(px, e) ; read(px)              // accept: body never opened
  r = pick(c, &excl mut px, &excl mut py)
                                     // accept: origin set {'x,'y} written in the signature;
                                     //   both 'x and 'y suspended until endpoint(r)
  write(r, 1)                        // accept: judged once through EVERY origin in the set
  read(px)                           // reject while r is live: 'x is suspended  [COST: over-suspension of the
                                     //   argument pick did not return; a precision loss, no runtime cost]
  ... endpoint(r) ... ; read(px)     // accept: claims resume at r's last use
```

Verdict: **accepted with a stated cost.** `pick` requires raising FN-1's
one-candidate ceiling to a **written finite origin set** and un-refusing
OWN-5's "no slice-valued control-flow join" for written sets. Both are
declaration-side, decidable, and change no caller's cost beyond the
over-suspension named above.

### P11 Write-once-then-frozen cache

```text
cache: own [Slot<V>; N] in 'C        // occupancy per slot; freeze per slot
get(k):
  if is_hole('C[k]) { put(&excl mut 'C[k], compute(k)) ; freeze('C[k]) }
                                     // accept: the fill claims 'C[k] ONLY (index split), not 'C
  return &shared 'C[k]               // accept: Frozen => the contents fact is program-wide invariant
r = get(k1)                          // r : ref<shared,'C[k1],V> on a Frozen path
s = get(k2)                          // accept: the fill of 'C[k2] claims a path disjoint from 'C[k1] iff k1 != k2
read(r)                              // accept if k1 != k2 is proved, OR if 'C[k1] is Frozen (then unconditional)
read(r)  with k1, k2 unrelated and 'C[k1] not frozen
                                     // reject: a may-overlapping write killed the contents fact;
                                     //   M7 payload: "prove k1 != k2" or "freeze the slot"
```

Verdict: **accepted with a stated cost** — the writer writes the `freeze`
transition. R1 alone passes the program (a slot goes `Hole → Init` once); the
`Frozen` state is what buys the reader the cross-fill fact and the
`!invariant.load` emission. Admission remains a capability question, and this
candidate answers it affirmatively at the cost of one state and one operation.

### P13 Relocation by a compacting third party

```text
pool: declared relocatable-by-a-third-party        // an R14(iii) actor right, written on the pool's declaration
h = handle(pool, obj)                              // accept: an index, not a path
p = pointer_of(h)                                  // reject AT FORMATION: no ref<_,'pool[..],_> may be formed
                                                   //   over a relocatable backing without a fixup form (R8a price)
pool.compact()                                     // accept: relocation is a declared event on 'pool's backing
read(pool[h])                                      // accept: handle indirection; backing('pool) Current
```

Verdict: **accepted as required** (the required verdict is a refusal at the
interior pointer, and it lands at the formation site, which is the repairable
place).

### P16 Abstraction over identities

```text
fn map_nodes<'g,T>(g: ref<excl mut,'g,Pool<Node<T>>>, f: fn(ref<shared,'e,T>) -> T)
     writes('g[_].data)                            // accept: one path parameter for the storage the callee names;
                                                   //   the element step is a bound wildcard, not N parameters
fn kernel<'s,E>(c: ref<excl mut,'s,Cols<E>>) writes('s.a,'s.b) ...
                                                   // accept: one parameter for eight columns; fields are derived paths
                                                   //   (R15's metric: parameters <= storages NAMED, not columns touched)
let h = |slice| helper(slice, input)               // accept: the closure type carries 'i from its capture;
                                                   //   the closure is non-escaping, bounded by endpoint of the capture
P6 with h                                          // accept: instantiation substitutes paths; facts cross the boundary
store h into a struct                              // reject unless the struct carries 'i as a parameter  [COST]
fn pick2<N: Nominal>(c: bool, x: N, y: N) -> N     // accept when N's own path parameters are declared;
                                                   //   distinctness of x and y is may-alias unless `distinct` is written
```

Verdict: **accepted with a stated cost** — reference-carrying closures are
second-class unless the storing type is parameterized, and a nominal that
hides a reference must carry its path parameter (today's STOR-5/BLK-4 area,
with BLK-4's recursive refusal staying reversed).

### P17 Partial operations

```text
q = a / d                            // reject: missing fact "d != 0"; M7 names it and the site
use d != 0 ; q = a / d               // accept: ProofContext discharges the domain; no branch emitted
b: u8 = narrow(x)                    // reject: missing "x < 256"
match narrow_checked(x) { Ok(b) => ... , TooLarge => ... }
                                     // accept: a written typed outcome (R12), the writer's own branch
y = v[i]                             // reject: missing "i < len(v)"
use i < len(v) ; y = v[i]            // accept
--- the frame half, which D1 decides ---
write(&excl mut 'v.data[j], e) ; y = v[i]
                                     // accept: the fact i < len(v) is supported by 'v.len, and the write's
                                     //   footprint is 'v.data[j]: the fact SURVIVES.  (Today ENT-5 kills at a
                                     //   whole-parameter footprint: 34 of 41 `len()` rebinds in the blind-writer
                                     //   corpus exist only for that reason.)
```

Verdict: **accepted as required.**

## 4. Requirements

### 4.1 Rows

| Row | Verdict | Reason (one sentence) |
|---|---|---|
| R1 | **met** | Occupancy and backing are per-path facts checked at every access, ending events are contract-visible, and a live claim never substitutes for a validity fact (P2, P4, P7). |
| R2 | **met** | Affine/linear `own` bindings, join-checked liveness and condition-term joins discharge every release exactly once on every path with no drop flag (P2, P8). |
| R3 | **met** | Copy/affine/linear classes are unchanged; `take`/`put`/`replace` are admitted as path-state events, restoring hole-and-refill (P7). |
| R4 | **met** | Distinctness comes from path steps (fields, proved indices, proved ranges) and formation freshness, and reaches values loaded from memory as per-load scopes (P5); a `shared·mut` path simply yields no fact. |
| R5 | **partial** | Ground (i) is met by footprints over paths plus the retained loan channel (P1, P2, P5, P6); grounds (ii) and (iii) need a checked-law channel and R14's level set, which this tuple neither supplies nor obstructs. |
| R6 | **partial** | Path-keyed kills remove the measured tax (P17's last line), but a whole-structure invariant whose support is the links still dies at every link write and costs one written `use` per operation (P3). |
| R7 | **partial** | The interface vocabulary carries every clause R7(a) lists (P9), but its size grows with states and origin sets, and the sufficiency clause stays provisional. |
| R8a | **met** | Every ending, relocating and replacing event updates `occupancy`/`backing`; interior references over a third-party-relocatable backing are refused at formation (P13). |
| R8b | **partial** | Nothing in the tuple obstructs alignment, layout or address-space demands, and nothing in it supplies them. |
| R9 | **met** | `shared·mut` admits several long-lived writers to one storage, and the only loss is the R4 facts on exactly those paths — which R9(d) assigns to R4 (P3, P7). |
| R10 | **partial** | A descriptor decomposes cleanly into three paths (wrapper `own`, description `shared·mut`, contents `foreign`), but P14 is underived here. |
| R11 | **met** | Domains are discharged by the fixed families or written steps; the frame half is path-keyed so bounds facts survive element writes (P17). |
| R12 | **met** | Outcome arms are ordinary branches; exit-state clauses are routed per variant, and each arm discharges its R2 obligations (P8, P9). |
| R13 | **partial** | Opt-in budgets are orthogonal to the tuple; nothing here proves a byte budget or a depth count. |
| R14 | **partial** | The mode/state vocabulary has a natural slot for R14(iv) (a `foreign` path state retaining no contents fact), but the model text itself is unwritten. |
| R15 | **partial** | Path parameters are ordinary type parameters and facts cross instantiation, but reference-carrying closures are second-class and parameter counts grow with storages named (P16). |
| M1 | **met** | Every family is fixed and terminating: path normalization, the four-ordering range family, index disequality, backward last-use liveness bounded by lattice height, and finite written origin sets; no search, no budget, no SMT. |
| M2 | **met** | No check, flag, count, generation or fence is introduced; holes, claims, states and condition terms are erased; P3's occupancy tag is data the source binds and branches on. |
| M3 | **met** | No writer-reachable escape; `shared·mut` weakens facts, never rules, and every axiom remains an enumerated entry. |
| M4 | **met** | One spelling per construct: two independent mode axes (not five mode names), one state per question, one name kind for identity/extent/distinctness. |
| M5 | **met** | Parallel permission remains a separate judgment that never feeds acceptance; a refused PAR-1 window leaves the sequential program. |
| M6 | **partial** | The state vocabulary is finite and enumerable, so the bounded small-model check is runnable per program, but the adequacy theorem is a stated later obligation. |
| M7 | **partial** | Every rejection above names either a missing discharge (`k != i`, `len < cap`, `d != 0`), a differing path, or a conflicting claim **with its endpoint** — but non-local mode conflict is reduced, not eliminated. |
| M8 | **violated** | The taught surface grows by two mode axes, four path-state facts, holes, origin sets, splitting and conditional exit clauses; it is paid for only partly by retiring OWN-3/4/10/11/14 and STOR-5, and K = 48k is already exceeded at ~130k. |
| M9 | **met** (as far as measurable) | The one measured fact channel in the project's history was produced by exactly this pair (resolved place under an exclusive reference), and P5/P6's obvious shape is the accepted shape. |
| M10 | **partial** | Per-statement work is quadratic in live paths (pairwise overlap) plus a residual-footprint subtraction set; the ceiling is plausible but unmeasured, and a one-token mode edit changes a bounded declaration set only because signatures pin the interface. |
| M11 | **met** | The revision is statable as a verdict diff over the retained corpus, and the retirement of regions is exactly what such a diff should measure. |

Counts: **15 met, 11 partial, 1 violated (M8).**

### 4.2 Price the candidate charges the compiler

| Forbidden to the compiler | Ground |
|---|---|
| Relocating any storage a reference names, absent a declared fixup form | R8a price, P13 |
| Inserting any check, flag, generation, lock or fence; eliding or inserting an outcome arm | M2, R9 price |
| Emitting a distinctness fact between two `shared·mut` paths, or between a parent and its child reborrow | R4(b) soundness; OWN-9's parenthesis |
| Emitting any fact the source did not check; re-deriving a stated fact to reach it | R4 price |
| Selecting acceptance by any budget, iteration cap or solver state | M1 |
| Reordering fields or dead-storing where a layout demand is written | R8b price |
| Deciding acceptance from a PAR judgment | M5 |

Free to the compiler: stack coloring and spill reuse of ended storage, loop
versioning and remainder loops, any fence implementation of a stated edge,
specialization of generic instances, and any schedule for a permitted overlap.

### 4.3 Writer cost

| Per | What must be written |
|---|---|
| Signature | one mode per reference parameter (always written, never inferred); one path parameter per storage named (elided when one per parameter); the footprint row; an entry/exit state clause per state-changing effect; a `distinct` clause per shared pair that must not alias; an origin set when a reference is returned |
| Loop | zero when entry and backedge agree; one `invariant` state line otherwise; one `use` step where an index or range disjointness is outside the fixed families |
| Join | zero — condition terms are derived from the source's own branch |
| Statement | `move`/`take`/`put`/`replace`/`split`/`freeze` where the operation occurs; one `use` step per partial operation whose domain the fixed families do not reach; one `use` step to re-establish a structure-wide invariant after a group of link writes |
| Never | region blocks, `outlives` bounds, endpoint annotations, drop flags |

Removed relative to today: the 120 region blocks the blind-writer corpus needed
against the OWN-6 wall, and 34 of 41 `len()` rebinds.

---

## 5. Consequences at D5–D13

| Point | Forced | Foreclosed |
|---|---|---|
| D5 interference source | **Loans on references beside footprints** (the loan channel survives for free, and PAR-1's source-equivalence ground is preserved verbatim); **Declared region partitions and index domains** for P6; **Permission site and window granularity** = statement window plus counted loop | **Footprints or rows alone, no loan clause**; **Fractional or counting permissions** (M1, M2); **Runtime dependence tracking**; **Unrestricted aliasing, exclusivity re-derived by the compiler** (M1 stability) |
| D6 distinctness default | A **hybrid**: two `excl` parameters are distinct by the exclusivity rule with no clause (the family's structural gift); shared parameters are **may-alias by default, callee copes**, with **pairwise clauses in the signature** where a fact is wanted; **index-arithmetic distinctness** for elements | **Distinct names are distinct storage** (unsound at P2's `S` vs `b1`); **whole-program inference**; **dynamic distinctness check** |
| D7 contract vocabulary | **Requires/ensures over identity states**; **footprint and frame clauses**; **existential result identities**; **outcome-routed states and result obligations**; a **closed catalog with a size budget** is mandatory given M8 | **No contracts: whole-program inference**; **prophecies and backward functions** (not needed once exit states exist); **derived contracts, writer-confirmed** (FN-1 stays a written interface) |
| D8 relocation | **Aggregates travel as handles, storage fixed**; **explicit relocating move as the storage-ending event**; **reallocation as a contract-visible name change**; **pinning** is the default for any path a reference names | **Compiler-inferred placement** where a reference exists; moving collectors; **relocation with a fixup channel** as a default (admitted only as a declared form) |
| D9 containers | **Path identity `'v[i]`**; **existential backing per formation**; **bounded views and proved subrange subdivision**; **split-and-join range tokens** (this is view splitting); **pools with stable index handles** plus writer-bound occupancy | **Generations and epochs**; **runtime bounds checks as the safety story**; per-element ghost tokens (a second name kind, M8) |
| D10 concurrency | **Lock as custodian of identity state** (the lock holds the claim while unheld); **typed reference capabilities and sendability** as a third axis on the same mode vocabulary; **structured fork/join with linear task handles** | **Transactions**; **shared storage keeps no facts** as the only story (R9 is already writable); **atomics with an exposed model** as the default sharing route |
| D11 external resources | **Three identities per descriptor**; **foreign identity: retain no contents fact** as a path state; **states as ordinary enums or identities with declared states** | **Second host-authority category**; ambient forgeable host access; an effect category keyed on host crossing (R10) |
| D12 surface form | **Qualifier-prefixed types and per-state spellings**; **elision and implicit identity parameters** (mandatory under M8); **region block and borrow-endpoint spelling** resolved as: no blocks, endpoints inferred and printable; **diagnostics as a specified surface** (M7's payload is part of the design, not the implementation) | **Modes as sugar over pointer plus state** (modes are primitive here); **conventions instead of pointer types**; **flat three-address source** |
| D13 validation | **Bounded exhaustive enumeration** per program (M6(i)); the **fixed discriminating program set**; **dual acceptance and acceptance-set diffs** to measure exactly what retiring OWN-3/4/10/11/14 gains and loses; **writer-trial and repair-loop benchmarks** as evidence with the model pinned | Acceptance criteria drawn from writer trials (owner decision 12); whole-corpus regeneration as evidence |

---

## 6. Weaknesses, and the strongest objection

### 6.1 Honest weaknesses

| # | Weakness | How far it is answered |
|---|---|---|
| W1 | **M8 is violated.** Two axes, four path states, holes, origin sets, splitting and conditional exit clauses all enter the taught surface. | Partly paid: OWN-3 regions, OWN-4 named-region liveness, OWN-10 borrow-storage duration, OWN-11's region role, OWN-14's reborrow family and STOR-5's region-free clause all retire, and one name kind replaces two. Net direction is unmeasured; I do not claim it is negative. |
| W2 | **`shared·mut` is a fact hole.** Every path reachable through it loses distinctness and contents facts. | Contained by construction: the loss is exactly on the paths the writer declared shared-writable (C5), it is visible in the type, and it degrades facts, never rules (M3 holds — it is not an escape). But a writer who reaches for it by habit gets a slow program with no diagnostic, which is the one failure this candidate cannot detect. |
| W3 | **P3's graph needs handles, not references.** Stored interior references into a reused pool slot are refused. | Answered as a D9 consequence, not a D1–D4 defect: under M2(ii) no design invalidates a stored pointer into a reused slot without a proved static index or writer-bound occupancy. The cost is one `match` per traversal step. |
| W4 | **Partial suspension and residual footprints are new checker state.** `'v` minus `{'v[i],'v[j]}` must be represented, normalized and compared. | Decidable and quadratic in live paths, on the existing OWN-7 path algebra; but it is a genuine addition to M10's measure and is unmeasured. |
| W5 | **Origin sets reopen a closed question.** OWN-5's "no slice-valued control-flow join" and FN-1's one-candidate rule were adopted for a reason. | Reopened only for **written** finite sets at declarations, never inferred at joins; the caller cost is over-suspension, which is a precision loss with no runtime component. The inference version stays refused. |
| W6 | **Last-use endpoints are still non-local.** The conflict moves from the end of a region to the last use of a holder, which can be far away. | Mitigated, not removed: the endpoint is computable and printable, so the diagnostic can name *both* the conflicting claim and the exact statement that ends it — which is what turns a coordinate-only message into a repair instruction. |
| W7 | **Two questions remain fused in the reference**: interference and aliasing. | Conceded as intended: they are the same question (who may write while this is held), and the family's value is precisely that one written mode answers it for both the checker and the backend. |

### 6.2 The strongest objection I expect

> **"You have not fixed the coupling, you have hidden it. A Rust-style
> reference answers five unrelated questions at once, and that coupling is the
> documented reason a change to ownership drags regions, effects and parallel
> permission along (MECHANISM-MAP §1). Your candidate keeps the reference as
> the permission carrier and then repairs each failure with a special case:
> partial suspension for P1, a fourth mode for P7 and P3, holes for P7, origin
> sets for P9, conditional exit clauses for P4, handles for P3, second-class
> closures for P16. That is seven exceptions to one rule. The hazard ladder's
> finding is that *no* hazard needs borrowing once storage state and identity
> exist; you have therefore paid M8 in full for a mechanism the ladder shows is
> optional, and M7's measured wall — non-local mode conflict, 120 region blocks
> and three coordinate-only diagnostics — is a property of the rule itself, not
> of its endpoints."**

Answered as far as I can:

1. **Three of the five questions do leave the reference.** Validity, lifecycle
   and frame-keying move to the path: a reference no longer blocks `free`
   (P7), no longer blocks `push` (P4), and no longer keys a kill (P17's last
   line). That is not a repair per program; it is one seam, cut once, and it is
   what makes P2, P4, P7 and P11 derivable. The remaining two questions —
   interference and aliasing — are one question, and fusing them is the point.
2. **The seven "exceptions" are two mechanisms.** Partial suspension, view
   splitting and bounded reborrows are one mechanism (a claim is subtractable
   along paths) enabled by D1. Holes, `Frozen` and conditional exit clauses are
   one mechanism (facts keyed by path, not by reference) enabled by the same
   choice. Origin sets are a declaration-side generalization of a rule that
   already exists (VIEW-6 admits sets; FN-1 caps them at one). Handles and
   second-class closures are D9 and D15 consequences that follow from M2, not
   from D4.
3. **The ladder's finding is about hazards, and it is correct.** Borrowing
   refuses no hazard here either: every rejection above cites a path state, a
   multiplicity, or a missing disjointness proof. What the mode buys is not
   safety — it is (a) the loan channel, which EVIDENCE §E records as *the whole
   of the information loss* when references are replaced by footprints, and
   (b) the per-load alias facts that were actually measured, whose derivation
   was a resolved place under an exclusive reference. A design that keeps the
   facts must re-manufacture an exclusivity claim on an identity, which is the
   alternative `permission-judgment.md` recorded as rejected for duplicating
   the borrow checker.
4. **On M7 I concede the shape of the objection and dispute its finality.** The
   measured wall is real, and endpoints alone do not remove non-locality. What
   they change is the payload: today's rejection can name only a coordinate,
   because a lexical region has no semantic end to point at; an endpoint is a
   statement, and a claim's conflict is a pair. Whether that converts into a
   measured repair-rate improvement is exactly the experiment D13 must run
   before this candidate is believed on M7, and I do not claim the result in
   advance.
5. **On M8 I do not dispute the objection.** The row is marked violated, the
   retirement list is the only payment offered, and the net token delta is
   unmeasured. If the owner fixes K and the subsystem share (owner decision
   16), this candidate is the one most likely to be refused on that row.


# File: candidate-refinement-heap.md

# Candidate core model: `refinement-heap`

Research date: 2026-09-16. Generator: `refinement-heap`. One coherent choice of
a family for each of D1, D2, D3, D4, derived against the settled requirement
list (VERDICT-D0 §2), the couplings (§4), the premises (§5), the owner interim
positions (§7), the hazard ladder (MECHANISM-MAP §3) and the discriminating
programs P1–P19. Nothing here is compared to another candidate; every claim
about a program is shown as pseudocode with per-line accept/reject comments in
the ladder's style. Supersede in place.

---

## 1. The tuple

| Point | Family (name exactly as in OPTIONS.md) | Members drawn on | Members explicitly not taken |
|---|---|---|---|
| **D1** | **Site-minted identity** | SYS-D1-01 (allocation named by its call site), RAD-D1-02 (SSA definition point), RAD-D1-18 (fresh nominal type per site), HIS-D1-22 ADOPTED (extent item by instance + `region_stmt` NodePath) | THE-D1-07 (generative functor per site) as a *surface*; THE-D1-26 (staged erasure) |
| **D2** | **State index on the computation type or threaded store** | RAD-D2-14 (threaded store type) as the semantic core; THE-D2-13 (parameterised index `M i j A`) as the *judgment* form `{Σ} s {Σ'}` | THE-D2-11 (Hoare monad) and THE-D2-12 (predicate-transformer index) as a *writer-visible* surface — direct-style imperative code is kept; the index is on the judgment, never on a monad the writer threads |
| **D3** | **Refinement predicates as state** *combined with* **State as a type index** | AI-D3-06 (predicates from `invariant` clauses), THE-D3-11 (refinement / liquid state), HIS-D3-19 FLOATED (refined integer domains and niches); RAD-D3-12 (state as a dependent type index), THE-D3-18 (layout as a type index) | The three-state minimum alone (AI-D3-01) is *contained*, not adopted: `Owned/Hole/Ended` are three cells of the store index, and everything finer is a refinement, not a fourth state |
| **D4** | **Declared coincidence** | AI-D4-03 (`alias 'a 'b;` per coinciding pair), RAD-D4-10 (declared coincidence sets), SYS-D4-03 (inverted `restrict`, checked), THE-D4-20 (identities declared equal at call or struct), HIS-D4-11 FLOATED (coincidence declared per pair at a boundary); **bunched spelling** from THE-D6-04 (`∗` disjoint vs `∧` overlapping per conjunct) and THE-D6-05 (bunched parameter list `,` vs `;`); **sub-atom refinement** from HIS-D4-13 ADOPTED (proved half-open view extents) and SYS-D4-10 (proved-disjoint byte ranges) | AI-D4-01 / THE-D4-02 (unrestricted, no declaration) — coincidence must be *stated* or R4 loses soundness at call boundaries (C3); THE-D4-01 / HIS-D4-01 (shared-xor-mutable) |

Prior art: Alias Types (Smith–Walker–Morrisett, ESOP 2000) and L3 (TLCA 2005)
for the store index with copyable pointers and strong update; Hoare Type Theory
(Nanevski et al., ICFP 2006) for `{Σ} · {Σ'}` on a declaration; Liquid types
(PLDI 2008), low-level liquid types (POPL 2010) and Flux (PLDI 2023) for
refinements as the state of a storage; RefinedC (PLDI 2021) for refinements
carrying both ownership and contents at C-level granularity; O'Hearn and Pym
(1999) and Ishtiaq–O'Hearn (POPL 2001) for the bunched `,`/`;` argument groups.

### Why these four cohere

| # | Claim | Derivation |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Site-minting supplies exactly the freshness that "declared coincidence" needs and nothing else.** | D4's default (distinct unless declared) is sound only if two *names* cannot silently denote one storage (C3: "never inequality of identity names"). A site-minted atom denotes the storage that site created; two sites therefore denote different storage *by construction*, not by an inequality the checker had to prove. The only way two names coincide is a coincidence declaration or an identity passed twice — both syntactically visible. |
| 2 | **Site-minting is deliberately coarse, and D3's refinements pay for the coarseness once.** | A site says nothing about parts of one allocation (P1 elements, P2 arena blocks, P5 columns, P3 pool slots). Rather than add finer identity kinds (D1's element/range/column families, each a new vocabulary), every sub-storage is the *same atom* under a **refined extent**. C1 asks for "one refinement vocabulary [to] serve state, distinctness, footprints and kills"; this tuple has exactly one, and D1 stays at one rule. |
| 3 | **The store index is the only place that can hold a state that is a property of storage rather than of a pointer.** | P7 requires a hole made through `p` to be visible through `q`. A pointer type that carried permission would have to be invalidated at `q`; a store index keyed by the atom is read by both. This is Alias Types' original result and it is why D2 must be the store index once D1 is an atom and D3 is a per-storage predicate. |
| 4 | **One decidable fragment serves R1, R4, R5, R6, R11 and R13.** | Extent membership (R1), extent disjointness (R4, R5), footprint overlap for kills (R6), operation domains (R11) and declared budgets and depths (R13) are all entailments in the *same* quantifier-free arithmetic. M8 is paid once; R11 and R13 cost zero extra vocabulary. This is the tuple's central economy and the reason D3 is a refinement family rather than an enumerated state set. |
| 5 | **M1 is kept by fixing the fragment, which is possible only because D1 is coarse.** | Liquid inference needs a solver because it searches for *which* qualifier holds. Here the goal is always supplied (an access names its extent; a footprint pair names two extents; a partial operation names its domain), so the checker only *decides* a stated goal — a fixed normal form plus a fixed closure, no search, no portfolio, no cap. A finer D1 would have pushed identity equality itself into the solver. |

---

## 2. The model

### 2.1 Identities, pointers, extents

```text
atom      ι   ::= the storage minted by one syntactic site
                  (an alloc call, a frame `let`, a parameter position, a record
                   field's storage, an arena/region block, a container formation)
extent    R   ::= a set of offsets described by an RF predicate over one index
                  variable, e.g. [0,n) | {i} | [w*s, w*s+s) | [0,n)∖{i,j} | .len
key       κ   ::= ι @ R
containment   ι' ⊑ ι     ("ι' was carved out of ι"; not distinctness)
pointer type  ptr(ι, δ)  where δ is a refined offset term
```

A pointer is **Copy**, carries **no permission, no duration, no region, no
state**, and is not invalidated by anything. Its type names one atom and one
offset term. Identity binders are **never invented by the writer**: a site
mints, the compiler prints, and the writer transcribes only where the atom
crosses a signature.

### 2.2 What the checker holds per storage — the store index Σ

Σ is a finite map from keys to **guarded cells**. A cell is one of:

| Cell | Meaning | R1 sub-property it answers |
|---|---|---|
| `Owned(τ[φ])` | live, initialized, contents satisfy refinement φ | (i) pass |
| `Hole(τ)` | live, no value (a `take` emptied it) | (i) fail on read |
| `Ended` | the identity ended; **permanent tombstone**, no rule ever re-adds an entry for that key | (ii) fail on any access |
| `Foreign(class)` | R14(iv) declared access class; no contents fact survives any operation the agent could interleave | (iv) |

A **guarded cell** is a finite list `[(g₁,c₁), …, (g_k,c_k)]` whose guards are RF
formulas over *captured branch atoms*, mutually exclusive and exhaustive. This
is D3's "state as a term over captured conditions" (C6) obtained for free:
a guard is an RF formula, so no second algebra is introduced.

Σ is **checker state indexed on the judgment** `{Σ} stmt {Σ'}`. The writer sees
it only at three places: signatures, loop heads, and the rare join whose guard
atom is not RF-expressible.

### 2.3 The refinement fragment RF (the M1 commitment)

```text
term       t  ::= Σ cᵢ·mᵢ + k              cᵢ, k literal integers
monomial   m  ::= x | x·y                  program variables, fixed order, degree ≤ 2
atom       a  ::= t ⋈ t'      ⋈ ∈ { =, ≠, <, ≤ }
                | t ≡ k (mod M)            M a literal (alignment, stride, niche)
formula    φ  ::= conjunction of atoms (goals and guards are QF conjunctions;
                  disjunction appears only as a guard list, never inside RF)
```

**Decision procedure** (specified, deterministic, terminating, solver-free):

1. canonicalize every term to the normal form above (fixed monomial order);
2. build a constraint graph over the monomials present in hypotheses ∪ goal,
   taken as opaque atoms;
3. close under a **fixed five-rule set**, creating no new monomial:
   (a) transitivity of `≤`; (b) addition of two constraints;
   (c) scaling by a positive literal; (d) **product monotonicity**
   `0 ≤ a ∧ b ≤ c ⇒ a·b ≤ a·c`; (e) congruence combination for a common literal
   modulus;
4. decide the goal by subsumption against the closure.

Termination is structural (the monomial set never grows). Cost is `O(n³)` in
monomials (transitive closure). There is **no widening, no iteration cap, no
budget and no search**; acceptance is a total function of the source bytes.
A goal the closure does not reach is **not** retried by another family: the
writer supplies an explicit finite `use` step from a closed lemma catalog, and
the checker verifies the written instantiation without rediscovering it.

### 2.4 How state changes

| Operation | Σ before | Σ after | Fact used |
|---|---|---|---|
| `alloc<τ>(n) as ι` | ι ∉ dom Σ | `ι@[0,n) ↦ Hole(τ)`; `size(ι)=n` | site freshness |
| `write(p:ptr(ι,δ), v)` | `ι@R ↦ Hole|Owned`, RF ⊨ `δ ∈ R` | split R at δ; `ι@{δ} ↦ Owned(τ[v])` | RF extent split |
| `take(p)` | `ι@{δ} ↦ Owned(τ[φ])` | `ι@{δ} ↦ Hole(τ)`; value out carrying φ | — |
| `put(q,v)`, `q:ptr(ι,δ)` | `ι@{δ} ↦ Hole(τ)` | `Owned(τ[v])` | q's type names ι; p is never consulted |
| `replace(p,new)` | `Owned(τ[φ])` | `Owned(τ[new])`; old out | one step, no intermediate hole |
| `free(ι)` / arena reset / scope exit | every key of ι `Owned`or`Hole`, no obligation open | every key of ι ↦ `Ended`; tombstone persists to the end of the declaration | permanence: no rule re-adds |
| relocating `move x` | `ι ↦ …` | `ι ↦ Ended`; fresh `ι'` at the destination site, refinements transported by renaming **in Σ only** | R8a event; pointer types are never rewritten |
| `push`/`reserve` | `ι_b ↦ Owned(…)` | guarded: `[(len₀<cap₀, Owned(ι_b …)), (¬, Ended(ι_b) ∧ fresh ι_b')]` | the one conditional Σ entry; the *caller* discharges the guard, the program does not branch |
| slot reuse in a pool | `ι@{s} ↦ Ended` | `ι@{s} ↦ Owned` at a **fresh occupant index** `o+1`; a pointer typed at `o` no longer satisfies its `requires` | erased ghost counter; never compared at run time |

### 2.5 Join and loop head

**Join (fixed rule J).** For each key, concatenate the arms' guarded lists with
the arm conditions conjoined, then canonicalize: sort conjunctions, drop
RF-unsatisfiable guards, merge syntactically equal cells. No lattice, no Top,
no widening. The guard list's length is bounded **structurally** — by the
number of syntactic writes to that key inside the declaration — not by a cap
(a cap would be a budget selecting acceptance, which M1 forbids).

**Loop head.** The writer writes one `invariant` Σ clause naming every key the
body changes. Keys not named must be untouched by the body's written footprint
(checked, not assumed). The checker verifies entry ⊨ invariant, body preserves
it, exit gives invariant ∧ ¬condition. **There is no fixpoint iteration at all**,
so M1 needs no lattice-height argument and M10's loop cost is linear in the
written invariant.

### 2.6 What a signature states (R7's vocabulary)

```text
fn name<'a, 'b, …>(params) -> τ
  requires  Σ_in                 // per key: cell class, refined extent, contents φ
  ensures   Σ_out                // same; ∃'c for fresh storage; Ended for ended
  reads     ('a @ R), …          // refined extents, not static field paths
  writes    ('b @ R), …
  ends      { 'b when φ, … }     // the storage-ending set, contract-visible
  outcomes  { Ok(τ) | Short(n) | … }   // each arm with its own Σ_out and ends
  groups    ('a , 'b ; 'c)       // `,` = distinct (default); `;` = may coincide
```

A record declaration carries the bunch once and every signature inherits it:

```text
struct Cols<E> { a ∗ b ∗ c ∗ d ∗ e ∗ f ∗ g ∗ h : buffer<E> }   // `∗` is the default
struct Dup    { head ; tail : ptr(…) }                          // `;` written once
```

Declaration-side checks (R7(a)): a `requires` that is RF-unsatisfiable is
rejected at the declaration; an `ensures` naming an origin no caller can name is
rejected at the declaration; a body that ends storage not in `ends` is rejected.

### 2.7 Erasure (M6(iii))

Erased before lowering: every atom, every Σ entry, every guard, every
refinement, every occupant index, every `use` step, every group declaration.
Lowering sees addresses and the writer's own branches. Licensed facts exported
under R4: per-load `!alias.scope` keyed by `(ι, R)`; `initializes(lo,hi)` from
`Hole→Owned` on a refined extent; parameter `noalias`/`readonly` from the
footprints and the `,` groups; `willreturn` from a written termination measure.
No fact is emitted for a pair inside a `;` group or for an `⊑` pair.

---

## 3. Derivations

Notation is the ladder's: pseudocode lines, an `accept`/`reject` comment, and
the fact used. `Σ:` lines show the store index.

### P1 Container split with a runtime index

```text
v : vec<u64> as 'v ; backing 'b                 // two atoms, two sites
// Σ: 'v.desc ↦ Owned(Vec{len=n, cap=c, backing='b}) ; 'b@[0,n) ↦ Owned(u64)

let (pi, pj) = split2(v, i, j)
  // sig: requires i < len(v) ∧ j < len(v) ∧ i ≠ j
  //      ensures 'b@{i} ↦ Owned, 'b@{j} ↦ Owned, 'b@([0,n)∖{i,j}) ↦ Owned
  // accept: RF ⊨ i<n, j<n from the descriptor's len refinement; i≠j is the
  //   writer's own premise at this call.  fact: RF extent split
write(pi, x)   // accept: key 'b@{i} is Owned.        W = {'b@{i}}
write(pj, y)   // accept: key 'b@{j} is Owned.        W = {'b@{j}}
// PAR: R5(a)(i) for the two statements:
//   goal {i} ∩ {j} = ∅ ; RF ⊨ from i ≠ j            ⇒ overlap permitted
//   no loan, no borrow scope, no duration was consulted

read(v[k])
  // reject [R1(i), precision]: the access names 'b@{k}; no key of Σ covers {k}
  //   because [0,n)∖{i,j} does not contain k without k≠i ∧ k≠j.
  // diagnostic (M7): missing fact `k ≠ i ∧ k ≠ j` at this read;
  //   tree location = this subscript; repair = a branch or a `requires`
if k != i && k != j {
  read(v[k])   // accept: the path condition adds the two atoms; RF ⊨ k ∈ [0,n)∖{i,j}
}              //   the only branch executed is the writer's (M2(ii))

merge2(pi, pj, v)
  // ensures 'b@[0,n) ↦ Owned : re-fuses the three keys into one
push(v, 8)
  // requires 'b@[0,len) whole.  Before merge2: reject, naming the two carved
  //   keys.  After merge2: accept.   fact: RF extent coverage
```

**Verdict: accepted as required.** Sequential legality is by RF entailment, not
by a borrow scope; parallel permission comes from the same entailment; the
`v[k]` diagnostic names the missing fact exactly; no runtime check exists.
Stated cost: `split2`/`merge2` must exist as kernel forms (two RF entailments
each); they are not free syntax.

### P2 Arena with independently released blocks

```text
arena A as ('M metadata, 'S bytes)               // one site, two atoms
// Σ: 'M ↦ Owned(Meta{bump=0}) ; 'S@[0,cap) ↦ Hole(byte)

b1 = alloc(A,64) as 'b1
  // sig: writes ('M) ; ensures ∃'x. 'x ⊑ 'S ∧ 'x@[0,64) ↦ Hole ∧ bump' = bump+64
  // accept.  fact: fresh atom minted at this site; ⊑ is containment, not distinctness
b2 = alloc(A,64) as 'b2
b3 = alloc(A,64) as 'b3

fill(b1) ∥ fill(b2) ∥ fill(b3)
  // fill sig: writes ('x @ [0,64)) ; reads nothing ; ends nothing
  // accept R5(a)(i): W₁={'b1@[0,64)}, W₂={'b2@…}, W₃={'b3@…};
  //   'b1,'b2,'b3 are three distinct minting sites ⇒ pairwise distinct by
  //   construction, no arithmetic needed.  fact: site freshness
  // 'M is written by alloc and free only — no fill row names it, so nobody
  //   holds A exclusively between operations (there are no loans in this model)

free(A, b2)
  // ends { 'b2 } ; writes ('M)
  // Σ: every key of 'b2 ↦ Ended (tombstone) ; bump unchanged (free-list in 'M)
b4 = alloc(A,32) as 'b4
  // fresh atom; ensures 'b4 ⊑ 'S.  Says nothing about 'b2's bytes.
read(p) where p : ptr('b2, 0)
  // reject [R1(ii)]: 'b2 is Ended, permanently.  The reuse of its bytes by 'b4
  //   is invisible: no rule maps addresses to atoms, so address reuse can never
  //   revive an ended identity.  fact: tombstone permanence
read(b1)                      // accept: 'b1@[0,64) ↦ Owned
free(A,b1); free(A,b3); free(A,b4)
  // each accept once; a second free rejects on cell = Ended, naming the first
// R4 negative test: the pair ('S, 'b1) is an ⊑ edge, never a disjointness edge,
//   so no `noalias` is emitted between the arena bytes and a live block.
```

**Verdict: accepted as required**, including R4's negative test and R2's
exactly-once accounting.

### P3 Graph with back edges in a pool

```text
pool P of Node as 'p                     // one atom; slots are extents 'p@{s}
// declared once, on the pool type:
//   invariant links : ∀s ∈ live. next(s) ∈ live ∧ prev(s) ∈ live
//   (a refinement over the pool's value; `live` is a refined index set in Σ)

insert(n, a, b):                          // requires a,b,n ∈ live ∧ a≠n ∧ b≠n
  set 'p@{a}.next = n   // accept.  W={'p@{a}.next}; kills only facts whose
                        //   support RF-overlaps that extent (R6)
  set 'p@{n}.prev = a   // accept: several writable paths reach node n and
  set 'p@{n}.next = b   //   nothing is exclusive — R9's shape, hazard is R1's alone
  set 'p@{b}.prev = n   // accept
  use links_insert(a, b, n)
      // one written finite step re-establishes `links` from the four writes;
      // the checker verifies the instantiation, it does not search for it (M1)

remove(m):
  ends 'p@{m}           // Σ: 'p@{m} ↦ Ended ; occupant(m) := occupant(m)+1
read(q) where q : ptr('p, {m} @ occ o₀)
  // reject [R1(ii)]: the extent is Ended, and after reuse the cell's occupant
  //   is o₁ ≠ o₀, so `requires occupant(m) = o₀` fails.  The occupant index is
  //   a ghost refinement, erased; no runtime word, tag or compare exists (M2)

par map over s in live(P) { set 'p@{s}.data = f(read('p@{s}.data)) }
  // accept R5(a)(i): for s ≠ s', goal {s} ∩ {s'} = ∅, RF ⊨ from the iteration
  //   domain's distinctness.  fact: RF extent disjointness within one atom
traverse: p = head; while p ∈ live { read('p@{p}.data); p = next(p) }
  // accept: `links` gives next(p) ∈ live without re-proving it per step (R6:
  //   the four link writes above named extents the invariant's support covers,
  //   and the invariant was re-established once by the `use` step)
```

**Verdict: accepted as required.** The invariant is stated once and reused; the
parallel map is permitted by RF distinctness of slot extents; removal
invalidates every path to `m`.
Stated cost: the erased occupant index appears in the pointer type and must be
written where it crosses a signature.

### P4 Cursor over a growing vector

```text
struct Cursor<'b> { at: ptr('b, ·), i: u64 }     // the atom is a type parameter
let v as 'v ; backing 'b ; Σ: 'b@[0,len) ↦ Owned
let c = Cursor { at: ptr_of(v), i: 0 }           // Cursor<'b>; a stored pointer

a = c.read()
  // requires 'b@{c.i} ↦ Owned ∧ c.i < len(v)
  // accept: RF ⊨ 0 < len from the caller's precondition.  fact: Σ lookup + RF

push(v, 5)
  // sig ensures: [(len₀<cap₀, backing='b ∧ 'b@[0,len₀+1) Owned),
  //               (¬(len₀<cap₀), Ended('b) ∧ ∃'b2. backing='b2)]
  // accept: push is never blocked — no borrow of 'b exists to block it

b = c.read()
  // reject [R1(ii)]: 'b's cell is guarded and the path condition entails
  //   neither arm.  diagnostic: missing fact `len₀ < cap₀`; the killing
  //   operation named is `push` (R6's killer diagnostic)
if len(v) < cap(v) { push(v,5); b = c.read() }
  // accept: the guard is discharged by the writer's own branch; the second
  //   read is legal because the candidate carried "still valid" across push
  //   as a proof, not as a borrow

reserve(v, m) ; c.read()
  // reject when RF ⊭ cap₀ ≥ m: reserve's `ends { 'b when cap₀ < m }` applies
free(v)      // ends { 'b, 'v }
c.read()     // reject [R1(ii)] forever: tombstone on 'b
```

**Verdict: accepted as required.** Validity is decided by state and proof; the
stored pointer never blocks `push`.

### P5 Struct-of-arrays kernel

```text
struct Cols<E> { a ∗ b ∗ c ∗ d ∗ e ∗ f ∗ g ∗ h : buffer<E> }
  // `∗` is the default for record fields: eight field-storage sites, eight
  //   atoms, pairwise distinct by construction.  The writer writes nothing.

fn kernel(c: &Cols<u64>, n: u64)
   requires  ∀ κ ∈ bunch(c). κ@[0,n) ↦ Owned(u64)
   reads  (c.c@[0,n)), (c.d@[0,n)), (c.e@[0,n)), (c.f@[0,n)),
          (c.g@[0,n)), (c.h@[0,n)), (c.a@[0,n)), (c.b@[0,n))
   writes (c.a@[0,n)), (c.b@[0,n))
   groups (∗ c)          // one bunched binder, not eight identity parameters
{
  for i in 0..n
    invariant  ∀ κ ∈ bunch(c). κ@[0,n) ↦ Owned(u64)     // one written line
  {
    set a[i] = f_wrap(a[i], c[i], d[i])
      // accept: 'a@{i} ↦ Owned ; RF ⊨ i < n from the loop domain
      // overflow behavior selected per site by the operator spelling (R11)
    set b[i] = g_wrap(b[i], e[i], f[i], g[i], h[i])
      // accept
  }
}
// R5(a)(i), PAR-2 iteration overlap, i ≠ i':
//   W_i = {'a@{i}, 'b@{i}} ; goal {i} ∩ {i'} = ∅ ; RF ⊨ from i ≠ i'  ⇒ accept
// R4 export: each load carries its key ('x, {i}); the eight atoms are pairwise
//   distinct by minting ⇒ eight `!alias.scope`s, one per column, on the loads
//   — per-load, not per-parameter.  Nothing in the language forbids retention.
```

**Verdict: accepted as required.** The obvious shape is the fast shape: the
eight distinctness facts come from the record declaration's default `∗`, with
zero writer annotation, and reach lowering per load.

### P6 Range partition helper

```text
fn helper<'o>(s: slice<'o,u8>, input: &In<'in>)
   reads  ('in @ [0,m))
   writes ('o @ extent(s))
   groups ('o , 'in)
   ends   { }

let out as 'out ; Σ: 'out@[0,n) ↦ Hole(u8)
let s = n / k                     // requires k ≠ 0 (R11) — writer's precondition
for w in 0..k
  invariant 'out@[0, w*s) ↦ Owned(u8) ∧ 'out@[w*s, n) ↦ Hole(u8)
{
  helper(slice_of(out, w*s, w*s + s), input)
    // slice_of: requires w*s + s ≤ n ; ensures extent = [w*s, w*s+s) ⊑ 'out
    // accept: RF ⊨ w*s+s ≤ k*s ≤ n by rules (b),(c),(d) from w+1 ≤ k ∧ 0 ≤ s
}
// R5(a)(i) for iterations w ≠ w' (say w+1 ≤ w'):
//   goal  [w*s, w*s+s) ∩ [w'*s, w'*s+s) = ∅
//   reduce to  w*s + s ≤ w'*s , i.e. (w+1)*s ≤ w'*s
//   RF rule (d) product monotonicity with 0 ≤ s (free: s : u64) and w+1 ≤ w'
//   ⇒ accept, automatically, no `use` step
// R7: the caller judged the whole thing from helper's `writes` row alone;
//   the helper body was checked once against it.  No worker count appears.
```

**Verdict: accepted as required** — *conditional on RF rule (d) being in the
fixed family*. This is the design commitment that makes P6 free; without it the
program needs one `use mul_mono(s, w, w')` step per loop.

### P7 Take, put, replace through aliases

```text
// p and q both name atom 'A: the writer passed 'A twice inside a `;` group,
//   or q was formed from p.  Both are ptr('A, ·), both Copy.
v = take(p)
  // Σ: 'A ↦ Hole(T).  fact: state is a cell of Σ keyed by the atom
read(q)
  // reject [R1(i)]: 'A ↦ Hole.  The hole is visible through q because q's type
  //   names 'A; nothing about p, its scope or its "borrow" is consulted.
put(q, move v)
  // Σ: 'A ↦ Owned(T[v]).  fact: another alias may fill the hole
read(p)                 // accept: 'A ↦ Owned
old = replace(p, new)
  // Σ: 'A ↦ Owned(T[new]); old out.  No intermediate hole exists (SET-2 shape)
read(q)
  // accept, and RF ⊨ contents = new: the refinement carries the value fact
  //   through the alias without a second mechanism
free('A)                // Σ: 'A ↦ Ended (tombstone)
read(p)                 // reject [R1(ii)] forever: no rule re-adds a key for 'A
```

**Verdict: accepted as required.** This is the tuple's home case: "state is a
property of the storage, not of the pointer" is not a rule here, it is the
shape of Σ.

### P8 Conditional release and loop exits (CASES.md B10–B13, L04–L06)

```text
// B10–B13
if c { free(a) } else { free(b) }
// join by rule J; guards are the captured atom c:
//   'a ↦ [(c, Ended), (¬c, Owned)]       'b ↦ [(c, Owned), (¬c, Ended)]
// no runtime bit was created: c is a value the source already branched on

use_survivor(a, b)
  // reject: requires Owned on both keys; neither guard is entailed by the
  //   path condition at this point.  diagnostic (M7): key 'a is Owned only
  //   under guard ¬c — names the path whose state differs
if c { use(b); free(b) } else { use(a); free(a) }
  // accept both arms: the path condition discharges the guard on each key.
  // The branch executed is the writer's own; there is no drop flag, because
  // the guard is erased and the cell class was never a runtime value (M2(ii))
// at the declaration's exit: for each guard, every minted key is Ended or
//   transferred out by `ensures` ⇒ R2 definiteness on every path

// L04–L06
loop
  invariant 'p ↦ Owned(T)            // one written loop-head Σ clause
{
  if stop { break }                  // break edge carries Σ: 'p ↦ Owned
  v = take(p)                        // 'p ↦ Hole
  …
  put(p, move v)                     // 'p ↦ Owned — matches the invariant
}
// accept: body-end state equals the invariant after canonicalization
free(p)
  // accept: every exit edge (break and the normal exit) carries 'p ↦ Owned
// a body that forgot `put` rejects at the loop's back edge, naming the key and
//   the invariant line it failed to re-establish
```

**Verdict: accepted as required.** No drop flag; the writer's branches carry
the state; rejection names the path whose state differs.

### P9 A callee that changes storage state

```text
fn drain<'x>(x: &T<'x>)
   requires 'x ↦ Owned(T)   ensures 'x ↦ Hole(T)   writes ('x)

fn reserve<'b>(v: &Vec<'b>, m: u64)
   ensures [(cap₀ ≥ m, backing = 'b ∧ 'b@[0,len₀) Owned),
            (cap₀ < m, Ended('b) ∧ ∃'b2. backing = 'b2 ∧ 'b2@[0,len₀) Owned)]
   ends   { 'b when cap₀ < m }
   writes ('v.desc), ('b @ [0,len₀))

fn pick<'x, 'y>(c: bool, x: ptr('x,·), y: ptr('y,·)) -> ∃'r. ptr('r,·)
   ensures ('r ≍ 'x) ∨ ('r ≍ 'y)        // a finite origin set, from the signature
   reads {} ; writes {} ; ends {}       // returns a pointer, takes no permission

// caller, judging from the signatures alone:
drain(&t); read(t)
  // reject [R1(i)]: `ensures` left 'x ↦ Hole.  fact: the interface, not the body
reserve(v, 100); read(pe)               // pe : ptr('b, {j})
  // reject unless RF ⊨ cap₀ ≥ 100.  diagnostic names `reserve` as the killer
let r = pick(c, px, py)
write(r, 1)
  // accept; and the write kills facts of 'x and 'y and of nothing else,
  //   because the stated origin set is exactly {'x,'y} (R6 precision by the
  //   written interface; C8: effect roots are identities)
```

**Verdict: accepted as required.** Each effect is visible in the interface; the
caller's verdict is a function of the call site plus the interface; the body is
checked once against it.

### P11 Write-once-then-frozen cache

```text
cache : array<Slot<T>> as 'k, extent [0,K)

// Form A — Σ state as the occupancy (the pure store-index form):
//   Σ: 'k@[0,K) ↦ Hole(T)
get(key):
  if is_init(cache,key) { read(&cache[key]) }
  // reject: `is_init` would have to read Σ's cell class, which is erased.
  //   There is no runtime representation of Hole vs Owned to test.  A checker
  //   that admitted this would need a runtime occupancy word — refused by M2(ii).

// Form B — occupancy as ordinary data the source writes (the accepted form):
cache : array<Option<T>> as 'k ; Σ: 'k@[0,K) ↦ Owned(Option<T>)
get(key):
  match read(&cache[key]) {
    Some(v) => v                     // accept: the slot storage is always Owned
    None    => { set cache[key] = Some(compute(key))
                 // accept: W = {'k@{key}}
                 read_some(&cache[key]) }   // accept: refinement from the write
  }
// a reader holding pr : ptr('k, {key}) across a fill of slot key':
read(pr)
  // accept unconditionally [R1]: the extent is Owned either way — the pointer's
  //   validity never depended on occupancy
// but the *contents fact* about slot key:
//   killed by the fill unless RF ⊨ {key} ∩ {key'} = ∅, i.e. key ≠ key'
//   (R6: kills by the written footprint's extent, not by the whole array)
// what is NOT available: after the one-time fill, no fact says the slot will
//   never change again, so no `!invariant.load` reaches the backend.
```

**Verdict: accepted with a stated cost.** Under R1 alone the write-once cache
**passes**, and a reader may hold a pointer to a slot across another slot's fill
unconditionally (contents facts survive only with `key ≠ key'`). The cost is
that "frozen after first write" is not statable: the store index has no
access-mode state and RF is quantifier-free arithmetic over the present state,
not a temporal claim. **Needs a mechanism from D3** — the *Access-mode states on
the identity* family (SYS-D3-09 `Frozen`, AI-D3-03) — if the freeze fact is
wanted for the backend. why-whitefoot §5's stance is recorded: this is a
performance argument, so admitting `Frozen` is a capability question, not a
safety one.

### P13 Relocation by a compacting third party

```text
h : handle('pool, idx)                // (atom, refined index); Copy; no address
p = pointer_of(h)                     // p : ptr('pool, slot(idx) @ occ o)
  // accept: forming an interior pointer is free; it names the extent that
  //   exists now

pool.compact()
  // sig: ends { 'pool }                                  // R8a event, contract-visible
  //      ensures ∃'pool2. ∀ h. live(h) ⇒ h ↦ 'pool2      // handles transported
  //      writes ('pool), ('pool.meta)
read(p)
  // reject [R1(ii) / R8a]: p's extent of 'pool is Ended.  The candidate
  //   supplies no fixup form, so an interior pointer and third-party
  //   relocation are mutually exclusive, exactly as R8a demands.
  // diagnostic: `compact` ends 'pool at line …; a handle survives, a pointer
  //   does not; repair = re-form the pointer from h
read(pool[h])
  // accept: the handle's contract transported idx into 'pool2; the read names
  //   'pool2@{idx}, which is Owned
p2 = pointer_of(h); read(p2)          // accept: re-formed after the event
```

**Verdict: accepted as required** (the requirement is a refusal, and the
refusal falls out of the `ends` clause). A *fixup* form — rewriting live
pointers — is **not** supplied and **needs a mechanism from D8**: the
*Relocation with a fixup channel* family (SYS-D8-06, SYS-D8-12, RAD-D8-11),
which under M2(ii) would have to be a written operation, not a runtime sweep.

### P16 Abstraction over identities

```text
// (a) P3 generic over the node type
fn map_nodes<T, 'p>(g: &Pool<'p, Node<T>>, f: fn(&T) -> T)
   requires 'p @ live ↦ Owned(Node<T>)
   reads ('p @ live) ; writes ('p @ live)
   // accept: one identity parameter.  Node<T>'s own bunch is declared on the
   //   type: struct Node<T> { data ∗ next ∗ prev }, so T's storage separates
   //   from the links without a second parameter (R15 metric: parameters are a
   //   function of the *bunched shape*, not of the storages touched)

// (b) P5 over the column type
fn kernel<E>(c: &Cols<E>, n: u64) writes (∗ c .a), (∗ c .b) …
   // accept: `groups (∗ c)` is one bunched binder; eight facts, one parameter

// (c) P6's helper as a closure
let h = |s: slice<'o,u8>| helper(s, input)
   // closure type: ∀'o. fn(slice<'o,u8>) -> ()  writes ('o @ extent)
   //   captures: input, with a capture row `reads ('in @ [0,m))`
   // accept: 'o is universally quantified at the closure type, so P6's
   //   derivation is unchanged; the capture row is part of the closure's type
for w in 0..k { h(slice_of(out, w*s, w*s+s)) }    // accept, as P6

// (d) P9 `pick` through a nominal
fn pick<N: Nominal>(c: bool, x: N, y: N) -> N
   ensures identities(result) ⊆ identities(x) ∪ identities(y)
   // accept: N carries its own identity row; the result's origin set is
   //   computed from the signature alone (HIS-D1-14's finite static origin set)
// instantiation: decidable by the fixed cycle check (HIS-REQ-07); the bunch of
//   the instantiated type must refine the bunch of the bound — syntax-directed
```

**Verdict: accepted with a stated cost.** Identity, state and effect facts
cross every boundary, and R15's metric is met (parameters bounded by the
argument types' bunched shape, not linear in storages). The cost is a new
declaration-site obligation: **every record type declares `∗` or `;` per field
group**. The default is `∗` and the common case writes nothing, but the
obligation exists on every type declaration in the language.

### P17 Partial operations

```text
q = a / d
  // domain: d ≠ 0.  RF goal `d ≠ 0`.
  //   d : u64 where d ≥ 1        ⇒ accept by subsumption (refined type)
  //   inside `if d != 0 { … }`   ⇒ accept from the path atom
  //   otherwise                   ⇒ reject.  diagnostic: missing fact `d ≠ 0`
q = a /? d -> { Ok(q) | DivByZero }
  // accept: a written outcome arm (R12); each arm has its own Σ_out and
  //   discharges every obligation

b : u8 = narrow(x)
  // domain: x ≤ 255.  x : u64 where x < 256 ⇒ accept by subsumption
  //   else reject naming `x ≤ 255`, or write narrow? with an outcome arm

y = v[i]
  // domain: i < len(v).  The descriptor's cell carries `len` as a refinement,
  //   so RF ⊨ i < len(v) from the loop domain or a `requires`.
  //   else reject naming `i < len(v)`

s = x +wrap y            // accept: wrapping selected at this site
t = x +checked y -> {Ok|Overflow}   // accept: outcome arm
u = x + y                // reject unless RF ⊨ x + y ≤ MAX at this site;
                         //   `+` with no selection and no proof is rejected at
                         //   the operator, naming the three spellings (M7)
```

**Verdict: accepted as required.** Every domain is a goal in the *same*
fragment that carries extents, so R11 adds no vocabulary — the tuple's largest
M8 saving.

| P11 | accepted with a stated cost; the freeze fact needs D3 *Access-mode states* |
| P13 | accepted as required (as a refusal); a fixup form needs D8 *Relocation with a fixup channel* |
| P16 | accepted with a stated cost (a bunch mark per record declaration) |
| P17 | accepted as required |

---

## 4. Requirements table

### 4.1 Hazard and duty rows

| Row | Verdict | Reason (one sentence) |
|---|---|---|
| R1 Sequential memory safety | **met** | Σ's four cell classes answer (i) hole reads, (ii) ended access with permanent tombstones that address reuse cannot revive, and (iii) stale layout via the occupant/layout index, each checked per access against the key the access names. |
| R2 Resource lifecycle accounting | **met** | An obligation is a Σ entry, guarded cells give per-path definiteness at joins and at every outcome arm's exit, and the exit rule (every minted key `Ended` or transferred under each guard) is static with no bookkeeping the source did not bind. |
| R3 Value classes and transfer | **met** | Copy/affine/linear is a property of the value's type; `take`/`put`/`replace`/`move` are the four Σ rewrites of §2.4, and the "used twice" diagnostic (multiplicity) is a distinct rule from "never released" (the exit rule). |
| R4 Licensed facts for the backend | **met** | The distinctness relation is RF extent-disjointness over the `⊑` containment structure, never inequality of atom names, so P2's (`'S`,`'b1`) pair yields nothing while P5's eight columns yield eight per-load scopes; a missing entailment costs speed only. |
| R5 Data-race freedom and permitted overlap | **met** | Ground (i) is RF disjointness of write footprints (P1, P3, P5, P6); ground (ii) reuses the existing closed operator table with the law discharged in RF; ground (iii)'s level set is R14's to state and this tuple neither supplies nor obstructs it. |
| R6 Frame: proof-fact retention | **met** | A write kills exactly the facts whose support RF-overlaps the written extent and a call kills exactly those overlapping its declared `writes` extents, so the measured 34/41 `len()` rebinds vanish: an element-extent write does not overlap the descriptor's `len` key. |
| R7 Compositional call judgement | **met** | The `requires`/`ensures`/`reads`/`writes`/`ends`/`outcomes`/`groups` block states every item R7(a) lists, the declaration-side checks reject an unsatisfiable `requires` and an unnameable result origin, and the caller's verdict is a function of the call site plus that block. |
| R8a Storage-ending and relocation events | **met** | The ending set is exactly the operations with a non-empty `ends` clause, completeness is enforced at the declaration (a body that ends storage not in `ends` is rejected), and P13 shows an interior pointer refused across third-party relocation with no fixup form. |
| R8b Placement and physical demands | **partial** | Alignment and stride demands are RF congruence atoms (`base ≡ 0 mod 64`) that reach lowering, but the foreign-boundary representation, address spaces and the erasing-store demand are not carried by this tuple and would need their own vocabulary. |
| R9 Shared mutation among several holders | **met** | Coincidence is declared, not forbidden: several writable pointers to one atom are ordinary (P7), P3's four link writes through several paths are accepted sequentially, and the price is exactly R9(d)'s — no R4 fact is emitted for a `;` group and kills widen there. |
| R10 External resources as ordinary objects | **met** | A descriptor is three atoms (wrapper, description, contents) with ordinary Σ cells, the contents cell is `Foreign(class)`, and no rule of acceptance mentions a host crossing — the same `requires`/`ensures`/`ends` block serves files and memory. |
| R11 Partial operations and overflow | **met** | Every domain is an RF goal in the same fragment as extents; the overflow behavior is chosen by the operator spelling per site; failure is a rejection naming the missing fact or a written outcome arm, never a repair. |
| R12 Failure paths and typed outcomes | **met** | Each outcome arm carries its own `Σ_out` and `ends`, so R2's exit rule is discharged per arm, and a context can forbid an arm by a `requires` that makes it unreachable. |
| R13 Resource bounds where demanded | **met** | A declared byte budget is a refinement on the arena's bump (`bump ≤ B`), a declared depth is a refined counter parameter, and a termination measure is a written well-founded integer term — all three in RF, so opt-in bounds cost no new vocabulary. |
| R14 Stated execution model and external conditions | **partial** | The tuple supplies (iii) (non-program actors as `ends` and `Foreign` clauses) and (iv) (the `Foreign(class)` cell retaining no contents fact), but (i) the memory model, (ii) the level set, (v) the exclusion set and (vi) the observation model are outside D1–D4 and remain unstated. |
| R15 Abstraction | **partial** | Identity, state and effect facts cross generics, closures and nominals (P16), and the parameter metric is met via bunched types, but the row is provisional and the closure-capture row and the bunch-refinement check at instantiation are new obligations the corpus has not exercised. |

### 4.2 Meta rows

| Row | Verdict | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| M1 Specified deterministic acceptance | **met** | RF is a fixed normal form plus a fixed five-rule closure over a non-growing monomial set, joins are a canonicalization with a structural (not capped) guard bound, and loop heads are written rather than iterated — no order, budget, solver state or machine speed can select a verdict. |
| M2 No unstated failure edge, no unchosen cost | **met** | Every cell class, guard, refinement and occupant index is erased; no runtime word, tag, flag, counter or compare exists; the only branches are the writer's own (`if k != i && k != j`, `if len < cap`, the `match` in P11 Form B). |
| M3 Enumerated, writer-closed trusted base | **met** | RF's decision procedure and the `use`-lemma catalog are compiler code and specification text, not axioms; no writer-reachable assume exists; a `use` step is a verified instantiation, never a discharge by assertion. |
| M4 Writer regularity | **partial** | One production per construct holds in the grammar, but one fact can be stated as a refined type, a `requires` clause or a path condition — the semantic-duplicate case M4 itself names as beyond its lint, and this tuple creates three instances of it. |
| M5 Acceptance independent of permission | **met** | Acceptance reads Σ and RF; the permission judgment reads them too but nothing reads the permission judgment, so disabling PAR leaves every program accepted. |
| M6 Soundness evidence | **met** | Σ over bounded extents with RF over bounded monomials is finitely enumerable, so M6(i)'s bounded small-model check per program is runnable now; the standing obligation is frame soundness (ii), which rests on `writes` being a genuine may-write over-approximation — checked at the declaration. |
| M7 Repairable rejection | **met** | Every rejection is a *named failed RF goal at a named tree location* (`k ≠ i ∧ k ≠ j`, `len₀ < cap₀`, `d ≠ 0`, `'a is Owned only under ¬c`) plus the killing operation where R6 applies; the repair is to supply that fact, and supplying it cannot reproduce the same rejection at the same location. |
| M8 Teaching and retrieval budget | **violated** | RF's atom forms and five closure rules, Σ's four cell classes with guarded cells and the join rule, extent split/merge, minting and occupant rules, the bunched `∗`/`;` declaration, the seven-clause signature block and the `use`-lemma catalog plausibly consume 12–16k tokens against an ~18.5k subsystem share of a provisional K = 48k — even after R11 and R13 come free. |
| M9 Measured performance floor | **partial** | The candidate is the one that makes P5's per-load fact channel *expressible* (eight scopes from the record's default `∗`), but the row is unmeasurable on the current compiler because no alias channel exists, so the floor is argued, not measured. |
| M10 Checking cost, scaling and edit stability | **violated** | RF closure is cubic in monomials — within the per-family ceiling — but the per-declaration total is monomials-cubed times writes-squared, which exceeds "at most quadratic in written proof steps" because guard atoms and extent goals grow with branches and accesses, not with written steps; M10's own amendment route must be taken and the exponent measured on the `growing` bundle. |
| M11 Evolution with stated loss | **met** | The fragment, the closure rule set and the lemma catalog are spec tables, so a revision states its verdict diff over the retained corpus; written `use` steps survive a revision that does not change their lemma. |

**Counts: 20 met, 5 partial (R8b, R14, R15, M4, M9), 2 violated (M8, M10).**

### 4.3 The price this candidate charges the compiler

| # | Price |
|---|---|
| 1 | RF must be implemented as a specified normal form plus the five closure rules, byte-deterministic across machines, with **no** solver, widening, iteration cap or work budget, and **no** second family retried when the first fails. |
| 2 | Σ must be a keyed map over RF-described extents with split, merge, guarded cells and a canonical guard normal form (sorted conjunction sets with subsumption removal); the normalizer must be total, or precision becomes order-dependent and M1 fails. |
| 3 | No runtime check, trap, tag, flag, counter or word may be inserted: occupant indices, guards, cells and refinements are erased entirely. |
| 4 | The compiler may **not** re-derive a refinement whose check failed; a missing fact is a rejection, never a fallback analysis that selects acceptance. |
| 5 | R4 facts must be exported keyed by `(atom, extent)` — per-load `!alias.scope`, `initializes(lo,hi)`, parameter `noalias`/`readonly` from `,` groups — and must **not** be emitted for a `;`-group pair or an `⊑` pair. |
| 6 | Every declaration's `ends` clause must be checked complete against its body, and a declaration with an RF-unsatisfiable `requires` or an unnameable result origin must be rejected at the declaration. |
| 7 | No fixpoint at loop heads: the invariant is written, so the compiler may not iterate to one — a deliberate removal of implementation freedom in exchange for M1 and M10. |
| 8 | Storage reuse the program cannot reach (stack coloring, spill reuse) stays free; relocation of storage an interior pointer names is forbidden with no fixup form. |

### 4.4 Writer cost

| Site | What must be written | P1–P9 estimate |
|---|---|---|
| **per record declaration** | `∗` (default, nothing written) or `;` for a field group that may coincide | 0 for `Cols`, `Node`, `Vec`; 1 mark for a record with two names for one storage |
| **per signature** | `requires`/`ensures` Σ clauses for each state-changing effect; `reads`/`writes` refined extents; `ends`; one `Σ_out` per outcome arm; a `groups` line only when two parameters may coincide; identity binders only where the argument type does not supply them | P6 `helper`: 2 lines; P9 `reserve`: 4 lines; P9 `drain`: 2 lines; P5 `kernel`: 3 lines |
| **per loop** | one `invariant` Σ clause naming every key the body changes, plus any RF fact the body needs | P5: 1 line; P6: 1 line; P8: 1 line |
| **per join** | nothing — guards are captured automatically — unless the branch condition is not RF-expressible (a call result, a float comparison), then one written Σ clause | 0 across P1–P9 |
| **per statement** | nothing, except a `use` step where RF's closure does not reach the goal | P3: 1 per structural update; P1: 0; P6: 0 given rule (d) |

The AI-writer shape of this cost is deliberate: a `use` step is a *copy* of a
named lemma from a closed catalog with its arguments instantiated, and an
identity binder is *transcribed* from a printed minting site — the two
operations the premises table records models as good at — while nothing in the
list requires inventing a name or restructuring around a non-local rejection.
