ground rules.

---

## 1. The tuple

| Point | Family (OPTIONS.md name, verbatim) | Members drawn on | Members explicitly refused inside the family |
|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | **No storage identity (values only)** — primary | AI-D1-10 (values only, projections not pointers), THE-D1-21 (no pointer type at all) | RAD-D1-14 (immutable values only): in-place mutation is kept |
| D1 | **Index into a named pool / row key** — for shared and cyclic structure | SYS-D1-04 (index only, append-only pool), SYS-D1-02 ((cache, slot) in a type-stable pool), RAD-D1-04 (table row key, no pointers) | HIS-D1-25 REFUSED (bare `u64` index): the handle is a nominal `Handle<T>`, never an integer |
| D2 | **Access path or parameter convention per call** | AI-D2-05 (permission in the access path per call), THE-D2-04 (access convention per call), SYS-D2-09 (parameter calling convention), HIS-D2-10 FLOATED (mutable value semantics per access path) | the Swift half of HIS-D2-10 ("falls back to dynamic checks for class storage"): no dynamic exclusivity anywhere (M2) |
| D3 | **No states: validity by construction** — primary | AI-D3-09 (no holes, no partial init), THE-D3-21 (every constructor valid), HIS-D3-01 ADOPTED (init keyed to binding liveness), SYS-D3-16 (arrays defined by a map) | RAD-D3-01 (nothing ever ends): affine consumption still ends storage |
| D3 | **State as ordinary data or typed outcome** — for holes and vacancy | HIS-D3-04 ADOPTED (vacancy as an `Option`-shaped value), AI-D3-11 (three states, rest typed outcomes) — taken as *zero* states, all typed outcomes | HIS-D3-12 / SYS-D3-18 (per-slot tag or parallel validity bitmap as *language* state): vacancy is the writer's own field, never checker-known occupancy |
| D4 | **Scoped projections and non-escaping references** — primary | THE-D4-17 (projections with lexical spans), THE-D4-18 (second-class references) | THE-D4-19 (capture-checked first-class references): capture polymorphism is not paid for |
| D4 | **Overlap judged by resolved paths and proved extents** — the decision procedure inside the primary family | HIS-D4-12 ADOPTED (overlap by complete resolved paths), HIS-D4-13 ADOPTED (proved half-open view extents), SYS-D4-10 (proved-disjoint byte ranges) | HIS-D4-14 REFUSED (literal-only or equal-size ranges) |

### Why the four cohere

They are one idea applied four times: **the program's storage is a tree of
values rooted at bindings, and the only names are access paths into that
tree.** Each point is the others' consequence, not an independent choice.

| Implication | Why |
|---|---|
| D4 ⇒ D1 | If no reference can be stored or returned, no name outlives the binding it was projected from. A type-level storage identity exists to let a name survive its syntactic scope; nothing here needs to survive, so nothing needs a name. C1 (identity granularity) and C3 (distinct-by-default identity parameters with call-site discharge) are not *answered* — they are dissolved. |
| D1 ⇒ D2 | With no identity in any type, the only place a permission can attach is the syntactic access at a call. The parameter convention *is* the footprint, so R5(b)'s "read and write footprints per statement over storages" and R7(b)'s "footprints per identity" are the same three keywords. |
| D2 ⇒ D3 | Exclusive access is granted for a call or a block, and a binding is initialized where it is bound and ends where it is unbound. No program point observes a vacant place, so `Init`/`Uninit`/`Gone` has no instance to distinguish. What remains — a slot the writer *wants* to be empty — is the writer's own sum type. C6 (storage state as a term over captured conditions) is not needed and is not paid for. |
| D3 ⇒ D4 | Conversely, holes are the reason a reference must carry state. With vacancy as data, a projection carries nothing but a path, so a projection can be purely lexical and second-class. |
| D1-pool ⇒ the rest | The tree cannot express graphs, back edges, or a structure shared by several long-lived holders. Those move wholesale into a pool: one value, elements addressed by ordinary copyable data. The graph's aliasing becomes index arithmetic *inside one storage*, which the same path-and-extent algebra already decides. This is `why-whitefoot.md` §10's doctrine taken as the language rule rather than as a pattern. |

The tuple's single sentence: **there are no pointers, so there is nothing to
name, nothing to track and nothing to invalidate; permission is where the
access is written, and everything a tree cannot hold lives in a pool.**

---

## 2. The model

### 2.1 What a "pointer's" type says

There is no pointer type. Three forms replace it.

| Form | Spelling | What it says | Lifetime |
|---|---|---|---|
| Value binding | `let x: T`, `var x: T` | `x` denotes storage of type `T`; the storage exists exactly while the name is bound | lexical |
| Projection (second-class) | `f(inout c.a[i])`, `with inout v[lo..hi] as s { … }` | access to the subtree at a **resolved path**, for the lexical span of the call or block; may be passed *down*, never up, never stored, never returned | the call or block |
| Handle | `h: Handle<Node>` | ordinary copyable data: a row key. It denotes **nothing** on its own; every use is `pool[h]`, which needs the pool value in scope | none — it is data |

`Handle<Node>` is nominal (not `u64`, not `Handle<Edge>`), so HIS-D1-25's
`index`/`len`/foreign-handle confusion is a type error. It is *not* an
identity: two pools of `Node` share the handle type. §6 W1 prices that.

### 2.2 What the checker holds

No per-storage state. Five facts, and nothing else:

| Fact | Form | Decided by |
|---|---|---|
| `BIND(n)` | per name, a boolean: still bound | a two-point lattice, joined by conjunction |
| `PATH(p, q)` | two resolved paths overlap iff one is a prefix of the other after refinement | syntactic prefix comparison over root + ordered steps (HIS-D4-12) |
| `EXT(p, q)` | element/range steps refine `PATH` by half-open extents | a fixed linear-arithmetic fragment over loop indices and `requires` terms (HIS-D4-13) |
| `AFF(x, y)` | two **distinct live non-copy values** occupy disjoint storage | R3's multiplicity discipline; a fixed-table fact, no proof, no annotation |
| `REF(e)` | ordinary value refinements (`i < len(v)`, `d != 0`) | R11's existing discharge; not a storage fact |

`AFF` is the fact the retired `scoped-alias-channel` prototype already used
(*"`buffer<T>` is affine single-owner: two distinct live buffer values never
overlap"*, EVIDENCE §B.2). Here it is a consequence of the type discipline
rather than a backend re-derivation from resolved places.

### 2.3 Take / put / replace / free / move / realloc

| Operation | Spelling | What the checker does | What changes |
|---|---|---|---|
| take | `let v = replace(inout s, None)` | nothing: `replace` is a total function on `Option<T>` | a value moves out; `s` still holds a valid `Option<T>` |
| put | `s = Some(sink v)` | `BIND(v) := false` | ordinary assignment |
| replace | `let old = replace(inout s, sink new)` | `BIND(new) := false` | one exclusive access to path `s` |
| free / end | `sink x`, or `x` leaves scope | `BIND(x) := false`; the affine release runs here | the storage ends; **no name can refer to it**, because no name reaches into it |
| move | `f(sink x)`, `return x` | `BIND(x) := false` | bytes may or may not move; unobservable, because no projection outlives the statement |
| realloc | `push(inout v, e)` | one exclusive access to path `v`; exit clause `len(v) = old(len(v)) + 1` | the backing is anonymous, so **there is no fact to invalidate** |

A commitment the model makes and Swift does not: **no implicit deep copy, no
implicit retain/release, no implicit copy-on-write.** A non-`Copy` value is
moved (`sink`) or explicitly cloned. Otherwise a copy the source did not write
is an allocation the source did not write — M2(ii) and R13's price.

### 2.4 Join and loop head

```text
if c { sink a; b } else { sink b; a }      // each arm unbinds one name
// join: BIND(a) = false, BIND(b) = false, and the if-expression yields one value
```

- **Join rule.** `BIND` joins by conjunction. A name bound on one arm and not
  the other is unbound after the join, and the diagnostic names the arm that
  unbound it (M7). There is no drop flag, and none is representable: the merge
  of two owned values is a value merge, not a state merge.
- **Loop head.** The `BIND` fixpoint has height 2 and is reached in one pass:
  a name consumed in the body is unbound at the back edge, rejected as
  "consumed in a loop" naming the consuming statement. **Nothing is written at
  a loop head for memory safety.** Written `invariant` clauses appear only for
  R11 index refinements, which every candidate pays.

### 2.5 What a signature states

```text
fn helper(inout out: Buf<u8>, let input: Buf<u8>)
fn reserve(inout v: Vec<T>, m: u64)                ensures cap(v) >= m
fn drain (inout v: Vec<T>) -> Vec<T>               ensures len(v) == 0
fn close (sink fd: File) -> Result<(), Errno>
subscript pick(let c: Bool, inout s: S) -> inout T  origin { s.x, s.y }
```

The interface vocabulary is: **three conventions** (`let`, `inout`, `sink`),
types, value refinements, outcome types, and one addition — an `origin` set on
a yielded projection (HIS-D1-14's finite static origin set). Absent: identity
parameters, region parameters, lifetime parameters, entry/exit storage states,
loan clauses, effect rows for memory.

### 2.6 What the writer writes, and where

| Site | What is written | Count |
|---|---|---|
| signature | one convention keyword per parameter; `origin` only on a yielded projection | = number of parameters; 0 extra |
| loop head | nothing for memory safety | 0 |
| join | nothing | 0 |
| statement | `sink` at a consuming transfer; `with … as x` only when one projection spans several statements | 0 in the common case |
| per storage | nothing | 0 |

R11 proofs (`i < len`, `d != 0`) and R12 arms are charged to their own rows.

### 2.7 What is erased

Everything except what the writer wrote as data. Conventions lower to
`byval`/`sret`/`noalias`/`readonly`/`initializes`; projections lower to
`getelementptr`; `PATH`/`EXT`/`AFF` lower to `!alias.scope` per resolved path
root on loaded pointers (R4's channel). Retained at run time: `Option`
discriminants, pool free-list heads, handle integers — each of which is a field
the source declared.

---

## 3. Derivations

Notation as §2. Facts cited by name: `BIND`, `PATH`, `EXT`, `AFF`, `REF`.

### P1 Container split with a runtime index

```text
fn split_write(inout v: Vec<u64>, i: u64, j: u64, k: u64)
  requires i < len(v) && j < len(v) && k < len(v) && i != j
{
  with inout v[i] as pi, inout v[j] as pj {      // accept: PATH(v[i], v[j]) refined by EXT; i != j from requires
    pi = 1                                        // accept: exclusive on path v[i]
    pj = 2                                        // accept: exclusive on path v[j]; PAR-1 overlap permitted, footprints {v[i]} vs {v[j]} disjoint (R5(i))
    let x = v[k]                                  // reject: PATH(v[k], v[i]) unresolved. missing: k != i /\ k != j
  }                                               // both projections end at the block; no "put back" is written
  push(inout v, 7)                                // accept: BIND(v) exclusive again; the projections are gone
}
```

Repaired form the writer branches, exactly as the program demands:

```text
    if k != i && k != j { let x = v[k] }          // accept: EXT discharges both inequalities from the branch
```

The two writes carry no runtime comparison: `i != j` is a precondition, not a
check (M2(i)). The `v[k]` diagnostic names `k != i /\ k != j` at the tree
location of the read (M7).

**Verdict: accepted as required.**

### P2 Arena with independently released blocks

The arena cannot hand out a pointer into `S`; it hands out **the bytes**. `A`
is a pool of slabs; `alloc` moves one out as an affine value.

```text
var A: Arena                                      // { slabs: Pool<Buf<u8>>, free: FreeList }
let b1 = alloc(inout A, 64)?                      // accept: A exclusive for this call only; b1 : Buf<u8>, affine
let b2 = alloc(inout A, 64)?                      // accept: same
let b3 = alloc(inout A, 64)?                      // accept: same
par { fill(inout b1); fill(inout b2); fill(inout b3) }
                                                  // accept: AFF — three distinct live affine values are disjoint.
                                                  //         no index proof, no annotation, and A is not held here (R2 (e))
free(inout A, sink b2)                            // accept: BIND(b2) := false. metadata written only here and at alloc
let b4 = alloc(inout A, 32)?                      // accept: may reuse b2's storage
fill(inout b2)                                    // reject: BIND(b2) = false. "b2 was consumed at line 8"
read(let b1); free(inout A, sink b1); free(inout A, sink b3); free(inout A, sink b4)
                                                  // accept: each name bound exactly once here; double free is BIND-rejected
```

Every required property except one is delivered with no state vocabulary:
blocks exclusively owned (affinity), metadata touched only at `alloc`/`free`,
`A` unheld between operations, and *"every old pointer into `b2` refused
afterwards"* delivered in the strongest form — **no old handle can exist**,
because `Buf` is affine and was consumed.

The cost is the arena's shape. Variable-size carving from one contiguous `S`
needs `split(sink b, at) -> (Buf, Buf)` and a rejoin whose precondition is
"these two were split from one buffer" — a provenance fact, i.e. an identity in
disguise. HIS-D9-12 (split/join protocol) is REFUSED; split-without-coalesce
and size-class slabs are what remain.

**Verdict: accepted with a stated cost** — size-class slab pool or a
non-coalescing bump arena. The general coalescing arena **needs a mechanism
from D9** (split-and-join range tokens, AI-D9-08 / THE-D9-05), which
reintroduces per-formation provenance.

### P3 Graph with back edges in a pool

```text
var g: Pool<Node>                                  // Node { next: Handle<Node>, prev: Handle<Node>, data: u64 }

// insert n between a and b — four link writes through several paths to one node
g[a].next = n                                      // accept: one statement, one path g[a].next. sequential aliased
g[n].prev = a                                      // accept: writes need no judgment (ladder Step 0)
g[n].next = b                                      // accept: no proof that a != n, n != b is required
g[b].prev = n                                      // accept
// the invariant "next/prev point to live nodes" is one written clause on Pool<Node>, stated once (R6 (e))

// traversal
var h = start
loop {
  match g[h] {                                     // accept: total; vacancy is data, not state
    None    => break                               // the writer's arm: this is where removal is observed
    Some(nd)=> { use(nd.data); h = nd.next }       // accept: REF discharges h in bounds from Pool's own invariant
  }
}

// parallel map over all nodes
par for h in g.keys() { g[h].data = f(g[h].data) } // accept: footprints {g[h]} for pairwise distinct h; EXT over the
                                                   //         key iteration (the same fact as P5's i != i')

// removal
remove(inout g, m)                                 // accept: slot m := None
```

Then the divergence:

```text
let m2 = insert(inout g, node)                     // reusing pool: may return the same key as m
let stale = old_handle_to_m
match g[stale] { Some(nd) => use(nd.data) }        // ACCEPTED, and WRONG: reads m2's data.
                                                   //   not an R1 violation (no storage ended, nothing uninitialized)
                                                   //   but P3's "removal invalidates every path to m" is not delivered
```

Under the **append-only** discipline (`why-whitefoot` §10's current doctrine,
SYS-D8-07) the slot is never reused, `g[stale]` is `None` forever, and the
required property holds — at the cost that P3's own line *"the storage of `m`
is reused for a later insert"* cannot be run.

| Configuration | removal invalidates every path | storage reused | price |
|---|---|---|---|
| append-only pool | yes, by the written `None` arm | no | memory grows with total insertions |
| reusing pool | **no** — type-correct wrong occupant | yes | silent logic error |

**Verdict: partial — the candidate is at fault.** Sequential link writes and
the parallel map are accepted as required and with zero annotation; the
removal-invalidation clause holds only in the append-only configuration, which
cannot execute the program's reuse line. The repair is a per-slot generation —
either a runtime compare (M2(ii): refused) or a generation as a proof term
(AI-D1-12), which reopens D1.

### P4 Cursor over a growing vector

```text
struct Cursor { i: u64 }                           // no pointer field: there is no pointer type
fn read_at(let v: Vec<u64>, let c: Cursor) -> u64
  requires c.i < len(v) { v[c.i] }                 // accept: REF

var v = …; let c = Cursor { i: 0 }
let a = read_at(let v, let c)                      // accept: REF from the caller's own i < len fact
push(inout v, 5)                                   // accept: exclusive on path v. ensures len(v) == old(len(v)) + 1
                                                   //         the backing is anonymous — nothing to invalidate (R8a)
let b = read_at(let v, let c)                      // accept: REF survives — c.i < old(len) <= len.
                                                   //         R6: push's footprint is the path v; it transforms len(v),
                                                   //         it does not kill it
sink v; let d = read_at(let v, let c)              // reject: BIND(v) = false — and in fact unwritable: there is no v
```

The required property *"validity decided by state and proof, not by a borrow
that blocks push"* holds with **state** replaced by an ordinary value
refinement. The required property *"a stored pointer or handle to a container
in a struct"* does not: a cursor stores an index, and the container is
re-supplied at every use. A cursor is therefore unusable where the container is
not in scope (a stored iterator, a callback holding a cursor).

**Verdict: accepted with a stated cost** — the cursor stores the index only;
`free(v); c.read()` is refused *by unwritability*, so R1's diagnostic for that
line has no instance (an M7 subtlety, not a gap).

### P5 Struct-of-arrays kernel

```text
struct Cols { a,b,c,d,e,f,g,h: Buf<u64> }

fn kernel(inout k: Cols, n: u64) {
  for i in 0..n {
    k.a[i] = f(k.a[i], k.c[i], k.d[i])             // accept: PATH — k.a, k.c, k.d are distinct field steps of one root.
                                                   //         fixed-table, no proof, no annotation
    k.b[i] = g(k.b[i], k.e[i], k.f[i], k.g[i], k.h[i])
                                                   // accept: same; AFF additionally gives element-memory disjointness
                                                   //         for the eight live Buf values
  }                                                // PAR-2: iteration footprints {k.a[i], k.b[i]} disjoint by EXT (i != i')
}
```

Per-load alias facts: the identity licensed to lowering is the resolved path
(`k.a`, `k.b`, …), one `!alias.scope` per column on the *loaded* data pointer
— the half parameter `noalias` cannot reach (EVIDENCE §B.2). The obvious shape
*is* the source: one `inout` parameter, an ordinary indexed loop, no hints, no
guards, no versioning.

**Verdict: accepted as required.** This is the candidate's strongest program.

### P6 Range partition helper

```text
fn helper(inout out: Buf<u8>, let input: Buf<u8>)  // the convention IS the footprint: writes exactly `out`, reads `input`

for w in 0..k {
  helper(inout out[w*s .. (w+1)*s], let input)     // accept: EXT — [w*s,(w+1)*s) pairwise disjoint over distinct w,
                                                   //         by the fixed linear-arithmetic fragment.
                                                   //         PAR-2 overlap permitted from the arithmetic alone
}
                                                   // the caller learns what helper writes from `inout out` and nothing else (R7 (e))
```

No worker count beyond `k`; no schedule in the source; the extents are the only
proof and the writer wrote them as the argument.

**Verdict: accepted as required.**

### P7 Take, put, replace through aliases

The program's premise — two names for one slot — is **unwritable**: two
`inout` projections of one path in one scope are a `PATH` overlap error, and a
projection cannot be stored to become a second long-lived name. The program
re-expresses as one owner:

```text
var s: Option<T> = Some(t)

let v = replace(inout s, None)                     // accept: total; s now holds None
let r = read(let s)                                // ACCEPTED, returns None.  P7 requires "refused: hole" — NOT REPRODUCED.
                                                   //   the vacancy is the writer's own discriminant (HIS-D3-04), and the
                                                   //   read is safe in both arms, so no check is "required to reach safety"
s = Some(sink v)                                   // accept: BIND(v) := false
let r2 = read(let s)                               // accept: Some
let old = replace(inout s, sink new)               // accept: returns old; the next read sees new
sink s                                             // accept: the storage ends here
let r3 = read(let s)                               // reject: BIND(s) = false. "s was consumed at line 8" — free is permanent
```

Of the three required properties: *"state is a property of the storage, not of
the pointer"* holds vacuously (there are no pointers, and the `Option` is the
storage's contents); *"free is permanent"* holds through `BIND`; *"take leaves
a hole another alias may fill"* has no instance, since there is no second
alias.

**Verdict: partial — the candidate is at fault on line 2.** The hole read is
total rather than refused, at a price of one discriminant word per
vacancy-capable slot and one written arm per read of one.

### P8 Conditional release and loop exits

```text
// B10-B13: conditional release, then use the survivor
let s = if c { sink a; b } else { sink b; a }      // accept: each arm unbinds one name and yields the other as a value.
                                                   //         the join is a VALUE merge, so no drop flag is representable
use(inout s)                                       // accept: BIND(s)
sink s                                             // accept: exactly one release on every path (R2)

// the shape the program writes literally:
if c { sink a } else { sink b }                    // accept per arm
use(let a)                                         // reject: BIND(a) false on the then-arm.
                                                   //         "a is unbound on the path through line 1's then-branch"
                                                   //         mechanical fix: yield the survivor from the if (M7)

// L04-L06: loop with take and put, release after
loop {
  if stop { break }                                // accept
  let v = replace(inout p, None)                   // accept: total
  …
  p = Some(sink v)                                 // accept: BIND(v) := false
}                                                  // loop head: BIND fixpoint reached in one pass; NOTHING is written here
sink p                                             // accept: one release on every exit edge, including break
```

**Verdict: accepted with a stated cost** — one restructuring, the `if` becomes
an expression yielding the survivor. The rejection names the path whose state
differs and carries a local mechanical fix, and no drop flag exists anywhere in
the lowering, structurally rather than by policy.

### P9 A callee that changes storage state

```text
fn drain(inout v: Vec<T>) -> Vec<T>  ensures len(v) == 0
                                                   // accept: "leaves x's slot empty" is an exit refinement on an
                                                   //         ordinary value, not an exit STATE on a storage
fn reserve(inout v: Vec<T>, m: u64)  ensures cap(v) >= m
                                                   // accept: "may replace v's backing" needs no clause at all —
                                                   //         nothing names the backing (R8a has no instance here)

let d = drain(inout v)                             // accept: caller judges from the signature alone; len(v)==0 afterwards
reserve(inout v, 128)                              // accept: R6 — the footprint is the path v; facts about w, u survive

// pick: cannot be a function returning a pointer
fn pick(c: Bool, let x: T, let y: T) -> T          // accept only for Copy T: it returns a VALUE
subscript pick(c: Bool, inout s: S) -> inout T  origin { s.x, s.y }
with inout pick(c, inout s) as t { t = 1 }         // accept: a yield-once projection. for the span, facts about BOTH
                                                   //         s.x and s.y are killed (the origin set is the footprint)
let z = s.x                                        // reject inside the span: PATH(s.x, origin) overlaps
```

**Verdict: accepted with a stated cost.** `drain` and `reserve` are cheaper
than the row's own vocabulary anticipates (no state clause at all). `pick`
**needs a mechanism from D7**: a finite static origin set on a yielded
projection (HIS-D1-14), and it costs the union of the origin set's facts for
the span.

### P11 Write-once-then-frozen cache

```text
var cache: Pool<Option<V>>                          // a slot per key; "empty" is the writer's own constructor

fn get(inout cache: Pool<Option<V>>, k: Key) -> V   where V: Copy {
  match cache[k] {
    Some(v) => v                                    // accept: total read, no state consulted
    None    => { let v = compute(k); cache[k] = Some(v); v }
                                                    // accept: one exclusive access on path cache[k]
  }
}

// may a reader hold a pointer to a slot across another slot's fill?
with let cache[k1] as r { get(inout cache, k2) }    // reject unless k1 != k2 is proved: PATH(cache[k1], cache[k2])
with let cache[k1] as r { … }; get(inout cache, k2) // accept: the projection ended; no reference outlives its span
```

**Pass/fail under R1 alone: PASS, with no new vocabulary.** A slot never goes
from "holding no value" to "holding a value" — it holds a valid `Option<V>`
from construction. The write-once transition R1(b) deliberately excluded is not
needed, because it was never a storage state here. A held reader across another
slot's fill is admitted exactly when `k1 != k2` is proved, and is otherwise
rejected with that fact named.

**Verdict: accepted with a stated cost** — one discriminant word per slot and
one written arm per lookup; concurrent readers with one lazy writer is R9/D10,
not admitted here.

### P13 Relocation by a compacting third party

```text
let h = insert(inout pool, x)                       // accept: h : Handle<T>, ordinary data
let p = pointer_of(h)                               // UNWRITABLE: there is no pointer type
compact(inout pool)                                 // accept: exclusive on path pool for the call; may move bytes
let v = pool[h]                                     // accept: the key is stable by the pool's contract; one extra
                                                    //         indirection (key -> offset) is the price
```

R8a's *"interior pointers and third-party relocation are mutually exclusive
without a contract-visible fixup form"* is satisfied in the strongest way: the
two cannot both be written. The renumbering form of `compact` —
`compact(sink p: Pool<T>) -> (Pool<T>, Remap)` — is **refused** at the
declaration, because the handles it would invalidate are ordinary data
scattered in the program and the checker cannot enumerate them; only the
stable-key form is admitted.

**Verdict: accepted as required**, with a stated cost of one indirection per
pooled access and the refusal of key-renumbering compaction.

### P16 Abstraction over identities

```text
fn map_nodes<T>(inout g: Pool<Node<T>>, f: (let T) -> T)
                                                    // accept: ZERO identity parameters. parameters = storages touched,
                                                    //         which is R15's metric at its floor
fn kernel<E>(inout c: Cols<E>)                      // accept: same; PATH over field steps is type-agnostic

let hh = |inout slice: Buf<u8>| helper(inout slice, let input)
                                                    // accept: a SECOND-CLASS closure. captures `input` by let; may be
                                                    //         passed down, never stored, never returned
for w in 0..k { hh(inout out[w*s .. (w+1)*s]) }     // accept: EXT as in P6; the closure's footprint is its parameter list

fn pick_n<N: Nominal>(c: Bool, sink x: N, sink y: N) -> N
                                                    // accept for affine N: the unreturned operand is released at the call
                                                    // reject for linear N: "y is not consumed on the path returning x".
                                                    //         repair: -> (N, N, Which), returning both
```

**Verdict: accepted with a stated cost** — closures are second-class and
non-escaping; a linear `pick` must return both operands. Identity, state and
effect facts cross the boundary because none of them is a type parameter:
`PATH`/`EXT`/`AFF` are all structural in the generic body.

### P17 Partial operations

```text
let q = a / d           requires d != 0             // accept: REF, from a written requires or a preceding branch
match checked_div(a, d) { Ok(q) => …, DivZero => … }// accept: the written-outcome alternative (R12)
let b: u8 = narrow(x)   requires x < 256            // accept: REF
let y = v[i]            requires i < len(v)         // accept: REF
let y = v[i]                                        // reject: R11, missing fact `i < len(v)` at this tree location (M7)
```

Orthogonal to D1–D4, with one candidate-specific gain: because a call's
footprint is its `inout`/`sink` paths, `len(v)` survives a write to `w`, to
`v[j]`, or to any other column without a frame annotation, so index proofs are
rarely re-established.

**Verdict: accepted as required.**

---

## 4. Requirements

### 4.1 Row by row

| Row | Verdict | Reason (one sentence) |
|---|---|---|
| R1 Sequential memory safety | **partial** | (i)(ii)(iii) hold by construction — every binding is initialized where bound, storage ends only where a name is unbound, and no name reaches into storage that can change layout — but R1(e)'s P3 clause fails in a reusing pool, where a stale handle reads a type-correct wrong occupant. |
| R2 Resource lifecycle | met | Affine/linear bindings release at `sink` or scope exit, joins conjoin `BIND`, outcome arms are ordinary match arms, and no drop flag is representable. |
| R3 Value classes and transfer | met | This is the candidate's native vocabulary: `sink` is the transfer, `Option` is the hole, `replace` is the exchange, and the multiplicity lemma is the context discipline. |
| R4 Licensed facts | met | Distinctness comes from `PATH` (distinct field steps), `AFF` (distinct live affine values) and `EXT` (proved extents) — a containment-structured relation, never name inequality; P2's negative (`S` overlaps `b1`) holds because a projection of `S` shares its prefix. |
| R5 Race freedom and overlap | met | Ground (i) is discharged for P1, P2, P3's map, P5 and P6 from footprints that are already the parameter list; grounds (ii) and (iii) are orthogonal to this tuple. |
| R6 Frame precision | met | The footprint of an operation *is* its written access path, so the metric "facts killed whose support the stated footprint does not name = 0" is structural; the measured 34/41 `len()` rebind tax comes from whole-parameter footprints and has no instance here. |
| R7 Compositional call judgement | **partial** | Entry/exit states, holes, ended storage and replaced backings are all expressible as types, conventions and refinements, but "a returned interior pointer" is only a yielded projection with an origin set — it cannot be stored, so a caller cannot keep it. |
| R8a Storage-ending and relocation | met | The ending set is small and syntactic (scope exit, `sink`, assignment-over, insertion, return), and relocation is unobservable because nothing names a subterm across a statement; R8a's price on the compiler is free here. |
| R8b Placement and physical demands | **partial** | Nothing in the tuple forbids alignment, layout or address-space demands, but value semantics leaves placement to the compiler, so any demand must additionally pin the binding's storage (making elision mandatory at that site rather than opportunistic). |
| R9 Shared mutation among holders | **partial** | Several long-lived holders each writing occasionally is expressible as several `Handle`s into one pool, but every write must be given `inout pool`, so writes are serialized through one path and R4 facts at the site cover only `pool[h]`; the concurrent half is D10's. |
| R10 External resources | met | A descriptor is an affine value closed by `sink`, the open-file description is a pool row two wrappers can name, contents are a `Foreign<T>` type, and no acceptance rule mentions host crossing. |
| R11 Partial operations | met | Orthogonal, and cheaper here: R6's path-exact frame means index and divisor facts survive unrelated writes. |
| R12 Failure paths and typed outcomes | met | Outcomes are ordinary sums and every arm must discharge `BIND`; the same mechanism already carries vacancy, so it is one construct, not two. |
| R13 Resource bounds | met | Orthogonal and opt-in; the no-implicit-copy commitment (§2.3) is what keeps "no allocation the source did not write" true under value semantics. |
| R14 Stated execution model | **partial** | The model text is the specification's to state, but the tuple supplies R14(iv)'s carrier: a foreign-writable storage is a *type* (`Foreign<T>`) whose reads are in the declared access class, since there are no identities to qualify. |
| R15 Abstraction | met | Zero identity parameters; parameters per interface equal the storages the callee touches, which is the floor of R15's metric, and `PATH`/`EXT`/`AFF` are structural inside a generic body. |
| M1 Deterministic acceptance | met | Four families: `BIND` (height-2 lattice), `PATH` (syntactic prefix), `EXT` (a fixed linear-arithmetic fragment), `AFF` (a fixed-table type fact) — no search, no solver, no budget, no iteration cap. |
| M2 No unstated failure edge / no unchosen cost | met, with a **declared boundary** | (i) every failure edge is a written arm and no trap is inserted; (ii) zero compiler-inserted branches and zero drop flags — the `Option` discriminant is a field the source declared and *both of its arms are safe*, so no rule of acceptance is satisfied by the presence of a runtime comparison; see §6 for the objection. |
| M3 Trusted base | met | No `unsafe`, and fewer axioms than an identity model needs; one new base entry only if a coalescing arena is wanted (the buffer split/join adjacency primitive of P2). |
| M4 Writer regularity | met | One spelling per construct across a tiny inventory — three conventions, one projection form, one `sink` — with no mode axis, no region syntax and no identity syntax. |
| M5 Acceptance independent of permission | met | Overlap permission is computed from footprints that are already in the signature; deleting the PAR judgment changes no verdict. |
| M6 Soundness evidence | **partial** | The bounded small-model check is unusually cheap (the state space is paths × a boolean per name), frame soundness (ii) is structural and erasure (iii) is total; the adequacy theorem is the same stated later obligation every candidate carries (owner decision 9). |
| M7 Repairable rejection | met | Four rejection kinds — overlapping paths at one access, `BIND` unbound at a join or loop, projection escape, missing `REF` — each with a local named fix and a non-empty missing-fact payload; P8's restructuring is the payload form M7 explicitly admits. |
| M8 Teaching budget | met | The taught surface for D1–D4 is three conventions, one projection form, path overlap, extent arithmetic and affine distinctness — no lifetimes, regions, identities, state lattice, loan durations or permission tokens. |
| M9 Measured performance floor | **partial** | P5/P6's obvious shape is the fast shape with per-column facts by construction and zero guards, and pooled traversal is index arithmetic rather than pointer chasing; against that, vacancy costs a tag word and a branch where it is used, pooled access costs an indirection, and guaranteed in-place `inout` plus named-return-value elision must be a lowering *rule*. |
| M10 Checking cost and edit stability | met | The only flow-sensitive fact is one boolean per name, so joins are linear in live names and the condition-atom growth risk of a term-valued state (MAP §8 Q10) does not arise; a one-token edit reaches the enclosing declaration plus the callers of a changed signature. |
| M11 Evolution with stated loss | met | Orthogonal; §6 W8 names the loss this tuple must state — the verdict diff against today's borrow rules is a rewrite, not a delta. |

**Counts: met 20, partial 7 (R1, R7, R8b, R9, R14, M6, M9), violated 0.**

### 4.2 The price this candidate charges the compiler

| Forbidden | Required | Free |
|---|---|---|
| implicit deep copy, implicit retain/release, implicit copy-on-write | in-place `inout` and named-return-value elision as a **lowering rule**, not an optimization | any relocation whatsoever: nothing names a subterm across a statement, so R8a's usual price is not charged |
| dynamic exclusivity checks anywhere (Swift's class/global fallback) | `!alias.scope` per resolved path root on loaded pointers, or M9's P5 claim is unbacked | field reordering and padding where no R8b demand is stated |
| storing or returning a projection in any lowering-visible form | a fixed linear-arithmetic fragment for `EXT`, stated with its degree under M10 | inlining, LTO, loop versioning, remainder loops (M2's backend carve-out) |
| key-renumbering pool compaction | `origin`-set killing for a yielded projection's span | choosing where a value lives when no demand pins it |

### 4.3 Writer cost

| Per | Written | Not written |
|---|---|---|
| signature | one convention keyword per parameter; `origin` on a yielded projection only | identity, region or lifetime parameters; entry/exit states; loan clauses; memory effect rows |
| loop head | nothing for memory safety | loop invariants over storage state |
| join | nothing | state merges, drop-flag reasoning, path annotations |
| statement | `sink` at a consuming transfer; `with … as x` only for a multi-statement projection | per-access permission, per-access identity |
| per storage | nothing | state declarations, generations, tokens |
| charged elsewhere | R11 `requires`/proofs, R12 arms, and one written arm per read of a vacancy-capable slot | — |
