Refused inside Pin: the runtime pin count (M2(ii)); *pinned* here means "some window is open", a checker structure |
| D3 (occupancy) | **State as ordinary data or typed outcome** | HIS-D3-04 ADOPTED (vacancy as an `Option`-shaped value) | A slot the writer wants empty is the writer's own value, matched in the writer's own branch. Refused: HIS-D3-12, HIS-D3-16, SYS-D3-18 as *language* state |
| **D4** | **Per-scope exclusivity windows** *(primary)* | AI-D4-06 (the writer opens explicit windows), RAD-D4-11 (exclusivity as a block property), SYS-D4-05 (block-scoped restrict, `noalias.scope.decl`), THE-D4-16 (access-span exclusivity, SE-0176), THE-D4-21 (adoption and focus, static focus blocks), HIS-D4-09 ADOPTED (suspension windows), HIS-D4-10 FLOATED (Aiken 2003 checked local `restrict`) | Exclusivity is a property of a **row's scope**, never of a reference's life. Refused: SYS-D4-09's Swift fallback to dynamic checks for class/global storage (M2); HIS-D4-01's OWN-5 unconditional exclusivity |
| D4 (the policy) | **Mixed strict and permissive policy per unit** | THE-D4-24 (gradual aliasing policy per module), AI-D4-10 (two dialects) — taken with the **unit reduced to one window**, not a module and not a function | Strict inside a carve's extent; permissive everywhere else. The family's own tension — *"the module boundary is where a runtime check would live, which M2 forbids"* — does not arise, because a window boundary is a syntactic point inside one function with both sides statically checked |
| D4 (the fact dial) | **Pay-per-fact exclusivity with tooling support** | AI-D4-07 (exclusivity as an opt-in optimization annotation), SYS-D4-07 (obligation discharged at the loop that needs it) | `@W` means "the callee writes it"; `@E` adds "and nobody else touches it here", which is the only grade that emits `noalias`. Refused: AI-D4-08/09 (compiler proposes, writer pins; fact-loss reports) — a second authorship channel |
| D4 (the decision procedure) | **Overlap judged by resolved paths and proved extents** | HIS-D4-12 ADOPTED (overlap by complete resolved paths), HIS-D4-13 ADOPTED (proved half-open view extents), SYS-D4-10 (proved-disjoint byte ranges) | How a carve is checked to be a partition. Refused: HIS-D4-14 (literal-only ranges) |
| D4 (the escape) | **Declared coincidence** | AI-D4-03 (`alias 'a 'b;` per coinciding pair), HIS-D4-11 FLOATED (coincidence declared per pair at a boundary), SYS-D4-03 (inverted `restrict`, checked), THE-D4-20, RAD-D4-10 | Two coarse names are distinct by default; `alias ρ σ` declares them the same storage and is *checked*, never trusted |
| D4 (the read axis) | **Read-only as a type flag, not a loan** | AI-D4-05, SYS-D4-04, HIS-D4-03 FLOATED | `&ro ptr<ρ,T>`: a flag with no duration and no region (C10) |

### Why these four cohere

They are not four choices. They are one choice — **a row's scope is a name's
scope** — read at four decision points.

| Step | Claim | Row / coupling it closes |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **D4 first, and D4 is about a scope, not a value.** The ladder's finding (MECHANISM-MAP §3, last row: *"borrowing is not the mechanism that refuses any hazard once storage state and identity exist"*) removes exclusivity from safety. What is left for it to do is R4 and R5: supply an interference fact. A fact has a *span*, not a lifetime. So exclusivity is scoped to the span over which the fact is claimed. | R4, R5, R9, C5 |
| 2 | **D4 ⇒ D1's two levels.** If exclusivity is scoped, the names that carry it are scoped too. A name that cannot outlive its window cannot appear in a type that outlives it — so a signature cannot mention it, and the identity vocabulary splits in two by construction rather than by fiat. | C1, C3, M8, M10 |
| 3 | **D1's split ⇒ D2's carrier.** A coarse name crosses a cut; a fine name does not. The only artifact that exists at exactly a cut and at exactly a block head is a **row**. So the row is where permission and state live, and the row's carve clause is what mints the fine names. | R7, C8, C14 |
| 4 | **D2 ⇒ D3's shape.** A row states an entry state and an exit state per name. That is an automaton edge. The state vocabulary must therefore be a finite declared automaton per type, with `Init`/`Uninit`/`Gone` as the default one — and a window's open/close are two more edges of the *same* automaton, not a separate concept. | R1, R7, R10, C7, C12 |
| 5 | **Closure.** Remove D4's scoping and fine names have no boundary, so they land in signatures and M8 pays for them. Remove D1's split and the row must name element identities at a cut, which C3's hardest clause (distinctness discharge *including sub-identities*) then charges at every call. Remove D2's row and a window has nothing to declare, so the carve becomes compiler inference and M1 dies. Remove D3's automaton and a window's open/close is a bespoke rule instead of an edge, and M4 pays for a second state concept. | — |

**One seam is deliberately cut:** *permission and interference are scoped;
validity and occupancy are not.* State lives on a storage forever (P7, P2, P4);
a fact about the partition of that storage lives only as long as the row that
claimed it. Today those two are one thing — a borrow is live ⇒ its referent is
valid — which is why P4's `push` is blocked and P3's back edges are unwritable.

**Why a seeded generator would not reach this combination.** Every seed word in
the D1–D4 space names a *carrier* (a name in a type, a ghost token, a
permission-carrying reference, an access path, a pinned certificate) and then
derives the other three points from it. This candidate fixes a *boundary*
first — where a fact stops being true — and lets the carrier fall out. That
order is what makes **Two-level granularity** (a family with one member and one
line of catalog text), **Window-scoped identity**, **Permission as an effect on
the arrow**, **Writer-declared typestate automata**, **Per-scope exclusivity
windows** and **Mixed strict and permissive policy per unit** cohere; taken as
starting points they look like six unrelated compromises.

---

## 2. The model

### 2.1 Names

```text
coarse  ρ ::= fresh atom minted at a formation site        -- appears in types, signatures, struct fields; erased
fine    n ::= ρ ↓ w . k                                    -- carve entry k of window w over ρ; never in any type

carve entry ::=  .f                 -- a field of the named type
              |  backing(.f)        -- the element storage behind a buffer/vector field   (the column shape)
              |  [i]                -- one element at a proved index
              |  [lo .. hi)         -- a proved half-open extent
              |  \ S                -- the complement of the entries listed in S
```

A carve is **total** when its entries partition the whole named storage
(the default field carve is total, padding included); otherwise **partial**.

### 2.2 What a pointer's type says

```text
ptr<ρ, T>          -- a copyable, storable pointer; ρ is a coarse store name
&ro ptr<ρ, T>      -- the same, read-only flag set (a flag, no duration, no region)
```

That is the whole of it. No permission, no borrow, no lifetime, no state, no
generation, no capability. A pointer may be copied, stored in a struct field
(P4's `Cursor`), stored in a node (P3's `next`/`prev`), returned and compared.

### 2.3 What the checker holds, per coarse name

| Held | Content |
|---|---|
| `auto(ρ)` | the automaton of ρ's type (default `Storage = {Uninit, Init, Gone}`) |
| `σ(ρ)` | the current state, one automaton state |
| `carves(ρ)` | a stack of open windows, each an ordered list of carve entries, each entry with its own `σ` |
| `facts(·)` | contents, measures (`len_of`, `cap_of`), invariants, keyed by a coarse or a fine name |
| `⊑` | the containment forest over coarse names (`ρ1 ⊑ ρS` for an arena block in its byte store) |
| `≡` | declared coincidences (`alias ρ σ`); absent, distinct names are distinct |

Distinctness is **never** name inequality: `dis(m,n)` holds iff `m` and `n` are
different entries of one carve, or their coarse roots are `⊑`-incomparable and
not `≡`-related (C3, and P2's `S` vs `b1` negative test).

### 2.4 The row

```text
row {  ρ : pre ⇒ post  @g  [carve { k1, k2, … }]      -- one line per coarse name the operation touches
       fresh ∃ρ' ⊑ ρ : post                            -- a promotion: a fine extent becomes a coarse name
       result : π ∈ {ρ, σ}                              -- a finite static origin set
       requires φ ;  ensures ψ                          -- ordinary facts
       outcomes { … }                                   -- R12 arms, each with its own exit states
    }
g ::= @0 | @R | @W | @E              -- fixed four-element chain 0 ⊑ R ⊑ W ⊑ E
```

`@W` = the operation writes it. `@E` = it writes it **and nothing else here
touches it**, which is the only grade that licenses `noalias`. Sequential
composition of grades is the join; two operations may overlap iff for every
name both touch, the grades are `@R`/`@R`, or the names are `dis`.

**The default carve.** A row entry with no written carve carves by the fixed,
specification-defined function of the *named type*: its fields, and the backing
of each buffer/vector field. This is a total function of a declaration, not a
search; it is not a fixpoint; it never consults a body. A total carve cannot
reject anything (§2.6), so the default is free.

### 2.5 State changes

| Event | Effect on `σ` and `carves` | Row clause that states it |
|---|---|---|
| `alloc(n)` | mint ρ, `σ(ρ) := Uninit` | `fresh ∃ρ : Uninit` |
| arena `alloc(A,n)` | split ρS: mint ρ' with `ρ' ⊑ ρS`, remove its extent from ρS's free extent | `ρS: Init ⇒ Init @W; fresh ∃ρ' ⊑ ρS : Uninit` |
| `take(p)` at `ρ.x` | `σ(ρ.x) := Uninit` (a hole in the storage, visible to every alias) | `ρ.x : Init ⇒ Uninit` |
| `put(q,v)` at `ρ.x` | `σ(ρ.x) := Init` | `ρ.x : Uninit ⇒ Init` |
| `replace(p,new)` | `Init ⇒ Init`, one event, no intermediate hole (SET-2) | `ρ.x : Init ⇒ Init @W` |
| `free(ρ)` | `σ(ρ) := Gone`, permanent; **requires `carves(ρ)` empty** | `ρ : Init|Uninit ⇒ Gone` |
| relocating `move` | old ρ `⇒ Gone`; fresh ρ'' `Init`; **requires `carves(ρ)` empty** | `ρ : Init ⇒ Gone; fresh ∃ρ'' : Init` |
| `push` / `reserve` | conditional: `cap ≥ m ⇒ backing unchanged; else backing(ρ) ⇒ Gone, fresh backing'` | two-armed row clause |
| window **open** | push a carve onto `carves(ρ)`; mint fine names; each entry's `σ` projected from the parent | the row of the `focus` block or of the call |
| window **close** | each entry's exit state written back into the parent's projection; retire the fine names | the same row's `post` |
| declared transition | `σ(ρ) := t(σ(ρ))` for an automaton edge `t` | `ρ : S1 ⇒ S2` |

### 2.6 The one rule that rejects an alias

> Inside a window carving ρ, an access whose resolved place **meets** a carve
> entry is accepted iff it names that entry, or the carve is **total** and the
> access covers a union of entries. Otherwise it is rejected, and the
> diagnostic names the entry it meets, the window head that opened it, and
> three repairs: name the entry, prove the access lies in the complement, or
> move the access outside the window.

This is the whole of D4's strictness. It never runs outside a window, and a
total carve (the default) satisfies it vacuously.

### 2.7 A join and a loop head

| Point | Rule |
|---|---|
| **join** | every name's `σ` must be **equal** on the incoming edges, and `carves` must be identical (windows are statement-shaped, so they are balanced by construction). A difference the writer wants is written as a value: an outcome arm or a sum (R12; HIS-D3-04). No lattice, no condition atoms, no widening, no drop flag. |
| **loop head** | the head carries a row. The default row is the identity on every name; if the body's composed row is the identity, the writer writes nothing. Otherwise the writer writes the head row and the checker verifies *initiation* (the entry edge refines it) and *consecution* (body ∘ row refines row) — two entailments, no fixpoint. |
| **window close** | every carve entry must reach the exit state the window's row declares (default `Init`). "Put both parts back" is enforced here (P1). |
| **call** | the callee's row is projected onto the actuals exactly as EFF-2 projects today (*"each declared path's root formal selects its actual, the path's static field suffix is appended to the actual's resolved place"*). If a carve of the actual's coarse name is open, every name the row touches must lie within **one** entry, and the call runs as a nested window over that entry. |

### 2.8 What the writer writes, and where

| Where | What | How often |
|---|---|---|
| **signature** | one row line per coarse identity the callee touches: `ρ: pre ⇒ post @g`; a `carve` clause only when the default is too coarse | always — this is the only mandatory annotation |
| **struct field holding a pointer** | the store name as a parameter of the struct: `struct Cursor<ρ> { at: ptr<ρ,V>, i: u64 }` | per stored pointer |
| **nominal type** | `states { … } transitions { … }` when the type has a protocol (a descriptor, a pool, a DMA buffer); nothing otherwise | per protocol type |
| **loop head** | a row only when the body's row is not the identity | rarely |
| **join** | nothing; arms agree, or the writer writes the difference as a value | per differing arm |
| **statement** | `focus ρ as { A = …, B = … } { … }` only where a finer carve than the signature's is wanted (P1's element split) | per runtime-indexed split |
| **call site** | `alias ρ σ` when two actuals are the same storage; an index or extent proof when a carve needs one | per coinciding pair, per split |

### 2.9 What is erased

Coarse names, fine names, carves, grades, rows, automaton states, containment,
coincidence declarations, every proof: all erased before lowering (M6(iii)).
The residue is exactly R4's licensed facts:

| Source fact | LLVM form | Why it is the same shape |
|---|---|---|
| a carve entry, inside its window | one `!alias.scope`, `!noalias` against its siblings | a scope is *"valid within a single iteration"* and *"must be duplicated when a loop is unrolled"* — a window is precisely that |
| window head | `llvm.experimental.noalias.scope.decl` | the decl marks where a scope becomes valid; the window head is where the carve becomes valid |
| a `@E` parameter | `noalias` | exclusive for the call's dynamic extent |
| a `@R` parameter | `readonly`; `@W` with no `@R` ⇒ `writeonly` + `initializes((0,n))` over the entry's extent | EFF-2's independence of reads and writes; *"the cleanest unexploited fact in the current spec"* |
| the whole row | `memory(argmem: …)`; `@0` on everything ⇒ `memory(none)` | rows are formal-rooted, so `argmem` covers them |
| `fresh ∃ρ` on a result | `noalias` return | *"disjoint from the storage for any other object accessible to the caller"* |

No emission-time re-derivation is needed: the identity the per-load metadata
wants is the carve name, which the checker already has. R4's price forbids
*requiring* re-derivation to reach a stated fact; this model never does.

---

## 3. Derivations

Notation follows the ladder. `σ(n)` is a state; `dis(m,n)` is the distinctness
relation of §2.3; `carves(ρ)` is the window stack.

### P1 Container split with a runtime index

```text
v : ptr<ρ, Vector<u64>>                          // σ(ρ)=Init, backing(ρ)=β, σ(β)=Init, len(β)=n
                                                 //   fact: β is a fine name of ρ's default (total) field carve
focus β as { A = β[i], B = β[j] } {              // open. carve obligations, discharged here or rejected here:
                                                 //   i < n, j < n  (the existing OP-4 bounds family)
                                                 //   i != j        (written by the writer, or from a prior branch)
                                                 // accept: carve is PARTIAL — complement β \ {i,j} is an entry
  va = take(A)                                   // accept: σ(A)=Init ⇒ Uninit. A hole in β[i], as in Step 2 of the ladder
  vb = take(B)                                   // accept: σ(B)=Init ⇒ Uninit
  write(A, f(va)) ∥ write(B, g(vb))              // accept overlap: footprints {A}@E and {B}@E, dis(A,B) by the
                                                 //   carve's partition ⇒ R5(a)(i). No runtime check, no worker count
  x = read(β[k])                                 // REJECT (no proof in scope): the place β[k] MEETS entries A and B.
                                                 //   M7 payload: rule §2.6, window head at L3, missing fact
                                                 //   "k != i && k != j"; repairs: prove it, name A/B, or hoist the read
  use k != i && k != j ;                         // the writer's own step (P1's "else the writer must branch")
  x = read(β[k])                                 // accept: β[k] now provably lies in the complement entry
  put(A, move va') ; put(B, move vb')            // accept: σ(A)=σ(B):=Init
}                                                // close: exit row demands σ(A)=σ(B)=Init.
                                                 //   If a put were missing: REJECT at the close, naming the entry
push(v, x)                                       // accept: carves(β) is empty (push's row requires it, R8a)
```

Backend: two `!alias.scope`s in a fresh domain declared at L3; both writes
carry `!noalias` against the other. **Verdict: accepted as required.**
Sequential legality comes from the carve obligation, not from a borrow scope;
the two writes overlap; the diagnostic names the missing fact; no runtime
check. Cost: one `focus` line and one written inequality.

### P2 Arena with independently released blocks

```text
A = arena_new()                                  // mint ρM (metadata) and ρS (byte store); σ=Init; ρM,ρS distinct
(b1,ρ1) = alloc(A,64)                            // row: { ρM: Init⇒Init @W;  ρS: Init⇒Init @W;
                                                 //        fresh ∃ρ1 ⊑ ρS : Uninit }
                                                 // accept: a SPLIT, not a window — ρ1 is promoted to a coarse name
                                                 //   with an independent lifetime, so it may be freed independently
(b2,ρ2) = alloc(A,64); (b3,ρ3) = alloc(A,64)     // accept: ρ2, ρ3 likewise; pairwise dis by the split's extents
fill(b1) ∥ fill(b2) ∥ fill(b3)                   // accept overlap: rows {ρ1@E}, {ρ2@E}, {ρ3@E};
                                                 //   dis(ρ1,ρ2), dis(ρ1,ρ3), dis(ρ2,ρ3) ⇒ R5(a)(i).
                                                 //   NOTE dis(ρ1,ρS) is FALSE: ρ1 ⊑ ρS. R4(b)'s negative test holds
                                                 // accept: A is not held: no carve of ρM or ρS is open between calls;
                                                 //   ρM is written only inside alloc's and free's own call windows
free(A,b2)                                       // row: { ρM: Init⇒Init @W; ρ2: Init ⇒ Gone; ρ2's extent returns to ρS }
                                                 // accept: σ(ρ2):=Gone, permanent; the affine owner b2 is consumed once
(b4,ρ4) = alloc(A,32)                            // accept: fresh ρ4 ⊑ ρS, reusing ρ2's bytes.
                                                 //   ρ4 is a NEW name; address reuse never revives ρ2 (R1(a) closing line)
read(b2)                                         // REJECT: σ(ρ2)=Gone. R1(a)(ii). M7 names the free at L8
read(b1)                                         // accept: σ(ρ1)=Init
free(A,b1); free(A,b3); free(A,b4)               // accept: each Init ⇒ Gone exactly once. R2 discharged on this path
                                                 //   a second free(A,b1): REJECT, the affine owner is consumed (R3)
```

**Verdict: accepted as required.** Blocks are exclusively owned because each is
its own coarse name at grade `@E`; metadata is written only inside `alloc`'s
and `free`'s own call windows; nobody holds `A` between operations; the stale
pointer is refused by state, not by address.

### P3 Graph with back edges in a pool

```text
pool P : ρP                                      // Pool declares:  states { } (default) ;  invariant Links (below)
                                                 //   slots are a total element carve of ρP's backing, entries ρP[k]
Node { next: ptr<ρP,Node>, prev: ptr<ρP,Node>, data: u64 }
                                                 // accept: a stored pointer names the COARSE pool store (C8).
                                                 //   It is copyable and storable: no permission, no duration
a, b, n : ptr<ρP, Node>                          // three live aliases into one store. Permissive policy: no window open
write(deref(a).next, n)                          // accept: σ(ρP)=Init; aliased writes need no judgment (ladder Step 0, R9)
write(deref(n).prev, a)                          // accept
write(deref(n).next, b)                          // accept
write(deref(b).prev, n)                          // accept: four link writes through several paths, sequentially legal.
                                                 //   A design that rejects these fails R9's negative test; this one does not
invariant Links : forall k. Occupied(ρP,k) ⇒ Occupied(ρP, next_of(k)) && Occupied(ρP, prev_of(k))
                                                 // stated ONCE on the nominal. Support: the .next/.prev columns and
                                                 //   the pool's occupancy data
par_for k in P.live { write(ρP[k].data, f(read(ρP[k].data))) }
                                                 // accept overlap: the element carve is total; dis(ρP[k], ρP[k']) for
                                                 //   k != k' by the partition; the footprint is .data only ⇒ R5(a)(i).
                                                 //   Links' support is .next/.prev, which no iteration names ⇒ Links
                                                 //   survives the whole loop (R6: no fact dropped whose support is unnamed)
remove(m)                                        // row: { ρP: Init⇒Init @W carve { [m], occupancy };
                                                 //        ensures !Occupied(ρP,m) ; ensures Links }
                                                 //   body: unlink first, then σ(ρP[m]) := Uninit (the slot is vacated)
read(deref(pm).data)                             // REJECT: the read of ρP[m] requires σ(ρP[m]) = Init; the row's exit
                                                 //   state is Uninit. R1(a)(i). Every path to m is refused, because the
                                                 //   state is on the slot, not on any of the pointers that reach it
insert(x) reusing m's slot                       // accept: σ(ρP[m]) := Init, Occupied(m) re-established, Links preserved
traverse: p = head; loop { d = read(deref(p).data); p = read(deref(p).next) }
                                                 // accept: each step discharges Occupied(next_of(k)) from Links by one
                                                 //   automatic entailment step; the invariant is stated once and reused
```

**Verdict: accepted with a stated cost.** Two costs, stated plainly:

1. A type-stable pool never *ends* a slot's storage, so "removal invalidates
   every path to m" is enforced by R1(a)(i) (a read of a vacated slot) rather
   than by R1(a)(ii). Storage that is genuinely ended (P2's arena block) uses
   a promoted coarse name and gets (ii).
2. `remove(h)` for a **runtime** `h` kills `Occupied(ρP,k)` for every `k`
   unless `h` is a captured symbolic index shared with the access
   (HIS-D1-23). Sound, and imprecise: the traversal re-discharges from
   `Links`, which is one entailment step, but a loop that held `Occupied(k)`
   across an unrelated `remove` pays a re-discharge. This is charged against
   R6 below.

### P4 Cursor over a growing vector

```text
struct Cursor<ρ> { at: ptr<ρ, Vector<u64>>, i: u64 }   // the store name is a struct parameter (C8)
c = Cursor { at: v, i: 0 }                             // accept: a pointer is storable. No loan is created, so nothing
                                                       //   is suspended and `v` remains fully usable
a = c.read()                                           // row of Cursor::read:
                                                       //   { ρ: Init⇒Init @R; backing(ρ): Init⇒Init @R;
                                                       //     requires σ(ρ)=Init && i < len_of(ρ) }
                                                       // accept: both discharged
reserve(v, len+1)                                      // (the writer's chosen shape) row:
                                                       //   { backing(ρ): Init⇒Init when cap>=len+1 | ⇒Gone otherwise }
push(v, 5)                                             // accept: carves(ρ) is empty — no window and no borrow blocks push.
                                                       //   row: { ρ: Init⇒Init @E ;
                                                       //          backing(ρ): Init⇒Init if len0<cap0 else Gone+fresh β' }
b = c.read()                                           // accept: cap0 > len0 was established at L4, so the row's first
                                                       //   arm applies: σ(backing(ρ))=Init, and len grew so i<len holds.
                                                       // Without L4: REJECT. M7 payload: "backing(ρ) may be Gone after the
                                                       //   push at L5; prove len0 < cap0 (e.g. reserve) or re-form c"
free(v)                                                // row: { ρ: Init ⇒ Gone }; carves(ρ) empty ⇒ accept
c.read()                                               // REJECT: σ(ρ)=Gone. R1(a)(ii). Permanent
```

**Verdict: accepted as required.** A stored pointer to a container lives in a
struct; validity is decided by state and a proof, never by a borrow that blocks
`push`.

### P5 Struct-of-arrays kernel

```text
struct Cols { a,b,c,d,e,f,g,h : buffer<u64> }
fn kernel(s: ptr<ρ, Cols>, n: u64)
  row { ρ : Init ⇒ Init @E }                     // ONE row line. No carve clause is written:
                                                 //   the DEFAULT carve of a named struct type is
                                                 //   { .a, backing(.a), …, .h, backing(.h), padding } — TOTAL
{
  for i in 0..n {                                // loop head: the body's row composes to the identity on every
                                                 //   name ⇒ no loop row is written
    set backing(.a)[i] = f(backing(.a)[i], backing(.c)[i], backing(.d)[i])
                                                 // accept: the three names are distinct entries of the total carve ⇒
                                                 //   dis pairwise ⇒ R4(b) supplies a per-load fact for EVERY load
    set backing(.b)[i] = g(backing(.b)[i], backing(.e)[i], backing(.f)[i],
                           backing(.g)[i], backing(.h)[i])
                                                 // accept: same
  }                                              // PAR-2 overlap: the two writes carry the proved affine map (1,0)
                                                 //   over L's binder; every read through those roots uses the same map
                                                 //   ⇒ iterations non-interfering ⇒ R5(a)(i). No guard, no versioning
}
```

Backend: eight `!alias.scope`s in one domain declared at function entry (the
window is the signature's row), each buffer load and store tagged. This is
exactly the fact EVIDENCE §B.2 calls *"the half Rust cannot reach"* — Rust's
`&mut Cols` gets parameter `noalias` but *"the Vec data pointers loaded through
it are fresh pointers the optimizer treats as possibly overlapping"* — and
here the identity is carried by the carve rather than manufactured at emission.

**Verdict: accepted as required, at zero extra writer tokens.** The obvious
shape is the fast shape (M9's testable clause): the writer wrote one row line
that R7 required anyway.

### P6 Range partition helper

```text
fn helper(out: ptr<σ, buffer<u8>>, input: &ro ptr<τ, Input>)
  row { σ : Uninit ⇒ Init @E ;                   // writes its whole extent, reads nothing of it ⇒ `initializes`
        τ : Init ⇒ Init @R }                     // the signature ALONE tells the caller what it writes (P6's demand)
{ … }                                            // body checked once against this row

out : ptr<ρ, buffer<u8>> of n bytes ; s = n / k
for w in 0..k {
  helper(slice_of(out, w*s .. (w+1)*s), input)   // the CALL is the window; the actual's extent IS the carve entry.
                                                 //   Entry obligation: [w*s,(w+1)*s) ⊆ [0,n) — from the arithmetic
                                                 //   of the ranges alone, by the existing affine family
}                                                // accept overlap of iterations: iteration w's footprint is
                                                 //   { ρ[w*s..(w+1)*s] @E , τ @R }. Two iterations w != w' have
                                                 //   dis entries by the half-open extent algebra (HIS-D4-13);
                                                 //   τ is @R on both ⇒ R5(a)(i). The worker count k is the writer's
                                                 //   own loop bound; no schedule, no tile size, no worker count added
```

Backend: `noalias` + `writeonly` + `initializes((0,s))` on `out`, `readonly` on
`input`, and a per-iteration `noalias.scope.decl` — which LangRef requires to be
duplicated on unroll precisely because the property is per iteration.

**Verdict: accepted as required, at zero extra writer tokens.** The program is
written exactly as PROGRAMS.md writes it.

### P7 Take, put, replace through aliases

```text
p, q : ptr<ρ, T>                                 // two pointers, one coarse name. Permissive policy: no window, no rule
v = take(p)                                      // row { ρ: Init ⇒ Uninit }. State is a property of the STORAGE
read(q)                                          // REJECT: σ(ρ)=Uninit. R1(a)(i). The hole p left is visible through q
put(q, move v)                                   // row { ρ: Uninit ⇒ Init }. Another alias fills the hole — legal,
                                                 //   because nothing about the hole was attached to p
read(p)                                          // accept: σ(ρ)=Init
old = replace(p, new)                            // row { ρ: Init ⇒ Init @W } — ONE event, no intermediate hole (SET-2)
read(q)                                          // accept: reads `new`. The contents fact for ρ was killed by the @W
                                                 //   and re-established by the row's `ensures contents(ρ) = new`
free ρ                                           // row { ρ: Init ⇒ Gone }; carves(ρ) empty ⇒ accept
read(p)                                          // REJECT: σ(ρ)=Gone, permanently. R1(a)(ii)
read(q)                                          // REJECT: same fact, same diagnostic. Neither pointer is privileged
```

**Verdict: accepted as required**, line for line.

### P8 Conditional release and loop exits

```text
// (a) the naive shape
if c { free(a) } else { free(b) }                // then-edge: σ(ρa)=Gone, σ(ρb)=Init
                                                 // else-edge: σ(ρa)=Init, σ(ρb)=Gone
use(survivor)                                    // REJECT at the join. §2.7: states must be EQUAL on incoming edges.
                                                 //   M7 payload names both edges by tree location and both names whose
                                                 //   state differs, and the repair: "make the survivor a value"
                                                 //   No drop flag is inserted — M2(ii) holds by construction

// (b) the accepted shape: the difference is a value the writer wrote (R12 / HIS-D3-04)
let s = if c { free(a); b } else { free(b); a }  // then-edge: σ(ρa)=Gone, ρb moved into s
                                                 // else-edge: σ(ρb)=Gone, ρa moved into s
                                                 // accept: on BOTH edges, a and b have left scope and exactly one
                                                 //   affine owner `s` is live with σ=Init. The origin set of s is
                                                 //   {ρa, ρb} (HIS-D1-14), which is all R2 and R4 need
use(s)                                           // accept: facts about s hold over the union of its origins
free(s)                                          // accept: released exactly once on every path. R2 discharged

// (c) the loop half, unchanged from the program text
loop {
  if stop { break }                              // break edge carries σ(ρ)=Init — the loop-head row
  v = take(p)                                    // σ(ρ) := Uninit
  …
  put(p, move v)                                 // σ(ρ) := Init — the body's row composes to the IDENTITY
}                                                // accept: no loop row written, because the identity is the default.
                                                 //   A body that took without putting: REJECT at the back edge,
                                                 //   naming the head's state and the body's exit state
free(p)                                          // accept: σ(ρ)=Init on every exit edge
```

**Verdict: (a) rejected by the candidate, and the candidate is at fault for the
naive spelling; (b) and (c) accepted as required.** The cost is one rewrite:
the branch must produce the survivor as a value. The alternative — D3's *state
as a term over captured conditions* (`ite(c, Gone, Init)`) — would accept (a)
verbatim; it is declined here so that the join rule stays equality, with no
condition atoms whose growth M10 would have to bound (map §8 Q10). The
requirement's own demands are met: no runtime drop flag, and the rejection
names the path whose state differs.

### P9 A callee that changes storage state

```text
fn drain(x: ptr<ρ,T>)  row { ρ : Init ⇒ Uninit }
                                                 // the hole is IN the signature — R7(b) "exit states per identity"
fn reserve(v: ptr<ρ,Vector<T>>, m: u64)
  row { ρ : Init ⇒ Init @E ;
        backing(ρ) : Init ⇒ Init            when cap_of(ρ) >= m
                   | Init ⇒ Gone, fresh β'  otherwise }
                                                 // the conditional replacement is a two-armed row clause (R8a, C9)
fn pick(c: bool, x: ptr<ρ,T>, y: ptr<σ,T>) -> ptr<π,T>
  row { ρ : Init⇒Init @R ; σ : Init⇒Init @R ; result : π ∈ {ρ, σ} }
                                                 // a finite static origin set; the result's grade is the meet of the two

// caller, judging by the signatures alone
drain(x) ; read(x)                               // REJECT: σ(ρ)=Uninit from drain's exit state. R1(a)(i).
                                                 //   The caller never opens drain's body
reserve(v, 100) ; read(pe)                       // accept iff cap_of(v) >= 100 was proved before the call.
                                                 //   Otherwise REJECT: M7 names "backing(ρ) may be Gone; the row's
                                                 //   second arm applies unless cap_of(v) >= 100"
z = pick(c, x, y) ; write(z, 1)                  // accept: the write's footprint is {ρ, σ} (the origin set), so facts
                                                 //   about BOTH are killed. Sound, and exactly as coarse as the set
focus ρ as { A = ρ.left } { pick(c, x, y) }      // REJECT: pick's row names ρ whole, which meets A but is not contained
                                                 //   in one entry. M7: "close the window or carve pick's row"
                                                 // (the same check that makes P13 work)
```

**Verdict: accepted as required.** Each effect is visible in the signature, the
caller judges by the signature alone, and the body is checked once against it.

### P11 Write-once-then-frozen cache

```text
type Slot<V> states { Empty, Filled } transitions { fill : Empty ⇒ Filled }
                                                 // a writer-declared automaton with NO edge out of Filled.
                                                 //   "Frozen" is the absence of a transition, not a new language state
cache : ptr<ρ, Table<K, Slot<V>>>
fn get(k: K) row { ρ : Init ⇒ Init @E carve { .slot(k) } }
{
  match slot_state(cache, k) {                   // the writer's own match on writer-visible data (HIS-D3-04);
                                                 //   the checker consults no occupancy structure of its own
    Empty => fill(ρ.slot(k), compute(k))         // accept: automaton edge Empty ⇒ Filled at grade @E on that entry
    Filled => { }                                // accept
  }
  read(ρ.slot(k))                                // accept: Filled ⇒ the slot's storage is Init on both arms.
                                                 //   §2.7's join: the arms agree on σ(ρ.slot(k)) = Filled
}

// a reader holding a pointer to one slot across another slot's fill
r1 = &ro ptr into ρ.slot(k1)                     // accept: a read-only flag, no loan, no duration
get(k2)                                          // accept. Fact question: get's row carves .slot(k), so with k2 a
                                                 //   distinct CAPTURED symbolic index, dis(.slot(k1), .slot(k2)) holds
                                                 //   and Filled(k1) survives (R6)
read(r1)                                         // accept — validity never depended on the fill at all:
                                                 //   σ(ρ) is Init throughout, so R1 is satisfied with no extra state
                                                 // If k2 is an unrelated runtime value: the carve degrades to `ρ` whole,
                                                 //   Filled(k1) is killed, and the read needs one re-discharge.
                                                 //   Never a rejection of the read's SAFETY, only of the contents fact
```

**Under R1 alone: pass.** A slot goes `Uninit → Init` once and never changes;
nothing in R1 is at risk, and no new state vocabulary is spent — the freeze is
a missing edge in a declared automaton. A reader may hold a pointer to a slot
across another slot's fill, unconditionally for R1 and conditionally on a
symbolic-slot carve for the contents fact. why-whitefoot §5's stance (the
absence of such cells is a performance argument) is preserved: admission here
costs nothing at run time and one automaton declaration at compile time.
**Verdict: accepted with a stated cost** — the cost is R6 precision under a
runtime key, and a D5 arithmetic fragment if the writer wants per-key kills.

### P13 Relocation by a compacting third party

```text
type Pool states { Settled } transitions { }     // a compacting pool
h = handle into the pool                         // an ordinary copyable value; not a pointer, carries no permission
focus ρP as { S = .slot(h) } {                   // pointer_of's row:
  p = pointer_of(h)                              //   { requires a carve entry naming .slot(h) ; result: ptr into S }
                                                 // accept: p's name is FINE — it exists only inside this window
  pool.compact()                                 // REJECT: compact's row is { ρP: Settled⇒Settled @E, relocates all }
                                                 //   and it REQUIRES carves(ρP) empty (§2.5, the relocating-move rule).
                                                 //   M7 payload: "the window opened at L3 names .slot(h); close it
                                                 //   before compacting, or use the handle form"
}
pool.compact()                                   // accept here: carves(ρP) is empty
read(p)                                          // REJECT at formation, not here: p is a fine name and may not escape
                                                 //   its window. There is no way to write this line at all
read(pool[h])                                    // accept: the handle is an ordinary value; `pool[h]` re-forms a
                                                 //   pointer inside a FRESH window after the compaction
```

**Verdict: accepted as required — and the window *is* the "contract-visible
fixup form" R8a demands.** R8a says an interior pointer into storage a
non-program actor may relocate is refused unless a fixup form exists. Here an
interior pointer is a window-scoped name by construction and a relocating
operation's row demands an empty window stack, so the mutual exclusion is
structural rather than a rule that must be stated and remembered. Price paid
willingly: the compiler relocates no storage while a window naming it is open.

### P16 Abstraction over identities

```text
fn map_nodes<T, ρ>(g: ptr<ρ, Pool<Node<T>>>, f: fn(&ro T) -> T row { @R })
  row { ρ : Init ⇒ Init @E }                     // ONE store parameter, ONE grade. The default carve of
                                                 //   Pool<Node<T>> is computed from the INSTANTIATED type, so every
                                                 //   instance gets the element partition (R15: facts cross the boundary)
{ par_for k in g.live { set elem(k).data = f(&ro elem(k).data) } }
                                                 // accept: dis by the element partition at every instance;
                                                 //   f's row is @R, so it adds no write to the footprint

fn kernel<E>(c: ptr<ρ, Cols<E>>) row { ρ : Init ⇒ Init @E }
                                                 // accept: the default carve names eight columns at every instance
                                                 //   of E. Eight per-load facts cost ONE interface parameter

let h = |slice : ptr<σ, buffer<u8>>| helper(slice, input)
                                                 // the closure's row is its body's row, with the CAPTURE as a row entry:
                                                 //   { σ: Uninit⇒Init @E ; τ: Init⇒Init @R }   (τ = input's store)
P6 with h                                        // accept: the caller reads h's row exactly as it read helper's;
                                                 //   iteration overlap by the same extent algebra

fn pick<N: Nominal>(c: bool, x: N, y: N) -> N
  row { stores(N)@x : Init⇒Init @R ; stores(N)@y : Init⇒Init @R ; result : origin ∈ {x, y} }
                                                 // accept: N's store parameters are N's own; the origin set is finite
                                                 //   and independent of N. Instantiation is decidable by the fixed rule
```

R15's metric — *parameters per interface ≤ a stated function of the storages
the callee touches* — is met with the function being **the identity on coarse
storages**: P5 generic over the column type costs one parameter, not eight,
because fine names are not interface vocabulary. That is the whole point of
D1's two levels. **Verdict: accepted as required.** Cost: one row entry per
captured store on a closure.

### P17 Partial operations

```text
q = a / d                                        // accept iff `d != 0` is discharged: a prior branch's condition, an
                                                 //   `ensures` on d's producer, or a written `use` step.
                                                 //   Else REJECT: M7 names "d != 0" at the operand's tree location
                                                 //   (R11; never repaired with an executable fallback)
q = match checked_div(a,d) { Ok(q)=>q | DivZero=>… }
                                                 // accept: a written typed outcome (R12), each arm discharging R2
b : u8 = narrow(x)                               // accept iff x < 256 proved; else REJECT naming "x < 256",
                                                 //   or the writer writes the two-armed form
y = v[i]                                         // accept iff i < len_of(backing(ρ)); len_of is a measure fact
                                                 //   supported by the descriptor (MSR-2, HIS-D3-18)
focus β as { A = β[i] } { … }                    // the carve obligation i < len_of(β) is the SAME obligation, in the
                                                 //   same vocabulary, discharged by the same family — the writer
                                                 //   learns one discharge form for domains and for carves
```

**Verdict: accepted as required.** D1–D4 neither add to nor take from R11; the
one interaction worth stating is that carve obligations reuse R11's obligation
vocabulary, so the taught surface does not grow a second proof idiom (M8).

## 4. Requirements

### 4.1 R rows

| Row | Verdict | Reason (one sentence) |
|---|---|---|
| **R1** Sequential memory safety | **met** | State is per coarse name with a per-window projection onto carve entries; (i) is the hole read (P7, P3), (ii) is `Gone`, which address reuse never revives (P2), (iii) is the layout automaton's state, and every access checks the named storage's state at that point. |
| **R2** Resource lifecycle accounting | **met** | Owners are affine bindings, every ending event is a row clause, joins demand equal states so definiteness is structural, and outcome arms carry their own exit states (P2, P8b). |
| **R3** Value classes and transfer | **met** | Classes stay type-level and unchanged; take/put/replace/move are four row clauses on the destination storage, and the multiplicity lemma stays separate from the state lemma (P7). |
| **R4** Licensed facts for the backend | **met** | Distinctness is a partition relation over a containment forest, never name inequality (`ρ1 ⊑ ρS` in P2), and every fact the lowering uses is a carve entry that existed in the checked program, so no emission-time re-derivation is required. |
| **R5** Data-race freedom and permitted overlap | **partial** | Ground (i) is supplied exactly and cheaply (P1, P3, P5, P6, P2), and a missing fact leaves an erasable construct sequential; grounds (ii) (the checked-law channel) and (iii) (the named level set) are R14/D5 vocabulary this tuple neither supplies nor obstructs. |
| **R6** Frame: proof-fact retention | **partial** | Inside a window a kill is confined to the carve entries a row names — which removes the measured tax (an element write does not name `len`, a column write does not name a sibling column, so 34-of-41 `len()` rebinds go away) — but a row entry with no carve kills its whole coarse name, and a runtime-indexed transition (P3's `remove(h)`, P11's `get(k)`) kills every sibling entry. |
| **R7** Compositional call judgement | **met** | The row *is* the interface, and it states exactly R7(b)'s list: entry and exit states per identity, footprints with grades, carves, existential fresh results, finite origin sets and outcome arms; the callee is checked once against it (P9, P6). |
| **R8a** Storage-ending and relocation events | **met** | Every ending or relocating event is a row clause requiring an empty window stack over the storage it moves, which makes the set complete and contract-visible and makes the interior-pointer rule structural (P13, P4, P2, P3). |
| **R8b** Placement and physical demands | **partial** | The tuple neither supplies nor blocks a demand vocabulary; the one synergy is that a column carve entry and a layout unit are the same object, so an `align(64)` demand on a column has a name to attach to. |
| **R9** Shared mutation among several holders | **met** | Outside a window the policy is permissive: several long-lived writable pointers to one storage are ordinary, the hazard is R1's alone, and facts weaken only for the storages the writer let coincide (P3's four link writes, P7's two aliases). The concurrent half waits on R14(i)'s trigger. |
| **R10** External resources as ordinary objects | **met** | A descriptor is three coarse names (close-obligation wrapper, description with cursor, foreign contents) each with a declared automaton — the same construct memory uses — so the acceptance relation has no premise mentioning a host crossing. |
| **R11** Partial operations and overflow | **met** | Unchanged from today, and carve obligations reuse the same domain-discharge vocabulary rather than adding a second one (P17). |
| **R12** Failure paths and typed outcomes | **met** | Outcome arms are row clauses with their own exit states; the equality join makes each arm discharge its own obligations, and this candidate leans on outcomes as its join mechanism (P8b). |
| **R13** Resource bounds where demanded | **partial** | The row is the natural carrier for a declared budget (`allocates(ρA) ≤ B`) and for a depth count, and the tuple obstructs neither, but it supplies no cost semantics and no termination measure. |
| **R14** Stated execution model and external conditions | **partial** | (iii) and (iv) have a home — a foreign-writable identity is a coarse name whose automaton has a device-owned state and whose contents facts are killed by any edge the agent could interleave (P12's shape) — while (i), (ii), (v) and (vi) are untouched. |
| **R15** Abstraction | **met** | Coarse names are ordinary type parameters, the default carve is a function of the instantiated type, and a closure's captures are row entries; P16's parameter metric is met with the identity function on coarse storages. |

### 4.2 M rows

| Row | Verdict | Reason (one sentence) |
|---|---|---|
| **M1** Specified deterministic acceptance | **met** | Acceptance is one syntax-directed pass composing rows, plus entailment of written rows at loop heads (initiation and consecution, not a fixpoint), plus the existing fixed affine family for carve obligations — no search, no budget, no widening, no solver state. |
| **M2** No unstated failure edge, no unchosen cost | **met** | Nothing in the model exists at run time: no drop flag (P8's join is a state-equality check), no generation, no pin count (a "pin" is an open window in the checker), no occupancy structure the compiler maintains; grades and carves lower to metadata only. |
| **M3** Enumerated, writer-closed trusted base | **met** | No new axiom and no writer-reachable escape: a declared automaton is checked against its transitions like any other rule, and `alias ρ σ` is checked, not trusted. |
| **M4** Writer regularity | **partial** | One construct carves, spelled once and appearing at the three places a row already exists (arrow, `focus` head, loop head) — but the identity vocabulary has two name kinds, which is the cost AI-D1-11's own tension line names, and the aliasing rule has a stated scope (inside a carve's extent) that a reader must hold. |
| **M5** Acceptance independent of permission | **met** | No PAR judgment is an input to acceptance: deleting the overlap judgment changes no verdict, and a missing fact at an erasable construct yields the sequential program. |
| **M6** Soundness evidence | **partial** | The bounded small-model check is unusually cheap here — states are finite, windows are syntactically balanced, and a window's model is bounded by its carve arity rather than by the function — but the operational semantics and the adequacy theorem remain the later obligation of owner decision 9. |
| **M7** Repairable rejection | **met** | Every rejection is one of four shapes, each with a tree location and a named fact: a state mismatch (both edges named), a missing carve obligation (the inequality named), a carved-extent access (the entry, the window head and three repairs named), or a non-empty window stack at an ending event (the window head named). |
| **M8** Teaching and retrieval budget | **partial** | The taught surface adds the row grammar, the four grades, the carve-entry grammar and the automaton construct — on the order of 4–5k tokens — and removes borrow modes, loans, reborrows, suspension rules and region containment; fine names cost nothing to retrieve because they never appear in a signature, but the total is an addition against a budget already red. |
| **M9** Measured performance floor | **partial** | The testable claim is strong and unmeasured: the default carve makes P5's and P6's obvious shapes carry per-load facts at zero extra tokens, and the facts are the exact LLVM forms the retired prototype had to manufacture at emission. |
| **M10** Checking cost, scaling and edit stability | **met** | Row composition is linear in statements; a carve's disjointness is *by construction of a partition*, so k entries cost O(k) rather than O(k²) pairwise proofs; and edit stability is bounded more tightly than the interface, because a fine name cannot escape its window, so an edit inside a window cannot change a verdict outside it. |
| **M11** Evolution with stated loss | **met** | The verdict diff is computable over the retained corpus and a mechanical migration exists in the direction that matters: today's `&uniq 'r p` is `ρ @E` with the default carve, today's `region` block is `focus`, and the retired prototype's per-field `!alias.scope` is the default carve's emission. |

**Counts: 18 met, 9 partial, 0 violated.** M1 and M2 are satisfied, not
declared violated; the members of the chosen families that would have violated
M2 (a runtime pin count in SYS-D3-03, SYS-D4-09's dynamic fallback, THE-D3-08's
gradual half) are refused by name in §1.

### 4.3 The price this candidate charges the compiler

| Charged to | Price |
|---|---|
| Backend | no storage may be relocated while a window naming it is open (no moving collector, no address-changing copy inside a `focus`); a `noalias` scope must be duplicated when a loop carrying it is unrolled; a marked `initializes` extent must be honored |
| Checker | a window stack per coarse name; a partition-checking pass per carve head (one pass over the entries, using the existing affine family); row composition and projection at every call (EFF-2's projection already exists); an automaton table per nominal |
| Emitter | one `!alias.scope` per carve entry per window, one `noalias.scope.decl` per window head, `noalias`/`readonly`/`writeonly`/`initializes`/`memory(...)` derived mechanically from grades — and *no* re-derivation of identity from resolved places at emission |
| Lowering | nothing else: grades, carves, rows, states and proofs are erased |

### 4.4 The writer's cost

| Per | Tokens | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| **signature** | one line per coarse identity touched | `ρ : pre ⇒ post @g`; a `carve` clause only where the default is too coarse; an `alias` or `requires` where the callee needs one |
| **struct** | one store parameter per stored pointer | `struct Cursor<ρ> { at: ptr<ρ,V>, … }` |
| **nominal with a protocol** | one `states`/`transitions` block | descriptors, pools, DMA buffers; nothing for ordinary types |
| **loop** | zero in the common case | a head row only when the body's row is not the identity (none of P1, P5, P6, P8, P3 needs one) |
| **join** | zero | arms agree, or the writer writes the survivor as a value (P8b: one `let`) |
| **statement** | one `focus` line where a runtime-indexed split is wanted | P1 only, among the derived programs |
| **call site** | one `alias ρ σ` per coinciding pair; one proof step per carve obligation the fixed family cannot close | P1's `k != i && k != j` |

Zero of the derived programs needs a fine name written in a signature, and
P5, P6, P7, P9, P13, P16 and P17 need nothing beyond the row lines R7 already
demands.

## 5. Consequences at D5–D13

| DP | Forced | Foreclosed |
|---|---|---|
| **D5** interference source | The source of an interference fact is **the carve plus the row**: a partition's entries are disjoint by construction and a row's grades say who touches what. An affine arithmetic fragment is required for extent and element entries (the existing OP-4 / PAR-2 family suffices for every derived program). | Whole-program points-to as the fact source (nothing to attach it to, and M1 would then depend on analysis precision); parameter-position-only facts (they cannot name a loaded column, EVIDENCE §B.2); a schedule or tile language inside the identity. |
| **D6** distinctness default | **Distinct-by-default coarse names with call-site discharge** (C3), with **declared coincidence** (`alias ρ σ`) as the only escape and the containment forest as the qualifier. C3's hardest clause — *"sub-identities included"* — is discharged structurally: sub-identities are fine names, and fine names never cross a call, so no call site ever discharges one. | A may-alias default; inequality-of-names as distinctness; whole-program re-derivation of distinctness. |
| **D7** contract vocabulary | **The row is the contract**, in one grammar: per coarse identity a pre-state, a post-state, a grade, an optional carve; plus fresh results, finite origin sets, outcomes, and later ordering edges. | A separate footprint language beside the effect row; borrow modes on parameters; loan annotations independent of the row (C14's loan channel is absorbed: `@E` *is* the loan, and it is the row's, so PAR-1's second channel disappears). |
| **D8** relocation and moves | Every relocating operation's row carries **"requires no open window over this storage"**; `Pinned` is a checker predicate ("a window is open"), never a runtime count. Promotion (`fresh ∃ρ' ⊑ ρ`) is the split form, windows are the scoped form: one carve algebra, two dispositions. | A moving collector; a relocating copy inside a `focus`; interior pointers surviving a relocation without a fixup (R8a's price, taken willingly). |
| **D9** containers and backings | A container's backing is a **carve entry of its coarse store** (the column/plane shape), `push`/`reserve` are two-armed row clauses, and a run's initialized region is a declared sequence automaton (`len_of`/`head_of`/`cap_of` with descriptor support). | Element identity in signatures; a universal occupancy bitmap; per-element compiler state for a runtime-indexed pool (P3's cost). |
| **D10** concurrency | Strongly prepared: a **lock is a window** whose carve is the protected storage and whose open and close are acquire and release, which is exactly R9(b)'s question ("which primitive holds the storage's state facts while no thread holds them") answered by the carve's state. Ordering edges become row entries; a spawn's non-erasable rejection reads the same `dis` relation. C11's problem reappears in a named form: two windows on one carve do not nest. | Ambient per-thread permission; interior mutability as a mode; a runtime exclusivity check at a module boundary. |
| **D11** external resources | The most natural extension: a descriptor is three coarse names with declared automata (P14), a DMA loan is a **window whose closer is the observed completion event** (P12), and a foreign-writable identity is a coarse name in R14(iv)'s access class whose contents facts die at every edge the agent could interleave. | A compiler-special I/O path; host-mechanism categories in the type system. |
| **D12** surface form | `row { … }` on every declaration; `focus ρ as { … } { … }`; `@0/@R/@W/@E`; `&ro`; `alias ρ σ`; `states`/`transitions` on a nominal. Every carve name is written at its window head, so M7 always has a tree location to point at. | Elision sugar that hides which name is carved or which grade is claimed (M7 would lose its anchor); a second spelling for "exclusive" beside `@E`. |
| **D13** validation and migration | The acceptance-relevant unit is a window, so M6(i)'s bounded model is **per window** and bounded by its carve arity rather than by a function's size — the cheapest validation target of any unit in this space. Migration is mechanical in the load-bearing direction: `&uniq 'r p` → `ρ @E`, `&'r p` → `&ro`/`@R`, `region` block → `focus`, the retired prototype's per-field scopes → the default carve. | A gradual-typing boundary between checked and unchecked units (M2 forbids the check that boundary would need). |

---

## 6. Honest weaknesses, and the strongest objection

### 6.1 Weaknesses, stated without hedging

| # | Weakness | How far it can be answered |
|---|---|---|
| W1 | **Two name kinds.** AI-D1-11's own tension line is exactly right: *"One vocabulary at cut points and another in bodies doubles the spec-side vocabulary M4 pays for; weak spot: mixing the levels."* | Partly. The spelling is not doubled — one `row`, one `carve` grammar — but a reader must know that a carve entry cannot be written in a type. The compiler can make the mistake unmissable: the parser rejects a carve entry in type position with a fixed message. M4 is graded **partial**, not met. |
| W2 | **A fine name cannot escape its window.** A function cannot return `&mut v[i]`. An iterator yielding element references, a `get_mut`, a `split_at_mut` returning two halves across a call boundary: none is writable. | Stated loss. The writer returns an index, or the caller passes a closure whose row names the entry (P16's closure form), or the operation becomes a `focus` at the call site (P1). This is a real expressiveness cost and it is the price of keeping fine names out of signatures. |
| W3 | **Runtime-indexed occupancy kills coarsely.** `remove(h)` with a runtime `h` kills `Occupied(k)` for every `k` (P3), and `get(k2)` with an unrelated runtime key kills `Filled(k1)` (P11). | Partly. The re-discharge is one entailment step against an invariant stated once, and a captured symbolic index recovers precision where the writer reuses the same value (HIS-D1-23). R6 is graded **partial** for exactly this. |
| W4 | **Adding a `focus` can reject a program that was accepted without it.** The writer pays for a fact with a rejection risk. | Largely answered by the **totality rule** (§2.6): a total carve — which is every default carve, hence every field and column split — cannot reject anything, because an access to the parent is an access to the union of the entries. Only a *partial* carve (an extent or an element split) can reject, and that is exactly the case where the writer asked for a runtime-indexed partition and must say which side an index falls on. It remains true that `focus` is the one construct with this shape. |
| W5 | **P8's naive shape is rejected.** `if c { free(a) } else { free(b) }` needs a rewrite. | Conceded, with the alternative named: D3's *state as a term over captured conditions* would accept it verbatim. The trade is deliberate — an equality join has no condition atoms, so M10 has nothing data-dependent to bound and the small-model check has no term language to model. If the owner prefers the naive shape, the repair is to adopt condition terms at the join only; the rest of the tuple is unchanged by that. |
| W6 | **A call inside a window must fit one entry.** `pick(c,x,y)` cannot be called while a partial carve of `ρ` is open (P9's last line). | Necessary for soundness of the emitted scopes, and diagnosable: the row's name and the window head are both known, so M7's payload is complete. The writer closes the window or carves the callee's row. |
| W7 | **The default carve is a specification-fixed derivation.** Some readers will hear "inference". | It is a total function of a *type declaration*, not of a body; it has no budget, no order dependence and no search, so M1 holds. And it can only *add* facts: a total carve never rejects, so the derived default cannot flip a verdict from accepted to rejected. |
| W8 | **Nothing here supplies R5(ii)/(iii), R13 or most of R14.** | Stated: those are D5/D10/D11 and R14's own text. The tuple is compatible with all of them and forecloses none, but it does not deliver them, and four R rows are graded partial for that reason. |

### 6.2 The strongest objection

> **"This is Rust's borrow scope with a new name. You quoted the ladder's
> finding that borrowing refuses no hazard, and then reintroduced a lexical
> scope that rejects programs — P1's `β[k]`, the no-escape rule, the
> can't-call-across-a-carve rule. You have paid the borrow's cost and kept its
> restriction, while charging the writer an extra construct for the privilege."**

Three answers, in order of force.

**(a) Safety never consults a window.** Delete every window from the language
and the refusals in P2, P3, P4, P7, P9 and P13's first arm land on the same
lines with the same diagnostics, because each is a *state* fact: `Gone`,
`Uninit`, a row's exit state. Not one memory-safety rejection in §3 reads
`carves`. The rule in §2.6 rejects in exactly one situation: the source opened
a partition of one storage and then reached into the partitioned part without
saying which part it meant. Meanwhile the programs a borrow system refuses —
`push` while a cursor exists (P4), four link writes through several paths to
one node (P3), a hole made through `p` and filled through `q` (P7) — are all
accepted here, because a pointer carries no permission and no duration. A
borrow restricts what a *value* may do; this restricts what a *fact's scope*
may contain.

**(b) The scope is the fact's scope, and that is not a choice — it is the shape
of the fact.** LLVM defines `!alias.scope` as valid where its
`noalias.scope.decl` is declared, and says in as many words that the decl
*"must also be duplicated"* when a loop unrolls, *"otherwise the noalias
property it signifies would spill across loop iterations, whereas it was only
valid within a single iteration."* P1's two parts and P6's k slices are facts
about a span, not lifetimes of two references. A design that attaches those
facts to values must re-derive the span at emission — which is exactly what the
retired prototype did, manufacturing a scope from a resolved place on the fly —
and R4's price forbids *requiring* re-derivation to reach a stated fact. Making
the source-level name window-scoped is what makes the source fact and the
backend fact the same object.

**(c) It is opt-in, priced per window, and the default costs nothing.** A
program that writes no `focus` and claims no `@E` is checked entirely under the
permissive policy: unrestricted aliasing, safety from per-storage state, the
ladder's Step 0. It is fully memory-safe and carries fewer facts. A program
that writes `@E` on a signature gets the total default carve, which cannot
reject. Only a *partial* carve — a runtime-indexed split, the one case where a
human or a model must think anyway — can reject, and the diagnostic names the
index inequality it wants. Rust has no such dial: exclusivity there is charged
on every reference whether a fact is wanted or not.

**A second objection worth pre-empting: "a partition-by-construction assumes
the partition is decidable."** The carve grammar is closed and every entry's
obligation is discharged by the existing fixed affine family. A carve the
family cannot decide is *rejected at the window head*, with the missing
inequality named — never accepted on faith, and never searched for (M1, M7).
The failure mode is a diagnostic at a written line, which is the failure mode
M7 is written to demand.

**A third: "grades are a second permission system beside states."** They are
not: a grade says what an operation *does* to a name for the row's scope, a
state says what the storage *is* at a program point. They are never two
spellings of one fact — C13's ruling (modes retired instead of refined) is
honored, because the grade lives on the row and not on any pointer, and there
is no pointer in this language that carries a mode.


# File: critique-brand-context-cost.md

# Critique of `brand-context` — lens COST, DETERMINISM AND THE WRITER

Refuter lens: M1 (fixed terminating procedure, no search/budget/solver), M10
(checking cost as a degree in program size and written steps; does a one-token
edit reopen distant verdicts), M7 (locally repairable rejection), M8 (spec
tokens; count the constructs), M9 (obvious shape of P5/P6; surviving backend
facts), R15 (generics, closures, nominals in P16, or signature explosion).

Target: [`candidate-brand-context.md`](candidate-brand-context.md), 2026-09-16.
Tuple under test: D1 allocation-scoped location name (+ paths, element indices,
ranges, origin sets) × D2 implicit checker context × D3 three states refined by
`ite` terms over captured conditions × D4 unrestricted aliasing, safety from
per-storage state.

Evidence used, by path:

- `research/experiments/proof-use-cost/baseline-2026-09-14.tsv` — `growing`
  family 31,013 → 169,404 → 1,693,329 µs at N = 16/32/64 for 1452 → 2812 →
  5532 source bytes (fitted exponent ≈ 2.6–3.4); `control` 18,338 → 41,039 →
  166,826 µs. This is the curve `VERDICT-D0.md` M10(e) calls **red**, measured
  on today's mechanism, which has *no* state-term machinery at all.
- `research/experiments/blind-writer/2026-08-28/REPORT.md` — §0: "Zero `claim`
  statements were needed in any of the five programs. Every partial operation …
  was discharged by ordinary `if` branches and by `len()` rebinding."
  §6.2(1): **34 of 41** `let … = len(…)` bindings exist only to re-establish a
  fact a preceding call killed under `ENT-5`. §6.2(2): **120 `region` blocks**
  (39/28/22/16/15). §6.3: three of six diagnostics are coordinate-only, with no
  fix payload.
- `research/experiments/scoped-alias-channel/RESULTS.md` — the *retired* channel:
  whitefoot-facts 8 vector adds / 0 guards / 121 asm lines against rust-obvious
  65 / 29 / 2132; 2.0x at n = 8, parity at n ≥ 32. Its own stated ground for the
  fact is "`buffer<T>` is affine single-owner (OWN-1/T1): two distinct live
  buffer values never overlap. `&uniq` is exclusive (OWN-2/5) and loans have
  singleton provenance (T-A)."
- `EVIDENCE-mechanism-survey-2026-09-16.md` part B, §0 — "Backend: **nothing** —
  no alias or effect metadata is emitted at all"; the only thing the current
  fact base buys the backend is PAR-1/PAR-2 overlap actualization.

## 1. Findings

Severity: **fatal** = a hazard is admitted, or a requirement is violated in a
way the candidate did not declare. **serious** = a program verdict is wrong, a
stated cost is understated, or a needed mechanism is unnamed. **minor** =
wording.

| # | Sev | Concerns | Finding | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | **fatal** | M1, M10(b), M8; P1, P3, P4, P6, P16, P17 | **The "exactly four automatic families and no fifth" claim is false by the candidate's own derivations, and M1 is scored *met* on that count.** §4.1's M1 row and §4.2's price line fix the family set at: path normalization/equality; containment/overlap over paths; half-open affine interval disjointness; state-term evaluation and join. At least four more judgments are exercised and none is named, specified, or bounded. (i) **Atom entailment.** P1's `use k != i` "discharges the term to `Init`"; P4's `reserve` then `push` accepts because "the atom `len0 < cap0` discharges"; P17's `use i < len(v)` discharges a subscript. Deciding whether an assumption set (branch guards + `requires` + `use` steps) entails an atom occurring in a term is a propositional-plus-linear-arithmetic entailment procedure. In P4 it is not even syntactic match: `reserve` is supposed to supply `cap ≥ len0+1` and `push`'s guard atom is `len0 < cap0` — two different atoms related by integer arithmetic. (ii) **Quantifier instantiation.** P3's `inv_links` is `forall s. st('P[s]) = Init ==> …`, and P16's `map_nodes` has `reads forall s. 'P[s].data`. Discharging a `requires` against a universal, and framing a universal across a write, is instantiation, not path normalization. (iii) **Symbolic-coefficient interval arithmetic** — see F4. M1(b) requires "each family as a decision procedure with a stated bound"; M10(b) requires "the bound per family". Neither is supplied for any of the four, and their absence is not declared. | Enumerate the real family set — atom entailment over a fixed atom grammar, quantifier instantiation under a fixed trigger rule, interval arithmetic with the monotonicity lemma, and the kill scan — state each one's decision procedure and degree, and re-score M1 and M10 against the enlarged set. |

The blind-writer trial is the measured confirmation of which horn is real: a writer with no exposure discharged **every** partial operation in five programs with "ordinary `if` branches and `len()` rebinding" and wrote **zero** claims. | Define what a `use` step is — a named finite rule application with premises the checker checks — say that a disequality on two runtime scalars has no such rule, delete the `use` routes from P1 and P17, and re-price §4.3 as "one writer branch plus one outcome arm per unproved domain". |

M7 is scored **met**. The measured precedent is blind-writer §6.3: three of six diagnostics carry only a coordinate and those are the ones that cost the writer time. | Extend the payload to name the killing operation and the support binding, add "bind the guard before the write" to the taught routes, and re-score M7. |
| S8 | serious | M9, R4; P5 | **M9's "the obvious shape is the fast shape" rests on a fact source this tuple deletes and on a D12 rule it does not make.** The only measured alias-fact evidence in the repository is `scoped-alias-channel/RESULTS.md`, and its stated ground is affine single-owner `buffer<T>` plus `&uniq` exclusivity — D4 deletes exclusivity and D2 deletes per-reference permission, so the fact now comes entirely from the writer having written eight distinct identity parameters. §6.2 concedes that D12 elision "stops being optional and becomes load-bearing" and that this tuple does not decide it; but the M9 verdict and P5's derivation both assume the specific elision rule "the writer types `Cols<E>`; the checker holds eight names", i.e. elision mints a *fresh distinct* name per pointer-carrying field. Any other elision default (one shared name, or "write them or lose them") either loses the facts silently or reinstates eight annotations — and the row where M9 is measured is exactly this one.
