| S10 | serious | Price #3; M10 edit stability; R8b; R15 | "A handle's `gen` field exists in the layout **iff** some `open` consumes it" is a whole-program property of data layout. One `open` token added in one function changes `sizeof(H<P>)` for every handle in the program, hence the layout of every struct containing one (P3's `Node`, P4's `Cursor`), hence what a foreign boundary sees (R8b), hence every generic instantiation (R15's "checked once for all instances"). The lens's question — does a one-token edit reopen distant verdicts — has its worst answer here. It is vacuous in Tier A, where no `open` exists, but it is stated as a general rule of the model. | Either fix `H<P>`'s layout unconditionally, or make the `gen` field a declared property of the pool type (a local, writer-visible choice) rather than a whole-program erasure inference. |
| S11 | serious | R10, R12, R13 declared **met**; R15 **partial** | Each of these rows' acceptance test (e) names a program the candidate does not derive: R13 → P18 and P19, R12 → P18 and P14's short-read arm, R10 → P14's three identities with `dup` sharing one description. §0 of the requirement list marks a row whose (e) names only pending programs as **provisional**; answering it "met" by assertion is exactly what the ground rules forbid ("nothing is ranked by assertion"). The candidate derives 13 programs (P1–P9, P11, P13, P16, P17); P10 is legitimately deferred, but P12, P14, P15, P18 and P19 are not derived at all. | Downgrade R10, R12 and R13 to **partial (test not derived)** and derive P18 and P14, the two whose shapes the model directly touches. |
| m1 | minor | wording | The headline says "all fourteen derived programs are decided in Tier A"; thirteen are derived. | Say thirteen, and list the six undecided programs by name. |
| m2 | minor | M4; Price #3 | `open` (Tier B's generational match) and `open_window` (Tier A's relocation-suspension scope) are two different constructs sharing a stem, and Price #3's "some `open` in the program" is ambiguous between them. | Rename the Tier A construct (`pin_window`, `no_reloc`) so the erasure rule names one construct. |
| m3 | minor | §2.5 vs §6.4 | §2.5 says arms are "collapsed when equal"; collapsing two arms with one state and two conditions is a disjunction, which §6.4's "no disjunctive normal form is built" denies. | State that arms with equal states are kept as separate list entries and that "collapsed" means dropped-when-subsumed. |

Revised row tally, applying the findings above: R4 fatal-not-met (F1), R10/R12/R13 partial-not-met (S11), M1 violated-undeclared (F2, F3), M4 partial (S5), M7 partial (S7), M10 violated (S9), plus the declared M2 violation. **12 met, 12 partial, 3 violated** against the candidate's 18 / 8 / 1.

---

## 2. Program verdicts overturned

Each entry gives the candidate's verdict, my verdict, and the derivation in
the ladder's accept/reject style.

### P5 — overturned: "accepted as required, charges this program nothing, the obvious shape is the fast shape"

My verdict: **accepted, but the R4 facts are not established, silently**; with
them established the program costs a 28-fact written invariant and a
construction proof. The obvious shape is the *slow* shape.

```text
struct Cols { a,b,c,d,e,f,g,h : buffer<u64> }
  // §2.1: every container has backing('c.a) = 'b_a, backing('c.c) = 'b_c, …
  // D4 base stance: unrestricted aliasing; D1 refuses HIS-D4-01 (OWN-5); OWN-1
  //   affinity is not among the adopted members either
let shared = buffer<u64>(n)
c = Cols { a: shared, b: …, c: shared, d: …, e: …, f: …, g: …, h: … }
  // accept: nothing in D1–D4 refuses it.  backing('c.a) = backing('c.c) = 'b_shared
for i in 0..n {
  a[i] = f(a[i], c[i], d[i])
    // candidate's comment: "distinct('c.a[i], 'c.c[i]) by the containment structure"
    // REJECT THE FACT: 'c.a and 'c.c are distinct FIELD places holding two
    //   backing identities; the containment structure relates the fields to 'c,
    //   not the backings to each other.  Deriving distinct(backing('c.a),
    //   backing('c.c)) from a != c is exactly "inequality of identity names",
    //   which R4(b) refuses by name and which the P2 negative test (S(A) vs b1)
    //   is the standing counterexample to.
    // consequence 1 (soundness, F1): if the fact is emitted anyway it is false
    //   in the execution above -> R4(a) breached, M6(iii) breached.
    // consequence 2 (cost, the one that actually bites): if it is NOT emitted,
    //   M5 leaves the program sequential and accepted.  No diagnostic exists
    //   (R4 tolerates a missing "distinct"), so the writer sees a green build.
  b[i] = g(b[i], e[i], f[i], g[i], h[i])   // same, 15 more pairs
}
```

Repair and its price:

```text
struct Cols { … } invariant ICols: pairwise-disjoint(backing(a) … backing(h))
  // 28 pairs for 8 columns: O(f^2) in field count, not "steps are free"
Cols::new(...) -> Cols requires the 28 disjointness premises   // discharged at construction
fn kernel<'c,E>(c: &Cols<'c,E>) where ICols<'c>                // one more interface bound
```

So P5's writer cost is not `1 identity parameter + 1 footprint row + 0 + 0`.
It is `1 identity + 8 footprint entries + 1 invariant bound`, against a
once-per-type invariant with 28 conjuncts. The measured channel that made this
program interesting (`scoped-alias-channel`: 8 vector adds, 0 guards, 121 asm
lines, 2.0x at n=8) derived those 28 facts for free from OWN-1 affinity; this
tuple deletes that derivation and charges the writer for the result (S6).

### P6 — overturned: "accepted as required" with 0 written clauses

My verdict: **accepted with three written items**, not zero.

```text
out: buffer<u8> of n in 'o ; k workers ; s = n / k
  // accept: s is defined only under k > 0 -- the candidate concedes this premise
  //   is written, which already contradicts its own "per loop: 0 clauses" row
for w in 0..k {
  helper(view(out, w*s .. (w+1)*s), input)
    // accept extent formation:  w*s <= (w+1)*s     from s >= 0     -- affine in w
    // REJECT the in-bounds side condition as claimed:
    //   (w+1)*s <= n  needs  k*s <= n  needs  k*(n/k) <= n
    //   `n/k` is integer division of two runtime values.  Under the stated
    //   family ("normalise both extents to (base + coeff*w, length) and
    //   compare"), s is an opaque symbol; k*s and n are two unrelated symbols
    //   and no affine normal form relates them.  The fact is a division lemma.
    //   missing fact: k*(n/k) <= n   (M7 payload)   repair: one written `use`
    //   step, or `requires n % k == 0`
    // REJECT the parallel overlap as claimed:
    //   iteration w writes 'o[w*s..(w+1)*s) and READS 'input.
    //   R5(a)(i) needs write/read non-interference too: distinct('o, 'input).
    //   C3 makes that distinct-by-default WITH A CALL-SITE DISCHARGE; the
    //   derivation shows no discharge, and helper's signature states none.
    //   missing fact: distinct('o, 'input)   repair: one `requires` on helper
}
```

Written cost: `k > 0` premise + one division `use` step + one `distinct`
clause on `helper`'s interface = 3, versus the claimed 0. The overlap verdict
itself survives once the third item is written; the *derivation* as printed
admits a read/write race between a worker's read of `input` and another
worker's write to `out` when the two coincide.

### P4 — overturned: "accepted as required, and strictly"

My verdict: **not derived**; the program as written does not type-check under
§2.2, and under the only typing reading it exercises none of the candidate's
machinery.

```text
c = Cursor { at: H<'v>, i: 0 }
  // reject (type): §2.2 -- "H<P> says: the pool it indexes"; 'v is a Vector
  //   identity, and no pool of vectors is declared.  §2.1 gives H<P> runtime
  //   content {idx} into P; there is no P here, so h.idx has no meaning.
// reading (a): 'v is silently a one-slot pool
  // then push(v,5) is a grow of the ELEMENT stored in that pool slot, and the
  //   "handle survives the push" claim reduces to "the pool slot survived",
  //   which is §2.4's `grow` row for any root.  The slot map, the generation
  //   and Live(P) are all unused: the candidate's own §2.8 erases every one.
// reading (b): c.at is ptr<'v, Vector> -- the header pointer
b = c.read()
  // accept: push's footprint is {'v.meta, 'v.backing}; the pointer names 'v,
  //   whose state is Init; R6 frames the pointer's validity in.
  // NO handle, NO slot, NO generation participates.  The cost note in the
  //   candidate ("two loads: backing pointer, then element") is exactly the
  //   cost of an ordinary header pointer, which is the tell.
```

Consequence for §6.3: the rebuttal to "this is not really a generational
candidate" rests on three counts, of which count 1 ("P4's cursor stores the
identity in data") is now carried by an ordinary pointer. Count 2 (reuse) and
count 3 (P13's fixup) stand.

### P2 — overturned in scope: "accepted with a stated cost (one written pool invariant)"

My verdict: **the straight-line shape is accepted at the stated cost; the loop
shape of the same program has no stated termination for the checker and no
charged discharge for R2.**

```text
// straight-line form: as the candidate derives it.  Accepted.  IA is the cost.

// loop form -- the shape any real arena program has, and P18's shape:
for i in 0..n {
  b = alloc(A, 64)
    // §2.4: fresh ghost sigma_i not in Live(A); Live(A) ∪= {sigma_i}
    // §2.5 loop-head rule: (a) no PLACE's state is left changed by the body
    //   (each new place is fresh), (b) the body frees into no pool.
    //   -> ZERO invariant clauses are demanded.
    // reject the M1 claim: Live(A) grows by one fresh element per iteration.
    //   The ghost domain {Live(A), gen(A[.]), the existential backing names}
    //   has no finite lattice height (§2.4 rule 2 makes Gen a symbolic
    //   successor term "unbounded, so no wraparound"), and no widening is
    //   stated anywhere in §2.5.  M1(a) demands "a fixpoint terminates by
    //   lattice height, never by an iteration cap".  Neither is available.
  fill(b)
  if i % 2 == 0 { free(A, b) }     // gen(A[sigma_i]) := succ(gamma_i)
}
end of A
  // requires Live(A) = {} .  After the loop, Live(A) = { sigma_i : i odd }.
  // reject: the residual set is symbolic and unbounded; discharging it needs a
  //   written counting invariant over the loop.  §4.3's writer-cost table
  //   charges 0 clauses for this loop.  R2 is claimed "met" on the
  //   straight-line form only.
```

Fix: §2.5 gains a third loop-head trigger — "each pool whose `Live` or `gen`
the body changes" — and §4.3 charges it. That trigger is what makes the
candidate's `alloc`-in-a-loop terminate and what makes R2's leak check
dischargeable; it also raises P2's and P18's writer cost above the figure in
the table.

### P1 — overturned in ground: "accepted as required", 1 written premise

My verdict: **accepted, but on a family the candidate did not name**; the
premise count is right and the family count is not.

```text
(part_i, part_j) = take2(v, i, j)        // accept, as derived: i<n, j<n, i!=j
  // effect: state('b[i]) := Uninit ; state('b[j]) := Uninit
  // the STATE MODEL is per place.  'b[i] with symbolic i is one place per
  //   symbolic index expression, so "all the other elements are still Init"
  //   is a quantified fact: forall m < n. m != i && m != j -> state('b[m]) = Init
put2(part_i, part_j)                     // accept: the two places return to Init
push(v, x)
  // candidate: "requires state('b[i]) = Init for all i<n -- both back"
  // reject the FAMILY: discharging a universal over a symbolic range, after two
  //   symbolic-index holes were punched and refilled, is the array/quantifier
  //   domain.  None of the four families in §4.1's M1 row covers it:
  //   - literal-conjunction entailment decides path conditions, not universals
  //   - affine normalisation compares extents, it does not maintain a
  //     quantified state map
  //   - the lattice-height fixpoint is over the state term, whose height claim
  //     F3 already refuses
  //   - syntactic instantiation verifies WRITTEN steps; none is written here
```

Either the family is named with its degree (and M10's ceiling applies to it —
the array domains that decide this class are not cheap), or `push` requires a
written whole-buffer `invariant`, and P1's writer cost rises from 1 premise to
1 premise + 1 invariant. The same substitution decides P5's
`state('c.a[i]) = Init`, P3's `parallel map over Live(G)` footprint
`'G[*].data`, and P11's `Array<Option<V>, N>` construction.

### P3 — overturned in cost: "one pool invariant plus two `use` steps"

My verdict: **that, plus one loop clause per live handle at every loop that
frees, plus S8's post-compaction re-proof if the pool is compacting.**

```text
loop over a worklist {
  m = pop(work) ; unlink(m) ; free(G, m)
    // §2.4 rule 1: free kills every fact `gen(G[sigma]) = gamma` whose sigma it
    //   cannot separate from sigma(m).  sigma(m) is data-derived, so it is
    //   separated from nothing: EVERY gen fact of G dies (§6.2 #3, conceded).
  h = G[sigma_x].next ; read(G[h].data)
    // reject on the second iteration: Live(h) needs gen(G[sigma(h)]) = gamma(h),
    //   killed by the free above.  Repair per §2.5: restate the liveness fact
    //   at the loop head -- ONE CLAUSE PER LIVE HANDLE, not one per pool.
}
// §4.3 charges "1 clause per pool the body frees into" = 1.
// §2.5 charges "for every handle-liveness fact the loop body uses after the
//   free" = one per cursor, per worklist element type, per stored handle.
// The two statements are inconsistent; the second is the one the kill rule
//   forces.  A three-cursor traversal pays 3, a worklist algorithm pays more.
```

### P13 — overturned in cost: "accepted as required"

My verdict: **accepted for reachability; every fact about the relocated
objects, including the pool invariant, is destroyed and the re-proof is
uncharged.**

```text
C.compact()
  // §2.4: "ends every place C[sigma].f"; Live(C) and gen survive.
read(C[h])
  // accept reachability: Live(h) framed in, as the candidate derives.
use IG                       // the pool invariant "next/prev point into Live"
  // reject: IG's support IS the set of ended places C[sigma].next/.prev.
  //   R6(a): a fact survives only if the footprint does not name its support.
  //   compact's footprint ends them all, so IG is killed by the candidate's
  //   own frame rule.  missing fact: IG after the compaction.
  //   repair: compact must carry `ensures IG` -- i.e. the built-in operation
  //   must be parameterised by the writer's declared invariant and discharge
  //   it.  That mechanism is named nowhere in §2.
x = C[h].data                // any value fact established before the compaction
  // reject: contents facts on C[sigma].data are killed identically.
```

The candidate's cost line for P13 is "one extra load per access". The true
line is "one extra load per access, plus re-proof of every pool invariant and
every contents fact after each `compact`, plus the unnamed invariant-carrying
`ensures` mechanism that makes the re-proof possible at all".

### P16 — overturned in metric: "accepted with a stated cost" (monomorphised invariants named as the only unmeasured item)

My verdict: **accepted with three costs, of which the one the candidate names
is the third largest.**

```text
fn kernel<'c, E>(c: &Cols<'c, E>)
  writes 'c.a[0..n), 'c.b[0..n)
  reads  'c.c[0..n), 'c.d[0..n), 'c.e[0..n), 'c.f[0..n), 'c.g[0..n), 'c.h[0..n)
  where  ICols<'c>                              // F1's 28-conjunct invariant bound
  // cost 1 (first-order, unstated): 8 footprint ENTRIES.  §2.7 prices "one
  //   footprint row"; R15's metric is "parameters per interface bounded by the
  //   storages the callee touches", and this interface is linear in PLACES.
  // cost 2 (first-order, unstated): the ICols bound, and O(roots^2) call-site
  //   distinctness discharges wherever two roots meet (C3).
  // cost 3 (the one the candidate names): ICols and IG are parameterised over
  //   E / T and instantiated per monomorphisation -- unmeasured, and the
  //   measured proof-use series (17 / 119 / 731 / 5500 ms at N = 16/64/128/256,
  //   exponent 2.62 -> 2.91) says written-step count is the scaling driver.

fn map_nodes<'G, T>(g: &Pool<'G, Node<T>>, f: fn(&T) -> T)  writes 'G[*].data
  // `'G[*]` is a QUANTIFIED footprint over a pool.  §2.6's interface vocabulary
  //   lists per-identity states, interior pointers, fresh allocations,
  //   read/write/end footprints, outcomes and resource effects.  A wildcard
  //   over a ghost slot set is none of these and is unnamed (F2).

let h = |slice: View<'s,u8>| helper(slice, input)
  // candidate: "the captured identity 'input is read-only in every instance,
  //   so the k instantiations remain pairwise non-interfering"
  // reject: read-only-ness of 'input gives reader/reader non-interference
  //   between the k closure bodies.  It does NOT give non-interference between
  //   instance w's READ of 'input and instance w' 's WRITE of 's_w'.
  //   missing fact: distinct('input, 'o) -- the same fact S1 finds missing in
  //   P6's non-closure form, now hidden one level deeper inside a capture set.
```

---

## 3. What survives

The findings above do not touch three things, and I record them so the
critique is not read as a rejection of the tuple:

1. **P7 and P8 are correct as derived.** Per-storage state, one kill visible
   through every alias, no drop flag, and a rejection naming the differing
   path — these fall straight out of D2/D3 and cost the writer nothing. The
   join rule's entailment is genuinely linear *given* atoms with defined
   identity, which F3 asks for at loop back edges and nowhere else.
2. **P13's shape answer is right even though its cost is wrong.** The handle
   *is* a contract-visible fixup form written by the source, which is what
   R8a demands and what a duration-shaped identity cannot supply. S8 charges
   it more; it does not refute it.
3. **The Tier A / Tier B split is honest and the concession is real.** No
   finding above depends on Tier B, and M11's verdict diff for admitting it
   ("exactly the set of programs containing an `open`") is correct.

The cost verdict, stated plainly: this tuple's writer cost is dominated not
by generations — which are free in Tier A — but by three charges the document
prices at zero. Per-aggregate backing disjointness (F1/S4), because dropping
affinity and exclusivity moved a fact that used to be structural onto the
writer's page. Quantified container state (F2), because per-place state plus
symbolic indices always ends in the array domain. And per-liveness-fact loop
clauses (S3), because a `free` with a data-derived slot kills the whole pool.
Against a proof-use series already at exponent 2.9 and rising, those three are
the M10 story, and the monomorphised pool invariant the candidate names as
"the largest unmeasured item" is the smallest of the four.


# File: critique-generational-handles-soundness.md

# Critique of candidate `generational-handles` — lens SOUNDNESS

Research date: 2026-09-16. Refuter lens: soundness and the programs. Target:
[candidate-generational-handles.md](candidate-generational-handles.md).
Scope: P1, P2, P4, P7, P9, P13 re-derived independently; hazards R1–R3, R11,
R12; M2(ii) violations hidden as a library or a typed outcome; facts used but
never sourced; couplings C1–C18 silently retuned. Every claim below is derived
against the candidate's own §2 rules, not asserted. Where the candidate's text
and its derivation disagree, the derivation is overturned in §2.

The candidate's headline concession is that Tier B violates M2(ii). That
concession is honest and is **not** what this critique is about. The finding
is that **Tier A does not stand either**: the fact Tier B checks at run time is
a fact Tier A never says who proves, and the pool machinery Tier A needs is
either compiler-maintained bookkeeping (M2(ii)) or an unenumerated trusted
entry (M3). Both are undeclared.

---

## 1. Findings

Severity: **fatal** = a hazard is admitted or a requirement is violated in a
way the candidate did not declare; **serious** = a program verdict is wrong, a
stated cost is understated, or a needed mechanism is unnamed; **minor** =
wording.

| # | Sev | Program / requirement | Finding | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | fatal | P2, P3; M2(ii), M3, D2's own refusal list | §2.4 gives `alloc` the runtime behaviour "the pool's own written free-list pop" and `free` "free-list push", while the checker applies the ghost effects `Live(P) ∪= {σ}`, `gen := succ(γ)`, `∃σ fresh`. Either these are **language primitives**, in which case the free list is bookkeeping state the compiler maintains — refused by M2(ii) by name and by the candidate's own D2 line "nothing the *compiler* maintains exists at run time" (HIS-D2-08/09 refused) — or they are **ordinary WF functions**, in which case the language needs ghost-state-mutating contracts (`Live ∪= {σ}`, `gen := succ`, slot freshness at a call) that §2.6's interface vocabulary does not contain. The candidate takes M3 "met" on the second reading and §2.4 on the first. Tier A therefore violates M2(ii) or M3, undeclared. | State which; if library, add ghost-state effects and a freshness judgment to R7's interface vocabulary and price them under M8/M10. |
| F2 | fatal | every pool program; R11, M6(iii), M2(ii) | §2.1 gives a handle `runtime {idx} + ghost {σ, γ}` and **never relates `idx` to `σ`**. §2.8 erases `σ`, `γ` and `Live`, keeping `idx`. So (i) `C[h]` lowers to an index into the pool's backing with no stated source for `idx < cap(P)` — a partial operation whose domain R11 requires be discharged, and which in Tier A is discharged by nothing; and (ii) erasure is unsound as stated, because the checked program's meaning is defined over `σ` and the lowered one over `idx`, with no theorem connecting them (M6(iii)). This is exactly the bridge Tier B's `open` checks at run time: Tier A **asserts** it. The M6 row declares only "frame soundness under generation kills" as undischarged, not this. | Add the pool's slot-map invariant `σ ∈ Live(P) ⟹ idx(h) = index_of(σ) < cap(P)` as a stated, writer-proved obligation, and state the erasure theorem over it. |
| F3 | fatal | P7; R2, R3, R10 | §2.4's `free(P, h)` requires only `Live(h)`. It does **not** require `state(P[σ(h)]) = Uninit`. P7's derivation accepts `free A` at a point where `A` is `Init` holding `new`. A linear occupant (R3: consumed exactly once) is silently leaked; an external resource occupant is leaked, and R10's verdict ("a descriptor is a handle into a descriptor pool") makes this the *normal* descriptor shape, so `free(fd_pool, h)` drops an open description with no `close`. R2 is claimed "met". | `free(P,h)` requires `state(P[σ(h)]) = Uninit`; P7 must `take` before `free A`. |
| F4 | fatal | P2; R11, R12, M2(i) | `alloc(P)` in §2.4 has **no precondition and no outcome**: "fresh ghost `σ ∉ Live(P)`". A pool of capacity `N` with `\|Live(P)\| = N` has no fresh σ. A full fixed-capacity pool is not heap exhaustion, stack exhaustion or an OS quota, so it is **not** in R14(v)'s excluded set (owner decision 5's interim (b) does not reach it). Either the checker carries an unstated counting obligation `\|Live(P)\| < N` at every `alloc` — which the candidate charges nowhere and R13 makes opt-in — or the lowered free-list pop returns garbage on an empty list (R1 hazard) or takes a failure edge absent from source (M2(i)). M2(i) is claimed to "hold everywhere" in Tier A. | Give `alloc` either a stated domain `\|Live(P)\| < cap(P)` discharged at every site, or an R12 outcome arm; price the counting fact. |
| F5 | fatal | P13; R8a, R1(a)(ii)/(iii), M3 | §2.4's `compact` row says it **"ends every place `P[σ].f`"**. P13's derivation then rejects `read(p)` *and accepts* `read(C[h])` — but `C[h]` resolves to `C[σ(h)].data`, a place the same rule just ended, and `move x`'s rule says an ended place is "never revived". The two verdicts cannot both follow. Under the rule as written R8a's demanded fixup form does not exist and P13 fails. Under the intended reading (a layout-version bump that preserves the ghost place) the candidate needs an **identity-preserving relocation primitive** that §2.4 does not have and that ordinary WF code cannot express — so M3's "no compiler-primitive pool" is false for the compacting pool, which is the candidate's flagship. | Split the event set: `relocate` (layout version bumps, ghost place and state survive, interior pointers refused under R1(a)(iii)) versus `end` (R1(a)(ii), permanent); state `relocate` as a primitive and enumerate it in M3. |
| F6 | fatal | P9; R4 soundness, R6, M6(ii) | `pick` returns `ptr<ite(c,'x,'y),T>` and the caller writes through it **without branching on `c`**. The derivation then claims "a later read of `'y` is accepted under `c` and killed under `!c`". There is no path condition: the caller wrote no branch. Either (a) the write's footprint is the may-write union `{'x,'y}` — and the claimed precision is undeliverable, or (b) the candidate retains a contents fact for `'y` across a write that may have falsified it, which is a frame under-kill: an R4(a) soundness violation (a licensed "unwritten over a span" fact that is false in some execution) and an M6(ii) failure. The candidate declares the frame obligation only "under generation kills". | Make an `ite` footprint a may-write union for kills and a must-write only under an entailed path condition; restate P9's line. |
| F7 | fatal | P3; R1(a)(ii) | The candidate never states **when a pool invariant may be assumed and when it must be re-established**. `IG` ("next/prev point into `Live`") is assumed at `h = G[σx].next` to discharge `Live(h)`, and §2.4's `free` requires only `Live(h)` — nothing requires `IG` to hold after a `free`. A program that frees `m` without unlinking therefore keeps `IG` assumable, and the next `read(G[G[σb].prev].data)` through the stale back edge is accepted: use-after-free through data-derived handles, the exact hazard R1(a)(ii) and P3's "removal invalidates every path to `m`" name. The derivation's `use IG_restore_after_remove(m)` is a writer courtesy, not a checked obligation. | Every operation in a pool's footprint discharges the pool's invariant at its exit; `free` is rejected when `IG` is not re-established. |

## 2. Program verdicts overturned

Each overturn is derived from the candidate's own §2 rules.

### P1 — candidate: "accepted as required". Overturned to: **parallel half not derived.**

```text
(part_i, part_j) = take2(v, i, j)
  // candidate effect: state('b[i]) := Uninit ; state('b[j]) := Uninit
write(part_i, x)
  // REJECT under §2.2: "a dereference of ptr<π,T> is accepted iff ... state(π) = Init".
  //   state('b[i]) is Uninit here, by the line above.  No rule in §2.4 admits a write
  //   into a hole through a pointer.  "exclusive view" is permission on a reference,
  //   which D4/C12 refuse.                                              (S1, S2)
// Only reading consistent with §2.2: take2 yields two VALUES.  Then:
write(part_i, x)            // accept, but the footprint is a LOCAL, not 'b[i]
write(part_j, y)            // accept, same
  // the two footprints are trivially disjoint; this is not P1's requirement, which is
  // that the two writes THROUGH THE PARTS overlap.  The stores to 'b[i], 'b[j] happen
  // at put2, sequentially -> R5(a)(i) overlap for P1 is NOT derived.
read(v[k])                  // reject -- but the ground is distinct('b[k],'b[i]) missing,
                            //   an R4-relation question, not a state-term entry.   (S4)
push(v, x)                  // requires a QUANTIFIED fact "state('b[i]) = Init for all i<n";
                            //   outside M1's four families.                        (S10)
```

Verdict: **accepted for the sequential half; the parallel half and the `push`
precondition are not derivable under the stated rules.**

### P2 — candidate: "accepted with a stated cost". Overturned to: **not derivable as written.**

```text
b1 = alloc(A,64)   // F4: no precondition; a full arena has no fresh sigma and no arm
free(A, b2)        // runtime column: "free-list push".  Into WHOSE bytes?
                   //   if the pool is ordinary WF code (M3 row), this write targets
                   //   S(A)[sigma2] whose state the same operation set to Gone
                   //   -> R1(a)(ii): a PROGRAM access to ended storage.
                   //   if it is a primitive, the free list is compiler-maintained
                   //   bookkeeping -> M2(ii), and D2's own HIS-D2-08/09 refusal.  (F1)
// the derivation's comment "allocator metadata written inside b2's bytes: admitted,
// R14(iii)" is WRONG: R14(iii) admits a NON-PROGRAM actor.  An in-language arena is
// a program actor.  Taking R14(iii) makes the pool a trusted entry and falsifies the
// M3 row's "adds no trusted-base entry" -- and then every Live(h) fact in Tier A
// rests on an unenumerated axiom.
b4 = alloc(A,32)   // reuses b2's bytes.  Re-establishing IA at this point needs
                   //   "free extents are disjoint from live extents", which IA does
                   //   not state and the candidate never writes.                   (S5)
fill(b1) || fill(b2) || fill(b3)
                   // overlap discharged by "IA instantiated at (sigma1,sigma2)" --
                   //   invariant instantiation is not one of R4(b)'s discharge forms
                   //   and price #4 assumes it reaches lowering.                    (S6)
p2 = old pointer into b2 ; read(p2)
                   // reject: correct, PROVIDED pointer formation records the ghost slot
                   //   step for a byte arena with runtime extents -- undefined.      (m4)
```

Verdict: **the reject of `p2` survives; the arena itself does not — P2 is
accepted only by assuming a pool the candidate's M2/M3 verdicts forbid.**

### P4 — candidate: "accepted as required, and strictly". Overturned to: **not derivable as written; and the stated mechanism is not the one doing the work.**

```text
c = Cursor { at: H<'v>, i: 0 }
  // H<'v>: 'v is a VECTOR, not a pool.  §2.1 defines Live(h) as
  //   sigma(h) in Live(P) AND gen(P[sigma(h)]) = gamma(h).  There is no Live('v),
  //   no gen, no slot.  Live(c.at) is UNDEFINED here.                        (S8)
  // Cursor stores an identity: needs struct-level identity parameters (C8),
  //   never stated; §2.7 charges parameters per signature only.              (S8)
push(v, 5)
b = c.read()
  // the derivation's ground -- "Live(c.at) is a fact about 'v, NOT about backing('v)"
  // -- is really just state('v) != Gone.  What buys P4 is NAMING THE ROOT instead of
  // the backing.  A plain ptr<'v, Vector> to the header buys it identically.
  // NO GENERATION IS INVOLVED, so §6.3's claim that the generation "discharges ...
  // P4's read-after-push with no proof of len0 < cap0" is false for P4.
free(v); c.read()      // reject: correct.
```

Verdict: **accepted only after an unstated second handle form and struct
identity parameters are supplied; the candidate's distinguishing machinery
(generation, `Live`, slot) plays no part, contrary to §6.3(1).**

### P7 — candidate: "accepted as required". Overturned on the last three lines.

```text
old = replace(p, new)   // accept: state stays Init; A now holds `new`
read(q)                 // accept: reads new
free A
  // ACCEPT under §2.4 as written (it requires only Live(h)) -- and that is the defect:
  // state(A) = Init and the slot holds `new`.  If `new` is linear, R3's "consumed
  // exactly once" is broken and R2's "released exactly once on every path" fails: the
  // value is leaked with no diagnostic.  If the pool is R10's descriptor pool, this
  // is a dropped open-file description with no close.                          (F3)
  // CORRECT verdict: reject, missing fact state(A) = Uninit.
read(p) ; read(q)       // reject: correct once the free is repaired
```

Verdict: **accepted for the take/put/replace half; `free A` must be rejected,
and the candidate's R2, R3 and R10 "met" verdicts do not survive it.**

### P9 — candidate: "accepted as required". Overturned on two lines.

```text
reserve(v, 100)
len_fact_after = len(v)
  // candidate: "accept: len fact framed in -- reserve's footprint does not name it"
  // WRONG: reserve declares `writes 'v.meta`, and len('v) lives in 'v.meta.  The
  // footprint DOES name len's support, so R6 kills it.  It survives only because
  // reserve also wrote `ensures len('v) = len0`.  The "(R6's measured tax: 0 rebinds
  // needed here)" claim is therefore false and §4.3 under-counts one ensures clause
  // per container call.                                                        (S3)
z = pick(c, px, py) ; write(z, 1)
  // candidate: "footprint { ite(c,'x,'y) } ; under path condition c it is 'x" and
  // "a later read of 'y is accepted under `c` and killed under `!c`".
  // THE CALLER WROTE NO BRANCH ON c.  There is no path condition.  So either the
  // footprint is the may-write union {'x,'y} (and the claimed precision is not
  // delivered), or a contents fact for 'y is retained across a write that may have
  // falsified it -- a frame under-kill, R4(a) soundness and M6(ii).            (F6)
  // Also: `cap0 < m` in reserve's `ends ... when` clause is an atom from a CONTRACT,
  // not from a branch the writer wrote, contradicting §6.4.                    (S4)
```

Verdict: **accepted for `drain`; `reserve`'s framing ground and `pick`'s
precision claim are both wrong, and the second is a soundness defect.**

### P13 — candidate: "accepted as required" (the flagship). Overturned to: **self-contradictory; not derivable.**

```text
C.compact()
  // §2.4: "ends every place P[sigma].f (layout version bumps; interior pointers
  //   refused)"; §2.4 `move`: an ended place is "never revived".
read(p)
  // reject: correct, but note the candidate gives TWO grounds (R8a end and R1(a)(iii)
  //   stale layout) that cannot both apply to one event.
read(C[h])
  // CANDIDATE: accept.  DERIVED: REJECT.  C[h] resolves to the place C[sigma(h)].data,
  //   which the compact rule just ENDED and which is never revived.  Live(h) is
  //   sigma in Live(C) AND gen = gamma -- it says nothing about state(C[sigma].data).
  //   Under §2.4 as written, R8a's demanded fixup form does not exist.          (F5)
  // Under the intended reading (relocation preserves the ghost place, only the layout
  //   version changes) the candidate needs an identity-preserving relocation primitive
  //   that §2.4 lacks and ordinary WF code cannot express -- falsifying M3's
  //   "no compiler-primitive pool" for the compacting pool.                     (F5)
  // and idx: after erasure the access is pool_backing[slotmap[h.idx]] with no stated
  //   source for h.idx < cap(C).                                                (F2)
open_window(C) { p2 = pointer_of(C[h]) ; loop { read(p2) } }
  // an undefined construct: a duration-scoped prohibition on an operation, i.e. a loan
  //   (C10/C14), absent from §2.4, unenforceable across calls without a negative effect
  //   clause R7 does not have, and unpriced -- while carrying M9's only mitigation. (S7)
```

Verdict: **overturned. Either `read(C[h])` is rejected and P13 fails, or the
relocation/ending distinction and an identity-preserving relocation primitive
are added, at which point M3's verdict changes.**

## 3. What the candidate must declare if it keeps this shape

1. Tier A violates **M2(ii) or M3** (F1) — pick one and state it in the
   headline beside the Tier B concession.
2. The **ghost-to-runtime bridge** (F2) is an undischarged obligation on a par
   with the frame-soundness obligation the M6 row already declares.
3. **R2, R3, R10 are not "met"** until `free` carries a state precondition
   (F3); **R11/R12/M2(i) are not "met"** until `alloc` carries a domain or an
   arm (F4); **R8a is not "met"** until ending and relocation are different
   events (F5); **R4/R6/M6(ii) are not "met"** until `ite` footprints kill as
   may-writes (F6); **R1 is not "met"** until pool invariants have a stated
   re-establishment discipline (F7).
4. Couplings silently retuned: **C1** (place granularity inside `'v.meta`,
   S3), **C2** (a fifth R4 discharge form and a pool-wide kill, S6/S12),
   **C3** (no call-site discharge, S9), **C6** (the atom set, S4), **C8**
   (struct identity parameters, S8), **C10/C14** (`open_window`, S7).

Corrected counts on the candidate's own §4.1 table: **7 rows move from "met"
to "violated"** (R1, R2, R3, R4, R8a, R10, R11), **M2 is violated in Tier A as
well as Tier B**, and **M3 and M6 move from "met"/"partial" to "violated"** on
F1 and F2.

# Critique: ownership topology — lens COST, DETERMINISM AND THE WRITER

Research date: 2026-09-16. Target:
[candidate-ownership-topology.md](candidate-ownership-topology.md). Lens: M1
(fixed terminating procedure, no search or budget), M10 (checking-cost degree
and edit stability), M7 (locally repairable rejection), M8 (spec tokens and
construct count), M9 (obvious shape of P5/P6, surviving backend facts), R15
(generics, closures, nominals in P16). Requirement text from
[VERDICT-D0.md](../../whitefoot-access-effects-research/research/investigations/access-effects/VERDICT-D0.md)
§2; programs from
[PROGRAMS.md](../../whitefoot-access-effects-research/research/investigations/access-effects/PROGRAMS.md);
ladder from
[MECHANISM-MAP.md](../../whitefoot-access-effects-research/research/investigations/access-effects/MECHANISM-MAP.md)
§3; measured evidence from
[EVIDENCE-mechanism-survey](../../whitefoot-access-effects-research/research/investigations/access-effects/EVIDENCE-mechanism-survey-2026-09-16.md)
parts A.5/B, `research/experiments/proof-use-cost/baseline-2026-09-14.tsv`,
`research/experiments/blind-writer/2026-08-28/REPORT.md`,
`research/experiments/scoped-alias-channel/RESULTS.md`.

The candidate declares **Met: 17. Partial: 10. Violated: 0**, and declares no
violation of M1 or M2. This critique's central claim is that **M1, M10, R15,
R7 and R9 are claimed met on text that does not define the procedure the
programs need**, and that the two constraint rows are held only by a term
language the candidate never fixes.

---

## 1. Findings

| # | Sev | Row / program | Finding | One-sentence fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | **fatal** | M1; P4, P1 | §2.2 fixes the term grammar as `back(π) ::= Res \| Com \| Dec \| ite(c, back, back)` with *"c a Boolean binding in scope"*, and §2.4 decides join agreement by *"equal terms are syntactically equal"* — but §2.3 and P4 build `back(v.elems) := ite(len₀ < cap₀, Com, Dec)`, whose atom is an arithmetic comparison over measure terms, not a Boolean binding; once such atoms are admitted, the join's agreement test is entailment in the index fragment, not syntax, and neither the atom set nor its normal form is specified. | Close the atom language to a named fragment-decidable predicate set, define join agreement as fragment entailment, and restate M1 and M10 including the fragment calls per join. |
| F2 | **fatal** | M1, M2; P8 | The atoms are *source bindings*, and P8's own programs reassign bindings (`x = take(p)`, a loop-carried `phase`); a term `ite(c, …)` retained across a reassignment of `c` silently changes meaning, so acceptance is not a function of the source under the stated rule, and either the term is unsound or an unstated SSA/immutability rule exists that the writer must obey. | State that atoms are single-assignment Boolean bindings (or SSA names), and charge the immutability restriction to M4 and M8. |
| F3 | **fatal** | M1, M10; P1 | P1's closing line is `push requires com(v.elems[*])` — a *universally quantified emptiness query* ("no index term under `v.elems` is `Res`") over symbolic index terms, which is strictly outside the only delegated arithmetic the candidate names (D5's *disequality between two index terms of one parent*, §3 P1 "Fact used"); M1 is declared met "under the condition that D5's index fragment is a fixed, terminating, specification-named family", and that condition does not cover this query. | Name the wildcard-state judgment as its own family (`∀` over the recorded index terms of one parent), state its degree as quadratic in those terms, and add it to the M1 condition list. |
| F4 | **fatal** | M1; P3 | §2.4 joins *state terms for a fixed path set*; nothing joins **the path a binding denotes**. P3's traversal `p = p.next` has entry path `n₀` and back-edge path `n₀.next`, then `n₀.next.next`, …; with no path-join rule the loop-head computation does not terminate, so M1's "termination is by the syntactic atom count" is false (the atom count does not bound the path set). | Add path-join = `⊔` (least common ancestor with a wildcard tail) as the second half of LOOP HEAD, and re-derive the writer cost it forces (below, §2 P3). |
| F5 | **fatal** | M10 | M10 is declared met with *"edit reach stops at the declaration and its direct callers, because a path is relative to a binding."* Rows are **written**, not inferred, and §6.3 states the body check "rejects a write outside the row"; therefore widening a leaf callee's row makes every transitive caller's row under-declared and rejected. The reach of a one-token row edit is the transitive caller closure, which is not a function of the edit's syntactic reach. | State the reach honestly as the transitive caller closure, or adopt infer-and-pin for rows (R7(d) leaves authorship open) and measure the reach on the pinned bundle. |
| F6 | **fatal** | R15; P16 | R15 is declared met, but §2.1 fixes `ptr<π,T>` as carrying *"a path and nothing else"* and §2.5's signature grammar attaches rows only to `fn name(params)` declarations — there is **no effect row on an arrow type**. P16's `map_nodes<T>(g, f: fn(&T) -> T)` therefore cannot state what `f` may touch, so `map_nodes`'s own row `writes g.slots.*.data` is either unsound or silently assumes `f` pure; the same hole makes P6's closure `h` unusable under `par for w`, since a `captures` clause states what `h` *reads from its environment*, not what it *writes through its parameter*. | Add effect-row parameters on arrow and closure types (the THE-D2-14 member the tuple already cites but never spells), and re-count R15(e)'s metric with effect parameters included. |
| F7 | **fatal** | R7; P2 | §2.5 states *"A result path is an expression over the parameter bindings, not a fresh name"*, yet P2's `alloc(A, 64)` has result path `A.bytes.⟨b1⟩` where `⟨b1⟩` is a **caller** binding occurrence not nameable from `alloc`'s parameters. R7(a)/(b) require a fresh allocation to be stateable at the interface; the row grammar has no clause that states it (`inits` is `Res→Com`, not minting), so P2's central operation has no writable signature. | Add a `mints r.⟨fresh⟩` clause instantiated at the call site to the caller's binding occurrence, and count it in M8. |
| F8 | **fatal** | R9, M7; P13 | §6.1's whole defence is *"a sequential program is never rejected because of aliasing … The only rejections are state rejections"*, and R9 is declared "sequentially met in full". P13 rejects `Pool.compact()` **because another reference exists**: `pin` is set by *forming* an interior pointer and cleared by "releasing the last one", and the diagnostic's repair is *"end p's live range"* — a reference-liveness restriction with a restructuring repair, i.e. exactly the OWN-5/OWN-6 shape D12 claims to retire, and M7's Price forbids a rule whose only fix is non-local and unnamed. | Declare the pin axis as a reference-liveness rule, name the scope construct that bounds a pointer's live range, and restate R9 as "aliasing rejects only where a `rebases` row demands `Mov`". |
| S1 | serious | M10 | §2.3 states downward propagation as *"`ends π` sets `Dec` on the whole subtree"* — as written, work is proportional to the *number of leaf paths*, which is exponential in nested type-declaration depth (`struct A { x: B, y: B }` d deep ⇒ 2^d leaves from O(d) source); M10's ceiling is "never exponential". The stated degree `O(paths × ending sites)` also omits the program-point factor and the per-join fragment calls of F1. | Specify `ends` as a mark at the node plus an ancestor query at each access (degree O(path depth) per access), and restate the per-declaration degree as `O(points × paths × atoms)` with the fragment calls counted. |
| S2 | serious | M8 | The candidate calls the taught surface *"one path grammar, one five-value state vocabulary, one row grammar and one join rule — small"*. Counted: `ptr<π,T>`, 6 path steps (`.name`, `.⟨site⟩`, `[e]`, `[lo..hi)`, `.*`, root), `⊔`, the `@` result-path annotation, the type region parameter, `region`/`arena`/`pool`, `partition`, `split`, 9 row clause keywords (`reads`,`writes`,`inits`,`ends`,`rebases`,`takes`,`puts`,`lends`,`partitions`), `unless`, `requires`, `ensures`, `fresh`, `captures`, `with_fixup`, and declared foreign states — ≈ 31 source constructs, plus 6 checker notions the diagnostics name (`back`, `pin`, `layout`, `msr`, `ite`, `⊤`). Against M8's measured red (≈130k vs K = 48k, ownership subsystem ≈18.5k), retiring the mode vocabulary does not obviously pay for this, and no count is given. | Publish the construct inventory and a token count of the taught surface against K before M8 is called "partial". |
| S3 | serious | M9; P5 | M9 is declared partial because *"no fact channel exists"* and the P5 claim is "to be measured". It **has** been measured: `research/experiments/scoped-alias-channel/RESULTS.md` reports 8 vector adds / 0 runtime guards / 121 asm lines against Rust's 65 / 29 / 2132, and the same record says the time delta is real only at short trip counts (2.0× at n=8, 1.18× at n=16, tie at n ≥ 32) — the durable win is code size and guard count. Citing the claim as unmeasurable overstates the candidate's novelty in exactly the row that prices it. | Cite the retired channel, restate the P5 claim as "reproduce 8/0/121 on the current compiler", and carry the honest note that the time win amortizes away at n ≥ 32. |
| S4 | serious | M9; P5, P6 | §2.8 claims *"R4's relation and the metadata form are the same shape, so no translation layer decides granularity."* Per EVIDENCE §B, `llvm.experimental.noalias.scope.decl` *"must be duplicated when a loop is unrolled … otherwise the noalias property would spill across loop iterations"* — a symbolic index child `x.a[i]` or extent child `out[w*s..(w+1)*s)` has **no static scope**; it needs a per-iteration scope declaration. Those are precisely the children P1, P5's `par-2` and P6 rely on, so the "free" channel covers only the field-level half (`x.a` vs `x.b`) that the retired prototype already had. | State that index and extent children reach the backend only as per-iteration scope declarations or as parameter `noalias` on an outlined helper, and price that translation layer. |
| S5 | serious | R6, M7 | R6's red value is *"34 of 41 `len()` rebinds in the blind-writer corpus exist only because ENT-5 kills at a whole-parameter footprint"*, and `blind-writer/2026-08-28/REPORT.md` names *"rebinding `len()` after every write"* as the recurring tax. The candidate's wildcard footprints (`g.slots.*`, `x.*`, `pick`'s `⊔`) reproduce the whole-parameter kill at exactly those sites, yet §4.3's writer-cost table lists no rebind class at all — the largest measured writer tax in the repository is relocated, not removed, and is uncounted. | Add a "facts re-established after a wildcard-footprint call" row to §4.3 and measure it against the blind-writer corpus's 34/41. |
| S6 | serious | M7; P8 | §2.4's loop rule collapses to `⊤` any path whose arms disagree on an atom bound inside the loop, and offers one repair: *"the writer must write one `invariant` clause naming its state"* — but the rule's own premise is that such an atom **is not nameable at the head**, so the escape cannot express the state and the only remaining repair is restructuring the loop. §4.3 nonetheless prices a loop at "0, unless … then 1 `invariant` clause". | Distinguish loop-carried bindings (nameable, invariant-repairable) from per-iteration branch conditions (not nameable, restructuring-repairable), and price the second class in M7 and §4.3. |
| S7 | serious | R15; P16 | §2.1: *"A pointer stored in a struct field forces the struct type to carry one region parameter."* Therefore `Cols<E>` instantiated at any `E` that stores a pointer must itself carry `E`'s region parameters, and `kernel<E>`'s row must be quantified over them; P16's table row "kernel (P5) — 8 columns — identity parameters written: 0" is wrong for that instantiation, and R15(e)'s metric (parameters per interface as a function of storages touched) is therefore unanswered, not "beaten". | Add region-parameter-kind polymorphism to the generic form, and re-state P16's table per instantiation class (pointer-free `E` vs pointer-carrying `E`). |
| S8 | serious | R7; P13, P4 | `pin` is a per-path fact (§2.2) that P13 needs at a call boundary (*"requires mov(Pool)"*), and a stored `Cursor<'v>` carries a pin across calls — but §2.5's signature grammar lists only `requires`/`ensures` over *"state and measure preconditions"*, and §2.2's state vocabulary for signatures is `back`; `pin` appears in no interface clause. R7 is declared met. | Add `pin` to the `requires`/`ensures` vocabulary and to R7's per-storage entry/exit state list. |
| S9 | serious | M3; P5, P2 | W4 charges *"one enumerated entry per foreign allocator"* for sibling disjointness. The same axiom is needed once per container and pool library type: the claim that `x.a.elems` and `x.b.elems` are disjoint, or that two pool slots are, is asserted by "the tree invariant" and proved only for the language's own arena "from the extent arithmetic in `alloc`"; with OWN-1's affine-single-owner mode retired by D12, nothing stated re-establishes it for `buffer`, `pool` or any view-constructing operation. P5's entire distinctness rests on it. | Enumerate one M3 entry per backing-owning library type, or state the construction rule that makes sibling `elems` disjointness a checker fact rather than an axiom. |
| S10 | serious | P1 | The P1 derivation fills each hole twice: `write(pi, x)` is annotated *"Res → Com"* and then `put(pi); put(pj)` is annotated *"accept: Res → Com at both"*. After the writes the paths are `Com`, so the puts are `Com → Com` (or rejected as puts into a full slot), and P1's required property — "push allowed only after both are back" — is discharged by the writes, not by the puts. | Rewrite the derivation with one fill per hole, and state whether `put` into a `Com` path is an error or a `replace`. |
| m1 | minor | D3 / §1 | `Res`/`Com`/`Dec` reuse SYS-D3-04's *Reserved / Committed / Decommitted* names for different meanings (`Res` here is a value-less hole, not reserved address space), which mis-credits the prior art and will mislead the M8 count. | Rename to `Empty`/`Full`/`Ended` or state the re-definition explicitly. |
| m2 | minor | §2.2, M2 | *"releasing the last one unpins"* states a cardinality, which reads as a counter the row elsewhere forbids. | Say "the static set of live interior pointers into the subtree becomes empty". |
| m3 | minor | §3 summary | *"Rejected: none"* conflates program-level with statement-level verdicts; P13 and P8 each contain a **required** rejection that is the point of the program. | Report per-program verdicts as "required rejections present / absent". |
| m4 | minor | §2.8 | `!alias.scope` domains and `!tbaa` parent chains are different trees with different rules (EVIDENCE §B says TBAA is "likely subsumed by per-identity alias scopes"); citing both as one channel shape is loose. | Cite `!alias.scope`/`!noalias` only. |
| m5 | minor | M4 | M4 is declared met, but the pool has two reading disciplines for one storage (concrete minted path; wildcard plus invariant, W3) — a semantic duplicate that M4(d) concedes the spelling lint cannot see and that the row's status should record. | Record the duplicate under M4(d)'s stated limit rather than claiming an unqualified met. |

Counts: **fatal 8, serious 10, minor 5.**

---

## 2. Program verdicts overturned

Notation follows the ladder: `// accept:` / `// reject:` with the fact used;
`⊨` means discharged.

### P1 — from *accepted with a stated cost* to **not derivable in the stated procedure (M1)**

```text
(pi, pj) = split_out(v, i, j)   // accept: takes v.elems[i], v.elems[j]
write(pi, x)                    // accept: Res → Com at v.elems[i]
write(pj, y)                    // accept: Res → Com at v.elems[j]
put(pi)                         // reject (candidate says accept "Res → Com"):
                                //   back(v.elems[i]) = Com already; the hole was
                                //   filled by the write. §2.3 gives no Com → Com
                                //   transition for `puts`
push(v, 5)                      // UNDECIDED: the stated precondition is
                                //   `com(v.elems[*])`, i.e. ∀ index terms t under
                                //   v.elems . back(v.elems[t]) ≠ Res.
                                //   the state map holds symbolic keys i, j, k, c.i …
                                //   deciding emptiness of the Res set over symbolic
                                //   keys is a quantified query; §3's "Fact used"
                                //   delegates only "a disequality between two index
                                //   terms of one parent" to D5.
                                //   ⇒ M1's condition does not cover the judgment
                                //     P1's closing requirement needs
```

Derivation of the cost, once the query is named: for a container with m
distinct recorded index terms, `com(π.*)` is m disequality discharges against
each `Res`-keyed term, i.e. O(m·r) fragment calls per wildcard precondition,
and a wildcard precondition appears on every growth operation. That degree is
absent from §4.1's M10 entry (`O(paths × ending sites)`). **New verdict:
accepted only after a second automatic family is admitted; M1 "met" and M10
"met" are both unearned until it is named and bounded.**

### P2 — from *accepted as required* to **the central operation has no writable signature (R7)**

```text
b1 = alloc(A, 64)   // candidate: "mints child ⟨b1⟩ at this binding",
                    //   result path A.bytes.⟨b1⟩
                    // but §2.5: "A result path is an expression over the
                    //   parameter bindings, not a fresh name"
                    // ⟨b1⟩ is a CALLER binding occurrence: `alloc`'s parameters
                    //   are (A, 64); no expression over them denotes ⟨b1⟩
                    // ⇒ `alloc` cannot be declared in the stated grammar
free(A, b2)         // accept, conditionally: `ends A.bytes.⟨b2⟩` is expressible
                    //   only because ⟨b2⟩ is a caller binding the CALL site can
                    //   name — so the row is instantiated per call site, which is
                    //   a mechanism (call-site path instantiation) §2.5 does not
                    //   state
```

Everything else in P2 (reuse without revival, ancestor/descendant
non-distinctness, four frees) survives and is genuinely good. **New verdict:
accepted as required *for the identity model*, rejected as derived: R7 is
partial, not met, until a fresh/minting result clause exists.**

### P3 — from *accepted with a stated cost* to **the loop does not terminate under the stated procedure (M1)**

```text
traverse: p = p.next; read(p.data)
          // entry:      p : ptr<n₀>
          // back edge:  p : ptr<n₀.next>
          // next round: p : ptr<n₀.next.next>   …
          // §2.4 JOIN is "for each path π mentioned in either map" — it joins
          //   STATE TERMS at a fixed path set. There is no rule that joins the
          //   PATH a binding denotes.
          // ⇒ the path set grows without bound; "termination is by the syntactic
          //   atom count" does not apply, because the growth is in paths, not atoms
```

The repair is available (`⊔` from §2.5: `n₀ ⊔ n₀.next = n₀.*`), and it is what
the candidate silently assumes when it writes `p : ptr<P.slots[*].*>`. But
naming it changes the writer cost: **every traversal binding is a wildcard at
its loop head**, so every loop that walks a linked structure loses per-path
facts and needs the invariant-plus-`use` discipline, not only the mutation
sites. §4.3's "per loop: 0" and W1's "one `use` step per mutation site" both
understate it. **New verdict: accepted only with an unnamed path-join rule,
whose writer cost is one invariant per traversal loop in addition to one `use`
per mutation site.**

### P4 — from *accepted as required* to **the state term is outside the stated grammar (M1)**

```text
push(v, 5)   // candidate: back(v.elems) := ite(len₀ < cap₀, Com, Dec)
             // §2.2: back(π) ::= … | ite(c, back, back)   // c a Boolean BINDING
             // `len₀ < cap₀` is a comparison over measure terms, not a binding
reserve(v, n+1); push(v, 5); b = c.read()
             // candidate: "the ite collapses to Com"
             // that collapse is an ENTAILMENT (cap ≥ n+1 ∧ len ≤ n ⊢ len₀ < cap₀),
             //   not §2.4's "equal terms are syntactically equal"
             // ⇒ the join's agreement test is a fragment query at every join
```

P4's *property* — validity carried across `push` by proof rather than by a
borrow — is genuinely achieved and is the candidate's best result. What is
wrong is the claim that it costs nothing procedurally. **New verdict: accepted
as required on the language question; M1 and M10 must be restated with an
entailment-based join and its per-join fragment-call degree.**

### P5 — from *accepted as required* to **accepted, but the M9 claim is not the candidate's**

```text
x.a[i] = f(x.a[i], x.c[i], x.d[i])   // accept: siblings of one node
                                     //   ⇒ scope x.a in domain x — CORRECT, and
                                     //   already achieved by the retired channel
                                     //   from the resolved place of the field
par-2 over i                         // accept for permission (R5(i)) …
                                     // … but NOT as a backend fact: x.a[i] vs
                                     //   x.a[i'] is a per-ITERATION disjointness,
                                     //   which LangRef says needs
                                     //   llvm.experimental.noalias.scope.decl
                                     //   duplicated per unrolled iteration.
                                     //   §2.8's "the scope tree is the path tree"
                                     //   has no form for a symbolic index child
```

And the ground under the fact is S9's: sibling disjointness of `x.a.elems` vs
`x.b.elems` is an asserted tree invariant, not a checker proof, once OWN-1's
affine single-owner is retired with the modes. **New verdict: accepted, with
the M9 claim demoted to "reproduces the retired channel's field-level half
(8 adds / 0 guards / 121 asm), time-neutral at n ≥ 32", and the per-iteration
half named as an unpriced translation layer.**

### P6 — from *accepted as required* to **accepted for permission, unproved for the backend**

```text
parts = partition(out, k, s)     // accept: one obligation discharged once — the
                                 //   candidate's genuinely strong result
par for w in 0..k { helper(parts[w], input) }
                                 // accept: R5(i), disjoint extent children
                                 // backend: the extent bounds are symbolic in w,
                                 //   so no static scope exists; the only surviving
                                 //   form is parameter `noalias` on the outlined
                                 //   helper (which the CURRENT emitter does not
                                 //   emit: EVIDENCE A.5, "Anything in the current
                                 //   backend — only align, GEP inbounds, mul nuw")
```

**New verdict: accepted as required for R5 and R7; the R4/M9 half is
unsupported and should be stated as such rather than as a free channel.**

### P8 — from *accepted as required* to **the term language is unsound under reassignment, and one repair class is missing (M1, M2, M7)**

```text
if c { free(a) } else { free(b) }   // back(a) := ite(c, Dec, Com)
… c = recompute()                   // c is a BINDING; §2.2 says atoms are bindings
use(a)                              // the retained term still reads `ite(c, …)`,
                                    //   now denoting the NEW c
                                    // ⇒ acceptance is not a function of the source
                                    //   under the stated rule (M1), and a state the
                                    //   source did not bind is being consulted (M2)

loop {
  if per_iteration_cond() { x = take(p) } ; …    // atom bound INSIDE the loop
  if other_cond()        { put(p, x) }
}
// LOOP HEAD: arms disagree on an atom bound inside the loop → collapse to ⊤
// §2.4's escape: "the writer must write one `invariant` clause naming its state"
// but the same rule says such an atom "is not nameable at the head"
// ⇒ for this class the escape cannot be written; the only repair is restructuring,
//   which M7's Price forbids as a rule whose only fix is non-local and unnamed
```

**New verdict: accepted for the drop-flag-free property (which is real and
important); rejected as a complete rule — M1 and M2 hold only under an unstated
single-assignment restriction, and M7's residue includes a restructuring-only
repair class that §4.3 prices at zero.**

### P9 — from *accepted with a stated cost* to **the cost is a whole-call-graph cost, not an LCA cost (M10)**

```text
fn pick(c, x, y) -> ptr<T> @ (x ⊔ y)   // accept: canonical origin set
r = pick(c, &v.a[3], &v.b[7]); write(r, 1)
                                       // accept; kills v.* contents facts — the
                                       //   candidate's stated R6 tax, correct
fn g(...) { … return pick(…) }         // g's result path is an expression in g's
                                       //   parameters, derived from pick's
                                       // ⇒ widening pick's result path widens g's,
                                       //   and every caller of g, transitively
// and the row direction:
//   widening a LEAF callee's `writes` clause under-declares every transitive
//   caller's row, each of which is then REJECTED by the body check (§6.3)
//   ⇒ one-token edit reach = transitive caller closure, not "the declaration and
//     its direct callers"
```

Measured context: `proof-use-cost/baseline-2026-09-14.tsv` already shows the
`growing` bundle at 31 → 164 → 1690 ms for N = 16 → 32 → 64 (exponent ≈ 2.9),
red against M10's ceiling *before* a per-path state map with `ite` terms and
per-join fragment calls is added. **New verdict: accepted with a stated cost
for R6/R7; M10 "met" is overturned to red on both the degree and the reach
function.**

### P13 — from *accepted as required* to **a reference-liveness rejection the candidate says it does not have (R9, M7)**

```text
p = pointer_of(h)    // pin(Pool.slots[h]) := Pin, propagated to pin(Pool)
Pool.compact()       // reject: "requires Pool to be Mov; it is Pin because of the
                     //   interior pointer p formed at line L. missing step: end p's
                     //   live range"
                     // ⇒ this rejection is caused by the EXISTENCE OF ANOTHER
                     //   REFERENCE, not by any storage's state.
                     // §6.1: "a sequential program is never rejected because of
                     //   aliasing … The only rejections are state rejections"  FALSE
                     // §4.1 R9: "Sequentially met in full"                      FALSE
                     // repair: "end p's live range" — a restructuring; the
                     //   construct that bounds a pointer's live range is unnamed
                     //   (D12 claims "no borrow-scope syntax of any kind")
drop p; Pool.compact()   // accept — so the language does have a scope-ending form
```

**New verdict: accepted for the path-≠-address property and the fixup form;
R9 overturned from "sequentially met in full" to partial, M7's residue
enlarged, and D12's "no borrow-scope syntax of any kind" contradicted by the
rule's own repair.**

### P16 — from *accepted with a stated cost* to **R15 violated (undeclared)**

```text
fn map_nodes<T>(g: &mut Pool<Node<T>>, f: fn(&T) -> T)
    reads g.slots.*  writes g.slots.*.data
                       // f's type is `fn(&T) -> T`. §2.1: a pointer type carries
                       //   "a path and nothing else"; §2.5 attaches rows to fn
                       //   DECLARATIONS only.
                       // ⇒ nothing states what f may read, write or end.
                       //   either map_nodes's row is unsound (f may write outside
                       //   it) or f is silently required pure — a restriction the
                       //   candidate never declares.
                       // R15(a): "identity, state and effect facts cross
                       //   abstraction boundaries"  VIOLATED

let h = |slice| helper(slice, input)   // "captures reads input.*"
P6 with h                              // a `captures` clause states what h reads
                                       //   from its ENVIRONMENT; it does not state
                                       //   what h WRITES THROUGH ITS PARAMETER.
                                       //   the `par for w` needs the latter.

fn kernel<E>(x: &mut Cols<E>, n)  writes x.a, x.b
                                       // if E stores a pointer, §2.1 forces Cols<E>
                                       //   to carry E's region parameter, and the
                                       //   row must be quantified over it.
                                       //   "identity parameters written: 0" holds
                                       //   only for pointer-free E.
```

**New verdict: R15 overturned from met to violated (undeclared). The fix —
effect rows on arrow and closure types, plus region-parameter-kind
polymorphism — is exactly the signature growth R15(e) exists to measure, and
it lands on M8's already-red budget.**

---

## 3. What survives

The critique does not touch these, and they are the candidate's real results:

- **P2's identity model.** Identity as a tree position, so address reuse never
  revives an ended identity, and ancestor/descendant is never a distinctness
  fact (R4(b)'s negative test). This is correct and cheap.
- **P7 in full.** State on the path, seen by every alias; `Dec` absorbing. No
  finding above touches it.
- **P4's property.** Cursor validity decided by a capacity proof rather than by
  a borrow that blocks `push` — the shape R8a and P4 were written to demand.
- **P6's partition.** One arithmetic obligation at the split site converted
  into structural disjointness for every later pair, with no worker count in
  the source. This is the single strongest cost argument in the candidate and
  no finding weakens it.
- **P8's drop-flag-free release.** Conditional release by a term over the
  writer's own branches, with no bookkeeping state, is exactly M2(ii)'s
  demand — subject to F2's single-assignment repair.


# File: critique-ownership-topology-soundness.md

# Critique of `candidate-ownership-topology.md` — lens SOUNDNESS

Research date: 2026-09-16. Lens: **soundness and the programs.** Method: P1, P2,
P4, P7, P9 and P13 re-derived from scratch against the candidate's own §2 rules
(path grammar §2.1, per-path facts §2.2, transition table §2.3, join/loop §2.4,
signature form §2.5), then checked against R1–R3, R11, R12, the R4/R5 fact rows,
the M1/M2 constraint rows, and the couplings C1–C18. Nothing is taken from the
candidate's §3 comment column on trust; the comment column is the object under
test. Where a rule the candidate needs is not in §2, it is reported as unstated
rather than charitably supplied. Supersede in place.

Summary: **7 fatal, 9 serious, 4 minor.** Five of the six assigned programs have
at least one accept/reject line that is wrong under the candidate's own rules,
and two of them (P4, P9) contradict each other on the same program text. The
single deepest defect is that the candidate abolished pointer duration (§2.1:
"No mode, no region-lifetime, no duration, no permission") and then wrote three
rules that cannot be evaluated without one (`pin` release, `drop p`,
`with_fixup`).

---

## 1. Findings table

| # | Sev | Program / requirement | Finding | One-sentence fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | **fatal** | P4, P13, R8a, M2(ii), M4 | **`pin` has no release rule, because the candidate deleted the only mechanism that could state one.** §2.2 sets `pin(π) := Pin` when an interior pointer is formed and clears it when "releasing the last one" — a *last-holder* condition over pointer values that §2.1 declares copyable, duration-free, storable in struct fields and returnable as LCA path expressions. Nothing in §2 computes a last holder, so either `Pin` is permanent (P13's `drop p; Pool.compact()` must **reject**, and every region that ever had an interior pointer is permanently un-`rebases`-able: P3's `a, b`, P4's `Cursor`, P7's `p`/`q` all pin their regions for the rest of the program) or the checker runs a pointer-liveness analysis that is a borrow checker under another name, contradicting §6.1's "ownership is unique, reference is free" and D12's "borrow-scope syntax of any kind" foreclosure. | Either state a pointer-duration mechanism (and re-price D12, M4, M8) or make `Pin` a monotone, never-cleared state and re-derive P13 with that. |
| F2 | **fatal** | P9, P7, R1(a)(i)(ii) | **A wildcard path has no state, so access through an LCA result reaches holes and ended storage.** §2.1 admits `π.*` ("supplies containment, no distinctness"); §2.2 holds `back`/`pin`/`layout` *per path*; no rule says what `back(π.*)` is or what an access through a wildcard requires. P9 therefore accepts `write(r, 1)` with `r : ptr<v.*>` unconditionally. Take one leaf out first — `w = take(&v.a[3]); r = pick(c, &v.a[3], &v.b[7]); read(r)` — and a hole read is admitted by every stated rule (R1(a)(i)).
