## 2. Program verdicts overturned, with derivation

### 2.1 P1 — overturned: *accepted with a stated cost* → **not derivable as written**

Re-derived strictly from §2.2, §2.3 and §2.4:

```text
v : Vec<u64>, tree v ▸ {meta, elems ▸ [0..n)}

(pi, pj) = split_out(v, i, j)   // accept: row `takes v.elems[i], v.elems[j]`
                                //   back(v.elems[i]) := Res, back(v.elems[j]) := Res
                                //   BUT: this state is not expressible in §2.2's grammar.
                                //   `i`, `j` are runtime u64s; the map must become
                                //   λm. ite(m=i ∨ m=j, Res, Com), a symbolic store.
                                //   unstated mechanism (F9)
write(pi, x)                    // per §3's own comment this is `puts`-shaped: Res → Com.
                                //   so after this line back(v.elems[i]) = Com
write(pj, y)                    // back(v.elems[j]) = Com
read(v[k])                      // ACCEPT under the rules as written — every element is Com.
                                //   the candidate's `reject` is WRONG (F8), and with it the
                                //   diagnostic P1 requires ("names the missing fact") never fires
put(pi); put(pj)                // §2.3 defines `put` only as Res → Com; here both paths are Com.
                                //   NO stated transition applies. If admitted it is Com → Com,
                                //   which for a non-Copy element discards the occupant with no
                                //   discharge (R2/R3); if refused, P1's required "put both parts
                                //   back" fails
push(v, 5)                      // requires com(v.elems[*]) — a ∀ over a runtime extent, again
                                //   outside §2.2's grammar (F9)
```

The alternative reading that saves the `read(v[k])` reject is that `write(pi, x)`
does **not** fill `v.elems[i]` — but then §2.1 owes an account of what storage `pi`
addresses while `v.elems[i]` is `Res`, which no production supplies. Either way
the printed trace is not a derivation. **New verdict: P1 undecided pending a
stated symbolic-store representation and a decided reading of `write` through a
taken-out part; the stated cost ("delegated to D5's index fragment") understates
the gap, which is a representation, not a decision procedure.**

### 2.2 P4 — overturned: *accepted as required* → **required property met only vacuously**

```text
struct Cursor<'v> { at: ptr<'v.elems[·]>, i: u64 }
c = Cursor { at: ptr_of(v.elems[0]), i: 0 }
                                // accept, and pin(v.elems) := Pin, propagating to pin(v) := Pin.
                                //   nothing in §2 ever clears it (F1)
a = c.read()                    // accept
push(v, 5)                      // accept; back(v.elems) := ite(len₀<cap₀, Com, Dec)
b = c.read()                    // reject unless len₀ < cap₀ — this line stands
reserve(v, n+1); push(v, 5); b = c.read()
                                // REJECT, not accept. reserve's own row is
                                //   `ends v.elems unless cap(v) >= n+1 ; inits fresh v.elems`,
                                //   so back(v.elems) = ite(cap₀ >= n+1, Com, Dec) *after reserve*.
                                //   the arm on which reserve does any work is the arm on which
                                //   c.at is Dec. c.read() is admissible only under cap₀ >= n+1,
                                //   i.e. only when reserve was a no-op.
                                //   P9's `reserve(&mut v, 100); read(pe)` rejects this exact
                                //   shape — the two derivations contradict (F6)
ptr_of(v.elems[0])              // after the push: under §2.3's "a fresh minted child replaces it",
                                //   `v.elems` is Dec on one arm, so a pointer formed AFTER the
                                //   growth is refused too — unless the fresh child reuses the name,
                                //   in which case back(v.elems) = Com and the `b = c.read()`
                                //   reject above collapses. Both cannot hold (F7)
free(v); c.read()               // reject — stands
```

**New verdict: P4 accepted only for a cursor that never crosses a growth that
grows. PROGRAMS.md P4's required "validity decided by state and proof, not by a
borrow that blocks push" is satisfied by the *form* of the rule and not by any
admitted program; R1(e) and R8a(e) name P4 as their acceptance test, so those
rows' "met" scores do not stand as written.**

### 2.3 P7 — overturned in one line: *accepted as required* → **accepted except `free A`**

```text
p = ptr_of(A.slot); q = ptr_of(A.slot)   // accept; also pin(A.slot):=Pin → pin(A):=Pin, never cleared (F1)
w = take(p)                              // accept: back(A.slot) := Res
read(q)                                  // reject: Res — correct, and this is the candidate's best line
put(q, move w)                           // accept: Res → Com — correct
read(p)                                  // accept — correct
old = replace(p, new)                    // accept: Com → Com — correct; `old` is now an undischarged
                                         //   affine/linear binding (F18)
read(q)                                  // accept: reads `new` — correct
free A                                   // NOT simply accept: back(A.slot) = Com, and the occupant
                                         //   `new` has an obligation §2.3 does not discharge.
                                         //   If `new` is linear this violates R2(a) outright (F10);
                                         //   if affine, the candidate owes the derived-release rule
read(p); read(q)                         // reject: Dec — correct, and absorbing as required
```

Variant that breaks the row, using only §2.1 and §2.5:

```text
r = pick(c, p, ptr_of(A.other))          // result path A.* (LCA under one root — legal here)
w = take(p)                              // back(A.slot) := Res
read(r)                                  // ACCEPT: no rule gives back(A.*) a value or requires a
                                         //   ∀ over the subtree. Hole read admitted. R1(a)(i) (F2)
```

**New verdict: P7's sequential aliasing story holds and is the candidate's real
strength; its `free` line admits an R2 hazard, and the wildcard variant admits an
R1(a)(i) hazard.**

### 2.4 P9 — overturned: *accepted with a stated cost* → **`pick` not well-formed; `write(r,1)` unsound**

```text
fn drain(x: &mut Buf) takes x.slot writes x.meta
drain(&mut buf); read(buf.slot)          // reject: back(buf.slot) = Res from the row alone — correct

fn reserve(v: &mut Vec, m) writes v.meta ends v.elems unless cap(v)>=m inits fresh v.elems
reserve(&mut v, 100); read(pe)           // reject — correct, and it is P4's accept line (F6)

fn pick(c, x: ptr<T>, y: ptr<T>) -> ptr<T> @ (x ⊔ y) reads x, y
                                         // REJECT AT THE DECLARATION. §2.1's path grammar has one
                                         //   root production and no join; `x` and `y` are two
                                         //   distinct roots, so `x ⊔ y` denotes nothing. R7(a)
                                         //   requires rejection of a declaration whose result names
                                         //   a root no caller can name (F3)
r = pick(c, &v.a[3], &v.b[7])            // if the declaration were admitted: result path v.*
write(r, 1)                              // the candidate says accept. UNSOUND as a general rule:
                                         //   no stated rule checks any descendant's state, so the
                                         //   same line accepts when v.c is Res or v.b is Dec (F2)
r2 = pick(c, &v.a[3], &v.a[7])           // result v.a[*] — same wildcard-state hole, narrower
```

**New verdict: P9's `drain` and `reserve` lines are correct and are the
candidate's cleanest demonstration of R7. `pick` is not derivable: cross-root LCA
is undefined, and same-root LCA yields a wildcard whose access rule is unstated
and, as printed, unsound. The "stated cost" the candidate books for P9 (R6
fact-loss at the LCA) is the small half of the problem; the large half is that
the LCA result is not safely readable at all.**

### 2.5 P13 — overturned: *accepted as required* → **two of four lines not derivable**

```text
region Pool = compacting_pool<T>
h : handle = index into Pool.slots
p = pointer_of(h)                // accept; pin(Pool.slots[h]) := Pin, propagated to pin(Pool) := Pin
Pool.compact()                   // reject: requires mov(Pool) — CORRECT, and the diagnostic is good
drop p; Pool.compact()           // NOT derivable. `p` is a Copy machine word with no duration
                                 //   (§2.1); `drop` of a Copy value neither consumes it nor bounds
                                 //   the set of surviving copies, and no rule computes "the last
                                 //   holder". Under the rules as written pin(Pool) stays Pin and
                                 //   this REJECTS (F1)
read(p)                          // the candidate's "reject: p is out of scope" presupposes the
                                 //   scope discipline §2.1 abolished; the layout-token argument is
                                 //   sound, the scope argument is not
read(Pool[h])                    // undetermined: accept under slot-stable compaction (which needs an
                                 //   unnamed address-indirection table, an unpriced per-access cost),
                                 //   reject under occupant-moving compaction (back(P.slots[h]) = Res
                                 //   after the occupant leaves). §2 states neither (F14)
with_fixup(p) { Pool.compact() } // accept only under an unstated restriction: the fixup re-forms
                                 //   every live copy of p, a root-set walk the source did not write,
                                 //   over a copy set the checker cannot bound (F1, F13). M2(ii)
```

**New verdict: P13's *negative* half — `compact()` refused under an interior
pointer, with a diagnostic naming the pin and its origin — is correct and is real
evidence for R8a. P13's *positive* half (unpin, handle survival, fixup form) rests
on three mechanisms the candidate does not state, one of which (the fixup root
set) is an M2(ii) violation it does not declare.**

### 2.6 P2 — overturned in two lines: *accepted as required* → **accepted with an unstated liveness condition**

```text
region A = arena(cap)            // "children of A.bytes are pairwise disjoint sub-extents"
b1, b2, b3 = alloc(A, 64) ×3     // accept: three minted binding-occurrence children
fill(b1) ∥ fill(b2) ∥ fill(b3)   // accept: R5(i) — correct, and this is the candidate's best result
alloc(A,_) ∥ alloc(A,_)          // reject: write-write on A.meta — correct
free(A, b2)                      // accept; but a recycling allocator's link write into ⟨b2⟩ and the
                                 //   next alloc's read of it are program accesses to Dec storage (F12)
read(p : ptr<A.bytes.⟨b2⟩.f>)    // reject: Dec by ancestor propagation — correct, and the
                                 //   identity-as-position answer to address reuse is genuinely right
b4 = alloc(A, 32)                // accept, ⟨b4⟩ ≠ ⟨b2⟩ — correct for R1(a)(ii).
                                 //   BUT the sibling invariant now asserts ⟨b2⟩ and ⟨b4⟩ are
                                 //   disjoint sub-extents while they are the same bytes (F5).
                                 //   The invariant is sound only conditioned on both being non-Dec,
                                 //   which makes disjoint(·,·) state-dependent and retunes C1/C2
distinct(A.bytes, A.bytes.⟨b1⟩)? // NO — correct, R4(e)'s negative test passes cleanly
drop A                           // accept per the candidate; but ⟨b1⟩,⟨b3⟩,⟨b4⟩ are already Dec and
                                 //   §2.3 says "no operation maps Dec anywhere" (F11); and any
                                 //   occupant still Com is discarded undischarged (F10)
```

**New verdict: P2 remains the candidate's strongest program for R1(a)(ii) and
R4(e), and its identity-as-binding-occurrence answer is correct. Its load-bearing
tree invariant is nevertheless false as stated of its own trace, and the repaired
(liveness-conditioned) form is a different relation from the one §1.2 and §4.1
price.**

## 4. What survives

Stated so the repair does not throw away the working parts. The following are
correct derivations under the candidate's own rules and are real evidence for the
tuple: P7's take/put/replace/`Dec`-absorbing sequence (R1(a)(i), R3);
P2's minted binding-occurrence identity defeating address reuse (R1(a)(ii)) and
its ancestor/descendant non-distinctness (R4(e)'s negative test); P2's
three-way parallel `fill` from sibling disjointness among *live* minted blocks;
P5's eight declared-field children, which F4 does not touch as long as `Cols` is
never also partitioned; P6's once-discharged tiling obligation, again subject to
F4 where index children coexist; P8's `ite` join and one-step loop-head collapse,
which are the cleanest drop-flag-free account in the candidate; P13's *refusal*
of `compact()` under an interior pointer; and P9's `drain`/`reserve` rows as an
R7 demonstration. The defects above are concentrated in three places — the
wildcard/LCA path, the pin lifecycle, and the sibling-disjointness rule — and
none of the three is load-bearing for the parts just listed.

Refuter lens: M1 (fixed terminating procedure, no search/budget/solver), M10
(checking cost as a degree; edit stability), M7 (locally repairable rejection),
M8 (spec tokens; count the constructs), M9 (obvious shape of P5/P6; surviving
backend facts), R15 (generics, closures, nominals in P16).

Target: [`candidate-reference-refined.md`](candidate-reference-refined.md),
2026-09-16.

Evidence used, by path:
`research/experiments/proof-use-cost/baseline-2026-09-14.tsv` (growing family
31,013 → 169,404 → 1,693,329 µs at N = 16/32/64; source bytes 1452 → 2812 →
5532 — the checking-cost curve M10(e) calls red);
`research/experiments/blind-writer/2026-08-28/REPORT.md` (§6.2: 34 of 41
`len()` rebinds exist only because `ENT-5` kills at a whole-parameter
footprint; §5: **120 `region` blocks**, 39/28/22/16/15 across five programs;
§6.3: three of six diagnostics are coordinate-only, `OWN-6` among them);
`research/experiments/scoped-alias-channel/RESULTS.md` (the retired channel:
8 vector adds / 0 guards / 121 asm lines against rust-obvious 65 / 29 / 2132,
and its own statement of the ground for the fact).

## 1. Findings

Severity: **fatal** = a hazard is admitted, or a requirement is violated in a
way the candidate did not declare. **serious** = a program verdict is wrong, a
stated cost is understated, or a needed mechanism is unnamed. **minor** =
wording.

| # | Sev | Concerns | Finding | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | **fatal** | P5, P16, R4(b), D1 | **The path grammar has no indirection step.** §2.1's steps are `.field`, `[literal]`, `[proved index]`, `[proved range]`. Every derivation nevertheless names storage reached *through a loaded pointer*: `'v.buf[i]` (P1), `'v.buf` (P4), `'s.a[i]` (P5), `'C[k]` (P11), `'P[a].next` (P3). The ladder's own notation has `ptr_of(deref(b).x)` at Step 1; this candidate dropped `deref` and then leans on the omission: P5 accepts with "distinctness by FIELD STEP of one resolved path — no proof obligation". A field step proves the two *pointer slots* `'s.a` and `'s.b` distinct; it does not prove their referents distinct. If a column field holds a reference rather than an owning buffer — and P16 makes `Cols<E>` generic over the column type, so `E = ref<shared mut,'q,[u64]>` is an instance — the model emits `!alias.scope`/`noalias` between two accesses to the same storage. That is exactly R4(b)'s forbidden move ("never inequality of identity names") and it admits an aliasing/ordering hazard at the backend. | Add a deref step whose distinctness is decided by the pointee's existential brand or by the affine single-owner rule; restrict field-step distinctness to *owning* fields. This is what the measured channel actually used (RESULTS.md: "`buffer<T>` is affine single-owner … two distinct live buffer values never overlap"). |
| F2 | **fatal** | M1, M10, P8, P4, P11 | **Condition terms import an unnamed decision procedure and an exponential representation.** §2.2 admits any fact as `if c then f₁ else f₂`; §2.4 makes that the join rule. §4.1 then claims M1 **met** and lists five families: path normalization, the four-ordering range family, index disequality, backward last-use liveness, finite origin sets. Term entailment is not among them. But P8's accepting line — `if c { use(b) } else { use(a) }  // each arm's term discharges against the arm's own condition` — is a propositional entailment `c ⊢ term = Init` over source-bound conditions. Over *d* sequential diamonds each touching one path, the term is `if c_d then T_{d-1} else U_{d-1}` with both sub-terms carried, so size *S(d) = 2·S(d−1)+1 = O(2^d)* unless hash-consing is specified (it is not), and deciding the entailment on a DAG representation is propositional satisfiability. M1(a) requires a specified terminating procedure with a stated bound; M10(a) says never exponential (HIS-D0-11). Neither is declared violated. | Restrict terms to one level whose arm condition is *syntactically* the enclosing branch's condition, discharge by syntactic match only, and state that bound; otherwise fall to the meet and reject. Then re-derive P8. |
| F3 | **fatal** | R7(a), M10, M8, P11 | **`freeze` is program-wide and one-way but is absent from the interface vocabulary.** §2.2 makes `freeze('p)` a per-path fact; §2.3 makes it a one-way transition; §2.1's table gives a `Frozen` path a **program-wide** contents fact and `!invariant.load`. §2.5 enumerates what a signature states — occupancy, backings, returned origin sets and modes, existential results, footprints, outcome-routed states, resource effects — and **freeze is not in the list**, nor in §4.3's writer-cost table. P11's `get(k)` performs the freeze inside a callee and returns a reference whose reader depends on it. So a caller's facts change through a callee with no clause saying so (R7(a) violated), and deleting one `freeze` token flips the verdict of every reader of that path in every declaration, with no signature to pin the reach — M10's edit-stability clause, claimed "bounded … because signatures pin the interface", fails on the one fact that is not in a signature. | Add a freeze clause to the R7 vocabulary and to §4.3, and charge it at M8. |
| F4 | **fatal** | M2(ii), P11, R1 | **P11 queries an erased fact at a runtime index.** The derivation is `get(k): if is_hole('C[k]) { put(…); freeze('C[k]) }`. `occupancy` is a checker fact erased before lowering (§2.7); `k` is a runtime key. Either (i) the compiler materializes a per-slot discriminant so `is_hole` can run — bookkeeping state the source did not bind, refused by M2(ii); or (ii) the writer binds the tag as data (`Slot = Empty \| Live(V)`, as P3 does), in which case `put` can no longer require static `Hole(T)`, and `freeze('C[k])` happens on one arm of a runtime branch so the join carries `Frozen ⊓ Open = Open` — the return value is not on a Frozen path and the whole `!invariant.load` payoff evaporates. Neither horn is declared. | Re-derive P11 with a writer-bound `Slot` enum and *withdraw* the Frozen payoff, or restrict `freeze` to statically-resolved paths and state that lazily-filled caches are outside it. |
| F5 | **fatal** | M1, M9, P6 | **P6's partition needs multiplication monotonicity, which no named family decides.** The derivation cites "the fixed four-ordering family (s >= 0 => s*w + s <= s*w')". That is not an ordering comparison between two linear terms: it multiplies an unknown stride by an unknown worker index and needs `w < w' ∧ s ≥ 0 ⇒ s·w + s ≤ s·w'`, i.e. monotonicity of multiplication. Worse, PAR-2 needs it for *all* pairs `w ≠ w'`, a universally quantified statement, where the index-disequality family decides concrete pairs. M1 is claimed met with the five-family list; this family is absent. P6 is one of M9's two named fast-shape programs. | Name a linear-arithmetic-with-monotonicity family and state its bound, or require one written `use` step per partition — and then withdraw P6's "no worker count appears beyond k". |
| F6 | **fatal** | R9, M7, P7, P3, P17 | **`shared·mut`'s loss is not confined to R4.** §2.1 says a `shared·mut` path's contents facts are "killed by any may-overlapping write"; W2 calls this "degrades facts, never rules", and R9 is scored **met** because "the only loss is the R4 facts on exactly those paths". In a language where partial operations are admitted only by a fact (R11, P17), a killed `i < len(v)` is a **rejection**, not slowness. And the kill is not local: §2.1 says *may-overlapping*, and P3 shows that an unproved index step degrades the path to its root (`'P[?]` → `'P`), so one `shared·mut` reference into a container kills contents facts for the whole container. The repair named by the diagnostic would be "stop using this mode" — a global restructuring, which M7(a) forbids as the only fix. | State that `shared·mut` forfeits domain facts as well as distinctness facts, score R9 partial, and supply a local repair (a written `use` re-establishing the domain after each shared write). |
| F7 | **fatal** | R15(a), P16, M8 | **P16 is not expressible in the stated model.** Three gaps in four lines of pseudocode: (i) `fn map_nodes<'g,T>(g: …, f: fn(ref<shared,'e,T>) -> T)` leaves `'e` **unbound** — there is no higher-ranked path binder (`for<'e>`) anywhere in §2.1–§2.6; (ii) function types carry no footprint row, so the callee's `writes`/`reads` for `f` cannot be stated and the caller cannot judge the call (R7); (iii) `writes('g[_].data)` uses a **wildcard step `[_]`**, a fifth step kind that §2.1's list does not contain and whose intersection rule with a `[proved index]` step is unstated. R15's declared cost is about *storing* closures ("second-class unless the storing type is parameterized"); the inability to *take* one is not declared. | Add `for<'…>` binders and footprint rows to function types, name the wildcard step and its may-overlap rule, and price all three at M8. |
| S1 | serious | M10 | **The checking cost is understated and its measure is wrong.** §4.1 says "Per-statement work is quadratic in live paths … the ceiling is plausible but unmeasured". Live paths at a statement are Θ(program size) — the source mints a path at every field and index expression. Quadratic per statement × Θ(n) statements is already **cubic in program size**, i.e. at M10's ceiling with no margin, *before* adding (a) residual-footprint comparison (`'v.buf \ {i,j}` needs pairwise index disequality, O(k²) per comparison, nested inside the O(paths²) scan), (b) origin-set judgments ("judged once through EVERY origin"), and (c) F2's terms. M10(a) also bounds "total work per declaration at most quadratic in **written proof steps**" — this candidate's dominant cost driver is paths, which the writer never writes, so a declaration with zero written steps can carry quadratic-to-cubic work. The measured baseline is already red at a *coarser* granularity: proof-use-cost `growing` runs 31,013 → 169,404 → 1,693,329 µs for 1452 → 2812 → 5532 source bytes (exponent ≈ 2.6–3.4). Per-path facts multiply that constant and the exponent's base. | State a bound per family (residual subtraction, claim overlap, origin-set judgment, term compare) as M10(b) requires, and re-run the pinned bundle with per-path facts before calling the ceiling plausible. |
| S2 | serious | M9 | **M9 is scored "met (as far as measurable)" on a row whose status is "unmeasurable on the current compiler".** The supporting numbers (8 adds / 0 guards / 121 lines vs 65 / 29 / 2132) come from the retired `scoped-alias-channel` prototype, and M9(e) already records that this class of evidence "disclaims that the fact channels caused the win". The candidate also mis-attributes the ground: RESULTS.md derives the disjointness from `buffer<T>` being **affine single-owner** in its own allocation (plus `&uniq` for the struct memory), not from "the resolved place of the field reached through the exclusive reference". §1's D1×D2 coherence claim rests on that mis-attribution, and F1 is its consequence. | Score M9 *unmeasured*, and re-state the D1×D2 join on affine owner identity plus existential brands. |

The obvious shape gets them only because the writer writes the loop bound as the minimum of the eight lengths — the measured kernel is described in RESULTS.md as "loop bounded by the imin of all lengths". ## 2. Program verdicts overturned

### P5 — "accepted as required … zero writer annotation beyond the row" → **accepted with two stated costs, and unsound as derived under P16**

```text
fn kernel<'s>(s: ref<excl mut,'s,Cols>) writes('s.a,'s.b) reads('s.c..'s.h)
  for i in 0..n {
     s.a[i] = f(s.a[i], s.c[i], s.d[i])
                              // REJECT as written: `s.c[i]` is a partial operation (R11/P17).
                              //   Missing facts i < len('s.c), i < len('s.d), i < len('s.a).
                              //   Nothing in the signature supplies them.
     s.b[i] = g(s.b[i], s.e[i], s.f[i], s.g[i], s.h[i])
                              // REJECT: five more domains, same reason.
  }
  --- repaired, and this is the shape that was actually measured ---
  for i in 0..imin(len('s.a),…,len('s.h)) { … }
                              // accept: eight domains discharged from one written bound.
                              //   COST 1: the bound is writer annotation beyond the row, and
                              //   it is eight conjuncts wide -- the interface is linear in columns
                              //   although R15's parameter metric reads 1.  (S3)
  --- the distinctness fact, re-derived ---
  scope('s.a[i]) noalias scope('s.b[i])
                              // REJECT the stated ground: "distinctness by FIELD STEP".
                              //   A field step separates the SLOTS 's.a and 's.b.  The loads are
                              //   at the referents.  With no deref step in the grammar (F1) the
                              //   model cannot distinguish "field holding an owned buffer" from
                              //   "field holding a reference".
  Cols<E> with E = ref<shared mut,'q,[u64]>      // P16 makes this instance legal
     s.a[i] and s.b[i]        // ADMITS A HAZARD: both resolve to 'q, and the model emits noalias
                              //   between them.  R4(b): distinctness is never name inequality.
  --- sound ground, which the measurement actually used ---
  's.a and 's.b are affine single-owner buffers, each its own allocation
                              // accept: element ranges disjoint by owner identity / brand, not by
                              //   the field step.  COST 2: the fact is unavailable for reference-
                              //   typed columns, so P16's generic instantiation loses it.
```

### P6 — "accepted as required" → **not accepted by any named family**

```text
for w in 0..k { helper(slice_mut(out, w*s, (w+1)*s), input) }
   need: for all w != w', [w*s, w*s+s) ∩ [w'*s, w'*s+s) = empty
   step 1: w < w' and s >= 0  =>  w*s + s <= w'*s
                              // REJECT: this is monotonicity of multiplication by an unknown.
                              //   The "fixed four-ordering range family" compares two linear
                              //   terms; it does not multiply an inequality by a symbolic s.
   step 2: the claim is quantified over all pairs (w, w')
                              // REJECT: index disequality decides a named pair.  PAR-2's
                              //   injective element map covers i |-> [i]; it does not cover
                              //   w |-> [w*s, w*s+s) without step 1.
   --- repaired ---
   use monotone_mul(s, w, w') for each pair       // O(k^2) written steps, or
   name a monotonicity family with a stated bound // an addition to M1's five-family list
                              // either way, "no worker count appears beyond k" fails: the
                              //   worker structure re-enters as written steps or as a new family.
```

### P7 — "accepted with a stated cost … the R4 fact loss on `'A` and on nothing else" → **accepted with an acceptance loss on later, unrelated statements**

```text
p = &shared mut 'A ; q = &shared mut 'A       // accept, as stated
… take/put/replace/free lines …               // accept, as stated -- the occupancy half is right
--- what the cost line omits ---
use i < len('A.v) ; y = 'A.v[i]               // accept here
write(q, …)                                   // a may-overlapping shared write
y2 = 'A.v[i]                                  // REJECT: the domain fact i < len('A.v) was killed
                                              //   with every other contents fact on a path that
                                              //   may overlap 'A.  This is a RULE outcome (R11),
                                              //   not a speed outcome, contradicting W2's
                                              //   "degrades facts, never rules".
repair?                                       // the diagnostic can name "prove i < len('A.v)",
                                              //   but the writer must re-establish it after EVERY
                                              //   shared write, and if the index step degraded to
                                              //   the root ('A[?] -> 'A, P3's rule) there is no
                                              //   sub-path left to re-establish against.  The
                                              //   only general fix is to change the mode --
                                              //   non-local, which M7(a) forbids as the only fix.
```

### P8 — "accepted as required" → **acceptance rests on an unnamed and exponential procedure**

```text
if c { free(a) } else { free(b) }
join: occupancy('a) = if c then Ended else Init            // a term, per §2.2
if c { use(b) } else { use(a) }
                                   // the accept requires deciding  !c  |-  (if c then Ended else Init) = Init
                                   // REJECT the stated ground: this is propositional entailment over
                                   //   source-bound conditions.  M1's family list (path normalization,
                                   //   four-ordering ranges, index disequality, backward liveness,
                                   //   finite origin sets) contains no such family.
--- the scaling the derivation never shows ---
if c1 { free(a) } else { … } ; if c2 { use(a) } else { free(a) } ; … d diamonds
                                   // term size S(d) = 2*S(d-1) + 1 = O(2^d) with no hash-consing
                                   //   rule stated, and entailment on the shared DAG is SAT.
                                   // M10: "never exponential" (HIS-D0-11).  M1: no stated bound.
--- what survives without terms ---
join by meet: Hole ⊓ Init = ⊥                              // P8's FIRST and LAST blocks still accept
if c { free(a) } else { free(b) } ; if c { use(b) } else { use(a) }
                                   // REJECT under the meet: 'a is Ended ⊓ Init.
                                   // So either the term family is named, bounded and paid for at
                                   //   M8, or P8's middle line is refused and the writer must
                                   //   restructure into one branch.
```

### P11 — "accepted with a stated cost (the writer writes the `freeze`)" → **rejected as derived; accepted only without the `Frozen` payoff**

```text
cache: own [Slot<V>; N] in 'C
get(k): if is_hole('C[k]) { … }
                                   // REJECT: `occupancy` is erased (§2.7) and k is a runtime key,
                                   //   so `is_hole` is a runtime query of a checker fact.
                                   //   Horn 1: the compiler materializes a discriminant --
                                   //           refused by M2(ii) (bookkeeping the source did not bind).
                                   //   Horn 2: the writer binds the tag as data (P3's Slot enum) --
                                   //           then the next line fails:
        put(&excl mut 'C[k], compute(k))
                                   // REJECT under horn 2: `put` requires static occupancy Hole(T)
                                   //   (§2.3) and the writer's tag is not that fact.
        freeze('C[k])              // performed on ONE arm of a runtime branch
  return &shared 'C[k]
                                   // REJECT the Frozen claim: the join of the two arms carries
                                   //   freeze = Frozen on the then-edge and Open on the else-edge;
                                   //   `is_hole(…)` is not a captured immutable value, so §2.4's
                                   //   term rule does not apply and the meet gives Open.
                                   //   No program-wide contents fact, no !invariant.load.
--- and the interface hole ---
get's signature states occupancy, backings, origin set, footprints … but §2.5 lists NO freeze clause,
   so even a statically-indexed freeze inside a callee is invisible to the caller (F3, R7(a)).
```

### P16 — "accepted with a stated cost (closures second-class)" → **rejected: not expressible**

```text
fn map_nodes<'g,T>(g: ref<excl mut,'g,Pool<Node<T>>>, f: fn(ref<shared,'e,T>) -> T)
     writes('g[_].data)
                                   // REJECT (i): 'e is unbound.  The binder list is <'g,T>.  A path
                                   //   parameter occurring in a function-typed parameter needs a
                                   //   higher-ranked binder (for<'e>); §2.1-§2.6 define none.
                                   // REJECT (ii): the model gives no footprint row to a function
                                   //   TYPE, so what `f` writes is unstated and the body cannot be
                                   //   checked once for all instances (R15(a)).
                                   // REJECT (iii): `[_]` is a fifth step kind absent from §2.1.
--- and if [_] is admitted with may-overlap semantics ---
caller: use a < cap ; x = read('g[a].data) ; map_nodes(g, f) ; y = read('g[a].data)
                                   // REJECT the second read's contents facts: writes('g[_].data)
                                   //   may-overlaps 'g[a].data, so every element fact dies at the
                                   //   call.  The monomorphic version keeps them.  R15(a)'s
                                   //   "facts cross abstraction boundaries" fails at exactly the
                                   //   program R15(e) names.
let h = |slice| helper(slice, input)
                                   // REJECT: same as (ii) -- the closure's type must carry
                                   //   writes('d) reads('i) for P6's caller to judge the call, and
                                   //   closure types have no row.  The declared cost ("second-class
                                   //   when STORED") does not cover being PASSED.
```

### P3 — verdict "accepted with a stated cost (one `use` step per insert)" → **cost understated; the step needs an unnamed family**

```text
invariant links_live(pool)                  // a predicate over every slot of the pool
… four link writes …                        // each kills it: its support IS the links (correct)
use links_live_after_insert(n,a,b)          // "one written step per insert"  [the stated cost]
                                   // REJECT the cost accounting: verifying this step means deriving
                                   //   a quantified conclusion (for all slots s: link(s) live) from
                                   //   premises about four named slots.  That needs instantiation
                                   //   or induction -- no such family is in M1's list, and its
                                   //   measure is the pool's slot count, a RUNTIME quantity, which
                                   //   M10 does not admit as a degree.
                                   // Honest cost: either the invariant is restricted to the paths
                                   //   the footprint names (and then it is not "stated once and
                                   //   reused", so R6(e)'s P3 clause is failed outright), or the
                                   //   family is named, bounded and charged at M8 and M10.
```

### P2 — verdict "accepted as required" → **accepted as written; not accepted as scaled**

```text
b1 = alloc(…); b2 = alloc(…); b3 = alloc(…)     // accept: three SITES, three brands
par { fill(b1); fill(b2); fill(b3) }            // accept, as stated
--- the shape an arena is actually used in ---
for i in 0..k { blocks[i] = alloc(&excl mut 'A.M, 64) }
par_for i { fill(blocks[i]) }
                                   // REJECT: one allocation site mints one static brand, so
                                   //   blocks[3] and blocks[4] carry the SAME identity and the
                                   //   footprints are not disjoint.  "Disjoint by formation"
                                   //   is a per-site rule; per-iteration freshness needs an
                                   //   index-parameterized brand family that is not named,
                                   //   not bounded, and not charged.
```

---

## 3. What would change my ranking

Three of the seven fatals are repairs to the *text*, not to the family: F3
(put freeze in the vocabulary), F7 (add `for<'…>` binders and rows on function
types) and F4 (withdraw P11's Frozen payoff). F1 is a repair to D1 that makes
the candidate *stronger* and re-aligns it with the only measured channel the
project has. F2, F5 and F6 are load-bearing: terms, the range family and
`shared·mut` are each a place where the candidate bought a program verdict with
a procedure it did not name, and each one lands on M1 — the row this candidate
scores met and the row the whole design is supposed to be organized around.
Under this lens the candidate's own M8 row is not its worst score; **M1 is**,
and M1 is scored met.

[candidate-reference-refined.md](candidate-reference-refined.md). Method: P1,
P2, P4, P7, P9 and P13 re-derived line by line from the candidate's §2 model
text alone, with no charitable completion. Where the model text is silent, both
readings are taken and the worse one is reported (the brief's default-to-report
rule). Requirement text is VERDICT-D0 §2; couplings §4; ladder MECHANISM-MAP §3.

The candidate's own declared violations (M8, and the costs at P3/P4/P7/P9/P16)
are not re-charged here. Everything below is either undeclared or contradicts
the candidate's own text.

## 2. Program verdicts overturned

### P4 — overturned: **not accepted**, or accepted only with unsound emissions

The candidate's headline for this program is "the rejection moved from `push`
to the read". My derivation, using only §2.1's mode table and §2.2's definition
of *usable*:

```text
c = Cursor<'v.buf> { at: ref<shared,'v.buf,[u64]>, i: 0 }
                                     // accept: struct carries the path parameter
a = c.read()                         // REJECT (S1): no line establishes i < len;
                                     //   the candidate asserts "i < len fact live" with no support
use 0 < len(v) ; a = c.read()        // accept
push(&excl mut 'v, 5)
   -- reading (a): claims are tested over the containment cone (F1's fix)
                                     // REJECT: the excl·mut claim on 'v spans 'v.buf, where the
                                     //   cursor's shared claim is live to its endpoint at b = c.read()
                                     //   §2.2: "usable is derived (claims has no overlapping stronger
                                     //   claim)" -- the excl claim IS the overlapping stronger claim
   -- reading (b): a shared claim is not a claim for the conflict test
                                     // accept -- but then §2.1's excl·mut row "Other usable paths may
                                     //   exist: no" is false of an accepted program, and param `noalias`
                                     //   on push's 'v is a fact untrue in an admitted execution (R4(a)),
                                     //   as is `readonly` on any shared·const parameter whose storage an
                                     //   excl sibling parameter writes during the same call
b = c.read()                         // under (b) and the §2.5 spelling of the reallocation clause
                                     //   (`occupancy('v.buf0) = Ended`), 'v.buf is untouched: ACCEPT,
                                     //   reading the freed old buffer -- R1(a)(ii)  [F5]
                                     // under the §2.3 spelling: reject, as the candidate claims
free(v) ; c.read()                   // reject only if F1's downward closure exists; §2.3's free writes
                                     //   occupancy('v) and the cursor reads occupancy('v.buf)
```

Verdict I record: **P4 is undecided under the model as written**, and every
completion of it costs the candidate something it did not declare — either its
central claim about `push`, or `noalias`/`readonly`, or R1(a)(ii) at the second
read. The requirement P4 tests (R1(e), R8a(e): "validity decided by state and
proof, not by a borrow that blocks `push`") is therefore **not shown met**.

### P2 — overturned: **not accepted as required**

```text
b1 = alloc(&excl mut 'A.M, 64)       // accept, but the freshness clause is unbacked  [F4]
b2, b3 = alloc(...)                  // same
par { fill(b1); fill(b2); fill(b3) } // NOT PROVED: disjointness of 'B1,'B2,'B3 rests on freshness of
                                     //   brand names; R4(b)/C3 refuse inequality of identity names as
                                     //   a ground, and no stated obligation makes formation imply
                                     //   disjointness.  Under R5 this is a non-erasable-grade failure
                                     //   only at spawn/join; at PAR-1 it degrades to sequential (M5)
p2 = &shared 'B2[0]                  // accept
free(&excl mut 'A.M, move b2)        // accept: occupancy('B2) := Ended per §2.3
read(p2)                             // ACCEPT under the model as written  [F1]:
                                     //   p2's path is 'B2[0]; §2.3's free wrote occupancy('B2) and
                                     //   §2.2 defines occupancy per path with no ancestor closure.
                                     //   occupancy('B2[0]) was Init and nothing changed it.
                                     //   >>> use after free; R1(a)(ii) admitted <<<
b4 = alloc(&excl mut 'A.M, 32)       // accept; 'B4 fresh -- and, absent F4's obligation, nothing
                                     //   forbids 'B4 from overlapping the still-live 'B1
read(p2)                             // ACCEPT again, same reason
```

P2's stated required property — "a pointer into freed `b2` is refused even
though its address is reused by `b4`" — is the exact line the model as written
accepts. This is the one refusal the whole D1 choice exists to deliver, and it
is delivered by a closure rule the candidate never wrote. With F1's fix it
lands; without it the program is a counterexample to R1.

### P13 — overturned: **accepted with an undeclared R1/R11 gap, and inexpressible for an affine element**

```text
pool: declared relocatable-by-a-third-party
h = handle(pool, obj)                // accept: an index, not a path
p = pointer_of(h)                    // reject at formation -- agreed, and this is the required refusal
pool.compact()                       // accept -- but with WHAT footprint?  The model states none.
                                     //   If 'pool whole: every occupancy and contents fact on 'pool[..]
                                     //   dies, and P3's par_map and traversal facts die with it (R6).
                                     //   If narrower: the narrowing is a fact nobody stated.
read(pool[h])                        // REJECT, not accept: after compact, nothing in the model says
                                     //   occupancy('pool[h]) = Init, and R11 has no discharge for
                                     //   "h is a live handle".  The candidate's ground -- "backing('pool)
                                     //   Current" -- is a fact about the container, not about the slot
                                     //   the read names.
                                     // Additionally: with interior reference formation refused over this
                                     //   backing, `read` can only copy out, so the line does not exist
                                     //   for a non-Copy element type -- P13's shape is unwritable there.
```

The R8a half of P13 (interior pointers and third-party relocation are mutually
exclusive) is met and met early, at formation. The rest of the program is not
derived, and the candidate's "accepted as required" overstates it.

### P1 — partially overturned: two accepted lines are wrong as written

```text
(pi,pj) = split_mut(v,i,j)           // accept ONLY under a capture rule for [i] the model lacks  [F3]
write(pi,1) ; write(pj,2)            // accept
i = j                                // ACCEPTED: no rule bars it
                                     //   >>> under the re-read semantics, pi and pj now name one place
                                     //       while both excl·mut claims are live; the PAR-1 grant below
                                     //       becomes a race and the emitted scopes are false  <<<
par { write(pi,1) ; write(pj,2) }    // accept only if [i],[j] were captured at the split
x = v[k]                             // reject: missing k != i, k != j -- agreed, and ALSO missing
                                     //   k < len(v), which the candidate's accept line below omits
use k != i ; use k != j ; x = v[k]   // REJECT, not accept: R11's bound is undischarged  [S1]
use k != i ; use k != j ; use k < len(v) ; x = v[k]   // accept
push(v, x)                           // accept after both endpoints
```

The candidate's P1 cost line ("no runtime check: the proof is the writer's
`i != j`") understates by one `use` step per element read and by whatever the
capture rule of F3 costs the writer.

### P7 — partially overturned: the `shared·mut` shape is unsound as specified

The eight lines the candidate derives are individually right **given F1's
closure rule**. The program's own premise — two live writable references to one
place — is what makes the missing rule bite, so the refutation belongs here:

```text
a: own S in 'A                       // S = { x: u64, y: u64 }
p = &shared mut 'A ; q = &shared mut 'A
                                     // accept: bounded shared-write (the candidate's P7 opening)
px = split(p).x                      // accept: mints ref<excl mut,'A.x>;
                                     //   §2.3: "the parent's claim is suspended on those sub-paths only"
                                     //   -- singular "the parent's claim": p is suspended, q is NOT.
                                     //   Nothing in the model suspends the other holder.
*q = S{ x: 9, y: 9 }                 // ACCEPT under the model as written: the resolved path is 'A;
                                     //   claims('A) = {p,q}, both shared·mut, compatible;
                                     //   px's excl·mut claim lives in claims('A.x) and is never consulted
read(px)                             // accept -- and px's mode licenses `noalias` and a per-load
                                     //   !alias.scope on 'A.x, both false of this execution
                                     //   >>> R4(a) soundness violated <<<
v = take(p) ; take(q)                // ACCEPT under the model as written: §2.3 states no precondition
                                     //   for take, so the affine value is produced twice  [S11]
```

The candidate's `shared·mut` price is stated as "the R4 fact loss on `'A` **and
on nothing else**" (W2, C5). That is false as written: the loss reaches any
`excl` claim minted beneath a `shared·mut` path, so the D6 "structural gift"
("two `excl` parameters are distinct by the exclusivity rule itself — no clause
needed") is sound only after F1's fix forbids the shape above.

### P9 — verdict stands, cost misattributed

`drain`, the `pick` origin set and the over-suspension are derived correctly.
Two corrections: `reserve`'s exit clause as written in §2.5 is the spelling that
admits F5, and the over-suspension charged as an unavoidable cost is removable

P5 and P6 are re-derived without a finding: field-step distinctness under one
`excl·mut` reference and the four-ordering range family carry them, the emitted
facts are the ones EVIDENCE §B.2 records as actually measured, and the writer

# Critique of `refinement-heap` — lens COST, DETERMINISM AND THE WRITER

Refuter lens: M1 (is every judgment a fixed terminating procedure with no
search, budget or solver?), M10 (checking cost as a degree in program size and
written steps; does a one-token edit reopen distant verdicts?), M7 (is every
rejection locally repairable from the diagnostic?), M8 (how many spec tokens
does the vocabulary need; count the constructs), M9 (does the obvious shape of
P5 and P6 stay fast; what backend facts survive?), R15 (does it survive
generics, closures and nominals in P16, or explode in signature size?).

Target: `candidate-refinement-heap.md` (2026-09-16).
Requirement list: VERDICT-D0 §2; couplings §4; premises §5; owner interim
positions §7. Hazard ladder: MECHANISM-MAP §3. Programs: PROGRAMS.md P1–P19.
Measured evidence used: `research/experiments/proof-use-cost/` and
`research/investigations/proof-certificate-architecture/CHECKING-COST.md`
(proof-use-cost scaling), `research/experiments/blind-writer/2026-08-28/REPORT.md`
(the writer taxes), EVIDENCE-mechanism-survey §B and
`research/experiments/scoped-alias-channel/` (the retired alias channel).

Severity key, as set by the debate: **fatal** = a hazard is admitted, or a
requirement is violated in a way the candidate did not declare; **serious** = a
program verdict is wrong, a stated cost is understated, or a needed mechanism
is unnamed; **minor** = wording.

| **F1** | fatal | M1; §2.3 decision procedure | **The stated closure does not terminate.** Rules (b) "addition of two constraints" and (c) "scaling by a positive literal" generate unboundedly many *distinct constraints* over a fixed monomial set: from `1 ≤ x` derive `2 ≤ 2x`, `3 ≤ 3x`, `4 ≤ 4x`, … and every positive combination of any two of them. "Termination is structural (the monomial set never grows)" is a non-sequitur — the closure iterates the **constraint** set, not the monomial set, and the coefficient space is infinite. An implementation terminates only by (i) retaining one canonical constraint per monomial pair, i.e. a difference-bound matrix, which cannot express the three-monomial goals P5/P6 need (`w·s + s ≤ w'·s`), or (ii) an iteration count, which is exactly the budget M1(a) forbids. ## 2. Program verdicts overturned

Notation follows the ladder: per-line `accept` / `reject` comments with the
fact used. `Σ:` lines show the store index. Where I overturn, I give the
candidate's verdict, then my derivation, then the corrected verdict.

### P6 Range partition helper — **overturned**

Candidate: *"accepted as required — conditional on RF rule (d) being in the
fixed family"*, §4.4 charging the loop 1 line and per-statement 0.

The condition cannot be met as written. Take the candidate's own goal.

```text
for w in 0..k
  invariant 'out@[0, w*s) ↦ Owned(u8) ∧ 'out@[w*s, n) ↦ Hole(u8)
{
  helper(slice_of(out, w*s, w*s + s), input)
}
// R5(a)(i) goal for iterations w ≠ w', say w+1 ≤ w':
//   [w*s, w*s+s) ∩ [w'*s, w'*s+s) = ∅
//   normalizes to   w·s + s ≤ w'·s
// hypotheses: 0 ≤ s ; w+1 ≤ w'
// monomials present in hypotheses ∪ goal: { s, w, w', w·s, w'·s }
```

Now apply rule (d), `0 ≤ a ∧ b ≤ c ⇒ a·b ≤ a·c`, at `a = s`, `b = w+1`,
`c = w'`:

```text
premise 1: 0 ≤ s                      // present
premise 2: w+1 ≤ w'                   // present
conclusion: s·(w+1) ≤ s·w'
// the conclusion's left side is not a term of the fragment until it is
// distributed to  s·w + s , which requires the product monomial s·w
//   — if (d) is read over TERMS, the rule has just admitted the product of a
//     degree-1 term with a degree-2 term (degree 3 in general: a = x·y,
//     b = z+1 gives x·y·z), so the monomial set GROWS and §2.3's termination
//     argument ("the monomial set never grows") is false.  reject M1.
//   — if (d) is read over VARIABLES (a, b, c program variables), then b = w+1
//     is not an admissible instantiation, no closure rule relates w+1 ≤ w'
//     to s·w + s ≤ s·w', and the goal is NOT reached.  reject the goal.
```

There is no third reading: the candidate's own §6.3 table asserts
`0 ≤ s ∧ w < w' ⇒ [w·s, w·s+s) ∩ [w'·s, w'·s+s) = ∅` is "yes, by rule (d)",
which requires the term reading, which the termination argument forbids.

Note also that even the term reading does not reach the goal in one step: from
`s·w + s ≤ s·w'` the checker must still commute `s·w` with `w·s` (fixed
monomial order handles this) and then apply rule (b). Fine — that part works.

**Corrected verdict: accepted only with one written step per loop.**

```text
for w in 0..k
  invariant 'out@[0, w*s) ↦ Owned(u8) ∧ 'out@[w*s, n) ↦ Hole(u8)
{
  use mul_mono(s, w, w')      // WRITTEN: 0 ≤ s ∧ w+1 ≤ w' ⇒ (w+1)·s ≤ w'·s
                              //   accept: the checker verifies the
                              //   instantiation; it did not find it
  helper(slice_of(out, w*s, w*s + s), input)   // accept, as before
}
```

Consequences the candidate must carry: §4.4's "per statement: nothing, …
P6: 0 given rule (d)" becomes 1 written step per range-partition loop; §6.3's
table loses its second row to the "no" column; and P6 stops being the program
that shows the fragment is free — the only remaining free multiplicative case
is degree-1. This matters because P6 is the candidate's evidence that the
bunched signature alone tells the caller what a worker writes.

### P3 Graph with back edges in a pool — **overturned**

Candidate: *"accepted as required. The invariant is stated once and reused"*.

```text
pool P of Node as 'p
invariant links : ∀s ∈ live. next(s) ∈ live ∧ prev(s) ∈ live
// reject [M1 / §2.3]: this is not an RF formula.
//   RF  φ ::= conjunction of atoms ;  atom a ::= t ⋈ t' | t ≡ k (mod M)
//   term t ::= Σ cᵢ·mᵢ + k ;  monomial m ::= x | x·y  (program variables)
//   `∀ s ∈ live` is a binder over a dynamic index set — RF is declared
//     quantifier-free, and §2.2 says "disjunction appears only as a guard
//     list"; there is no quantifier production at all.
//   `next(s)` and `prev(s)` are uninterpreted functions of the STORE, not
//     program variables; no monomial form admits them.
//   `∈ live` is a membership in a refined index set that varies with Σ; the
//     extent language R describes offsets, not a set of live slot indices
//     that `remove` mutates.

insert(n, a, b):
  set 'p@{a}.next = n    // accept: key is Owned; W = {'p@{a}.next}
  set 'p@{n}.prev = a    // accept
  set 'p@{n}.next = b    // accept
  set 'p@{b}.prev = n    // accept
  use links_insert(a, b, n)
  // reject [M1(b) / M3]: `links` is a ∀-statement over `live`.  Re-establishing
  //   it from four writes is not a lemma INSTANTIATION — the checker must know
  //   that the four writes changed the only slots whose link fields could have
  //   left the invariant, i.e. it must run a frame argument over a quantified
  //   predicate.  §2.3 says the checker "verifies the written instantiation
  //   without rediscovering it"; there is nothing here to instantiate, because
  //   there is no RF goal.
```

The R6 headline for P3 — "the invariant is stated once and reused", the thing
that makes the traverse loop free — therefore has no mechanism behind it. The
parallel map line survives on its own (`s ≠ s'` is an RF goal); the remove and
occupant lines survive. It is the *invariant* that does not.

**Corrected verdict: needs a mechanism.** P3 is accepted for distinctness and
for removal, and is *not* accepted for the structural invariant, which requires
the D7 family *predicate-based contracts: refinements and abstract predicates*
(quantified abstract predicates with a footprint and a fold/unfold or
frame-instantiation rule). That family is priced nowhere in §4.2's M8 row and
its instantiation rule must be shown decidable under M1 — which is the whole
difficulty separation logic's practitioners meet, and it is a *second*
decidable fragment, contradicting §1's coherence claim 4.

### P2 Arena with independently released blocks — **overturned in part**

Candidate: *"accepted as required, including R4's negative test and R2's
exactly-once accounting"*.

R2's accounting and the tombstone line are right and I do not contest them.
The parallel line is wrong.

```text
arena A as ('M metadata, 'S bytes)
b1 = alloc(A,64) as 'b1
  // ensures ∃'x. 'x ⊑ 'S ∧ 'x@[0,64) ↦ Hole ∧ bump' = bump+64
  // NOTE: the extent [0,64) is in 'x's OWN coordinates.  Nothing in this
  //   contract says WHERE in 'S those 64 bytes are.  `⊑` is declared
  //   "containment, not distinctness".
b2 = alloc(A,64) as 'b2      // same contract, fresh atom
b3 = alloc(A,64) as 'b3

fill(b1) ∥ fill(b2) ∥ fill(b3)
  // candidate: "accept R5(a)(i) … 'b1,'b2,'b3 are three distinct minting
  //   sites ⇒ pairwise distinct by construction, no arithmetic needed."
  // reject this derivation [R4, C3]:
  //   §4.1's R4 row states the distinctness relation is "RF extent-
  //   disjointness over the ⊑ containment structure, NEVER inequality of atom
  //   names".  The line above is exactly inequality of atom names.
  // and the shortcut admits a hazard:
  //   the arena is ordinary writer code — there is no privileged allocator in
  //   this language — so `alloc`'s body is checked once against the contract
  //   above.  A body that returns overlapping byte ranges (a free-list bug, a
  //   bump that does not advance on a size-0 request, two blocks carved from
  //   one recycled cell) satisfies that contract: it mints a fresh atom and
  //   asserts ⊑ 'S.  The checker then licenses fill(b1) ∥ fill(b2) over
  //   OVERLAPPING BYTES.  Ladder step 2's index disjointness — the first
  //   place the ladder says arithmetic is needed — never runs.
```

The repair is not cosmetic: it is what buys P2 back.

```text
b1 = alloc(A,64) as 'b1
  // ensures ∃'x. 'x ≍ 'S@[bump₀, bump₀+64) ∧ 'x@[0,64) ↦ Hole
  //          ∧ bump' = bump₀ + 64
  // accept: the block's extent inside the parent is now a fact
fill(b1) ∥ fill(b2)
  // goal  'S@[bump₀, bump₀+64) ∩ 'S@[bump₀+64, bump₀+128) = ∅
  // RF ⊨ by rule (a)+(b) from bump₀ + 64 ≤ bump₀ + 64     ⇒ accept
  //   — and this is one RF goal per pair, i.e. arithmetic after all
free(A, b2); b4 = alloc(A,32) as 'b4
  // 'b4's extent now comes from the free list, so the alloc contract must
  //   also carry the free list's disjointness obligation, which is a
  //   quantified statement over the free list — see P3: same missing family
```

**Corrected verdict: accepted only with an extent-carrying `alloc` contract;
as written, P2 admits overlapping parallel writes.** And the corrected form
costs what the candidate said it did not: one RF goal per block pair (k²/2 per
arena region), plus — for the free-list case — the same quantified-predicate
family P3 needs. The claim "no arithmetic needed" was the cost saving; it is
withdrawn.

### P5 Struct-of-arrays kernel — **cost overturned, verdict retained**

Candidate: *"accepted as required. The obvious shape is the fast shape … zero
writer annotation"*, §4.4 charging the loop 1 line.

Acceptance stands. Three costs do not.

```text
fn kernel(c: &Cols<u64>, n: u64)
   requires  ∀ κ ∈ bunch(c). κ@[0,n) ↦ Owned(u64)
   // (1) `∀ κ ∈ bunch(c)` is a BINDER.  RF is quantifier-free.  For a concrete
   //   record it expands to 8 conjuncts, so it is finite meta-syntax rather
   //   than a logical quantifier — acceptable, but it is a construct §2.3 does
   //   not contain and §4.2's M8 count does not list, and every requires,
   //   ensures and invariant using it expands 8-fold into the goal set.
{
  for i in 0..n
    invariant ∀ κ ∈ bunch(c). κ@[0,n) ↦ Owned(u64)     // "one written line"
  {
    set a[i] = f_wrap(a[i], c[i], d[i])
      // §2.4 write rule: "split R at δ; ι@{δ} ↦ Owned"
      // Σ after: 'a@{i} ↦ Owned ; 'a@([0,n)∖{i}) ↦ Owned      — TWO keys
    set b[i] = g_wrap(b[i], e[i], f[i], g[i], h[i])
      // Σ after: 'b@{i} ↦ Owned ; 'b@([0,n)∖{i}) ↦ Owned      — TWO keys
  }
  // back edge: must re-establish  'a@[0,n) ↦ Owned  from the two keys.
  // (2) reject [§2.4]: §2.4's table has a split row and no merge row.  §6.4
  //   states merge2 is a KERNEL FORM, and P1 calls it explicitly.  So either
  //   the writer writes two merges per iteration — §4.4's "P5: 1 line" is
  //   wrong — or the loop rule contains an automatic re-fusion whose normal
  //   form, determinism and cost are unstated, and §4.3's price list does not
  //   mention it.
}
// (3) R4 export: "eight `!alias.scope`s, one per column, on the loads".
//   reject as stated: an alias.scope list alone licenses nothing.  LangRef's
//   rule is a SUBSET TEST between one instruction's alias.scope list and
//   another's noalias list, within a domain.  To license "the load of a[i]
//   does not alias the store to b[i]" each load must carry
//     !alias.scope !{its own scope}   AND   !noalias !{the other seven}
//   plus a domain node.  That is 1 + 7 metadata operands per load, O(k²) per
//   loop body, and 16 columns in the measured addendum (guards 29→111 on the
//   Rust side, WF 183 asm lines).  §2.7 prices zero.
```

**Corrected verdict: accepted, with the writer cost raised from 1 line to
1 line plus a re-fusion rule the model does not state, and the R4 export
restated as per-load scope-plus-noalias-list metadata that is quadratic in the
column count.** The retired-channel evidence still supports the *shape* of the
win (0 runtime guards, 17x code size, time parity at n ≥ 32) — it does not
support "zero annotation" or "eight scopes".

### P4 Cursor over a growing vector — **cost overturned, verdict retained**

Candidate: *"accepted as required. Validity is decided by state and proof; the
stored pointer never blocks `push`."*

```text
let c = Cursor { at: ptr_of(v), i: 0 }
push(v, 5)
b = c.read()
  // reject: 'b's cell is guarded and the path condition entails neither arm.
  //   — correct, and the diagnostic is good.
// the named repair:
if len(v) < cap(v) {
  push(v,5); b = c.read()        // accept
} else {
  // the candidate's derivation stops here.  It must not:
  //   'b is Ended and the backing is a fresh 'b2, so `c : Cursor<'b>` is now a
  //   cursor over a tombstone.  The writer must re-form the cursor:
  push(v,5);
  let c2 = Cursor { at: ptr_of(v), i: c.i }   // accept: 'b2 is Owned
  b = c2.read()                                // accept
  // and every later use of the cursor must be written against c2, so the
  //   whole remaining body is duplicated or the two arms must rejoin on a
  //   guarded Cursor — which means the STRUCT's identity parameter becomes
  //   guarded, a case §2.2 does not cover (guards live on Σ cells, not on a
  //   value's type parameter).
}
```

**Corrected verdict: accepted, at the cost of a written capacity branch, a
re-formed cursor in the else arm, and an open question about how a guarded
identity parameter rejoins.** This is a per-push writer cost inside every loop
that pushes while a cursor is live; §4.4's "per statement: nothing" and M9's
"the obvious shape is the fast shape" both need it.

### P16 Abstraction over identities — **overturned to partial**

Candidate: *"accepted with a stated cost"*, the cost being the `∗`/`;` mark on
every record declaration, and R15's metric declared met.

```text
// (c) P6's helper as a closure
let h = |s: slice<'o,u8>| helper(s, input)
   // closure type: ∀'o. fn(slice<'o,u8>) -> ()  writes ('o @ extent)
   //   captures: input, with a capture row `reads ('in @ [0,m))`
for w in 0..k { h(slice_of(out, w*s, w*s+s)) }
   // accept for THIS use — but R15(a) quantifies over "closure-carrying code",
   //   not over closures used immediately at their binding site.
let jobs : array<Job, k> = [ Job { f: h, … }, … ]
   // reject [§2.6]: h's type carries a live capture row `reads ('in @ [0,m))`.
   //   Storing h means storing a value whose type mentions 'in, an identity
   //   bound in THIS declaration.  §2.6's ensures has `∃'c` for fresh storage;
   //   there is no existential PACKING form for an identity captured inside a
   //   stored value, and no unpack.  Cursor<'b> parameterises by hand over ONE
   //   identity known at the declaration site; a closure captures a set whose
   //   size is a property of the closure body.
   // and the size: a closure capturing j storages carries j identity binders
   //   and up to 2j effect-row entries in its type.
```

Against R15(e)'s metric — "parameters per interface ≤ **a stated function** of
the storages the callee touches (not a linear-in-parameters tautology)" — the
candidate writes "parameters are a function of the *bunched shape*, not of the
storages touched" and never states the function. For records that restatement
holds (P16(a), (b): one binder per argument). For closures it is false: the
capture row is linear in the captured storages, which is exactly the
linear-in-storages shape R15(e) was written to exclude.

```text
// (d) pick through a nominal
fn pick<N: Nominal>(c: bool, x: N, y: N) -> N
   ensures identities(result) ⊆ identities(x) ∪ identities(y)
   // reject as "no new vocabulary" [§1 claim 4]: `identities(·)` is a
   //   set-valued function on a type and `⊆` is a set relation.  RF has no
   //   set sort.  This is a SECOND decidable vocabulary (finite sets of
   //   identity names with union and inclusion), which is fine as a design
   //   but contradicts the tuple's central economy claim and is absent from
   //   the 12–16k M8 estimate.  P9's `'r ≍ 'x ∨ 'r ≍ 'y` is a third spelling
   //   of the same relation (a disjunction, which §2.3 forbids inside RF).
```

**Corrected verdict: partial.** The generic and record cases (a), (b) hold.
The closure case holds only for immediately-applied closures and has no stated
form for a stored one; the nominal case introduces an unnamed and unpriced
identity-set vocabulary; and R15's metric is declared met without the function
R15(e) demands being written.

---

## 3. What survives

I do not contest, and the candidate should keep:

- **P7.** The store-index shape genuinely makes "state is a property of the
  storage" fall out rather than be a rule, and the derivation is exact.
- **P8.** Guarded cells and rule J give the conditional-release case without a
  drop flag, and the rejection does name the differing path. (S7 is a
  determinism defect in the *normalizer*, not in the shape.)
- **P17.** Folding every partial-operation domain into the same goal language
  is the largest real M8 saving on the table, and the diagnostics are the best
  of the set.
- **P13.** The refusal is the requirement, and it falls out of `ends`.
- **P11.** Form A's rejection is correctly derived and correctly attributed to
  M2(ii); Form B is the honest answer.
- **The M8 and M10 self-declarations.** The candidate declares both violated
  rather than arguing them away, which is worth more than a tidier tuple that
  does not. My objection is that both declarations understate, not that they
  were withheld.

The decisive items are F1 and F2. The tuple's whole claim on M1 is "the
fragment is fixed, so acceptance is a total function of the bytes" — and the
procedure as specified is not a terminating procedure at all, while the one
rule that buys the flagship program contradicts the one argument offered for
termination. Everything else on this page is priceable; those two are the
candidate's own load-bearing sentence failing to hold.


# File: critique-refinement-heap-soundness.md

# Critique: `refinement-heap`, lens SOUNDNESS

Refuter lens: **soundness and the programs**. Scope: P1, P2, P4, P7, P9, P13
re-derived independently under the candidate *as written* (`candidate-refinement-heap.md`
§2 is the model; §3 is the candidate's own derivation); hazards R1–R3, R11, R12;
M2 clause (ii); unstated facts; couplings C1–C18 silently retuned.

Method: I took §2 as the complete rule set and §3 as a claim about it. Where §3
uses a fact §2 does not supply, I recorded it. Where §2's rule as written admits
a hazard, I built the smallest program that reaches it. Where the two disagree, I
followed §2, because §2 is the candidate.

Summary: **8 fatal, 10 serious, 5 minor.** The tuple's centre — Σ keyed by
`ι@R`, RF as the one vocabulary, `⊑` as containment, `;` as declared
coincidence, tombstone permanence — does not survive contact with P2, P7, P9 and
P13. The single most damaging defect is one word: §2.4's kill rule says
"RF-overlaps" where soundness needs "not provably disjoint", which is C2's two
exactness directions collapsed into one and which admits a division by zero in
an accepted program.

---

## 1. Findings table

| # | Sev | Program / requirement | Finding | Fix (one sentence) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **F1** | fatal | P9 (`drain`/`reserve` shape); R6, R11, M6(ii), M2(i), C2 | §2.4/§3 state the kill rule as "kills exactly the facts whose support **RF-overlaps** the written extent". `RF-overlaps` is a *provable-overlap* test. A held refinement whose support the checker cannot **prove** overlaps a callee's declared `writes` extent therefore **survives a call that wrote it**, and the stale refinement then discharges an R11 domain (§2). | Restate the kill test as the negation of the disjointness test — kill unless RF ⊨ support ∩ footprint = ∅ — and say so in both directions, as C2 demands ("R4 tolerates a missing *distinct*, R5 does not, R6 needs a may-write over-approximation"). |
| **F2** | fatal | P2; R4(a), R6, M6(ii) | `ι' ⊑ ι` is declared "containment, not distinctness" and is given **no coordinate relation**. `'b1@[0,64)` and `'S@[o,o+64)` are keys in two unrelated index spaces, so no RF goal relating them is even well-formed, so a write through `'b1` kills nothing keyed on `'S` and vice versa. Parent facts survive child writes. | Make `⊑` carry the offset map (`'b1 ⊑ 'S at base β`, β an RF term) so child and parent extents are comparable, and require every kill and every distinctness goal to be taken after translating through the chain of `⊑` edges. |
| **F3** | fatal | P7 (the candidate's own home case); R1(i), R9, C5 | `;` (may-coincide) has **no Σ rule**. Its only stated consequences are §2.7 (no R4 fact emitted) and R9's "kills widen". Nothing widens a *state change*: `take` through `'a` sets `'a@{δ}` to `Hole` and leaves `'b@{δ}` `Owned`. A callee with `groups ('a ; 'b)` called with one atom twice reads a hole. | Either require, for every `;` pair, that a class-changing operation on one member set the other to an explicit unknown cell (which the model must then add), or refuse `;` for any storage whose cell class the declaration changes. |
| **F4** | fatal | P2; R4(b), R5(a)(i), C3 | P2's `fill(b1) ∥ fill(b2) ∥ fill(b3)` is granted by "three distinct minting sites ⇒ pairwise distinct by construction, **no arithmetic needed**". There are not three sites: `alloc` is one declaration with one minting site, reached three times, and §2.4's `ensures ∃'x` confirms the atoms are existential per call, not per site. So the ground is **inequality of identity names**, which R4(b) and C3 forbid outright (and forbid naming P2 as the reason). The obligation the allocator must actually discharge — this block is disjoint from every previously carved block — is universally quantified and outside RF, and after `free(A,b2)` it needs the free-list's own quantified invariant. | Replace "site freshness" with an explicit existential-unpacking rule that obliges the *minting operation* to prove disjointness from the extents it has already carved, and state where that (quantified) obligation is discharged — an M3 axiom entry or a new RF extension, priced. |
| **F5** | fatal | P13 (`occ o`), P3; R1(ii) | §2.2: `Ended` is a "**permanent tombstone, no rule ever re-adds an entry for that key**". §2.4's slot-reuse row re-adds an entry for that key. The two rules are contradictory, and §2.1's pointer type is `ptr(ι, δ)` with **no occupant component**, so a pointer formed by the ordinary rule carries no occupant, names the reborn key, and is accepted after reuse. | Put the occupant in the key (`ι@R@o`) and in the pointer type as a mandatory component, delete the permanence clause, and re-derive P2's refusal from key inequality rather than from permanence. |
| **F6** | fatal | P13; R8a | `read(pool[h])` cannot be accepted. `h : handle('pool, idx)` names `'pool`, which `compact`'s `ends { 'pool }` tombstoned; §2.4 says of the one relocation rule the model has that "**pointer types are never rewritten**" and that refinements are transported "in Σ only". `ensures ∀ h. live(h) ⇒ h ↦ 'pool2` is a universally quantified **retyping of every live value of handle type**, a mechanism §2 never defines; and any retyping rule strong enough to transport `h` transports `p` too, which admits the dangling read P13 requires refused. | State the retyping as a typed, contract-visible *brand-transport* operation applied to a named, enumerable set of values (the pool's own handle table), so that it can be given to handles and withheld from interior pointers by construction — and price it, since it is the D8 fixup channel the candidate claims not to supply. |
| **F7** | fatal | P9 (`pick`); R1, R2, R7 | A class-changing operation through an existential origin has no stated Σ update. §2.5 forbids a Top cell ("No lattice, no Top"), so after `take(r)` with `'r ≍ 'x ∨ 'r ≍ 'y` the only completions are: set both to `Hole` (R2 double-accounting — one value taken, two holes to refill, or one affine value released twice) or set neither (use-after-take / use-after-free through the surviving alias). The candidate shows only `write(r,1)`, the one operation that happens not to change a cell class. | Add an explicit unknown/joined cell for a key whose origin set has more than one member, and forbid ending or taking through a multi-origin pointer; or forbid multi-origin results entirely and declare P9's "with its permission" clause unmet. |
| **F8** | fatal | P4, P9; R11, R1 | `len₀`, `cap₀`, `bump`, `len(v)` are **storage-content terms** used inside RF goals, guards, `requires` and `ensures`, and §2 defines **no old-state binder and no versioning discipline**. §2.3's RF is one-state ("a conjunction of atoms" over "program variables"), and P11 says so explicitly ("RF is quantifier-free arithmetic over the present state"). Under that reading, P4's `if len(v) < cap(v) { push(v,5); … }` discharges `len₀ < cap₀` from a formula whose terms `push` has since changed — and the same reading accepts `if k < len(v) { truncate(v,m); y = v[k] }` where the R11 domain `k < len(v)` is discharged by a stale hypothesis. | Give RF explicit state-versioned terms (`len(v)@σ`) with an `old`/`σ_in` binder in the signature block, and make every write to a key rename the terms rooted at it — then re-price M8 and M10, since this multiplies the term set. |
| **S1** | serious | P1 (verdict overturned), P4 | §2.4's `write` rule **splits R at δ on every element write**, and §2 states no re-fusion rule. Either extent coverage is an RF goal — and then `push(v,8)` accepts before `merge2`, overturning P1's stated reject and dropping P1's required "push allowed only after both are back" — or it is not, and then `v[0]=1; push(v,2)` rejects and P5's loop invariant `κ@[0,n) ↦ Owned` is unre-establishable at the back edge. The candidate's own P4 says "push is never blocked", contradicting its P1. | State the key-normalization rule (adjacent/covering keys with syntactically equal cells re-fuse, as part of the total canonicalizer §4.3 price 2 already demands) and then withdraw P1's push verdict. |
| **S2** | serious | P7 (verdict overturned) | Σ is keyed by `ι@R`, but §3's P7 keys by atom alone (`Σ: 'A ↦ Hole(T)`). In the instantiation the candidate itself names first — "the writer passed `'A` twice inside a `;` group" — nothing supplies **offset equality** `δ_p = δ_q`; a coincidence declaration gives atom coincidence only. With `δ_p`, `δ_q` opaque, `put(q, move v)` requires key `'A@{δ_q} ↦ Hole` and no key covers `{δ_q}`, so it **rejects**. | Say that P7's accepting lines require `q` to be *formed from* `p` (syntactic offset equality) and record that the `;`-group instantiation of P7 is a precision rejection, not an accept. |
| **S3** | serious | all six; C1, M8 | §2.3's term grammar admits only integer program variables and degree-≤2 monomials, but every derivation uses (a) ghost functions of an atom (`len(v)`, `size(ι)`, `bump`, `occupant(m)`, `extent(s)`), (b) **atom-valued** facts (`backing = 'b`, `h ↦ 'pool2`, `'r ≍ 'x`), (c) **disjunction** (`('r ≍ 'x) ∨ ('r ≍ 'y)`, explicitly excluded by §2.3) and (d) **quantifiers** (`∀ κ ∈ bunch(c)`, `∀ h. live(h)`, `∀ s ∈ live`, the pool's `links` invariant). That is at least three vocabularies, not one; §1 claim 4 and C1's "one refinement vocabulary serves state, distinctness, footprints and kills" are unearned, and M8 — already declared violated — is understated. | Either extend RF and re-derive M1/M8/M10 against the extended fragment, or name the second (identity/origin-set) algebra and the third (bunch/quantifier) form explicitly and price each. |

The candidate answers a weaker program than the one written and does not say so. | Say the model has no permission to carry (pointers carry none by §2.1) and restate P9's clause as "with its origin set", recording the divergence from the written program. |
