---

## 3. What survives

To be clear about what this lens does **not** break. `ptr` carrying no
permission, one view per storage, `uninit` as a hole visible through every
alias, gnames never reminted so address reuse cannot revive an identity, and
the frame rule giving R6 kills = 0 by construction — these are derived
correctly and P7's core and P2's `b4`/`p2` lines are the cleanest treatment of
R1(i) and R1(ii) I can construct under this tuple. The failures above are of
three kinds: steps with no rule (F2, F3, F4, S1, S3, S5, S6, S7, S12), a
release rule that leaks (F5), and scores claimed on mechanisms the file does
not have (F1, F6, F7, S2, S13).


# File: critique-whole-program-pinned-cost.md

# Critique of **whole-program-pinned** — lens: COST, DETERMINISM AND THE WRITER

Refuting lens: M1 (fixed terminating procedure, no search/budget/solver), M10
(degree in program size and written steps; one-token edit reach), M7 (local
repair from the diagnostic), M8 (spec tokens; construct count), M9 (P5/P6
obvious shape; surviving backend facts), R15 (generics, closures, nominals in
P16; signature size). Evidence used: the `proof-use-cost` pinned series, the
blind-writer taxes, the retired `scoped-alias-channel` prototype, and
EVIDENCE-mechanism-survey part B (the current emitter emits no alias facts).

The candidate is at
[candidate-whole-program-pinned.md](candidate-whole-program-pinned.md); its
section 4 answers M1 **met**, M3 **met**, M4 **met**, M7 **met**, R4 **met**,
R6 **met**, and M10/M8/M9/R15 **partial**. Every finding below is against a
claim it makes, not against the family it chose.

---

## 1. Findings

| # | Severity | Program / requirement | Finding | One-sentence fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **F1** | **fatal** | M1 (answered "met"); D3 family row | For a writer who writes **zero** tokens — the candidate's own headline — the set of programs that can be accepted is exactly the set `wf pin` can pin, so the tool *is* the acceptance relation; the candidate then permits **widening** inside it ("permitted **here only**, because this is not acceptance"), and OPTIONS' own D3 row rules on that family that "widening is a budget in disguise; precision decides acceptance, which M1 forbids". M1(e)'s test ("the corpus on two machines and under a 10x CPU throttle yields byte-identical verdicts **and diagnostics**") is run over a writer's corpus, which under this candidate is unpinned. M1(b)'s escape ("a certificate-producing search may exist as a writer-side tool") presumes a human who accepts or rejects the tool's output; here the output *is* the program. | Specify the derivation family as a non-widening, terminating procedure with a stated bound and charge it to M1 and M10 like any other acceptance family — i.e. delete the "widening permitted here only" line — or declare M1 violated. |
| **F2** | **fatal** | M10 edit stability; R15; **P16** | A one-token edit — adding one instantiation `kernel::<Packed>(cols2)` — forces a weaker **meet** for a generic body that is "checked ONCE for all instances", and therefore can flip **previously accepted, arbitrarily distant** call sites (`kernel::<u64>(cols)`) to rejected. M10(a) requires the changed-verdict set to be bounded by a function of the edit's *syntactic* reach; the syntactic reach here is one call site and the verdict set is every caller of the generic. The candidate notices only that the *new* site may reject. | Make the parametric pin a set of per-instantiation pins (specialization by default) and state the M10 program-size cost, or add an instantiation-indexed pin form with a stated reach function. |
| **F3** | **fatal** | M10 degree ceiling; M1(b) "each family as a decision procedure with a stated bound" | **Not one** of the candidate's checking families has a stated degree. What entailment must decide is a combined theory: case split over `ite` terms (exponential in enclosing conditions — C6's own cost note is "M10 cost in condition atoms", never bounded here), ∀-quantified index schemas (`∀ i≠i'. dis(...)`, `∀ s live in 'P. next('P[s]) ∈ dom_live('P)`), symbolic products (`w*s` in P6), origin-set meets over `{'a,…,'a}`, and disjointness over a containment forest. That is at best Presburger-with-parameters; M10 caps every family at cubic. Measured floor: the pinned `growing` series is already N^2.5–3.4 at baseline and ≈N^2.6 on the current branch, with **premise admission 11.96 s of a 22 s compile at N=128** — on *writer-written* premises. A pinned program has strictly more premises (one per join, loop head, signature and partial-op site), so the measured exponent is a floor for this candidate, not a ceiling. | State a decision procedure and a degree for each of the six families, and normalize `ite` terms to a bounded condition set, before claiming M10 "acceptance cost improves". |
| **F4** | **fatal** | M3 (answered "met, **zero** entries"), R4 soundness, R5 ground (i); **P2** | `dis('b1,'b2)` for two arena blocks is asserted "by the freshness rule at `alloc`", but both are `contains('A.S, ·)` — *siblings in the containment forest*, which the candidate's own P2 line says yields no disjointness. Their disjointness is a functional-correctness property of the arena's allocator body, underivable in any fixed non-widening domain. So it is an **axiom on `alloc`**: an unenumerated M3 entry whose falsity licenses a wrong `dis` to lowering (R4 soundness) and admits a data race on `par { fill(b1); fill(b2); fill(b3) }` (R5 ground (i)). A hazard is admitted and M3 is answered "met" with zero entries. | Enumerate the allocator's block-freshness as an M3 entry with its boundary obligation, or state that P2's parallel fill requires a written `invariant` proving the arena's partition. |
| **F5** | **fatal** | R1/R2/R4; the D1 closed grammar; **P2**, **P3** | The printable identity grammar is `root \| 'a.f \| 'a[e] \| 'a[lo..hi) \| backing('a) \| ite(c,'a,'a) \| {'a,…,'a}`, and the origin set is explicitly **finite** (HIS-D1-14). It therefore cannot name an *iteration-indexed family* of existentials. One `for j in 0..n { bj = alloc(A,64); fill(bj) }` — P2 one loop away from the derivation shown — has no expressible loop-head pin: either the loop is rejected, or every allocation collapses into one summary identity, which deletes `dis` between blocks from different iterations and rejects the parallel fill. Allocation inside a loop is ordinary code and the candidate's derivations avoid it (P2 shows three straight-line allocs; P3 pre-indexes the pool). | Add an indexed existential form `∃'b[j]` with a per-iteration freshness schema to the grammar, and count its tokens (M8) and its entailment cost (M10). |
| **S1** | serious | M10 "pins are a firewall"; M7 no-reintroduction | The firewall condition is stated as "if an edit does not **falsify** a pin, no other declaration's verdict can change". The operative condition is "does not break the pin's **provability under the fixed family**", a strictly larger set: a pin can stay true and stop verifying when a one-token edit in a loop body pushes consecution outside the family. Then the writer must re-run the whole-program tool and pins change at arbitrarily many sites. The same error voids M7's ground ("repairs do not reintroduce the same rejection **because the monotone re-pin rule never rewrites a verifying pin**") — a rejection means a pin *failed*, so the monotone rule does rewrite, whole-program. | Restate both claims over provability, not truth, and measure the re-pin diff on a corpus before calling either bound. |
| **S2** | serious | M9; **P6** verdict | P6's disjointness is claimed from "affine range arithmetic over `w` and `s` in a **difference-bound fragment**". `[w*s, (w+1)*s)` versus `[w'*s, (w'+1)*s)` reduces to `(w'-w-1)*s ≥ 0`: a product of two unknowns, outside DBM and outside affine arithmetic. Either the fragment is misnamed (and the real fragment is Presburger-with-parameters, colliding with F3) or P6's obvious shape is **rejected** — and note it is rejected, not sequentialized, because the extent fact is also the R11 domain fact for forming the slice, so M5's erasable-construct fallback does not apply. | Name the actual fragment (symbolic-coefficient range arithmetic with a monotonicity rule) and its degree, or move P6 to "accepted with a stated cost: one written `invariant` per partitioned loop". |
| **S3** | serious | M8 (answered "partial, ~2–3k") and M4 (answered "met") | The construct count is wrong. Counting what acceptance must read: 7 identity productions; `Init/Uninit/Gone` plus per-subpart refinement; `window` with `len_of/head_of/cap_of`; `layout`; `backing`; `contains`; `dis`; `dis_set`; `fp` with reads/writes/ends; `ite` join terms; loop initiation and consecution; the `derived iface` normal form with **conditional clauses** (`if cap0 < m {…} else {…}` in P9), existential results (`ptr<∃'b>`), `mints fresh`, and a `fixup` clause; ∀-quantified schemas; the generic meet rule; a byte-canonical printer specification; and, per M1(b), **one decision-procedure specification with a stated bound per family** (≥6 families at ~0.5–1k each). 8–15k is the fair estimate, not 2–3k. M4's "one construct, `derived`, with four site positions and one production each" is false of this inventory. Separately, the M8 credit is a category error: the "authoring surface collapses to near zero" reduces *program* tokens, while K is the **taught** surface, and the writer must still be taught every pin construct in order to repair a rejection against it. | Re-estimate M8 against the enumerated inventory, drop the authoring-collapse credit against K, and correct M4 to "one construct plus a printed assertion language of N productions". |
| **S4** | serious | R6 (answered "met": "the measured 34/41 `len()` rebinds go to 0 **by construction**"); **P9** | The measured tax has two causes, and the candidate removes only one. Exact footprints fix the *coarse-footprint* cause. But P9's own `reserve` iface is conditional, and a caller that cannot derive `cap0 ≥ m` takes the meet of the two arms: `backing('v)` becomes an origin set `{'b0, fresh}`, so every element **and length** fact about the vector dies at the call — exactly the blind-writer shape (`set end = put_text<…>(destination: &uniq 'x line, …); let room = len(line);`, 34 of 41 bindings). The claim is a construction claim about a number that has two causes. | Restate R6 as "met for footprint-caused kills; the backing-replacement kill survives and is unmeasured", and price a `reserve`-with-proved-capacity form. |
| **S5** | serious | **P11** verdict; D3 vocabulary; R11 | The admitted shape ends `return unwrap(read(cache[k]))`. `unwrap` is a partial operation (R11) whose domain fact is "the discriminant is `Some`". The candidate's own table of what the checker holds per storage is `state / window / layout / backing / dis / fp` — there is **no contents or discriminant fact**, and `state('C[k]) = Init` says a value is present, not which variant. So the admitted shape is rejected at the `unwrap`, and the mechanism that would admit it (a refinement fact over a runtime-indexed slot's discriminant, surviving a join) is unnamed and costs further M8. | Either add a discriminant-refinement fact to D3's printable vocabulary with its entailment rule, or rewrite P11's admitted shape to return the value from the match arms and restate the cost. |
| **S6** | serious | R15; **P16** closures | `map_nodes<T>(g, f: fn(ro ptr<'e>) -> T)` pins `f: reads 'e, writes nothing` — a *fixed* footprint in the signature. Any closure that also writes its own capture (an accumulator, a sink, a counter) cannot be passed; higher-order code needs a **footprint/effect variable**, which the candidate never names. Without one, R15 is met only for effect-monomorphic higher-order code, or every call site forces specialization (M10 program size again). | Add printed effect parameters to the iface normal form, with their quantification rule and token count. |
| **S7** | serious | R15 metric | `kernel<E>` prints "identity params `{ 'c.a … 'c.h }`" — 8 parameters for 8 storages. R15(e)'s metric is "parameters per interface over generic P3/P5 ≤ a stated function of the storages the callee touches (**not a linear-in-parameters tautology**)". A linear function of storages touched is precisely the reading the metric refuses, so "R15's metric holds by the normal form" is unsupported; the `dis_set` one-liner answers the *pairwise* blow-up, not the parameter count. | Print one aggregate identity parameter `'c` plus a projection schema, and state the function of storages the parameter count obeys. |
| **S8** | serious | R4(a), R13, M9 | The erasure paragraph hands lowering "`dis`, footprints, `ro`, **termination witnesses**", but R4(a) requires a termination witness for any fact licensing call removal or reordering, and the candidate's own R13 row says termination measures "are writer intent and are never derived". In a zero-token program no witness is ever printed, so **no call in the language is ever removable or reorderable**. That is a standing M9 loss the candidate does not name while listing the witness as a delivered fact. | Delete termination witnesses from the erasure handoff and state the M9 consequence, or specify a derived-measure family for the syntactic-loop fragment and cost it. |
| **S9** | serious | **P3** verdict; M1, M10 | The handle-link half is accepted "because the 3-valued shape domain (RAD-D3-11) derives in-range+occupied". TVLA-style analysis iterates to a fixpoint over a domain whose height and precision depend on the chosen *instrumentation predicates* — precision selecting acceptance, the exact failure OPTIONS names on that row. Even granting the tool, acceptance must re-verify a ∀-quantified reachability invariant with an uninterpreted `dom_live` predicate by consecution across four link writes; no family for quantified-entailment is named or costed. | Name the quantified-entailment family and its degree, or move the handle-link half to "accepted with a stated cost: one written `invariant`", matching the raw-pointer half. |
| **S10** | serious | M1, M11 (answered "met"), M7 | The monotone re-pin rule ("a pin that still verifies is never touched") makes the source of record a function of **edit history**. Two writers who author byte-identical code reach different pinned files, and the one whose history left a stronger stale-but-true pin is accepted where the other is rejected. M11's "verdict diff over the pinned corpus" then measures the corpus's history, not the amendment; M7's diagnostics are no longer a function of the program. | Make `wf pin` idempotent on the source (always print the family's strongest pin, discarding history) and re-derive the churn bound from that, or state the history dependence as an M11 limit. |
| **S11** | serious | M9; **P5** attribution | The P5 claim rests on the retired `scoped-alias-channel` result, and that prototype derived per-load identity **at emission, from the resolved place of the field**, under OWN-1 affine single-ownership — no identity in the type, no pins (measured: 8 vector adds, 0 guards, 121 asm lines against rust-obvious's 65/29/2132; 2.0x at n=8, parity at n≥32; 16-column probe shows no large-n delta at any width). The candidate's marginal M9 gain over that on in-function P5 is **zero**; the genuinely new ground is the cross-procedural and loaded-pointer case, which is unmeasured, and the current emitter emits no alias facts at all. | Restate P5's M9 claim as "parity with the retired prototype in-function; the new claim is cross-procedural and is unmeasured". |
| **S12** | serious | M7 | Two rejection classes have no location with a local fix. (i) The three-hop generic case: a call site rejects because a meet weakened, because a *third* declaration added an instantiation — the payload can name at most one of the three. (ii) P11's naive shape: the named repair is a change of data representation across every producer and consumer of the cache, not a local fix. M7(a) requires the payload to name "a tree location where a local fix exists". | Specify the payload for meet-caused rejections to name the instantiation that forced the meet, and reclassify P11's rejection as a stated restructuring under M7's precision-rule clause. |
| **S13** | serious | M10 program-size measure | "Per-declaration work is linear in (pins × statements)" — but pins are *generated from* statements (one per join, loop head, signature, partial-op site), so that product is already quadratic in statements before any per-pin entailment cost; and each `ite`-term's size is exponential in enclosing branch depth with no normalization rule stated. | State the pin count as a function of statements and give `ite` a normal form with a bounded condition set. |
| m1 | minor | P1 | The `push(v, x)` rejection line is printed after `write(pi, x); write(pj, y)`, which already restore `Init`; as ordered, the rejection does not fire and the following `put(pi); put(pj)` is redundant. | Move the rejected `push` above the two writes. |
| m2 | minor | P7 | "Accepted as required, **with no pin at all**" contradicts the model's own rule that every signature carries a printed `derived iface`. | Say "no pin beyond the enclosing signature's iface". |
| m3 | minor | P5 | `g(b[i], e[i], f[i], g[i], h[i])` uses `f` and `g` as both column names and function names (inherited from PROGRAMS.md). | Rename the combining functions in the derivation. |
| m4 | minor | P13 | The claim "the compiler knows exactly which interior pointers are live across the compaction" names no **pin site** for that set, and acceptance can only read pinned text. | Name the pin site (a `derived at` on the `compact` call listing the live interior identities). |
| m5 | minor | §1 table vs §4 price | "Widening permitted **here only**, because this is not acceptance" and "The derivation family is **specification-fixed** … a compiler improvement that proves more is a language amendment" cannot both hold: if improving the family is an amendment, the family is inside the language. | Delete one line and say which. |
| m6 | minor | R4 erasure claim | "Pinned `dis` … survives to lowering **without re-derivation**" — but the LLVM construct a loop needs, `llvm.experimental.noalias.scope.decl`, is a per-iteration fact that "must be duplicated when a loop is unrolled", so the emitter does re-derive per-iteration scopes from a loop-head ∀ clause. | Reword to "without re-deriving the *proof*; the emitter still instantiates per-iteration scopes". |

---

## 2. Program verdicts overturned, with derivation

Notation as the ladder and as the candidate: `// accept:` / `// reject:` with
the fact used; `D{…}` is a pinned block.

### P2 — overturn "accepted as required" → **accepted only under an unenumerated M3 axiom; rejected once the arena is real**

```text
arena A in 'A ; D{ 'A.M metadata, 'A.S bytes ; contains('A.S, ·) }
D iface alloc(A,n) -> ptr<∃'b>  writes 'A.M ; mints fresh 'b with contains('A.S,'b)

b1 = alloc(A,64) ; b2 = alloc(A,64)
  // the candidate's line: "dis('b1,'b2) by the freshness rule at alloc"
  // reject (as a derivation): 'b1 and 'b2 are SIBLINGS under contains('A.S,·).
  //   The candidate's own P2 line says containment yields no disjointness
  //   ("NOT dis('A.S,'b1) — containment, not disjointness"). Sibling disjointness
  //   is not a forest fact; it is a property of alloc's BODY: that two calls
  //   return non-overlapping sub-ranges of 'A.S.        [missing: a proof of the arena's partition]
  // Therefore "the freshness rule at alloc" is an AXIOM on the iface, i.e. an
  //   M3 entry — and the candidate answers M3 "met, zero entries".

par { fill(b1) ; fill(b2) ; fill(b3) }
  // reject under M3 as answered: R5 ground (i) is discharged from dis, and dis
  //   here traces to no proof and to no listed base entry. M3's Price line:
  //   "every checker-emitted fact traces to a proof or a listed entry."
  // accept only if the arena's partition invariant is written by hand
  //   (one `invariant { … use … }` inside alloc) or alloc is enumerated in M3.

free(A, b2)
  // reject (as printed): "writes 'A.M" is false for any free-list arena — the
  //   free-list node is written INSIDE b2's bytes, i.e. inside 'A.S.
  //   The honest footprint is `writes 'A.M, 'A.S`.
read(b1.data)  // after the free
  // reject: 'A.S contains 'b1, so the free's footprint names the support of
  //   every element fact about every live block.               [fact: R6 frame, honestly applied]
  // This is exactly the R6 collapse the candidate says goes "to 0 by construction".
```

**Corrected verdict: accepted with two stated costs** — the allocator's block
partition is an M3 entry (or one written invariant), and a free-list arena's
`free` kills every element fact in the arena unless the free list is moved to
`'A.M`. The candidate's zero-entry M3 answer does not survive.

### P3 — overturn "accepted as required (handle links)" → **accepted with a stated cost in both link forms**

```text
D{ inv: ∀s live in 'P. next('P[s]) ∈ dom_live('P) ∧ prev('P[s]) ∈ dom_live('P) }
  // the candidate: "the 3-valued shape domain derives in-range+occupied for
  //   handle-typed links", printed once, reused across four link writes.

write(pa.next, n)
  // accept on the frame test — the footprint names 'P[a].next only.       [fact: R6]
  // BUT the pinned invariant must RE-HOLD, and re-holding is not framing:
  //   the written field IS in the invariant's support (`next('P[a])`).
  //   Consecution therefore needs: n ∈ dom_live('P).
  // reject unless the checker has a quantified-entailment family over an
  //   uninterpreted dom_live predicate.            [missing: a named family with a stated degree]

// and the derivation side:
  // the 3-valued domain (RAD-D3-11 / TVLA) iterates to a fixpoint whose height
  // and precision depend on the chosen instrumentation predicates — OPTIONS'
  // own note on that row: "precision decides acceptance, which M1 forbids".
```

**Corrected verdict: accepted with a stated cost under handle links *and* raw
interior-pointer links** — one written `invariant` in both, because neither the
derivation (instrumentation-predicate-dependent) nor the verification (quantified
entailment over `dom_live`) is a named fixed family. The candidate's claim that
R6's "stated once and reused" test is met "by construction" holds for framing
and fails for consecution.

### P6 — overturn "accepted as required" → **rejected under the stated fragment**

```text
out: buffer of n bytes in 'o ; s = n/k
for w in 0..k {
  D loop { 0 <= w < k ; extent of slice_of(out, w*s..(w+1)*s) = 'o[w*s .. (w+1)*s) ;
           ∀ w≠w'. dis('o[w*s..(w+1)*s), 'o[w'*s..(w'+1)*s)) }

  helper(slice_of(out, w*s .. (w+1)*s), input)
    // reject: forming the slice is a partial operation (R11): its domain fact is
    //   0 <= w*s  and  (w+1)*s <= n.  Both are products of two program variables.
    //   [missing: (w+1)*s <= n]
    // The candidate's stated fragment is "affine range arithmetic … in a
    //   DIFFERENCE-BOUND fragment with syntactic loop bounds". A DBM constrains
    //   x - y <= c for constant c; it cannot represent w*s at all.
}
par-2 over w
  // reject: the ∀-clause reduces, for w < w', to (w+1)*s <= w'*s, i.e.
  //   (w'-w-1)*s >= 0 — a product of two unknowns plus a sign condition on s.
  //   [missing: s >= 0 ∧ (w'-w-1)*s >= 0]
  // note: this is NOT an M5 sequential fallback. The same extent fact is the
  //   R11 domain fact above, so the failure is a REJECTION of the sequential
  //   program, not a loss of parallel permission.
```

**Corrected verdict: rejected as written; accepted only with one writer-written
`invariant` per partitioned loop, or by naming a larger fragment** —
symbolic-coefficient range arithmetic with a monotonicity rule — **whose degree
is then owed to M10 under F3.** This is the candidate's M9 row: P6's obvious
shape does not merely lose speed, it does not compile.

### P9 — overturn "accepted as required" → **accepted, and it carries the R6 tax the candidate says it removes**

```text
D iface reserve(v: Vec in 'v, m: u64)
        writes 'v ;
        if cap0 < m { ends backing('v) ; exit backing('v) = fresh 'b' ; exit cap >= m }
        else        { exit backing('v) = backing0('v) }

pe = ptr_of(v[i]) ; len0 = len(v)
reserve(v, m)                     // caller cannot derive cap0 >= m
  // accept the call.
read(pe)
  // reject: backing('v) is the meet of the two arms = the origin set {'b0, fresh},
  //         and state over an origin set is the meet of its members = Gone ⊓ Init.
  //         [missing: cap0 >= m]
len1 = len(v)
  // MANDATORY re-bind: every length and element fact keyed on 'b0 died at the call,
  //   not because the footprint was coarse but because the BACKING IDENTITY changed.
  //                                                        [fact: R6 kill by identity replacement]
```

**Corrected verdict: accepted as required for the interface mechanism; R6's
"the measured 34/41 `len()` rebinds go to 0 by construction" is overturned.**
Exact footprints remove the coarse-footprint cause of that number; the
conditional-reallocation cause survives untouched, and the blind-writer report's
own shape (`put_text` into a growable destination, then `let room = len(line)`)
is on the surviving side.

### P11 — overturn "accepted with a stated cost" → **the admitted shape is also rejected**

```text
cache: array<Option<V>> in 'C ; D{ state('C[*]) = Init ; window: full }
get(k):
  match read(cache[k]) {
    None    => { write(cache[k], Some(compute(k))) }   // accept: Init -> Init
    Some(v) => { }                                     // accept
  }
  return unwrap(read(cache[k]))
  // reject: unwrap is a partial operation (R11). Its domain fact is
  //   "discriminant(contents('C[k])) = Some".
  //   The candidate's own per-storage table holds state / window / layout /
  //   backing / dis / fp. There is NO contents or discriminant fact in it, and
  //   state('C[k]) = Init says only that a value is present.
  //   [missing: contents('C[k]) is Some]  — and no printable term can carry it,
  //   because k is a runtime index and the join term over the two arms is a
  //   fact about a VALUE, not about a storage state.
```

**Corrected verdict: rejected in both shapes under the stated D3 vocabulary.**
The admitted shape needs a discriminant-refinement fact keyed by identity and
surviving a join — an unnamed mechanism with its own M8 and M10 charges — or a
rewrite that returns the value out of the match arms, which changes the stated
cost from "one discriminant per slot" to "one discriminant per slot **plus** a
restructuring of every read site".

### P16 — overturn "accepted with a stated cost" → **M10 edit stability violated; the cost falls on the wrong site**

```text
D iface kernel<E>(c: Cols<E> in 'c)
        identity params { 'c.a … 'c.h } ; dis_set over them ; writes 'c.a[*], 'c.b[*]
// the generic body is checked ONCE for all instances, so its pin is the MEET
// of the per-instance pins.

// file 1, today:
kernel::<u64>(cols)
  // accept: the meet over {u64} is the u64 instance's own pin; the caller's
  //         downstream facts (exit dis_set, exit windows) are exact.

// file 2, tomorrow, one token added by an unrelated author:
kernel::<Packed>(cols2)
  // Packed's element identities coincide differently, so its per-instance pin is
  // weaker. The meet over {u64, Packed} drops the exit fact file 1 depended on.

// back in file 1, UNEDITED:
kernel::<u64>(cols) ; par-2 over i { read(cols.a[i]) ; write(cols.b[i], …) }
  // reject: the generic's exit pin no longer carries dis_set over 'c.a..'c.h.
  //         [missing: dis('c.a[i],'c.b[i]) after the call]
  // M10(a): "the set of declarations whose verdict can change under a one-token
  //          edit is bounded by a stated function of the edit's SYNTACTIC reach."
  //          Syntactic reach = one call site in file 2.
  //          Verdict set = every caller of kernel<·> in the program.  VIOLATED.
```

**Corrected verdict: violates M10, undeclared.** The candidate's stated cost is
"reject possible" at the *new* instance with specialization as the escape; the
actual cost is that adding an instance can reject *existing, unedited* call
sites arbitrarily far away, and the repair (specialize) must be applied at a
declaration neither author is looking at. Secondary: the determinism argument
for the meet — "unique and deterministic because the lattice is **finite**" —
is false. The identity grammar is recursive (`backing(backing(·))`,
`ite(c, ite(c', ·, ·), ·)`, arbitrary index expressions `e`) and state terms
range over captured conditions, so the pin lattice is infinite in both height
and width; the meet's existence, uniqueness and computability are all
unestablished, and with them the candidate's own "printer determinism" price.

---

## 3. What survives

The three claims I could not break are worth naming, because they are the
candidate's real content and they are unaffected by everything above:

1. **A pin is never trusted.** The checker re-verifies, so a stale pin is
   harmless or it is a local diagnostic. The standing staleness objection to
   the whole certificate direction is genuinely answered.
2. **D4's deletion of the exclusivity rule.** P7 and P3's sequential link
   writes pass with no mechanism, and R9's negative test is met. That is a real
   language claim and it costs nothing above.
3. **Exact derived footprints beat declared coarse footprints on the
   footprint-caused half of the measured R6 tax** (S4 only removes the other
   half of the claim, not this one).

Everything else in section 4's "18 met, 9 partial, 0 violated" is priced above.
By this lens the honest count on the rows I examined is: **M1 violated, M3
violated, M10 violated, M4 overstated, M7 partial, M8 understated by 3–5x, M9
partial-and-misattributed, R6 partial, R15 partial for a second, unnamed
reason (effect polymorphism).**


# File: critique-whole-program-pinned-soundness.md

# Critique of **whole-program-pinned** — lens: SOUNDNESS AND THE PROGRAMS

Refutation date: 2026-09-16. Target:
[candidate-whole-program-pinned.md](candidate-whole-program-pinned.md). Method:
P1, P2, P4, P7, P9 and P13 re-derived line by line from the candidate's §2
model *as written* (the tuple, the identity grammar, the per-storage fact
table, the state-change table, the iface normal form), not from its §3
narration. Where §2 and §3 disagree, both readings are derived and the
disagreement is itself the finding. Requirements cited are VERDICT-D0 §2 rows;
couplings are §4 C1–C18; the ladder is MECHANISM-MAP §3.

Severity: **fatal** = a hazard is admitted, or a requirement the candidate
marks *met* is violated without the violation being declared; **serious** = a
program verdict is wrong, a stated cost is understated, or a needed mechanism
is unnamed; **minor** = wording.

---

## 1. Findings

| # | Sev | Program / row | Finding | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | fatal | P1; R5(a)(i), R6, M6(ii), C2 | `D iface take2(…) requires dis('b[i],'b[j]) ; **writes nothing** ; exit state('b[i])=state('b[j])=Uninit`. A call that moves two slots `Init → Uninit` declares an **empty write footprint**. R5 reads footprints for ground (i) and R6 keys kills by the *stated* footprint, so `take2` is proved non-interfering with *every* statement and kills *no* fact — including `state('b[i])=Init`. `par { take2(v,i,j) ; a = read(v[i]) }` is admitted, and sequentially a pin `state('b[i])=Init` printed before the call survives it. The candidate declares R5, R6 and M6(ii) met. | State-changing clauses are footprint clauses: the printer must emit `writes 'b[i],'b[j]` for any identity whose entry and exit state differ, and the normal form must reject an iface whose exit-state set is not contained in its write ∪ end footprint. |
| F2 | fatal | P1; R1(a)(i) | The identity grammar admits `'a[e]` with `e` a source expression, and the candidate never states **when `e` is evaluated**. With `pi : ptr<'b[i]>` live and `i` assignable, `i := j` silently re-points a live pointer's identity term, and the pinned state term `state('b[m]) = ite(m=i, Uninit, ite(m=j, Uninit, Init))` re-evaluates with the new `i`, so the slot actually holding the hole becomes `Init` to the checker. A hole read is admitted (derivation in §2.1). | Index terms in identities and in pinned state terms are over values frozen at formation (an SSA/immutable-index rule); an assignment to a binding occurring in a live identity term is rejected, or the old term is retained as an opaque frozen root. |
| F3 | fatal | P2; R4(b), C3, R5 | `dis('b1,'b2)` is derived "**by the freshness rule at `alloc`**" — that is inequality of identity *names*, which R4(b) forbids verbatim ("never inequality of identity names") and which the candidate itself refuses one line earlier for `'A.S` vs `'b1`. Two fresh existentials both `contains('A.S, ·)` are siblings under one parent: exactly the configuration where disjointness must be *proved*. `alloc`'s printed iface states `mints fresh 'b with contains('A.S,'b)` and nothing else, so the caller has no premise for sibling disjointness, and P2's `par { fill(b1); fill(b2); fill(b3) }` accept — the program's central requirement — rests on an underived fact. If the arena body is consulted instead, R7 is violated. | `alloc`'s normal form gains a clause `dis('b, x)` for every live block `x` already minted from `'A.S`, discharged in the allocator body against a written arena invariant (bump monotonicity / free-list disjointness); freshness alone never licenses `dis`. |
| F4 | fatal | P2; R2, R1(a)(ii) | `D iface free(A, p:ptr<'b>) writes 'A.M ; ends 'b` carries **no entry-state clause**, and the §2 state table's `free` row (`'a → Gone, permanently`) states no precondition. `free(A,b2) ; free(A,b2)` therefore type-checks: the second call's `ends 'b2` maps `Gone → Gone`. P2's required property "four frees, no double" fails, and R2's "released exactly once on every path" — marked *met* — is violated. The ladder's Step 0 `dispose own_a; dispose own_a` rejection has no owner in this model, because D4 deleted the affine owner and pointers are `Copy`. | Every `ends 'a` clause carries `entry state('a) ≠ Gone`, and the state table makes an ending event on a `Gone` identity an R1(a)(ii) rejection; add a scope-exit obligation that every minted identity is `Gone` (the leak half of R2, currently unowned). |
| F5 | fatal | P2; M6(ii), R6, R14(iii) | The kill rule is stated over **names**: "no fact is dropped whose support the operation's stated footprint does not name" (R6's wording, repeated in §3 as "the invariant's support is not in that footprint", "the derived footprint names `'cols.a[i]` alone"). Over a containment forest, name-matching under-kills: a footprint naming `'b2` does not kill a fact supported by its ancestor `'A.S`, although `'b2 ⊆ 'A.S` and R14(iii) expressly lets the allocator write inside freed `'b2`. The candidate asserts "(ii) frame soundness is met (P7/P2 do not under-kill)". | State the kill rule as *not-proved-disjoint* rather than *named*: a fact is killed unless `dis(support, footprint)` holds — which makes ancestors and descendants kill each other and makes R6 the precision row it is meant to be, with C2's two exactness directions explicit. |
| F6 | fatal | P9; C2, R4(a), R1(a)(ii) | `pick` returns `ptr<ite(c,'X,'Y)>` and, when `c` is not a parameter, "the normal form falls back to the origin set `{'X,'Y}` and **the caller's facts are the meet over the set**". A single "meet" reading is applied to *effects* as well as to *assumptions*. A write or an end through an origin-set identity must be read as a **may** (join over the set) or the facts about both members survive: `q = ptr_of('X); a = read(q); write(pick(c,x,y), 42); b = read(q)` retains `contents('X)=a` — a licensed fact false in the `c`-arm, i.e. R4(a) violated; with `ends {'X,'Y}` the same reading leaves both `Init` and admits use-after-end. C2 says the relation is stated once and read in **opposite** exactness directions; the candidate says R4, R5 and R6 read it "identically". | Split the reading at the origin set: assumptions take the meet, footprints and ending sets take the join; state in §2 that `{…}` is a may-set in every effect position. |
| F7 | fatal | P13; M3, M2(ii), R8a | The `fixup : ptr<'P[x]@L0> -> ptr<'P[x]@L1>` clause is an **assumed identity re-mapping the checker never establishes**. Erased, it is unsound (the pointer's runtime value is the pre-compaction address); un-erased, it must consult the pool's forwarding map at run time, and the predicate it discharges — "this address was a live `'P[x]` at `L0` and this is its `L1` image" — is a safety predicate the checker did not discharge, which M2(ii) refuses by name (the Vale-wrapped-as-a-library case). Either way it is an assumption outside M3's enumerated base, while the candidate claims M3 adds "**zero** entries". | Delete the clause kind; a fixup is an ordinary function whose result identity is *proved* from a written pool invariant over the forwarding map, or the relocation is refused as R8a's price says, or `fixup` is enumerated as an M3 entry with its boundary obligation. |
| F8 | fatal | R8a, C7; P4 shape | The §2 transition table is offered as the complete ending set ("the ending set is exactly the identity-minting/ending table", R8a *met*), but R8a(a) enumerates **`own` parameter passing, container insertion, enum payload move, return, arena reset** and the table has no row for any of them. A pointer into a value subsequently inserted into a container (or moved into an enum payload, or returned) stays `Init` in the checker while its storage has ended — R1(a)(ii) admitted, on exactly P4's stored-pointer shape. | Add one table row per R8a member, each with its minting/ending effect, and make completeness of the table a checked property of the normal form rather than a claim. |
| F9 | fatal | R4(a); D4 "read-only as a type flag" | `ro` is listed in the set "handed to lowering as licensed facts" (`dis`, footprints, `ro`, termination witnesses). Under D4 there is no exclusivity, so `ro ptr<'a>` bounds **this pointer's** writes and says nothing about the memory: another alias may write `'a` during the same span. Any lowering that reads `ro` as a memory-invariance fact (LLVM `readonly`/`readnone` on a parameter, a hoisted load across a call) is a false licensed fact and R4(a) — marked *met* — is violated. | Say in §2 that `ro` licenses only "this pointer performs no write", which is already the write footprint, and remove `ro` from the licensed-fact set, or pair it with a proved no-other-writer span. |
| S1 | serious | P1, P4, P8; C6, M1 | §2 fixes two things the derivations break: `state('a) ∈ {Uninit, Init, Gone}` (a flat three-element domain) and "`ite` terms come from source-visible branch conditions **only** (C6)". P1 pins `state('b[m]) = ite(m=i, …)`, P4 pins `state('b) = ite(len0<cap0, Init, Gone)` — state *terms*, over index equalities and capacity comparisons, neither of which is a branch the writer wrote. The closed printable grammar that step 5 of "why the four cohere" makes M1 rest on therefore does not exist for the very facts the programs need. C6 is silently retuned from "captured conditions" to "arbitrary decidable predicates". | Give the state-term grammar explicitly (states × a named, closed condition grammar), and restate C6's reach so the coupling records the widening. |
| S2 | serious | P1 vs P4; R7, M4 | Two different printed ifaces are shown for one `push`: P1's has an unconditional precondition "no `Uninit` slot in `'b`", P4's is the conditional backing contract with no such clause. The printer is claimed "canonical to the byte". P1's stated *reason* ("relocation copies elements") holds only on the reallocating arm, so on the `len0 < cap0` arm P1's required rejection is not derived by the candidate's own contract. | Print one `push` iface (conditional contract plus an unconditional `∀m<len. state('b[m])=Init` entry clause, grounded on the relocating arm), and derive P1's rejection from that clause rather than from the arm-specific reason. |
| S3 | serious | P1; R11, M7 | `(pi,pj) = take2(v,i,j)` is marked **accept**, with the discharge attributed to "the writer's own `i != j` guard" — a guard that does not appear in the program shown, and which P1 does not require before the split. The line also forms `'b[i]` and `'b[j]` with no discharge of `i < len` / `j < len` (R11 domain facts for the index operation). | Mark the line accept-only-under `i≠j ∧ i<len ∧ j<len` with the missing-fact payload, as the same candidate does for `v[k]`. |

## 2. Program verdicts overturned, with derivation

Notation as the ladder. `D{…}` is a pinned block. Only lines whose verdict I
change or whose stated ground fails are shown.

### 2.1 P1 — overturned: *rejected as derived*; correct only under added rules

```text

D iface take2(v,i,j) -> (ptr<'b[i]>, ptr<'b[j]>)
        requires dis('b[i],'b[j]) ; writes nothing ; exit state('b[i])=state('b[j])=Uninit

  //   dis('b[i],'b[j])  — the cited `i != j` guard is not in P1; R11 domain facts
  //   i < len('b), j < len('b) — never mentioned.        [missing: i≠j ∧ i<n ∧ j<n]

par { take2(v, i, j) ; a = read(v[m]) }     // m proved ≠ i, j
  // ACCEPTED BY THE CANDIDATE, and it is a race + a hole read.
  // take2's footprint is EMPTY ("writes nothing"), so R5 ground (i) is discharged
  // against every statement whatsoever, and R6 kills nothing: the pin state('b[i])=Init
  // survives the call.  Substituting m := i then gives an admitted read of the hole.
  //                                                                 [F1: R5(a)(i), R6, M6(ii)]

// the identity-term hazard, on the accepted straight-line path:
(pi, pj) = take2(v, i, j)                   // with the guards of line 1 supplied
  // state: ite(m=i, Uninit, ite(m=j, Uninit, Init))
i := j
  // no rule in the candidate touches this: `i` is an ordinary binding, and `pi`'s type
  // is the TERM 'b[i], not a frozen identity.
write(pi, x)
  // accept under the candidate: 'b[i] now resolves to 'b[j]; Uninit -> Init, a fill.
a = read(v[i_old])                          // i_old the value i had at take2
  // ACCEPT under the candidate — and it reads the hole.  The pinned term re-evaluates
  // with the current i (= j), so m = i_old matches neither arm and yields Init, while
  // the slot is still Uninit.                                        [F2: R1(a)(i) admitted]

push(v, x)                                  // before the puts
  // reject — but NOT for the stated reason.  "relocation copies elements" holds only on
  // the `len0 >= cap0` arm; on the `len0 < cap0` arm P4's own printed contract leaves the
```

**Corrected verdict: rejected as derived** (F1 admits a race and a hole read;
F2 admits a hole read on the accepted path; S3 mis-accepts the split). P1 is
recoverable — exit-state clauses folded into footprints, index terms frozen at
formation, guards discharged explicitly — but not as written.

```text
D iface free(A, p:ptr<'b>)      writes 'A.M ; ends 'b

b1 = alloc(A,64) ; b2 = alloc(A,64) ; b3 = alloc(A,64)
```

| Coupling | What it says | What the candidate does |
|---|---|---|
| C2 | one relation, **opposite** exactness directions (R4 must, R5 rejects, R6 may-write over-approximation) | "read identically by R4, R5, R6"; the single-meet reading of origin sets (F6) and the name-based kill rule (F5) are the two consequences |
| C3 | distinct-by-default with **per-pair, sub-identity-inclusive** call-site discharge | `dis_set` presented as compressing the discharge as well as the notation (S12); sibling disjointness derived from freshness (F3) |
| C6 | state as a term over **captured conditions** | ite terms over index equalities, capacity comparisons and value parameters (S1, m2) |
| C7 | the **complete** storage-ending set | five R8a members absent from the transition table (F8) |
| C10 | read-only is a type flag, **never** a loan | `ro` nonetheless handed to lowering among the licensed facts (F9) |
| C1 | identity granularity is one vocabulary serving R1/R4/R5/R6/M8 | granularity becomes a *printer* choice ("granularity shapes the printer may emit") with no stated rule, so R6 precision and R4 fact strength are selected outside both the language and the acceptance relation — declared for M1 but not for C1 |

## 4. What survives

The refutation is not total, and three results stand unchallenged under this
lens:

1. **P7's alias half.** `take(p)` leaving a hole visible through `q`, and
   `put(q,·)` refilling it, is derived correctly and is the cleanest
   demonstration in the file that D4's deletion of exclusivity costs no
   sequential safety. The ladder's finding is confirmed, not weakened.
2. **P2's negative `dis` test.** `¬dis('A.S,'b1)` by containment is exactly
   R4(b)'s demand, and the candidate is right that the forest, not name
   inequality, is the structure. The finding at F3 is that the candidate
   applies its own rule to one pair and not to the sibling pair.
3. **P9's `drain`.** A callee-imposed exit hole judged from the interface with
   the body never opened is R7's content, and the printed iface carries it.

Everything else in the six programs turns on a fact the model does not state
where it comes from.

# Critique of `window-focus` (candidate-wildcard) — lens COST

Key: `window-focus`. Lens: **COST, DETERMINISM AND THE WRITER** — M1 (fixed
terminating procedure), M10 (degree in program size; edit reach), M7 (local
repair from the diagnostic), M8 (spec tokens; construct count), M9 (P5/P6
obvious shape; surviving backend facts), R15 (generics, closures, nominals in
P16).

Target: `core/candidate-wildcard.md` (2026-09-16). Evidence used:
VERDICT-D0 §2/§4/§5, MECHANISM-MAP §3, PROGRAMS.md, OPTIONS.md D1–D4,
EVIDENCE-mechanism-survey parts A.5/A.6/B/B.2, and the repository's measured
artifacts: `research/experiments/proof-use-cost/baseline-2026-09-14.tsv`
(the `growing` series), `research/experiments/blind-writer/2026-08-28/REPORT.md`
(the 34-of-41 `len()` rebind tax, three message-less diagnostics),
`research/experiments/scoped-alias-channel/RESULTS.md` (the retired channel).

The candidate's own score is **18 met, 9 partial, 0 violated**, with M1, M2,
M7, M10 and R15 all graded **met**. I find three of those five untenable and
one hazard admitted. Default position on uncertainty: report.

---

## 1. Findings

Severity: **fatal** = a hazard is admitted, or a requirement is violated in a
way the candidate did not declare. **serious** = a program verdict is wrong, a
stated cost is understated, or a needed mechanism is unnamed. **minor** =
wording.

| # | Sev | Concerns | Finding | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| F1 | fatal | P8, R2 (graded **met**) | §2.7's join demands `σ` **equal** on incoming edges and §1's seam says state lives on a storage forever. In P8(b) `let s = if c { free(a); b } else { free(b); a }`, `σ(ρa)` is `Gone` on the then-edge and `Init` on the else-edge, so the join the candidate offers as *the accepted rewrite* is rejected by the candidate's own rule. `free(s)` is then also undefined: `s`'s name is the origin set `{ρa,ρb}` and `free`'s row is `Init\|Uninit ⇒ Gone`, which `ρa` already fails on the then-path. P8 therefore has **no accepted spelling**, and R2's acceptance test is P8. | Adopt C6's state-as-a-term-over-captured-conditions at the join only (the candidate names this in W5 as the declined alternative) and pay M10's condition-atom bound; or define an ending event on an origin set as a one-of obligation, which is the same path-sensitivity under another name. |
| F2 | fatal | P16, R15 (graded **met**) | R15(a) requires generic definitions to be **checked once for all instances**. §2.4's default carve is "a fixed, specification-defined function of the *named type*", and §4.1's R15 row says it is "computed from the **INSTANTIATED** type". Then for `fn f<E>(c: ptr<ρ, Box<E>>)` the entry set of ρ's carve differs per `E` (`backing(.inner)` exists iff `E` is a buffer/vector type), so §2.6's meet/cover verdicts inside one unchanged body differ per instance. The body is checked per instantiation, not once. | Make the default carve a function of the *declared* type with type parameters contributing one opaque entry each, and require a written `carve` clause to reach an instantiated field; state the resulting loss of P5-over-`E` facts. |
| F3 | fatal | P9, R4(a), R5, M1 | §2.3 defines `dis(m,n)` only over names with a **coarse root**. A result-origin set (`result : π ∈ {ρ,σ}`, HIS-D1-14) has no single root, and no clause of §2.3 decides `dis(π, ρ)` or `dis(π, π')`. The nearest reading — "names differ ⇒ `⊑`-incomparable ⇒ `dis`" — makes `f(z, x)` with `z : π ∈ {ρ,σ}` and `x : ptr<ρ,T>` distinct, licensing parameter `noalias` on two overlapping actuals: UB by LangRef, a violated R4(a), and an admitted race at a non-erasable construct under R5. `dis` is therefore not a total procedure over the name grammar it must decide (M1). | Define `dis(π, n)` as `∀ρ ∈ π. dis(ρ, n)` and `dis(π,π')` as pairwise over the two sets, and state the O(\|π\|·\|π'\|) cost in M10's bound. |

## 2. Program verdicts overturned, with derivation

Notation follows the ladder and the candidate's own §3.

### O1. P8 — candidate: "(b) and (c) accepted as required". **Overturn: (b) rejected; P8 has no accepted spelling.**

```text
let s = if c { free(a); b } else { free(b); a }
// then-edge : σ(ρa)=Gone           (free's row: Init|Uninit ⇒ Gone, permanent, §2.5)
//             σ(ρb)=Init           (moved into s; the BINDING moved, the STORAGE state did not)
// else-edge : σ(ρa)=Init
//             σ(ρb)=Gone
// JOIN       REJECT by §2.7: "every name's σ must be EQUAL on the incoming edges".
//            σ(ρa) is Gone vs Init; σ(ρb) is Init vs Gone. Two names differ, not one.
//            The candidate's comment "on BOTH edges, a and b have left scope" is not
//            available to it: §1's seam says state lives on a storage FOREVER, and R1(a)(ii)
//            needs σ(ρa)=Gone retained so a stale copy of the pointer is refused later.
free(s)
// REJECT even if the join were waived: s's name is the origin set π = {ρa, ρb} (HIS-D1-14),
//   and §2.5's free row is stated over a single ρ. Applied pointwise it demands
//   σ(ρa) ∈ {Init,Uninit}, which the then-path already falsified. Applied to "one of",
//   it is a disjunctive obligation the model has no rule for.
```

Consequence: P8(a) is conceded rejected by the candidate; P8(b) is rejected by
§2.7; P8(c) is untouched and stands. R2's acceptance test names P8, so **R2 is
violated, not met**, and the violation is undeclared. W5 treats the condition-term
alternative as a refinement the owner may prefer; it is in fact load-bearing.

### O2. P5 — candidate: "accepted as required, at zero extra writer tokens". **Overturn: rejected as §2.6 is written; under the charitable patch, accepted with an unstated distinctness ground and a possible loop row.**

```text
fn kernel(s: ptr<ρ, Cols>, n: u64) row { ρ : Init ⇒ Init @E }
// the signature's row IS a window (candidate's own P5 gloss), carve = the DEFAULT:
//   { .a, backing(.a), .b, backing(.b), …, .h, backing(.h), padding }   -- 17 entries
for i in 0..n {
  set backing(.a)[i] = f(backing(.a)[i], backing(.c)[i], backing(.d)[i])
  // REJECT by §2.6 verbatim: the access MEETS entry backing(.a); it does not NAME that
  //   entry (it names a sub-place of it) and it does not COVER a union of entries.
  //   §2.6 admits exactly two shapes and this is neither.
}
```

Patch §2.6 to "lies provably within exactly one entry" (S1) and the loop body
is accepted. Two costs then remain that the verdict does not state:

```text
  // dis(backing(.a), backing(.b)) is claimed from "different entries of one carve".
  //   FALSE as a partition argument: a carve partitions ρ's EXTENT, and backing(.a)
  //   is storage OUTSIDE ρ reached through a pointer stored in ρ. The true ground is
  //   buffer<T> affine single-ownership (OWN-1) — unstated (F6).
}  // loop head: the body's composed row is backing(.a): Init⇒Init @W, backing(.b): Init⇒Init @W.
   //   Identity on STATE, not on GRADE. If a row includes its grades — and §2.4 says it does —
   //   the head row is NOT the identity and a loop row must be written (m2).
```

Revised verdict: **accepted with a stated cost** — one rule restatement, one
named premise, and a loop row under the literal reading of "identity".
"Zero extra writer tokens" survives only under the charitable reading of both.

### O3. P6 — candidate: "accepted as required, at zero extra writer tokens … written exactly as PROGRAMS.md writes it". **Overturn: accepted only with a written loop-head row and one of three unnamed mechanisms.**

```text
out : ptr<ρ, buffer<u8>> of n bytes, σ(ρ)=Uninit ; s = n / k
for w in 0..k {
  helper(slice_of(out, w*s .. (w+1)*s), input)
  // (1) helper's formal is `out: ptr<σ, buffer<u8>>` and σ must instantiate to the
  //     extent ρ[w*s,(w+1)*s). §2.1: a fine name is NEVER in a type. §2.2: a pointer's
  //     type names a COARSE store. So the actual's type cannot be formed. Three exits,
  //     none taken by the candidate: a fine name in a type (breaks D1), a per-iteration
  //     `fresh ∃ρ' ⊑ ρ` promotion (no re-merge operation is defined for the parent),
  //     or a per-iteration `focus` (a written token the verdict denies).           [S6]
}
// (2) loop head: the body's row is ρ[w*s,(w+1)*s) : Uninit ⇒ Init @E — NOT the identity
//     on ρ. §2.7 then requires a written head row, and the only invariant that makes
//     initiation and consecution go through is a prefix run:
//         head row { ρ : prefix [0,w*s) Init, suffix [w*s,n) Uninit }
//     i.e. HIS-D3-15's prefix-run automaton, written by hand at every buffer-filling
//     loop. §4.4's "loop: zero in the common case" is wrong for the commonest loop. [S5]
// (3) parallel overlap: the footprints are dis by the extent algebra, granted. But the
//     STATE map of overlapping iterations must compose, and §2.7 defines composition
//     only for incoming CFG edges under equality. No rule composes carve-entry exit
//     states across overlapping iterations.                                        [unnamed]
```

Revised verdict: **accepted with a stated cost** — one loop-head row with a
prefix-run invariant, plus whichever of S6's three exits the model takes.

### O4. P16 — candidate: "accepted as required. Cost: one row entry per captured store". **Overturn: R15(a) violated; three mechanisms unnamed.**

```text
fn kernel<E>(c: ptr<ρ, Cols<E>>) row { ρ : Init ⇒ Init @E }
// the default carve is "computed from the INSTANTIATED type" (§4.1 R15 row).
//   E = u64            ⇒ entries { .a … .h, padding }
//   E = buffer<u64>    ⇒ entries { .a, backing(.a), … , padding }
// §2.6's within-one-entry test therefore gives DIFFERENT verdicts for one unchanged
//   body at two instances ⇒ the body is checked per instance.
// REJECT the R15 grade: R15(a) requires "checked once for all instances".          [F2]

fn map_nodes<T, ρ>(g: ptr<ρ, Pool<Node<T>>>, f: fn(&ro T) -> T row { @R })
{ par_for k in g.live { set elem(k).data = f(&ro elem(k).data) } }
// dis(elem(k), elem(k')) is claimed "by the element partition". §2.1 has no entry form
//   for a symbolic family over a runtime-sized set, and carves(ρ) is an ordered LIST.  [S7]
// f's row is a row IN A FUNCTION TYPE; accepting a closure whose row is finer or
//   coarser needs a row subsumption judgment that is never defined.                   [S9]

let h = |slice : ptr<σ, buffer<u8>>| helper(slice, input)
// σ is a parameter of the closure's row ⇒ higher-rank store polymorphism. R15(a)
//   demands "instantiation is decidable by a fixed rule"; no rule is given.           [S9]

fn pick<N: Nominal>(c, x: N, y: N) -> N
  row { stores(N)@x : … ; stores(N)@y : … ; result : origin ∈ {x,y} }
// `stores(N)` and the `@x` qualifier are constructs absent from §2.4's grammar.       [S10]
// R15's metric is met at 2·|stores(N)|, NOT at "the identity on coarse storages".
```

Revised verdict: **violated as stated** for R15(a)'s check-once clause;
**partial** on the parameter metric.

### O5. P3 — candidate: "accepted with a stated cost". **Overturn: the parallel map is not expressible.**

```text
par_for k in P.live { write(ρP[k].data, f(read(ρP[k].data))) }
// accept requires dis(ρP[k], ρP[k']) "by the partition". The partition in question is
//   an element carve over ρP's backing with one entry PER LIVE SLOT at runtime.
//   §2.1's entry forms: .f | backing(.f) | [i] (a PROVED index) | [lo..hi) | \S.
//   None of them is a binder-indexed family, and §2.3's carves(ρ) is a finite ordered
//   list. So the fact the verdict rests on has no carrier.                         [S7]
// Note the four link writes and the removal are unaffected: they rest on state, and
//   the candidate's §6.2(a) argument for those stands.
```

Revised verdict: **accepted for the sequential half; the parallel half needs a
named parametric carve entry** and its `dis` rule, which is a fourth D1 member
the tuple does not claim.

## 3. What survives

The candidate's strongest claims are not damaged by any of the above: safety
never consults a window (§6.2(a)) is correct — none of P2, P3, P4, P7, P9 or
P13's refusals reads `carves`; the ladder's finding is honored; M2 holds by
construction (no drop flag, no pin count, no occupancy structure); M5 holds;
and M1 holds *for the judgments that are actually specified* — every failure I
found under M1 is an **absent** procedure (F3, F4, S7, S9), not a searching one.
The tuple's real cost profile, restated honestly, is:

| Row | Candidate | This critique |
|---|---|---|
| M1 | met | **partial** — four judgments unnamed (F3, F4, S7, S9); no admitted family searches |
| M7 | met | **partial** — two rejection shapes have non-local fixes; no repair measurement |
| M8 | partial, 4–5k | **partial, ≥10k** — ≥30 cards, no tokenizer, and suspension is not removed |
| M9 | partial | **partial** — P5 holds only for flat structs; P6 is not token-free; the emitter map is uncharged |
| M10 | met | **partial** — O(k²) for the entries that matter; type-edit reach exceeds the interface; the inherited family is measured red |
| R2 | met | **violated, undeclared** — P8 has no accepted spelling |
| R4 | met | **partial** — F5 and F6 license facts the model does not establish |
| R15 | met | **violated, undeclared** — per-instance default carve defeats check-once |

# Critique of `window-focus` — lens: SOUNDNESS AND THE PROGRAMS

Refuter lens: re-derive P1, P2, P4, P7, P9 and P13 independently under
[candidate-wildcard.md](candidate-wildcard.md) **as written**; find lines whose
accept/reject is wrong, hazards from R1–R3, R11, R12 that slip through, M2(ii)
violations hidden as a library or a typed outcome, facts the candidate needs
but never says where they come from, and couplings C1–C18 it silently retunes.
Nothing here is argued by assertion: every claim is a derivation from the
candidate's own §2 rules against the requirement text of VERDICT-D0 §2.

Where the candidate itself declares a loss (W1–W8, R5/R6/R8b/R13/R14 graded
partial, P8(a) rejected) I do not re-charge it. Every finding below is
something the candidate claims it does *not* pay.

C1 ("one refinement vocabulary serves state, distinctness, footprints and kills") is silently retuned: this vocabulary serves distinctness and footprints but not state. | State a third, persistent structure in §2.3 — a per-coarse-name map from *resolved paths* (not window-scoped fine names) to automaton states — and say how a window's write-back updates it; then re-grade M4 and M8, because that is a third name kind. |
