## 2. Program verdicts overturned, with derivations

Notation follows the ladder: per-line `accept` / `REJECT` with the fact used.
Each block is my derivation, not the candidate's.

### P13 — overturned: **hazard admitted**, not "accepted as required"

The candidate's headline claim is that the mutual exclusion of interior
pointers and third-party relocation is *structural*. It is not: there is no
type for the pointer it forms.

```text
struct Hold<ρ> { at: ptr<ρ, Node> }       // accept: §2.8 "struct field holding a pointer: the store name as a
                                          //   parameter of the struct". ρ is a COARSE name — §2.2 admits no other
type Pool states { Settled } transitions { }
h = handle into the pool                  // accept: an ordinary copyable value
focus ρP as { S = .slot(h) } {            // accept: a partial carve, one entry plus complement
  p = pointer_of(h)                       // the candidate says p's name is FINE. QUESTION IT NEVER ANSWERS:
                                          //   what is p's TYPE? §2.1: a fine name is "never in any type";
                                          //   §2.2: the whole type grammar is ptr<ρ,T> | &ro ptr<ρ,T>.
                                          //   The only well-formed typing is p : ptr<ρP, Node>
  hold = Hold { at: p }                   // accept: the field's type is ptr<ρP,Node>, p's type is ptr<ρP,Node>.
                                          //   No rule in §2 forbids this; §2.3's dis() already treats ρP as S's root
}                                         // close: S retires. `hold` names ρP and is untouched by the close
pool.compact()                            // accept: carves(ρP) is empty — the candidate's own L10 verdict
read(deref(hold.at).data)                 // accept under EVERY rule in §2: σ(ρP)=Settled, no window open, no carve
                                          //   to meet, no state edge to fail.
                                          //   >>> HAZARD: the object moved. R1(a)(ii)/(iii) and R8a's interior-
                                          //   pointer clause are violated with no diagnostic. M7 has nothing to say
```

The same hole is reachable without the struct: `p` itself, typed
`ptr<ρP,Node>`, may simply be read after the window closes, or returned.
The candidate's defence — "there is no way to write this line at all" —
requires a scope discipline on *bindings* and a fine-name-carrying pointer
type. Both contradict §2.2 and W2, and both are M4/M8 costs it has not
counted. **Revised verdict: rejected — R8a and R1 are violated undeclared,
and the fix is the two-level split's most expensive extension.**

Secondary overturn on the same program: `read(pool[h])` is **not** accepted
(S8) — `compact`'s `@E` killed the fact `pool[h]` needs, and no invariant
re-establishes it.

### P2 — overturned: **the parallel overlap has no ground, or the model emits a false fact**

```text
A = arena_new()                           // accept: mint ρM, ρS; σ=Init
(b1,ρ1) = alloc(A,64)                     // accept: row { ρM:Init⇒Init @W; ρS:Init⇒Init @W; fresh ∃ρ1 ⊑ ρS : Uninit }
(b2,ρ2) = alloc(A,64)                     // accept: likewise
(b3,ρ3) = alloc(A,64)                     // accept: likewise
                                          // >>> now ask for dis(ρ1,ρ2). §2.3 gives two clauses and neither fires:
                                          //   (1) "different entries of ONE carve" — no carve was opened. §2.5 lists
                                          //       "arena alloc" and "window open" as DIFFERENT events; a promotion
                                          //       is not a carve and mints no window
                                          //   (2) "coarse roots ⊑-incomparable" — ρ1 ⊑ ρS and ρ2 ⊑ ρS, so the roots
                                          //       COINCIDE. This is the reading that makes the candidate's own note
                                          //       "dis(ρ1,ρS) is FALSE" true; on the other reading (ρ1 and ρ2 are
                                          //       themselves the roots, mutually incomparable) distinctness comes
                                          //       from INEQUALITY OF NAMES, which R4(b) and C3 forbid by name
fill(b1) ∥ fill(b2) ∥ fill(b3)            // OVERTURNED. Reading (1): no R5(a)(i) ground ⇒ the construct is erasable,
                                          //   so M5 leaves it SEQUENTIAL. P2's requirement "must be permitted to
                                          //   overlap" is unmet.
                                          //   Reading (2): permitted, on a fact C3 forbids — R4(a) soundness fails
                                          //   if alloc's body ever returns overlapping extents, and nothing in the
                                          //   ROW (the only contract, R7) forbids it
free(A,b2)                                // accept on σ(ρ2):=Gone; but "ρ2's extent returns to ρS" is not a clause
                                          //   of §2.4's grammar (S7)
(b4,ρ4) = alloc(A,32)                     // accept the mint; dis(ρ4,ρ1) has the identical gap
read(b2)                                  // REJECT: σ(ρ2)=Gone. R1(a)(ii). The candidate is RIGHT on this line —
                                          //   and it is right for a reason that needs no carve and no window at all
read(b1)                                  // accept on state; but contents facts about ρ1 were killed by ρS @W at
                                          //   BOTH L6 and L9 (S10), a kill class R6's verdict does not mention
free(A,b1); free(A,b3); free(A,b4)        // accept
```

And separately, at the same L2:

```text
(b1,ρ1) = alloc(A,64)                     // §2.9 last row: "fresh ∃ρ on a result ⇒ noalias return", quoting
                                          //   "disjoint from the storage for any other object accessible to the
                                          //   caller".
                                          // >>> FALSE FACT: ρ1 ⊑ ρS, and ρS is reachable from the caller's A.
                                          //   The candidate's own P2 note says dis(ρ1,ρS) is FALSE. R4(a)'s
                                          //   soundness clause is violated by the model's own emission table
```

**Revised verdict: accepted sequentially, with the required parallel overlap
unmet — or accepted with an unsound licensed fact and a false `noalias`
return.** Not "accepted as required, —".

### P4 — overturned: **an unrepresentable post-`push` state and an R2 leak**

```text
struct Cursor<ρ> { at: ptr<ρ, Vector<u64>>, i: u64 }
c = Cursor { at: v, i: 0 }                // accept: §2.8 permits the stored pointer; no loan is created. This is
                                          //   the candidate's real win over a borrow design and it survives
a = c.read()                              // accept: σ(ρ)=Init, i < len_of(ρ) discharged
push(v, 5)                                // accept that the CALL runs (carves(ρ) empty, if a signature row is not a
                                          //   window — see F6, where the other reading blocks free(v) below).
                                          // >>> OVERTURNED on the post-state: the row's arms are selected by
                                          //   cap_of(ρ) >= len+1, a runtime value. A call is NOT a source-visible
                                          //   branch, so §2.7's join — which demands σ be EQUAL on incoming edges —
                                          //   has no edges to equate. §2.3 holds exactly ONE σ per name. The
                                          //   checker must now hold "σ(backing(ρ)) is Init or Gone depending on c",
                                          //   for which the model has no vocabulary: W5 refuses C6 (state as a term
                                          //   over captured conditions) precisely to keep condition atoms out
b = c.read()                              // the candidate's REJECT-without-reserve is the right ANSWER for the wrong
                                          //   REASON: there is no representable state to reject against
free(v)                                   // >>> OVERTURNED. row { ρ : Init ⇒ Gone } names ρ ONLY. The backing —
                                          //   β, or the β' push minted — is never ended. R2: "every allocation is
                                          //   released exactly once on every path" fails, silently.
                                          //   And if β' is meant to be a carve ENTRY of ρ, then push's `fresh β'`
                                          //   mints a FINE name, which §2.4's `fresh ∃ρ' ⊑ ρ` (a COARSE promotion)
                                          //   cannot express and which free's row cannot name (S6, C9 retuned)
c.read()                                  // REJECT: σ(ρ)=Gone. R1(a)(ii). Correct, and again carve-free
```

**Revised verdict: accepted only with the reserve proof *and* an unstated
disjunctive-state mechanism the candidate refuses elsewhere; R2 is violated on
the backing on every path.** Not "accepted as required, one reserve proof".

The part of P4 that genuinely works — a stored pointer in a struct does not
block `push` — needs none of D1's split, D4's windows or D3's automata. It
needs only per-storage state and a contract-visible reallocation event, which
is the ladder's Step 3.

### P9 — overturned: **`pick`'s result is untypeable and its state edges are undefined**

```text
fn drain(x: ptr<ρ,T>)  row { ρ : Init ⇒ Uninit }
drain(x) ; read(x)                        // REJECT: σ(ρ)=Uninit. R1(a)(i). Correct — for the whole-storage spelling.
                                          //   For the field spelling `row { ρ.f : Init ⇒ Uninit }` the exit state
                                          //   must survive the call window's close, and F1 says there is no carrier
fn reserve(v, m) row { ρ : Init⇒Init @E ;
    backing(ρ) : Init⇒Init when cap_of(ρ) >= m | Init⇒Gone, fresh β' otherwise }
reserve(v,100) ; read(pe)                 // >>> OVERTURNED on the unproved path, exactly as P4's push (F7): the
                                          //   "otherwise REJECT" verdict presumes a representable disjunction the
                                          //   model does not have. Either C6 comes back, or reserve must declare a
                                          //   typed OUTCOME the source writes — which makes every reserve/push site
                                          //   two-armed (R12's own red cost, unpriced here)
fn pick(c, x: ptr<ρ,T>, y: ptr<σ,T>) -> ptr<π,T>
    row { ρ:Init⇒Init @R ; σ:Init⇒Init @R ; result : π ∈ {ρ,σ} }
                                          // >>> OVERTURNED AT THE DECLARATION. §2.2: "ptr<ρ,T> — ρ is a coarse
                                          //   store NAME. That is the whole of it." π is a SET. There is no
                                          //   set-valued store parameter in the type grammar, and §2.3 defines
                                          //   dis() only over names, so dis(π, τ) is undefined for every later τ.
                                          //   R7 rejects a declaration whose result names an origin no caller can
                                          //   name; here no caller can even WRITE the result's type
z = pick(c,x,y) ; write(z,1)              // accept IF the type grammar is patched: footprint {ρ,σ}, both killed.
                                          //   The candidate's line is right, conditionally
free(z)                                   // >>> OVERTURNED — the candidate never derives this line, and it is the
                                          //   one that decides R2. §2.5's free is `ρ : Init|Uninit ⇒ Gone` on ONE
                                          //   name. Over {ρ,σ}:
                                          //     both ⇒ Gone: the survivor is unfreeable (R2 leak) and a later legal
                                          //                  read is wrongly REJECTED
                                          //     neither:     use-after-free is ACCEPTED (R1(a)(ii))
                                          //     one, chosen: by what? the choice is a runtime value — M2(ii)
take(z)                                   // same gap on the take edge, and here the hole is invisible through the
                                          //   un-updated name: a subsequent read(x) accepts on σ(ρ)=Init. R1(a)(i)
focus ρ as { A = ρ.left } { pick(c,x,y) } // the candidate REJECTS and calls it a feature (W6). Under §2.7's call
                                          //   rule this also rejects EVERY call whose row names ρ whole inside any
                                          //   partial carve of ρ — and under F6's first reading, inside every
                                          //   function body, since a signature row is itself a window
```

**Revised verdict: not accepted as required — `pick` is untypeable as
declared, and the origin set has no state semantics, which is the mechanism
P8(b) (the candidate's only accepted spelling of P8) also depends on.**

### P7 — overturned: **accepted only in its whole-storage spelling; §2.5's own field rule has no carrier**

The literal program survives. What fails is the mechanism the candidate states
for it, one level down — and R1(a)(i) says "initialized **in the selected
part**", so the field level is the requirement, not a refinement of it.

```text
p, q : ptr<ρ, T>
v = take(p)                               // accept: row { ρ : Init ⇒ Uninit }
read(q)                                   // REJECT: σ(ρ)=Uninit. R1(a)(i). Correct
put(q, move v)                            // accept: row { ρ : Uninit ⇒ Init }. Correct — and note this line needs
                                          //   only per-storage state: no window, no carve, no grade, no automaton
read(p)                                   // accept. Correct
old = replace(p, new)                     // accept: row { ρ : Init ⇒ Init @W }, one event (SET-2). Correct
read(q)                                   // accept: contents killed by @W, re-established by ensures. Correct
free ρ                                    // accept ONLY if no signature row opened a window over ρ (F6); §2.5's
                                          //   free "requires carves(ρ) empty"
read(p) ; read(q)                         // REJECT, REJECT: σ(ρ)=Gone. R1(a)(ii). Correct, neither privileged

// now the same program one level down — the ladder's Step 1, and §2.5's OWN spelling of `take`
s : S in ρ ; px = ptr_of(s.x) ; py = ptr_of(s.y)
v = take(px)                              // §2.5's table: "take(p) at ρ.x ⇒ σ(ρ.x) := Uninit (a hole in the
                                          //   storage, visible to every alias)".
                                          // >>> OVERTURNED: no window is open here. §2.3 gives ρ exactly ONE σ,
                                          //   plus per-entry σ's that live only inside `carves(ρ)`, "a stack of
                                          //   OPEN windows". There is no carrier for σ(ρ.x) at this point
read(py)                                  // Under the only coarsening the held structure permits (σ(ρ):=Uninit)
                                          //   this REJECTS — contradicting the ladder's Step 1 ("legal: 'a.x
                                          //   unchanged") and R1(a)(i)'s "initialized IN THE SELECTED PART".
                                          //   Under the alternative (a persistent per-path state map) the model
                                          //   gains a THIRD name kind the candidate never states, whose keys
                                          //   outlive every window — which is the thing D1's split forbids
read(px)                                  // REJECT: correct under either reading, for the wrong stated reason
```

**Revised verdict: accepted as written, on a mechanism that does not exist for
the field, element or slot spellings the same requirement covers (P3's
`σ(ρP[m])` after `remove` returns, P9's field-level `drain`, P11's per-slot
`Filled`).**

### P1 — overturned on two lines and on the exit rule

```text
v : ptr<ρ, Vector<u64>>
focus β as { A = β[i], B = β[j] } {       // accept the head, but the obligations `i<n, j<n, i!=j` have no place in
                                          //   §2.1's grammar to be WRITTEN (m2)
  va = take(A)                            // accept: σ(A) := Uninit
  vb = take(B)                            // accept: σ(B) := Uninit
  write(A, f(va)) ∥ write(B, g(vb))       // >>> OVERTURNED: `write` is not an edge in §2.5's table. As a `put` it
                                          //   sets σ(A):=Init; as a `replace` its Init⇒Init precondition FAILS on
                                          //   an entry the take just emptied ⇒ REJECT
  x = read(β[k])                          // REJECT: β[k] may meet A or B and names neither. Correct, and M7's
                                          //   payload is the strongest thing in the candidate
  use k != i && k != j ;
  x = read(β[k])                          // accept: provably within the complement entry. Correct
  put(A, move va') ; put(B, move vb')     // >>> OVERTURNED if the L4 writes were `put`s: σ(A)=σ(B)=Init already, and
                                          //   §2.5 admits `put` only as Uninit ⇒ Init ⇒ REJECT (or it is a silent
                                          //   `replace` that drops the old value — R2 for an affine element type)
}                                         // close: exit row demands Init. Correct for this path
push(v, x)                                // accept: carves(β) empty
```

and the escape the close rule does not cover:

```text
focus β as { A = β[i], B = β[j] } {
  va = take(A)                            // σ(A) := Uninit; va is an affine value
  if c { return }                         // >>> NO RULE. §2.7 attaches the exit obligation to "window close", and
                                          //   its join note asserts windows are "balanced by construction" —
                                          //   which a return or a break falsifies. β[i] leaves the window Uninit
                                          //   with no diagnostic (R1(a)(i) for any later read) and va leaves
                                          //   unreleased (R2)
  put(A, move va)
}
```

**Revised verdict: the program is accepted, but two derived lines are wrong
under the candidate's own §2.5 table, and the window has an unguarded exit
edge.** Not "accepted as required, one `focus` line and one written
inequality".

---

## 3. Couplings silently retuned

| Coupling | Retune | Where it shows |
|---|---|---|
| **C1** identity granularity: "one refinement vocabulary serves state, distinctness, footprints and kills" | The fine vocabulary serves distinctness and footprints; it cannot serve **state** outside a window, so state needs a third, unstated keying | F1; P7, P3, P9, P11 |
| **C3** distinct-by-default with call-site discharge, "never inequality of identity names", "sub-identities included" | Sibling promoted names are distinguished either by nothing or by name inequality. The candidate's D6 claim that C3's hardest clause is discharged "structurally, because fine names never cross a call" ignores that P2's blocks are **coarse** names sharing a parent | F3; P2 |
| **C5** sequential aliased writes allowed | Under the reading that gives P5 its per-load facts, §2.6's strictness is in force in every function body, so P3's runtime-pointer link writes are refused — R9's stated negative test | F6, S3; P3 |
| **C6** state as a term over captured conditions | Declared refused in W5, then required at two places with no substitute: a two-armed row at an unproved call, and P8(b)'s join | F5, F7; P4, P8, P9 |
| **C9** backing identity as an existential a contract may replace | Demoted from a coarse existential to a fine carve entry, and then needed at a coarse cut (`free`, a replaced `β'`) | S6; P4 |
| **C2 / R6** one distinctness relation, keyed the same way | Containment kills (a write to a parent kills every child's contents) are a third kill class R6's verdict does not name | S10; P2 |

---

## 4. What survives

Stated so the refutation is not read as a rejection of the whole tuple.

- **Per-storage state as the safety mechanism holds up.** Every memory-safety
  REJECT I could not overturn — P2's `read(b2)`, P4's `c.read()` after
  `free`, P7's four rejections, P9's `read(x)` after `drain` — reads `σ`, not
  `carves`. The candidate's answer (a) to its own strongest objection is
  correct: safety never consults a window. That is also the reason F1 is
  fatal rather than cosmetic — every one of those rejections is at the wrong
  granularity for R1(a)(i)'s "in the selected part".
- **P6's shape is genuinely clean** and I found nothing to overturn in it: the
  call is the window, the actual's extent is the entry, and the half-open
  algebra is the whole discharge.
- **M7's payload shape is the best in the candidate.** Four rejection shapes,
  each with a tree location and a named fact, is a real answer to a red row.
- **The `@0/@R/@W/@E` chain is decidable, monotone and erasable**, and I found
  no acceptance verdict depending on it (M5 holds).

The failures are concentrated in exactly one place: the two-level name split
does not have the closure property the candidate claims for it. Fine names
cannot carry state across a call (F1), cannot be typed when a pointer must
hold one (F2), cannot be minted in unbounded number (S4), and cannot be
replaced at a cut (S6) — while coarse names cannot express sibling
disjointness (F3) or a disjunctive post-state (F5, F7). Every fatal finding
is a case where the model needs a name in the level it just forbade.


# File: judge-1.md

# Judge 1 — the language designer who must keep the specification small

Research date: 2026-09-16. Scope: the twelve core-model candidates in
`core/candidate-*.md` and the twenty-four critiques in `core/critique-*.md`,
scored against VERDICT-D0 §2's settled rows, §4's couplings, §5's premises and
§7's settled owner interims, with the hazard ladder of MECHANISM-MAP §3 and the
programs P1–P19.

My lens is stated so the weighting is legible: I have to live with the chosen
core model for years and keep the specification small. That biases me toward
(a) a taught surface that is countable and closed, (b) one mechanism per
question, (c) failures that are *named and local* rather than *structural*, and
(d) repairs that are grafts rather than redesigns. It does not license me to
ignore a hazard; where a candidate admits one, the score falls regardless of
how small its specification is.

---

## 1. Method and the cap

Seven axes, 0–10 each, scored **after** the critiques, not from the candidates'
own scorecards:

| Axis | Rows |
|---|---|
| safety | R1, R2, R3, R11, R12, M2 |
| interference and facts | R4, R5, R6, R9 |
| modularity and abstraction | R7, R15 |
| storage and relocation | R8a, R8b |
| determinism and cost | M1, M10 |
| writer cost | M4, M7, M8 |
| performance | M5, M9 |

The cap: **a candidate that violates M1 or M2 without declaring it is capped at
3 on that axis.** M1 and M10 sit in *determinism and cost*; M2 sits in *safety*.
I applied the cap from the critiques' findings, not from the candidates' own
verdicts, and I did **not** re-charge a violation a candidate declared itself.

The cap fires on almost everything. That is the single most important fact this
debate produced, and it deserves stating plainly before the table.

### 1.1 The cap fires eleven times out of twelve

| Candidate | M1 violated undeclared? | M2 violated undeclared? |
|---|---|---|
| brand-context | yes (four unnamed families: atom entailment, quantifier instantiation, symbolic-coefficient intervals, the kill scan) | no (M10 declared; the M2 horn at P7's `free` is arguably R2) |
| brand-tokens | yes (exact-cover search over symbolic extents; dependent `Pt` types; loop multiset equality) | yes (P13's `fixup` unerased is a relocation-table lookup) |
| reference-refined | yes (propositional entailment over condition terms, exponential; P6's multiplication monotonicity) | yes (P3's occupancy tag and P11's `is_hole` at a runtime index) |
| value-semantics | **no** — M1 is genuinely met (BIND is a two-point lattice, PATH is syntactic prefix, AFF is a table, EXT is a fixed fragment) | yes (the bounds arm of `pool[h]`) |
| whole-program-pinned | yes (the tool *is* the acceptance relation; widening inside it; no family has a stated degree) | yes (the `fixup` clause) |
| generational-handles | yes (quantified container state as an unnamed fifth family; no widening for `Live`/`Gen` at a loop head) | yes (Tier A's free list is either compiler bookkeeping or an M3 entry; the Tier B concession does not cover it) |
| typestate-protocols | yes (the join is not a total function: the state hierarchy is undeclared and indexed states make the lattice infinite) | no (the failure is M3: `mints` is a writer-written distinctness axiom) |
| views-fold-unfold | borderline — M1 survives only by fixing an enumeration order over `r^m` witnesses; M10 is violated undeclared | yes (P13's `fixup`: erased it is uncomputable, unerased it is a relocation table) |
| ownership-topology | yes (the term grammar cannot hold the terms it uses; reassignable atoms; `p = p.next` does not terminate) | yes (`with_fixup`'s root-set walk) |
| columns-first | yes (P6's tiling goal is outside the only named family; atom eviction at the `k` bound is unspecified) | yes (P13's `read(pool[h])` needs runtime bookkeeping or an unerased map) |
| refinement-heap | yes (the stated closure does not terminate; rule (d) is self-contradictory) | no (the soundness critique explicitly found no smuggled check) |
| window-focus | yes (`dis` is not total over the name grammar it must decide; `fresh ∃ρ'` has no discharge) | no (M2 holds by construction: no drop flag, no pin count, no occupancy structure) |

Eleven of twelve violate M1 undeclared. Eight of twelve violate M2 undeclared.
**Exactly one candidate has a determinism story that survives its own
critiques.** That is `value-semantics`, and it survives it for a structural
reason, not by luck: it is the only tuple whose flow-sensitive state is one
boolean per name, so there is no term language to normalize, no context to
close over, no fixpoint to bound and no fragment to name beyond the one every
candidate needs for R11 anyway.

I want to be explicit that this is not me rewarding minimalism for its own
sake. M1 is a *constraint row*, not a preference. A candidate that cannot state
its own decision procedure has not produced a language; it has produced a
sketch of one, and I would be maintaining the sketch.

---

## 2. Scores

| Candidate | safety | interf. | modul. | storage | determ. | writer | perf. | **total** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **value-semantics** | 3* | 4 | 5 | 5 | 6 | 8 | 6 | **37** |
| window-focus | 3 | 4 | 3 | 3 | 3* | 5 | 6 | **27** |
| columns-first | 2* | 5 | 3 | 5 | 2* | 3 | 6 | **26** |
| brand-context | 2 | 4 | 3 | 4 | 2* | 5 | 5 | **25** |
| generational-handles | 2* | 4 | 4 | 5 | 2* | 4 | 4 | **25** |
| views-fold-unfold | 3* | 6 | 4 | 4 | 3 | 2 | 3 | **25** |
| ownership-topology | 2* | 4 | 4 | 3 | 2* | 5 | 5 | **25** |
| brand-tokens | 2* | 4 | 3 | 4 | 2* | 3 | 4 | **22** |
| reference-refined | 2* | 4 | 3 | 4 | 2* | 2 | 5 | **22** |
| whole-program-pinned | 2* | 4 | 3 | 3 | 2* | 4 | 4 | **22** |
| typestate-protocols | 2 | 3 | 3 | 4 | 2* | 3 | 4 | **21** |
| refinement-heap | 2 | 3 | 4 | 4 | 1* | 2 | 4 | **20** |

`*` = the axis is at or under the M1/M2 cap.

---

## 3. Derivation of the scores, candidate by candidate

### 3.1 value-semantics — 37

**safety 3 (capped).** The non-pool fragment is the strongest R1 story in the
whole set and it is strong *by construction*: every binding is initialized where
it is bound, storage ends only where a name is unbound, and no name reaches into
storage that can change layout. P2 gets the strongest possible form of "every
old pointer into `b2` is refused" — there is no old pointer, because `Buf` is
affine and was consumed. That is a better answer than any generation, brand,
token or view in the set.

Against it: the cost critique's F1 is correct and undeclared. `pool[h]`'s `None`
arm carries two conditions, and the second ("`h` is not a key of *this* pool")
is a bounds predicate the checker did not discharge, which M2(a)(ii) names
verbatim as refused. The candidate's §6 answer 3 defends only the vacancy
discriminant, where the defence is genuinely good (both arms safe, both written,
deleting the branch gives a wrong program not an unsafe one) — and does not
reach the bounds arm, where deleting the compare is an out-of-bounds read. So
the cap fires. Add the soundness critique's F3 (AFF is unsound for any non-copy
value reaching storage through a handle, a pool row or `Foreign<T>` — the
candidate's own R10 answer supplies the counterexample) and W1's stale-slot
residue, and 3 is the honest number.

I score it 3 rather than 2 because both defects have the *same* named repair
(brand `Handle` by its pool) and because the repair is a type parameter on one
library type, not a language mechanism. Compare with the eight candidates whose
fatal findings require adding a mechanism the tuple explicitly forecloses.

**interference and facts 4.** R6's "footprint = the written access path" is real
for projected calls — `helper(inout out[w*s .. (w+1)*s], let input)` is exactly
the shape the blind-writer report names as the fix for its 34-of-41 `len()` tax —
and false for whole-container calls (`push(inout v, …)`, `insert(inout g, …)`,
`get(inout cache, k)`), which is most of the interesting ones (cost S5). R5
ground (i) is discharged from the parameter list for P1, P2, P5 and P6. R4 rests
on three relations (PATH, EXT, AFF) where C2 demands one, and the weakest of the
three is read in R5's rejecting direction. R9 is narrowed: two simultaneous
long-lived writable names are unwritable, which is the shape R9 exists to admit.

**modularity and abstraction 5.** Zero identity parameters is the floor of
R15(e)'s metric and no other candidate is close; `PATH`/`EXT`/`AFF` are
structural inside a generic body, so the facts cross the boundary for free.
Against it: R15(a)'s check-once clause is violated at `pick_n` (one generic
definition, two verdicts by value class — cost F2), the closure's captured read
is missing from its interface (cost S11), the closure binder family does not
exist in the language today, and R7 fails for every pooled API because a
returned `Handle` names an origin no caller can read from the signature
(soundness S10).

**storage and relocation 5.** The best R8a answer in the set, and again by
construction: `pointer_of(h)` is *unwritable*, so interior pointers and
third-party relocation cannot both appear. The set of ending events is small and
syntactic. The costs are real — `read(pool[h])` after `compact` is not derivable
(soundness P13), key-renumbering compaction is refused, and R8b fights
compiler-chosen placement so every demand must pin a binding — but the shape of
the answer is right and cheap.

**determinism and cost 6 — the decisive axis.** Four families, each genuinely
fixed: `BIND` a two-point lattice reached in at most two passes over a reducible
CFG; `PATH` a syntactic prefix comparison; `AFF` a fixed-table type fact; `EXT`
a fixed linear-arithmetic fragment. No search, no solver, no budget, no
iteration cap, no term language, no condition atoms, no fixpoint over an
infinite lattice. The cost critique's own §2 concedes "M1 is met".

I do not score it higher because M10 is not clean: every EXT and REF fact enters
the ProofContext, whose measured growing cost is 29.9 / 164.5 / 1691.0 ms at
N = 16/32/64 with a cubic transitive product, and the candidate's own §4.2 lists
EXT's degree as unpaid (cost S1). The generic-instantiation reach in the callee
direction is also understated (cost S2). But these are *measurement* debts
against a family every candidate inherits, not an unnamed procedure — the
difference between "we owe an exponent" and "we owe a decision procedure".

**writer cost 8 — the axis my lens weights hardest.** The taught surface for
D1–D4 is three conventions (`let`, `inout`, `sink`), one projection form
(`with … as`), one `sink` statement, path overlap, extent arithmetic, and affine
distinctness. No lifetimes, no regions, no identities, no state lattice, no
condition terms, no loan durations, no permission tokens, no brands, no
automata, no views, no fold/unfold, no rows, no grades, no epochs, no
generations, no carve grammar, no split table. The cost critique counts eleven
constructs against the candidate's five and is right to; eleven is still less
than a third of the nearest rival's count and less than a quarter of
`views-fold-unfold`'s ~50.

M4 is the best in the set: one spelling per construct across a tiny inventory,
with no mode axis, no region syntax and no identity syntax to duplicate. M7 is
met for three of its four rejection kinds and fails only for the
projection-escape class, whose repair (threading a container parameter) is a
signature cascade — a real M7(a) failure and the reason this is 8 and not 9.

For the lens: this is the only candidate I could teach in one card set and
maintain without a second sub-language beside the one the compiler already has.

**performance 6.** P5 and P6's obvious shape is the written shape with no hints,
no guards and no versioning, and the per-column facts are a consequence of the
field discipline rather than a writer annotation. Against it: the backend scope
is still manufactured at emission from the resolved path exactly as the retired
prototype did (cost S7), so the claimed "type consequence rather than backend
re-derivation" gain is withdrawn; pooled access costs an indirection; vacancy
costs a tag word and a branch where it is used; and P6's disjointness needs
`ProvedRangePartition` with two retained nonnegativity proofs rather than the
named linear fragment (cost S3).

### 3.2 window-focus — 27

The highest-scoring of the rest, and the one with the best *idea*: "a row is
the only contract, and a row carves" is a genuinely new shape, and making the
source-level fine name and LLVM's window-scoped `!alias.scope` the same object
is the sharpest M9 argument anyone offered. M7's four rejection shapes, each with
a tree location and a named fact, is the best answer to a red row in the set.

What holds it to 27 is the soundness critique's closing sentence, which I think
is exactly right and is a structural indictment rather than a repair list:
**every fatal finding is a case where the model needs a name in the level it
just forbade.** Fine names cannot carry state across a call (F1), cannot be
typed when a pointer must hold one (F2 — and the interior pointer therefore
escapes and the use-after-relocation is admitted with no diagnostic), cannot be
minted in unbounded number (S4), cannot be replaced at a cut (S6); coarse names
cannot express sibling disjointness (F3) or a disjunctive post-state (F5, F7).
P8 has *no* accepted spelling, so R2's own acceptance test fails undeclared.
R15's check-once clause is violated undeclared because the default carve is
computed from the instantiated type.

Determinism 3 (at the cap): the M1 failures are *absent* procedures rather than
searching ones, which is the most repairable form of the failure, and the
checking model (row composition plus two entailments at a loop head, no
fixpoint) is structurally cheap. Writer cost 5: ≥30 cards and two name kinds
against a genuinely small per-program tax, and "removes suspension rules" is
false — the window stack is suspension re-spelled.

### 3.3 columns-first — 26

The best P5/P6/R6 results in the set, and the only candidate that answers R8b
without a second mechanism: the plane map *is* stride, offset and alignment, so
an `align(64)` demand has a home where the identity is declared. Its R6 story is
the cleanest statement of why the measured 34/41 tax disappears (the length
lives in a sibling plane, so an element write cannot kill it).

Against it: M4 is declared violated (four reference forms, two element spellings,
three carriers of absence) and +20 to +28 constructs against a budget already
2.7× red, which on my lens is decisive. And the soundness findings are not
repairs: extents have no liveness state, so P2's central negative test fails and
a double free is refused by nothing (F2); `disj` is an `iff` over four cases and
none applies to arena blocks (F3); origin sets are not in the grammar so a race
is admitted (F4); the ghost `slot_of` is erased so P13's accept reads the wrong
occupant (F5). Its own honest weakness list names the right thing: it wins the
programs that were never hard and pays in the pointer-shaped ones ownership
systems exist for.

### 3.4 The 25s

**brand-context** has the single best headline in the set — deleting the
exclusivity rule makes P7, P3's four link writes and R9 fall out for free, and
`distinct`-by-default keeps the default fact strong. Its M10 self-declaration is
honest where most would have hidden it. But `st` is a path-keyed map resolved
modulo may-equality at exactly one line of the whole document and by literal path
identity everywhere else, and every wrong verdict is an instance of that: a
double take duplicating an affine value, a traversal cursor reading ended
storage, a may-write marking both origins `Init`. Plus M1's "exactly four
families and no fifth" fails on its own derivations.

**generational-handles** is the most honest document in the set (its Tier A/B
split states its own refusal before the argument), and its P13 answer — the
handle *is* the contract-visible fixup form, written by the source — is
conceptually the best R8a result. But two independent critiques find that Tier A
also violates M2(ii) or M3 (the free list is either compiler bookkeeping or an
unenumerated entry), the ghost `σ` and the runtime `idx` are never related so
erasure has no theorem, and `free` requires only `Live(h)` so P7 leaks a linear
occupant.

**views-fold-unfold** has the best *interference* score in the set (6) and
deserves it: `⊗` genuinely *is* the disjointness relation, so C3's call-site
discharge problem disappears, and the frame rule gives R6 kills = 0 by rule
rather than by tuning a granularity. `Gone` as the absence of a view plus
never-reminted gnames is the cleanest treatment of address reuse anywhere. But
on my lens it is the worst candidate in the set on writer cost (2): ~50 taught
items, an open lemma family, and the writer authoring a proof script per
statement — and P5's unannotated fallback has a *measured* price in this
repository (2.1 vs 0.4 ns/element, 3.4–5.7×, flat across trip count), so M9's
obvious-shape clause is measured-negative, not at risk.

**ownership-topology** has the second-best authoring story of the
identity-carrying candidates — in P5, P6, P7, P8 and P9 the writer writes no
identity name at all — and one path grammar, one row grammar, one state
vocabulary is genuinely regular. It is undone by abolishing pointer duration and
then writing three rules that cannot be evaluated without one (`pin` release,
`drop p`, `with_fixup`), by index and extent children of one parent being
declared disjoint while overlapping, and by `p = p.next` not terminating.

### 3.5 The 20–22 band

**brand-tokens**, **reference-refined**, **whole-program-pinned**,
**typestate-protocols** and **refinement-heap** all pay a large specification
for a model whose central judgment its own critiques show is unspecified.

`reference-refined` deserves a specific note because it is the incumbent
family's best form: it correctly identifies the seam to cut (validity and
occupancy move to the path; permission stays on the reference), and cutting it is
what makes P2, P4, P7 and P11 derivable. But it adds ~45 addressable constructs
against a retirement list of six — roughly 7:1 in the wrong direction — and then
M1, the row the whole design is organized around, is violated undeclared in two
places. On my lens that is the worst trade in the set, which is why it scores 2
on writer cost.

`refinement-heap` is last because its load-bearing sentence fails on its own
terms: "the fragment is fixed, so acceptance is a total function of the bytes",
and the stated closure does not terminate while the one rule that buys its
flagship program contradicts the one argument offered for termination. It also
declares M8 and M10 violated, which I credit as honesty and still have to score.

---

## 4. Best base

**`value-semantics`.**

Four reasons, in the order my lens weights them.

1. **It is the only candidate whose acceptance procedure survives its own
   critiques.** M1 is met and the cost critique says so. Eleven of the other
   eleven violate M1 undeclared. A core model I cannot specify is a core model I
   cannot maintain.

2. **Its specification is the smallest by a factor of three.** Eleven constructs
   against 30–50 elsewhere, with one spelling per construct and no second
   sub-language beside the arithmetic fragment R11 already needs. That is the
   condition my lens exists to protect and no other candidate comes near it.

3. **Its residue is named, bounded and confined.** W1 states the loss, §3 grades
   P3 partial with the candidate at fault, and §6 answers the objection four ways
   without arguing it away. Compare with the eight candidates whose fatal
   findings were *undeclared*.

4. **Its repairs are grafts, not redesigns.** Branding `Handle` by its pool with
   a ghost generation closes the stale-slot residue, the bounds-arm M2 violation
   and the cross-pool confusion at once, and it costs one type parameter on one
   library type. Every other candidate's fatal findings require adding a
   mechanism the tuple explicitly forecloses — a fine name in a type, a per-extent
   liveness axis, an existential backing, an effect row on an arrow, a quantified
   token schema, a state-versioning discipline, a decision procedure that
   terminates.

What I am accepting by choosing it, stated so nobody has to discover it later:
second-class everything (no stored iterator, no stored callback holding a
projection, no `pick` returning a keepable reference), R9's two-simultaneous-
writers shape narrowed to sequential access through one path, and a migration
that is a rewrite rather than a delta. Those are capability losses, and they are
the right losses to take in exchange for a specification I can hold in my head.

---

## 5. What to graft

Each is a graft onto `value-semantics`, named with its source and the defect it
closes.

1. **Pool-branded handles with a ghost generation** — from `generational-handles`
   D1 (Tier A only: the generation is a ghost monotone term, never compared at
   run time). `Handle<P>` carries its pool; `Live(h)` is `σ(h) ∈ Live(P) ∧
   gen(P[σ(h)]) = γ(h)`. Closes W1's stale-slot residue, the cross-pool
   confusion, and the bounds arm of `pool[h]` that costs the M2 cap.

2. **A two-part footprint for container operations** — from `columns-first`'s
   plane/element split. A pool or cache operation names the addressed slot *and*
   a metadata path, instead of the whole container path. Closes P11's
   unconditional rejection of a held reader and restores R6 for whole-container
   calls, which is where the measured 34/41 tax survives today.

3. **The plane map as the layout vocabulary** — from `columns-first` D1/R8b.
   Declaring stride, offset, alignment and SoA/AoS where the type is declared
   answers R8b with no second mechanism, and it is the declaration P5 wants
   anyway. Moves R8b from partial to met without adding a construct.

4. **Restrict AFF to a proved relation over the containment structure** — the
   discipline from `brand-context` and `refinement-heap`'s reading of R4(b). AFF
   as a fixed table is unsound for any value reaching storage through a handle, a
   pool row or `Foreign<T>`; restrict it to values with no reachable indirection
   and derive the rest from PATH/EXT. Collapses three distinctness relations
   toward the one C2 demands.

5. **The `with` block as the scope-declaration site for `!alias.scope`** — from
   `window-focus`'s insight that a fact has a span, not a lifetime. The
   projection block is already exactly the shape
   `llvm.experimental.noalias.scope.decl` is defined to be, so the source
   construct and the backend fact become one object with no new vocabulary.

6. **The separating frame rule as the *statement* of R6** — from
   `views-fold-unfold`. Take the rule ("a call touches only what its footprint
   names, everything else survives by the rule, not by a kill heuristic"), not
   the view algebra that carries it. Value semantics already has the footprint;
   it lacks the statement.

7. **`old()`-indexed exit refinements with a fixed chaining rule** — a repair the
   value-semantics cost critique names as missing (S3). Without it P4's surviving
   cursor fact is accepted for a reason R6 does not grant.

8. **The four-shape rejection payload** — from `window-focus` M7. State, carve
   obligation, carved-extent access, non-empty stack at an ending event, each
   with a tree location, the missing fact, and the repairs. This is the best
   answer to a red row anyone produced and it is vocabulary-independent.

9. **`P1`'s missing-fact diagnostic form** — from `brand-context` and
   `brand-tokens`. The payload *is* the rule's own side condition
   (`k ≠ i ∧ k ≠ j`), which makes M7's non-empty-payload metric structural
   rather than aspirational.

10. **The read/write conflict table over overlapping paths** — a repair, not a
    graft, but it must be named: `value-semantics` states D4's decision
    procedure (`PATH`, `EXT`) and never states D4's *policy*. The four-cell table
    (`let`/`let` permitted; every pair containing `inout` or `sink` refused on
    overlap) is load-bearing for P1, P7, P9 and P11 and appears nowhere.

11. **Enumerate `Pool<T>` as an M3 entry or derive it in the language** — from
    the value-semantics soundness critique F2. Every interesting program lives in
    a pool and the candidate never says which it is. Nothing downstream is
    checkable until this is answered.

---

## 6. Disagreements the owner should settle personally

These are the questions where the debate produced two coherent readings and no
technical argument decides between them. Each one moves several candidates'
verdicts, and each is a language-design ruling rather than a defect report.

1. **Is a stale handle into a reusing pool an R1(a)(ii) violation or an M3(d)
   logic error?** `value-semantics` classifies the residue as a logic error the
   constitution leaves to the requirement author; its critique derives it as
   R1(a)(ii) ("address reuse never revives an ended identity"), since `remove`
   ran the node's affine release and the storage therefore ended. This decides
   whether the generation graft is mandatory or optional, and it decides P3's
   verdict for every pooled candidate in the set.

2. **Does M2(ii) refuse a bounds or occupancy compare wrapped in a total
   `pool[h] -> Option<T>`?** The candidate's test is "both arms are safe and both
   are written, unlike a drop flag whose deletion produces unsafety". The
   critique's test is "the check's condition is a safety predicate the checker did
   not discharge", which the bounds arm fails. This is the single line that
   decides `value-semantics`' M2 verdict and, by extension, the safety cap on the
   best base.

3. **Is a *ghost* generation — never materialized, never compared at run time,
   used only to key a static liveness fact — the mechanism M2(ii) refuses by
   name?** `generational-handles` declares Tier B refused and claims Tier A
   clean; two critiques find Tier A is also either M2(ii) or M3. If the owner
   rules ghost generations clean, graft 1 is free and the best base's largest
   residue closes. If not, the residue is permanent and the owner is choosing
   append-only pools with unbounded growth as doctrine.

4. **Owner decision 5, made concrete.** Three candidates write `alloc(A,64)?` —
   a typed allocation-failure outcome — while the settled interim (b) places
   heap exhaustion outside the outcome model under R14(v). Every arena
   derivation in the set depends on which. The owner should either restate the
   interim in a form the derivations can use or accept that P2 and P18 are
   currently written against a refused spelling.

5. **M8's K, the tokenizer, the per-file fraction and the subsystem share
   (owner decision 16).** Four candidates declare M8 violated with no count;
   three claim it met with no count; the critiques' independent counts run from
   11 to 50 constructs. Until K is fixed, "the specification stays small" is not
   a decidable criterion — which is my own lens's foundation, so I flag that my
   ranking's heaviest axis currently rests on a threshold nobody has set.

6. **Is second-class projection an acceptable permanent boundary?** No stored
   iterator, no stored callback holding a projection, no `pick` returning a
   keepable reference, no cursor that outlives its container's scope. This is
   `value-semantics`' largest *capability* cost, it is not a defect, and it is
   not a question a checker can answer. If the owner refuses it, the best base
   changes and `window-focus`'s two-level split becomes the right shape for the
   same problem.

7. **May R4's distinctness ever be grounded in the type discipline rather than
   in a proved relation over a containment structure?** R4(b) forbids inequality
   of identity *names* and is silent on type-level affinity ("two distinct live
   non-copy values occupy disjoint storage"). Three candidates lean on some form
   of it and four more lean on freshness-at-a-minting-site, which the critiques
   read as the forbidden ground in disguise. This one ruling decides P2 and P5
   for half the set.

8. **May the emitter re-derive the per-load identity from the checker's resolved
   place at emission time?** R4's price forbids *requiring* re-derivation to
   reach a stated fact. Four candidates claim their design avoids it; the retired
   `scoped-alias-channel` prototype did exactly that and is the only measured
   evidence anyone has. The reading of "requiring" decides four M9 claims and the
   whole per-load-channel argument.

9. **May the interface be machine-authored?** `whole-program-pinned` rests on
   R7(d)'s sentence that authorship is not R7's business, and its critique
   answers that once acceptance reads only pinned text, the tool is the
   acceptance relation. This is a fork in the road for the whole project, not a
   defect in one candidate, and it should be ruled on before another debate
   assumes either answer.

---

## 7. One closing observation for the record

The critiques converged on three places across almost every candidate,
independent of the tuple chosen:

- **the rules that create and destroy storage** (minting, retirement, reuse,
  relocation) and the names that must survive such an event;
- **the rules that split and rejoin state** (a free state variable in a refine
  rule, a share that escapes, a residual whose representation is unstated, a
  join whose meet is undefined);
- **the unstated bridge between an identity and the runtime values that
  determine it** (`len`, `cap`, a bump offset, a generation, a slot index).

Nine of the twelve candidates lose at least one program to the third of these.
Whatever tuple the owner selects, those three should be the first things written
out in full, and they should be written before the tuple is defended — because
on this evidence a tuple's stated verdicts are not a reliable guide to what its
rules actually admit.


# File: judge-2.md

# Judge 2 — compiler implementer's ranking of the D1–D4 core models

Lens declared up front, because it changes the ordering: I have to **build a
deterministic checker and a fact channel to the backend**. Two things weigh
more for me than for a language judge:

1. **A procedure that does not exist is worse than a procedure that is
   expensive.** A candidate whose central judgment is "search the context for
   a covering multiset", "instantiate an existential with no witness syntax",
   "compute the least common ancestor in an undeclared hierarchy" or "run the
   whole-program tool" is not a thing I can implement to a specification. A
   candidate whose judgment is a cubic closure I can implement, measure and
   then argue about.
2. **A fact channel that has to be re-derived at emission is a second
   compiler.** The retired `scoped-alias-channel` prototype already built that
   re-derivation once; R4's price forbids *requiring* it. Candidates that make
   the source-level identity and the LLVM metadata the same object are worth
   more to me than candidates that promise richer facts through a translation
   layer nobody has priced.

Scoring is after the critiques, not on the candidates' own scorecards. The
cap rule is applied as stated: an undeclared M1 violation caps
`determinism_and_cost` at 3; an undeclared M2 violation caps `safety` at 3.
I mark below where each cap fires, because the caps do most of the
discrimination.

---

## 1. Where the caps fire

| Candidate | Undeclared M1 violation | Undeclared M2 violation |
|---|---|---|
| brand-context | yes — ≥4 unnamed families (atom entailment, quantifier instantiation, symbolic-coefficient intervals, the kill scan), "exactly four and no fifth" false on its own derivations | yes — §2.3's `write`/`free` drop affine obligations, so either R2 leaks or the compiler inserts releases (M2(ii)) |
| brand-tokens | yes — the core judgment is exact-cover search over symbolic extents with no fragment, normalizer or bound | yes — `fixup(Fixup,p)` is a runtime relocation-table lookup or it is unsound; the candidate declares only M8 |
| reference-refined | yes — condition-term entailment is propositional SAT over a representation doubling per diamond, and is absent from the five-family list | yes — P11's `is_hole('C[k])` queries an erased fact at a runtime index; P3's `Slot` tag discharges the occupancy predicate |
| value-semantics | **no** — BIND (height-2), PATH (syntactic prefix), EXT (fixed linear fragment), AFF (type table). Both critiques agree M1 holds | yes — `pool[h]`'s bounds/occupancy arm is a branch on a safety predicate the checker did not discharge |
| whole-program-pinned | yes — for a zero-token writer the tool *is* the acceptance relation, and widening is permitted inside it | yes — the `fixup` clause is an assumed identity re-mapping: erased it is unsound, un-erased it is a runtime forwarding-map lookup |
| generational-handles | yes — a fifth family (quantified container state) plus an unbounded ghost domain (`Live`, `Gen`) with no widening | yes, **in Tier A** — the pool's free list is either compiler-maintained bookkeeping or an unenumerated M3 entry. Only Tier B is declared |
| typestate-protocols | yes — §2.4's join reads an undeclared state hierarchy that need not be a tree, over indexed states that make the lattice infinite | not clearly; M3 is violated instead (`mints #` is a writer-written distinctness axiom) |
| views-fold-unfold | borderline — M1 survives only by fixing an enumeration order over `r^m` witnesses; M10 is exponential and declared met | yes — `fixup(pobj, sigma)` over an erased post-existential |
| ownership-topology | yes — no path-join rule, so `p = p.next` does not terminate; `ite` atoms are arithmetic, not the Boolean bindings termination is argued from | yes — `with_fixup`'s root-set re-forming is a store the source did not write over a copy set the checker cannot bound |
| columns-first | yes — P6's tiling goal is a product of two variables, outside the only named family; atom eviction at the `k` bound is unspecified | yes — P13's `read(pool[h])` needs a materialized `atom→index` table that §2.9 erases |
| refinement-heap | yes — the stated closure **does not terminate**: rules (b) and (c) generate unboundedly many constraints over a fixed monomial set | not clearly; P11 Form A is refused honestly. M8 and M10 are declared |
| window-focus | **no** — four judgments are *absent* (dis over origin sets, the promotion discharge, the parametric carve entry, row subsumption), but nothing admitted searches | not clearly; there is no runtime state anywhere in the model |

Two candidates survive the M1 cap: **value-semantics** and **window-focus**.
That is the single largest discriminator in this debate, and it is the one I
weight hardest, because M1 is the row my implementation either satisfies or
does not — there is no partial credit in code.

---

## 2. Per-candidate notes, by axis

### value-semantics — 34

**Safety 3 (capped).** The frame/heap half is the strongest R1 story of the
set: there is nothing to invalidate because there is no name that outlives its
binding, and P2 gets the strongest possible form of "every old pointer into
b2 is refused" — there is no old pointer. But every interesting program lives
in a pool, and in a pool the guarantee falls twice: `pool[h]`'s bounds arm is
M2(ii) as written (both critiques, independently), and a stale handle in a
reusing pool reads a type-correct wrong occupant. The cross-pool confusion
(`g2[h_from_g1]` is type-correct) is worse than the declared residue, because
append-only does not touch it. R3's only acceptance test is P7, which the
candidate itself grades partial. Cap at 3 is right and the merit is at the cap.

**Interference and facts 3.** `AFF` is the load-bearing distinctness fact and
it is unsound as stated: two `dup`'d `File` wrappers sharing one pool row are
two distinct live non-copy values, and `par { seek(inout f1); read(inout f2) }`
is AFF-licensed. That is a race in R5's rejecting direction, licensed by the
weakest of the candidate's three relations. R6 is claimed met on "the 34/41
tax has no instance" and that is false at every whole-container call
(`push`, `reserve`, `drain`, `insert`, `get`, `compact`). The projected calls
(`helper(inout out[w*s..(w+1)*s], let input)`) are genuinely better than
today's ENT-5, and that part I believe.

**Modularity 4.** Zero identity parameters is R15's metric at its floor and it
is real. Against that: a returned `Handle<T>` names an origin no caller can
read from the signature (R7(a)'s provenance clause fails for every pooled API),
`pick_n<N>` gives one generic definition two verdicts (R15's check-once), and
the closure's captured read is missing from its interface.

**Storage and relocation 5.** Best in the set for R8a: `pointer_of(h)` is
*unwritable*, so interior pointers and third-party relocation cannot both be
written — mutual exclusion by construction rather than by a rule. The cost is
one indirection per pooled access and the refusal of key-renumbering
compaction, both stated. R8b is partial and honestly so: value semantics leaves
placement to the compiler, so any demand must pin a binding.

**Determinism and cost 7.** The reason this candidate wins. Four families, all
of which I can write down and implement: a two-point lattice joined by
conjunction; syntactic prefix comparison over root-plus-steps; a fixed linear
fragment for extents; a type-table fact. No search, no solver, no budget, no
fixpoint above height 2. The measured costs I have to carry are `EXT` and `REF`
entering the ProofContext (the `growing` series at exponent ≈2.6–3.4) and the
transitive instantiation closure for generics (378-line fixture at 82.4 s
against 1757-line `wfgrep` at 42.8 s) — both real, both *inherited* rather than
added, and both bounded by a measure I can state. Against every other
candidate's story (exact-cover search, `r^m` witness instantiation, a
non-terminating closure, an undeclared LCA over a possible DAG, a whole-program
tool with widening) this is not close.

**Writer cost 7.** Three conventions, one projection form, one `sink`. No
lifetimes, regions, identities, state lattice, loan durations or permission
tokens. The counted inventory is eleven constructs, not five (the closure
binder family does not exist in the language today), and the escape class
(P4's stored cursor, P16's stored closure) has no local repair — but this is
still the smallest taught surface on the table by a wide margin, and M8 is the
row every other candidate declares violated or is found to understate by
2.5–5×.

**Performance 5.** P5 and P6 are accepted in the obvious shape with the loop
bound the measured kernel already wrote. The backend gain is *withdrawn*: the
scope is still manufactured at emission from the resolved path, exactly as the
retired prototype did, so the tuple changes what justifies the scope, not who
derives it. Against that: one indirection per pooled access, one discriminant
per vacancy-capable slot, a branch per hole read, and in-place `inout` plus
NRVO must become lowering *rules*, not optimizations.

### window-focus — 27

**Safety 3.** Per-storage state carries every memory-safety refusal and none of
them consults `carves` — the candidate's own answer (a) to its strongest
objection is correct and I checked it. Three things break it. Per-entry state
has no carrier outside an open window, so `take(px)` on a field either
coarsens the whole storage to `Uninit` (rejecting the ladder's Step 1) or needs
a third, unstated name kind. The interior pointer escapes: `ptr<ρP,Node>` is
storable in a struct by §2.8, survives the window close, and is read after
`compact()` with every rule satisfied. And P8 has no accepted spelling at all:
the equality join rejects the candidate's own repair, so R2's acceptance test
is unmet.

defines `!alias.scope` as valid where its `noalias.scope.decl` dominates and
